# Changelog

Notable changes to aterm, in [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/)
format. Versions are `MAJOR.MINOR.0`; `docs/RELEASING.md` § *Versioning and the
build-number ledger* explains them and the build number.

Write each change by hand under `## [Unreleased]`, in an `### Added`, `### Changed`,
`### Removed` or `### Fixed` subsection, for a user to read: the release ships that
text verbatim as the Software Update window's notes, the GitHub release notes and the
update manifest's changelog. There is no generator. `targo --unverified ship release`
refuses a release whose `[Unreleased]` has no entry (comments, blank lines and bare
`###` headings do not count) or contains `'''` or a raw control character, and rolls
it into `## [X.Y.0] - <date>` itself.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Kimi Code runs under the `kimi-alab` harness with aterm Autopilot.** Kimi sessions now use
  aterm's turn-end, approval, question and wall policy, while the harness proves relaunch and
  upgrade claims, resumes the same conversation on a new build, and carries account-pool moves
  across the restart.

- **More of Homebrew runs natively in aterm's `brew`.** `brew nodenv-sync`, `brew pyenv-sync` and
  `brew rbenv-sync` link installed versions the way Homebrew does, `brew bundle` honours
  `HOMEBREW_BUNDLE_FILE`, `brew help` and subcommand help match Homebrew 7.0.13, and `brew install`
  of a shorthand tap name finds the package by its leaf name, as Homebrew does.

### Changed

- **Lines with right-to-left or mixed-direction text are laid out with less work.**

- **Harness versions since v0.191.0: `alab claude harness 0.30`, `alab kimi harness 0.19`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

### Fixed

- Native brew compatibility lets installed formulae share owned directory namespaces, preserves each formula's files when the other is unlinked, and restores aliases after failed activation.

- An agent that was idle for more than half an hour is relaunched after a restart or a crash. aterm kept its record of the agent for 30 minutes and renewed it only when the agent's screen changed, so a quiet agent's exit was never brought back. The record is now renewed every 5 minutes while the agent runs.

- **Setup no longer mistakes Apple's command-line-tools stubs for a compiler.** A developer
  directory whose `clang` leads back to the system stub is no longer reported as a working
  toolchain, so setup does not raise Apple's install dialog on that evidence and still finds a
  standalone toolchain when one is installed.

## [0.191.0] - 2026-11-09

### Changed

- **Release measurements spend less time waiting for idle memory samples.** The memory check
  reads after its quiet period without a second delay, retaining its limits and fresh samples.

- **Harness versions since v0.189.0: `alab claude harness 0.29`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

## [0.190.0] - 2026-11-09

### Added

- **More of Homebrew runs natively in aterm's `brew`.** `brew services list` and `brew services info`
  read launchd directly, formula aliases and old names (`python`, `openssl`, …) resolve as Homebrew
  resolves them, `brew bundle install` upgrades outdated entries, `brew doctor` runs Homebrew's PATH
  and deprecated-formula checks in Homebrew's order, and `brew cat` prefers tap files.

### Changed

- **An idle `aterm node serve` uses less CPU.** Its loops no longer wake 40 times a second each to
  check whether to stop, and its LAN responder reads the vault again only after the vault changes,
  instead of on every query.
- **Accessibility reads of many panes allocate far less.** Panes of the same size share one text
  buffer, so eight 24x80 sessions request about an eighth of the memory they did.

### Fixed

- **A valid update is no longer rejected when verification is slow.** An update whose signature
  check ran out of time while terminals were busy is retried a few seconds later instead of being
  counted as a failed launch, and what aterm had already verified about it is kept.
- **aterm no longer stalls at launch in macOS's crash-restoration dialog.** Restoration policy is set
  before AppKit loads, so a normal launch after a crash starts your terminals as usual.
- **Setup resumes the steps it paused once a needed software upgrade has arrived.**


## [0.189.0] - 2026-11-09

### Added

- **More of Homebrew runs natively in aterm's `brew`.** `brew log` reads tap histories the way
  Homebrew does, `brew list -t` and `-r` order like `ls`, `brew cleanup` prunes downloads by
  Homebrew's age rules, `brew uninstall --dry-run` stays native, linking follows Homebrew's
  directory modes, and pinning an already-pinned formula warns as Homebrew does.

### Changed

- **Mouse, wheel and rewind input on a split tab do less work.** They reuse one layout of the
  visible panes instead of rebuilding it, as pointer motion and hover already did.
- **An idle node no longer advertises itself on the LAN when it cannot read the clock.**

### Fixed

- **A failed update no longer blocks a newer one.** When installing an update fails, a newer
  verified release can replace it, and a replacement that could not start keeps its paced retry
  instead of dropping it.
- **A new install finds the newest release.** `install.sh` asks for the release pointer fresh
  each time, so a cached redirect can no longer hand a new install an older version.
- **A crash keeps its diagnostic.** When an Objective-C exception ends aterm, its log lines are
  written out before the process stops, instead of being lost in a queue.
- **Setup notices the system's developer tools as soon as they arrive**, even when a project
  selected a different Xcode, and a compiler check that was killed is no longer reported as
  broken developer tools.

## [0.188.0] - 2026-11-09

### Added

- **`brew unpack` runs natively in aterm's `brew`.** `brew cleanup`, `brew info` (its statistics
  when you name no package), `brew doctor` and `brew commands` follow Homebrew more closely, and
  downloaded bottles and manifests are cached under Homebrew's own `downloads/` names.

### Fixed

- **An automatic update of a managed tool honours a package choice you just changed.** A queued
  update reads your package choices and the selected checkout again before it fetches, so a
  package you excluded, or a development checkout you selected, while it waited is respected.

- **On a Mac whose Commons moved to a new home, reads of the shared account catalog, the account
  status check and `aterm db commons-tables` and `commons-inventory` check the previous home once per
  read, and `aterm db commons-status` once fewer than it did.** Each check spent part of
  one time bound, so a read on a loaded Mac could run out of time. A vault writer at work during a
  read of the account catalog now makes the read unavailable for that moment, its vault busy,
  rather than read as if this Mac had set up no catalog.

- **`aterm db commons-status` no longer reports this Mac's membership as inactive while its vault
  is being written.** A vault writer holding this Mac's vault during the read, or finishing partway
  through it, made it report `membership-inactive`, `enrollment-pending` or `history-pending`, or
  fail outright; it now reports `control-busy`, which the next read clears.

- **`aterm db commons-status` no longer fails on a Mac that has not opened Commons yet.** On a Mac
  whose vault names Commons but where no aterm window, `aterm node serve` or the Commons runtime
  had opened it yet (a Mac with no window and sharing off stays so), it failed naming a missing
  folder; it now reports `custody-pending`, and the read still creates nothing. `aterm db
  commons-tables` and the other reads of Commons this Mac already holds say so in plain words.

## [0.187.0] - 2026-11-09

### Added

- **More of Homebrew's commands run natively in aterm's `brew`.** `brew alias` and `brew unalias`
  (aliases expand when you run them), `brew formula`, `--prefix`, `--cellar` and `--caskroom` for
  several packages at once, `--prefix --installed`, and `--greedy`, `--greedy-latest` and
  `--greedy-auto-updates` for casks in `brew outdated` and `brew upgrade`.

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.184.0: `alab claude harness 0.28`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.
- **Moving the mouse over a split tab does less work.** Pointer motion, hover and zoomed splits
  reuse one layout of the visible panes instead of building it four or five times per move.
- **A secrets-vault peer check takes one look at the vault per stage**, instead of reading it
  again for each part of the stage.
- **Setup keeps the cause of a transient failure in its diagnostic log**, and a missing keyboard
  service is reported without telling you to retry setup by hand.

### Fixed

- **Release downloads keep working while GitHub's download host fails.** When
  `releases/download` answers with an error, `agh --anonymous asset fetch-public` and the package
  tools read the same file through GitHub's API instead.
- **An update that carries on after its window hands it off is no longer cancelled by the
  hand-off**, and a helper whose follower vanished no longer runs on indefinitely.
- **The companion no longer sits over the letters of a full page's last row** when its body
  slides up or the line has a gap.
- **A startup abandoned part-way rolls back the control lanes it had prepared.**

## [0.186.0] - 2026-11-09

### Fixed

- **`targo --unverified verify land` keeps a branch's CHANGELOG entries under `[Unreleased]`
  across a release cut.** A cut writes its version heading above the entries it ships, so a branch
  that merged main after one had each entry it wrote into `[Unreleased]` merged under that
  release, reading as shipped by it. The landing now moves such an entry back to the top of its
  kind under `[Unreleased]` (in its own merge, or after a merge made by hand in a commit of its
  own), and says which. A squash or revert after the cut strands none for good. An entry the
  branch wrote under a release, moved under one cut before it wrote the entry, or cut a release
  over itself stays, as does one a rebase of the branch's own commits replayed under a cut, which
  reads as written there. It also drops a stranded copy of an entry the changelog holds elsewhere,
  and an entry's old words that main rewrote and the merge brought back (the changelog's union
  merge keeps both sides, so the next release would have shipped the old words beside the new).
  Census's `changelog-repeat` finding names both copies of a repeat, since the tree cannot say
  which one shipped.

- **On macOS, quitting no longer kills a zsh with `less` or `vim` in front before it saves its
  history.** aterm held every terminal open while it waited for the shells to end, so a program
  in front waiting on its terminal never saw it close, the shell behind it never ran its exit,
  and aterm killed it about 1.5 s later with its history unsaved and `zshexit` unrun. Quit now
  lets go of each terminal it hangs up, the PTY keeper's copies included, so the program sees end
  of file and the shell exits by itself: measured on macOS 27.0.1, Quit with `less` or `vim` in
  front took 71–88 ms with history saved, where it took about 2.1 s and saved none. On Linux the
  shell is still ended about 1.5 s after Quit, as before.

## [0.185.0] - 2026-11-09

### Fixed

- **Settings ▸ Messages shows within half a second an entry aterm ends or changes on its own.**
  When the page had shown another change less than half a second before, an entry aterm then
  ended or changed while nothing else was happening (a render repair clearing its entry, for one)
  could stay as it was until something else woke aterm, as late as the next change of the page's
  "minutes ago" words.

- **macOS's bash keeps a function's definition and a line that starts with a subshell.** Under
  a bash before 5.3, macOS's /bin/bash 3.2 among them and Ubuntu 24.04's 5.2, a line that runs
  no simple command at its top (`f() { … }`, `function g { … }`, `(exit 3)`, `(cd x && make)`)
  had no command block, no exit status and no run in the session log: bash's DEBUG trap never
  fires for it, and only 5.3 has the hook that runs before every line. Such a line now gets its
  block and its run at the next prompt, from the history entry bash saved for it, with the
  status it left, so a failing `(cd x && make)` reads as failed. Its block starts only once
  the line has ended, after anything it printed, so its time reads as none. A line that ran
  nothing makes no run, though history saved it: a comment, a blank line, a syntax error, or a
  line cancelled with Ctrl-C at the `>` continuation prompt. Nor does a line history saves no
  new entry for: a space-led one under `HISTCONTROL=ignorespace` or `ignoreboth`, a repeat
  under `ignoredups`, one `HISTIGNORE` matches, or any with history off. A shell that loads
  bash-preexec is left to it, and before 5.3 it hears none of these lines either. bash 5.3 is
  unchanged.

## [0.184.0] - 2026-11-08

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.183.0: `alab claude harness 0.27`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

### Fixed

- **A staged update installs by itself with nobody at the Mac, and says what it waits for.** An
  update that arrived while the Mac setup offer was up waited: on 0.147.0 and earlier for a
  click or key in an aterm window, and since 0.148.0 for the setup's run or check under way to
  finish, which could itself wait for you. An offer nobody has touched no longer holds it,
  whatever the setup is doing. When something of yours must finish first (a password prompt, a
  setup draft you typed, an install's tab), `aterm ctl update status` names it as
  `apply_held=`, and the log says once what holds it and what lets it go.

- **`aterm help theme` and `aterm theme schema` no longer mention a message band the window does
  not have.** A theme name that resolves to nothing is now said to be explained by the listing,
  `aterm ctl theme`, Settings' theme row and Settings ▸ Messages, and the `accent_color` key no
  longer lists a message band's meter among the surfaces it colours. The theme template and the
  theme author's guide say the same.

## [0.183.0] - 2026-11-08

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.182.0: `alab claude harness 0.26`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- **Claude Code's permission chip says one bit, `yolo` or `lame`, and a click restarts the
  conversation to turn it over.** On a supervised Claude Code tab the chip beside the Autopilot
  chip reads `yolo` where Claude Code's pill reads bypass permissions and `lame` in every other
  mode: `auto` no longer counts as on, and plan, accept edits and the rest are no longer named
  on the chip. It shows at rest on every tab aterm's harness hosts, and a narrow rule gives up
  the Team chip before it, keeping it as long as it keeps the Autopilot chip; it draws nothing
  (no longer `◌ mode`) until the pill is read. Its hover says
  `no permission prompts · click: lame` or `not yolo · click: yolo`. A click no longer presses
  shift+tab through Claude Code's modes: it restarts the conversation, as an update does.
  From `yolo` the new command line has no permission flag, so Claude Code starts in the mode
  its own settings choose; from `lame` it has `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Every
  permission flag on the old line comes off first, whoever typed it; the conversation, build,
  model and login stay. A click waits as a press of ⬆️ does, for the turn, a box, a draft (a
  slash command being typed among them), a tab you hold, a usage limit or a sign-in, and is
  drawn `◐` with what it waits for on its hover; a second click takes it back until the
  restart begins. It goes past Claude Code's background shells, which the restart ends, and
  the hover says so (`· ends 1 shell`). It is refused, with the reason on its hover, where no
  restart can be made: Claude Code not started from a shell, a shell other than zsh, bash or
  fish, a command line that cannot be read or rewritten, a tab another supervisor holds, a
  credit claim's worker, or an agent that must end first. The click waits in memory only:
  closing the tab, or a seamless update, drops it. Claude Code's mode row is now rewritten in
  bypass only; in every other mode it stands as Claude Code draws it, its pill, key hints and
  effort hint included, so the effort can show there and beside `◆`. A new tab still starts
  yolo, and every other restart keeps the mode the pill shows.

### Fixed

- **An update no longer ends a Claude Code it cannot start again.** On an API-key or gateway route
  whose shell's environment aterm could not read (macOS keeps `/bin/zsh`'s unread), an update, a
  press of ⬆️ included, ended Claude Code and then waited for its account for good, leaving the
  tab at its shell. The update now checks the account before it ends anything, and waits with
  Claude Code still running.

- **A button held when the window loses focus, its tab switches or the stats lens closes is let
  go.** A press on a native control no longer stays held, and the stats lens no longer passes
  clicks through to Claude Code's glass under it.

## [0.182.0] - 2026-11-08

### Fixed

- **On Linux, restarting or updating the aterm node no longer closes your windows.** A window the
  node opened ran inside the node's own service, so every node stop or restart (an install, an
  update, `aterm node off`/`on`) ended the window and its shells with it. Each window now runs in
  its own systemd scope and outlives the node.

- **Page Down in Settings stops at the true end of a long page.** A page whose last screen already
  showed everything could take one more Page Down that only nudged the list a few points, or
  scrolled the last card's caption away. The last screen is now the first one that shows the
  list's end whole.

- **Clicks in a split's header, divider, pet or scrollbar reach them while the stats lens is
  open.** The lens no longer takes those clicks for itself.

- **A Claude Code sign-in that refreshes its token is no longer reported as signed out.** When a
  refresh raced another writer for longer than two seconds, aterm read the race as a sign-out; it
  now waits for the real answer.

## [0.181.0] - 2026-11-08

### Fixed

- **Resting Claude Code tabs no longer read `running` every 30 seconds.** Claude Code at rest
  redraws rows that read the same about every 30 s, and the tab's status took that for activity:
  it went running, then quiet again 6 s later, putting false activity into the survey and the
  harness's status. Status now counts only a change to what the screen shows (a character, a
  colour, an image) as activity.

- **The harness no longer ends a Claude Code turn one line short when its first look comes just
  before the reply's last line.** Under a status line, a wait whose first look at the session fell
  in the 23 ms between Claude Code's title going to rest and its reply's last line being drawn took
  that look for the end, so Land or Cruise could act on a reply missing its last lines. A look
  that finds the turn over under a resting title now waits one short settle and looks again.

- **Find and the network lens act on the window they were asked from.** Output in a window that
  was not in front left its open find bar's matches stale, and choosing Network from a window's
  menu opened the lens on the frontmost window instead; both now follow their own window. A
  scrollbar drag also ends when the window loses focus or its tab is switched away, instead of
  staying held.

## [0.180.0] - 2026-11-08

### Fixed

- **A clean quit's session closes now reach the bus.** When aterm quit, each session's close
  (`out=app-quit`) went only to the journal on disk, so a program reading the bus could tell a
  quit from a crash only by the bridge withdrawing the sessions, and a quit whose withdrawal
  missed the bus read as a crash and paged `exited gone`. aterm now closes every session at the
  quit and, while its bridge reaches the broker, waits at most the quit's half second for the
  bus to hold those closes before it tells the bridge goodbye; the journal writes the same
  closes. `aterm fabric brief` shows a quit's session `closed out=app-quit`, and its `--json`
  form says it too (a new `closed` key: the close's `out=` word, null while the session is
  open); `aterm link notify --on need` pages nothing for it or for the relaunch that restores
  it, and a crash still pages its exit once. A quit whose bridge cannot reach the broker waits
  for nothing once the bridge has said so (until then, at most the half second), its journal
  holds the closes, and on the bus it still reads as a crash at its relaunch and pages `exited
  gone` once.

- **Pane dividers, gap scrollbars and the find bar answer the pointer where they are.** A drag or
  release on a pane divider, a press on a scrollbar in the gap between panes, and the window's
  find-bar toggle now go to what lies under the pointer, as they did before the native tab strip,
  instead of reaching the pane beside them.
- **aterm on Linux no longer reconnects on every Wi-Fi scan.** A radio that is up but joined to
  nothing, and each router advertisement refreshing an IPv6 address, were read as a network move,
  so a Linux node redialled its peers over and over. Only a real change of route or address
  counts now.
- **A script-installed aterm turns on its fabric, as the app does.** On a Linux machine installed
  by `install.sh`, the fabric stayed off by default because the check looked for a Mac app
  bundle; it now recognises the installed `aterm` on the service's own path.

## [0.179.0] - 2026-11-08

### Added

- **The Accounts card marks each local midnight.** Its work row and every lane carry a short
  tick at the foot of the cell where each day begins on the work row's clock, so a week of use
  reads by day at a glance.

### Changed

- **Settings reads more clearly at every width and text size.** A picker tile's name, a field's
  path and a Messages entry's title wrap whole instead of being cut; a bar's buttons take their
  brief forms on one line before they stack; Themes' strip keeps its facts and errors whole;
  Customize, the palette slot and the color wheel spell a colour the same way; a trail colour
  that follows the cursor reads "Cursor color"; and an unavailable theme says why.
- **Universal Control's timing says when it really applies.** With "Keep ALab tools up to date"
  off, a saved change waits for the daily apply, which runs once a day when aterm starts.
  Settings now says so instead of promising a time it would not keep.

### Fixed

- **`aterm ctl settings` takes back the words it answers with.** After `settings unset`, typing
  the row's own reply (such as `Auto (default)`) back as a value was refused for some rows; it
  now writes nothing, for every kind of row. A default value is no value, and choosing the
  built-in Default theme in the palette removes the theme from the file, as Settings' picker
  does.
- **A secrets table opened while the vault is being written waits instead of failing.** The
  open read a writer's moment as "Commons membership is not ready for table access", which
  nothing retried; it now reads as busy and is retried.
- **The repository refresh refreshes clean checkouts on an older git.** On a git before 2.44
  (such as Ubuntu's stock 2.43) a clean checkout was never refreshed while its row said Ok.
  aterm's own git reads also no longer fetch missing objects by themselves outside its
  credential route.

## [0.178.0] - 2026-11-08

### Changed

- **A message in aterm's own window no longer waits to be shown.** No window has shown message
  rows above its tabs since they went, yet each message still waited for a place there: after a
  minute (or its hold, if longer) it ended as not shown, Settings ▸ Messages said "waiting to
  show" and then "not shown — too many at once", and an update warning said while no window was
  on screen never ended on its own. A message now lasts its hold from when it appears, and
  Settings ▸ Messages says `live`, then how long it was live (`live for 8 s`); an update warning
  said while no window is on screen waits for one, then lasts its hold. `aterm ctl messages` rows
  no longer carry `glass=` (the web terminal's message rows keep it), and `aterm ctl metrics`
  names the messages' deadline owner `messages` where it said `message_band`.

- **Quiet secrets sharing costs less CPU.** On a Mac sharing secrets with many peers, a round
  that exchanged nothing still re-derived and re-signed this Mac's access request each time it
  opened a table, and reread and re-verified the vault for every check. A round now reuses the
  request it made and a settled file's digest while nothing it read has changed; a change, or a
  writer mid-apply, is still read afresh.

### Fixed

- **The find bar and a banner shield the scrollbar and Settings' controls beneath them.** A
  pointer over the find bar or a paste banner could still light or press the scrollbar on the
  rows they cover, or hover a control on a Settings or editor page underneath.

- **Tab-strip clicks work with Settings or an editor in front.** A middle click on a tab closes
  it, and a right or middle press on the strip or the page settles a tab rename in progress, as
  they do over a terminal.

- **Settings' page list keeps its row whole.** After a resize or a text-size change the list no
  longer cuts or hides the open page's row; a click on a row at the list's foot opens that page,
  where it used to scroll the list and land on nothing; and Tab onto a row the wheel scrolled
  away brings it back into view.

- **The cursor companion stays on its row on very wide panes.** On a pane wider than 256
  columns, the companion setting off along its row toward a far caret could lose sight of the
  row and rise into the row above for a frame or two.

## [0.177.0] - 2026-11-08

### Changed

- **`aterm ctl @self sys jobs` no longer says a program waits on macOS's program check without
  evidence.** A process with no user thread yet and an old fork read `held`, so a `/bin/sleep`
  that was simply running could be reported as stuck at the check. A program is now `held` only
  where its pending request is seen; otherwise it reads as not started, and `verify`'s report of
  leftover processes says the cause is unconfirmed.

### Fixed

- **A link in another pane no longer lights under the pointer.** In a split window, a pointer over
  a pane other than the focused one was read at the nearest cell of the focused pane, so a link or
  path on that pane's edge underlined, and opened on a click, while the pointer was elsewhere.
  Links and paths are now found only while the pointer is inside the focused pane.

- **The find bar and a banner keep the pointer from what lies beneath them.** A pane divider under
  the find bar showed the resize cursor, and a right or middle press on the find bar or a banner
  went on to the tab or pane below. Both now stop there, and such a press settles a tab rename in
  progress.

- **Secrets that changed while sharing was paused reach this Mac once sharing resumes.** A vault
  pass that ran while sharing was off could finish without taking the work waiting for it, and
  nothing brought that work back when sharing came on again. The pause is now remembered and one
  fresh read of the vault follows, whatever the network's state or retry timer.

## [0.176.0] - 2026-11-08

### Changed

- **`aterm ctl metrics` no longer prints the `message_band_motion` deadline owner.** No window
  has shown message rows above its tabs since they went, so nothing on them moved, and the wake
  that timed their motion is gone with their drawing.

### Fixed

- **A process that rewrites its title no longer puts its arguments in the session log.** A
  program's name came from its `argv[0]` with the blanks dropped, so a title a process set for
  itself (`postgres: <user> <db> …`, `npm run <script>`, perl's `$0`) reached the log's
  `prog=`, `aterm ctl status`'s `program=`, the survey and the brief as one word holding its
  arguments. A title with a blank is now read whole only where it is the path of the very
  file the process runs (an app under a folder with a space); otherwise it names its program
  by its first word (`postgres`, `npm`), or the kernel's name for it. A first word that is a
  path cut at a space (`/opt/My Tools/tool`) names its program only where it is a program
  file, so a folder's name never stands in for it. A one-word `argv[0]` (`exec -a NAME`)
  still names the program. Deciding whether an agent handed its terminal to another program
  no longer looks up any path on the thread that draws the window. Run in private lab
  instances, bash 3.2 and zsh: a perl `$0` title, a postgres-style title and a real `npm run`
  read `qzt`, `postgres` and `npm`, with none of their argument words in the log's `prog=`,
  `status`'s `program=`, the survey's program or the brief.

- **A script that never ran is never named.** A `#!` script's name reached a command's
  `detail=` whenever any process in that command mapped its interpreter, so in
  `./a.sh && ./b.sh` whose first script failed, `b.sh` was logged though it never ran. A
  script is now named only where its interpreter's process was handed that very script where
  the kernel puts it, right after the words of the script's `#!` line (the path matched to the
  script's file by device and inode), so `sh -n ./b.sh` and `./lint.sh ./b.sh` no longer name
  `b.sh` either; otherwise the command reads its own job's program (`sh`) or nothing. Run in
  private lab instances, bash 3.2 and zsh: the failing chain, `sh -c 'sleep 1' && false &&
  ./c.sh`, `./lint.sh ./b.sh && ./b.sh` whose lint failed and `sh -c '…' ./b.sh && ./b.sh`
  read `sh`, and a script that ran still reads its own name, an `env -S` script and one whose
  `#!` line adds a flag among them. On Linux, a script heard only through the proc connector
  reads its interpreter.

- **`aterm.log` keeps no document path or shell path from an open failure or a failed
  launch.** A document that could not open and a launch that could not go on wrote their
  whole message to `aterm.log` once they stopped showing an alert. The log now keeps the
  message's title or kind and its length; the text still goes to stderr.

## [0.175.0] - 2026-11-08

### Added

- **On a Mac with one Claude Code login, `aterm harness accounts history` also shows the
  usage walls Claude Code's own transcripts record that this Mac's readings missed.** Each
  five-hour or weekly window that reached its limit before the readings history began, while
  the usage tap was off, or in a session run in another terminal, is a full window on the day
  it ended, marked `(backfill)`: `Tue Sep 16  5h 1 window, peak 100%, 1 full (backfill)`. Only
  walls from after the newest sign-in of another account aterm saw on that home, after the
  readings last showed another account there, after the newest `/login` the transcripts
  record, and after any conversation another login held, are shown; nothing is shown where
  the pool lists several logins, whose walls one home's transcripts mix, or where the home's
  profile cannot be read. The transcripts are read for at most 10 seconds and 1 GiB; a read
  cut short says `transcripts read in part`. `--json` adds `backfill` (`booked`, `complete`,
  `cut`, `why` and the windows, each `src: "backfill"`). It is worked out at each run and
  never written, and keeps no transcript text and no address.

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.174.0: `alab claude harness 0.25`, `alab kimi harness 0.18`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- **`aterm ctl help pointer` and `aterm ctl help chrome` no longer describe the message band.**
  aterm shows no message rows above your tabs, so `pointer click` counts no press against
  `notice act`'s ten a minute, and a development build's `chrome` prints `a11y` lines for
  Autopilot chips only.

### Removed

- **`aterm harness accounts stats --json` is schema 2: it no longer carries `fleet`,
  `machine.name`, a window's `cached`, a spend window's `machines` or a `used_by` entry's `name`.
  `aterm harness accounts --json` is schema 2 too: its windows no longer carry `cached`.** They
  never changed (`null`, `false`, 1 and 1, or `here`), since `accounts stats` polls no other
  machine. Every Mac's account rows are in `aterm harness accounts`' lab journal section,
  `aterm harness accounts history` and `aterm db alab quota`.

### Fixed

- **A notification, a bell and a mail now sit on what was running when they came.** The session
  log put every OSC 9 notification, BEL and mail mark on the session itself (`mark - notify`),
  even while a command or an agent's turn was open, so `log` could not say which command rang
  and no run or turn close ever counted its mail (`mail=`). They now attach to the deepest open
  node, as the design says: the open step, turn or run, else the session. A mail's landing and
  verdict, and the session's own facts (directory, title, input), stay on the session.
- **A command that ends just before its tab closes is now in the session log.** Commands were
  logged only when aterm's status sweep next looked at the tab, so a command that finished and
  was followed at once by a close (`aterm ctl @<sid> close` right after `wait`) left the closed
  log with no record of it and no count of the loss. Closing a session now reads its finished
  commands, and any notification or bell since the last look, before the log closes.
- **The session log no longer keeps the running command's line as the tab title.** aterm's
  shell integration sets the tab title to the command line while a command runs, and the log's
  in-memory title mark kept that text, arguments included, so `log tier=content` printed it.
  A title that is the command line now keeps only its fingerprint, in memory
  (`mark - title title_fp=<hex>` at `tier=content`); the saved log and the default `log` say
  only that the title changed. The prompt's title and a program's own title, such as Claude
  Code's summary of its conversation, keep their text in memory as before. The tab still shows
  the title the shell set.
- **Turning Claude Code's harness off (`[harness.claude] enabled = false`) now also turns off
  the window's limit reset and usage tap.** The window kept both on under `[harness] limit_reset`
  and `usage_tap`, so a Claude Code session still running as you switched it off could use the
  wall's one limit-reset attempt. A limit reset now checks the switch again just before it is
  claimed, and a headless instance that supervises nothing (`[harness] headless = false`) keeps
  both off as it does its other account switches.

- **The session log says how a key ended an approval box or a question.** When you, or an
  `aterm ctl key` or `send`, pressed Enter on a Claude Code box or question, the session log
  closed it `out=passed`, whatever the key chose; only the harness's own answers read
  `approved`, `declined` or `answered`. The close now reads the key and the option the screen
  showed it landing on: Enter on a focused Yes, or a Yes option's number, is `approved`; Enter on a
  focused No, a No option's number or Esc is `declined`; choosing a question's option is
  `answered`. These closes say `conf=heuristic`, since the screen shows what the key chose, not what
  the program did; a decline Claude Code reports as an interrupt still says `conf=strong`. `by=`
  still names who pressed it. A key aterm cannot place still closes `out=passed`: typed text, an
  option it cannot read, a No that also keeps a setting (`No, and block reads outside the working
  directories`, which aterm's box reader files with the kept Yes options), a screen read from
  before an earlier key took effect, or a box that changed since aterm last read the screen.
- **`aterm harness accounts history` counts each five-hour window once on a day a renamed
  account row's two series share.** Where one file kept only its `day` row, its windows were
  lost; a window that straddled the rename counted once in each file once its closes aged out
  (90 days); and a window the two files closed on two dates counted on both. A `day` row now
  names the windows it counts by their resets (`anchors`, with the full ones in `full`, at most
  six), and a window counts on the earliest date it ended, full where either file read it full.
  The usage tap's first reading after a row learned its lab key now carries that key, and a
  reading whose row now names another account is recorded under the account it was read for
  instead of being dropped.
- **On Windows, a PowerShell command's detail names the program it ran again.** Since 0.146.0
  a Windows session's `detail=` in `status`, `survey` and the session log named only shell
  builtins, because aterm had no way there to see what a command ran. aterm now lists the
  processes in the session's job (the one the shell runs in, which its programs join) as the
  tab's output is read: at most every 100 ms, and at once when a command starts or ends and at
  the output after each. It names a program by its file name without `.exe` or `.com`, in any
  case, as cmd and pwsh find it: `ping` names `PING.EXE`. It reads only each process's image
  path, never a window title, a command line or what the process holds. Only a shell that marks
  where its command starts gets this: pwsh and Windows PowerShell do, and cmd.exe's prompt
  cannot, so a cmd.exe tab still names only builtins. A program typed as a path, a program that
  starts and ends between two listings, or one that leaves the job is still not named. A
  program a command leaves running in the background is named in that command's block, not in
  the next one. `status` says `exec_watch=job`. This was built and checked on macOS for
  Windows; it has not been run on a Windows machine yet.
- **A stalled file system no longer costs the window a wait for every new program a running
  command starts.** aterm checks a typed command against the files programs ran from on one
  background thread. When that thread hung on a network mount, each status sweep that saw a
  new program in a running command (a build) waited up to 10 ms more on the window's thread,
  and the questions queued without end. Now, once the thread has hung for 10 ms on one
  question, the sweep neither waits nor asks until it answers, and at most 16 questions wait
  for it. A detail that needs that check names nothing meanwhile, and its program once the
  thread answers.

## [0.174.0] - 2026-11-07

### Added

- **On a Mac with one Claude Code login, `aterm harness accounts history` also shows the
  earlier usage walls Claude Code's own transcripts record.** Each five-hour or weekly window
  that reached its limit before this Mac's readings history began is a full window on the day
  it ended, marked `(backfill)`: `Tue Sep 16  5h 1 window, peak 100%, 1 full (backfill)`. Only
  walls from after the newest sign-in of another account aterm saw on that home, and after the
  newest `/login` the transcripts record, are shown, and nothing is shown where the pool lists
  several logins, whose walls one home's transcripts mix. The transcripts are read for at most
  10 seconds and 1 GiB; a read cut short says `transcripts read in part`. `--json` adds
  `backfill` (`booked`, `complete`, `cut`, `why` and the windows, each `src: "backfill"`). It
  is worked out at each run and never written, and keeps no transcript text.

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.173.0: `alab claude harness 0.24`, `alab kimi harness 0.17`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- **A test build gives back its compile's memory once its tests run, and a small build no
  longer waits behind one that cannot start yet.** A `targo test` claimed the most its whole run
  had taken, which is its compile's, and held all of it through its tests, which on this Mac take
  11% to 25% of that (`-p aterm-gui`: 17 GiB to compile, under 2 GiB to run), so every build
  behind it waited for memory nothing was using. Its claim now steps down to what its tests took
  in its earlier runs, a fifth more and at least 1 GiB more, as soon as it runs a program the
  build made, and back up to what it was admitted with should the run outgrow that, counting what
  a test took between two reads. A build with no run kept, its own or a wider selection's, learns
  the figure on its first run and claims as before; a wider selection's only bounds the step,
  and never raises what the build claims. And a claim that fits the free memory
  now goes ahead of a waiting claim that cannot start yet, as long as it takes no more than that
  claim can spare: the most it can hold without making the waiting claim start any later as the
  builds ahead of it end or step down. A waiting claim that asked to run alone spares nothing, so
  no stream of small builds starves it, and one that waits for room beside it no build holds (a
  VM's boot) spares what fit beside it before. `aterm pkg capacity` shows both: `stepped to 3 GiB
  as its run began` beside a held build's memory, and, beside a claim that cannot start yet, the
  most a claim behind it may take and go first (`--json`: `run_mem`, `stepped`, `spares`); a
  waiting claim's line says what it may take past the claims that cannot start.

- **An update from v0.147.0 or older no longer shows that release's message rows above your
  tabs.** Until the update committed, the new aterm took the old one's message band (1 to 3
  rows under the tab strip) and showed it, still but clickable, then dropped it, and every tab
  grew by those rows. It now takes no band: the messages still cross to Settings ▸ Messages,
  the window opens at the size of its tabs' grid, and nothing re-sizes at the commit. Where
  those rows come to what the Full stats deck adds to the Folded one, the window keeps its size
  and each tab grows by them once as it opens. During any update a carried message reads as
  waiting to show (`glass=-` in `aterm ctl messages`) until the commit, and no longer runs out
  its time unseen while the update waits.

### Fixed

- **The ALab lane reads the engine's ledger where promotes record it.** `lane run alab` mapped
  each signed release to its dev commit through `~/publication/mappings.json`, a checkout that
  releases no longer fast-forward, so on a Mac that cuts aterm it fell further behind every
  promote and left new releases unresolved. Each run, a dry run included, now reads the ledger
  on the engine repository's main through the staging host, as the staging identity; a main the
  host does not serve leaves the release unresolved and packs nothing.

- **Bash 4.4 under functrace records each typed line whole.** On bash 4.4 with `set -T` or
  `shopt -s extdebug`, each line after a session's first was recorded by its first simple command
  (`x=1` for `x=1 && echo c`, `ls /dev/null` for `ls /dev/null | cat`), so its command block
  (`aterm ctl blocks`' `cmdline=`) named only part of what ran. Bash 4.4 changes what `$HISTCMD`
  reads once a function that used `local -` returns, and aterm's helper uses `local -` under
  functrace; below bash 5 aterm now tells a typed line by the last history entry alone. Other bash
  versions record lines as before.

## [0.173.0] - 2026-11-07

### Added

- **`aterm harness accounts stats` says how far each window moved over the last day.** Each
  window's line ends with what its readings history on this Mac shows since 24 hours ago:
  `+18 since 24h`, `new window since 13:00` where the window it was in has ended, or
  `reset used since 13:00` where a limit reset was used. Where the history holds no reading
  near the span's start it says the span it did compare (`+5 since 3h`, `+30 since 2d1h`), and
  it never compares two accounts, whether another login signed in to the home or the row went
  to another account. `--since 3h` (a minute to 90 days) reads another span; `--json`
  carries it as each window's `since`, and the accounts report's `--json` gives each row's
  windows the same 24-hour `since`. It is for reading only: the harness decides nothing from
  it.

- **`aterm harness accounts history` prints each account's days.** For every row of the pool,
  or one named by its label or account key (`c-…`), one line per local day from this Mac's
  readings history: the week's figures and reset, how many five-hour windows ended and how
  many of them reached the limit, the day's highest five-hour figure, the window still open,
  each limit reset used and each time another login signed in, with that day's ledger and lab
  journal lines beneath. Only that account's readings count: a row renamed since keeps its
  older history, found by its account key, and a label given to another account shows none of
  the one before. `--since 7d` (a day to 400 days, 30 days unless named) sets the span,
  `--rows` adds the account's stored readings as written, and `--json` carries the days beside
  the lines it gave before. It stores nothing of its own; like every accounts read, it first
  completes an accounts update that was cut short.

### Fixed

- **The main watch lane finishes the tree it actually sampled when development work arrives.**
  Ordinary work keeps priority for the memory, cores or disk its next Background stage also
  needs, but no longer makes `verify watch` discard every completed stage and restart on another
  moving-main head. A Release or line still ends the repeatable judgment, and its first proven
  red still stops it. Red suspect ranges now start at the unique nearest passing ancestor by
  commit topology, never whichever old or unrelated verdict happened to publish last.

- **Dev checks judge the engine's committed files, not whatever a checkout holds.** `verify
  export-scan` and the census's `capture-privacy` read the publication engine's
  forbidden-content baseline and registry from `~/publication`'s working tree, which releases
  no longer fast-forward: on a Mac that cuts aterm they judged an ever-older baseline, and an
  uncommitted edit there counted as the engine's. They now read one commit of the engine, as
  a cut's ledger, `ship status`, `ship yank` and `ship provision`'s registry probe now do
  too: `PUBLICATION_ENGINE`'s HEAD, else the engine origin's main imported at the time through
  agh as this Mac's identity for it, never git's own transport (one to two seconds). An edit to the baseline is judged once it is pushed to the engine's origin, or,
  with `PUBLICATION_ENGINE` naming that checkout, once it is committed there.

- **A revoked ledger row is no longer anyone's source.** `ship release`, a cut by hand and the
  ALab lane read the publication engine's `mappings.json` without its `revoked` rows, as the
  engine's own projection does. A revoked aterm row could have been released by a cut, and the
  lane mapped ay's and trust-ir's signed commits to revoked dev commits (the first in sorted
  order). The lane now also refuses a signed commit that two live rows claim, rather than
  taking the first.

- **A release no longer loses its stage when another session moves `~/publication`.** On m3
  (2026-11-07) something fast-forwarded the shared engine checkout to a peer's engine code
  while 0.172.0's `pub stage` ran in it, and the engine refused the push 19 minutes in. A
  release now runs the engine in a clone only it writes, `<git common dir>/aterm-release/engine`,
  made and fast-forwarded from the origin `--engine`'s engine (default `~/publication`) names;
  nothing it does runs, syncs or writes that checkout. Until it has synced its clone, and
  throughout a dry run, it judges the engine's ledger and code on the origin's main, with the
  ledger rows its clone holds unpushed (an audit or ledger row whose push failed), which its
  next sync delivers instead of stranding them. A cut, `ship status` or `ship yank` run by
  hand reads the ledger on the engine's origin rather than a checkout's working tree.

- **A NEEDS YOU line stays up when the harness's settings change.** Each change to `[harness]`
  hands every tab's Autopilot over to a fresh loop, and that loop took down a NEEDS YOU the agent
  had named a few turns earlier, although the agent never said `NEEDS YOU: nothing`; where the
  need was still on screen, it put it up again and typed "Needs on screen; carry on." a second
  time. The new loop now keeps the need the window shows, also through the turn the old loop's
  last prompt started, and types "Needs on screen; carry on." only where the old loop had not
  typed it yet.

## [0.172.0] - 2026-11-07

### Added

- **A program macOS's program check stranded is named apart from one it holds.** When
  `syspolicyd` crashes, launchd starts another and new programs start, but a program the old
  one was checking can stay held before its first instruction while `status` reads
  `syspolicyd=ok`, and aterm said only that it was held. `status` now counts such programs
  (`program_check_stranded=` after `program_check=`), `privacy`'s `devtools` line counts them
  instance-wide, `sys jobs` names each (`finding kind=program-check-stranded ... daemon=`), and
  the message log records each once (`program-check.stranded`). aterm names a program it read
  unrun before the `syspolicyd` running now started, once that one has run 10 minutes awake
  with room in its pool and no newer program held, and keeps naming it while it reads it unrun
  as the same program; the count reads `0` only when every held program was judged, and `-`
  while one may be stranded and nothing read tells. Nothing is ended for you and no restart is
  needed: stop what started it and run it again.

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.171.0: `alab claude harness 0.23`, `alab agy harness 0.16`, `alab muse harness 0.19`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- **Each account's readings history also records walls and limit resets seen, and the usage
  forms aterm cannot read yet are kept as records.** The history file
  (`stats/u-<label>@<machine>.jsonl`) gains a row each time a session's screen shows that the
  Fable or Sonnet week reached its limit (that week and the reset it named), and each time
  aterm's limit reset first sees the limit resets left or sees them change (their kind, count
  and use-by time); `aterm harness accounts history` lists both among each day's events. Where
  a supervised Claude Code session's screen shows a usage form no reader here reads (Claude
  Code's own usage-credits box, or a limit wall or `You've used …` notice the stats do not
  read), the harness keeps that form as drawn in a `CAPTURED` journal record, a few of each
  kind, with e-mail addresses and the composer's unsent draft masked and nothing pressed. Both
  are records only: the harness decides nothing from them.

### Fixed

- **A credential request can be declined on the vault admin's Mac.** `aterm secrets need retire
  <id> --declined` told you a request another Mac raised could be declined on the vault admin's
  Mac, but there it refused in the same words, so a request from a Mac that was reinstalled or
  is gone kept asking for 30 days. On the vault admin's Mac it now declines another Mac's request
  that is waiting for a person, by the id `aterm secrets need ls --all` prints, and that Mac's
  ask comes down; its own request takes that id too. Where a Mac cannot decline for the lab, the
  refusal says why.

- **The drive-aterm skill no longer teaches a wait that ends mid-reply.** The skill aterm
  installs for driving another session taught waiting out an interactive agent's turn on its
  `esc to interrupt` footer hint (`turn settle=gone:esc.to.interrupt`, `await gone
  esc.to.interrupt`). Under a status line (aterm's usage tap or your own) Claude Code never
  draws that hint, and a gone wait answers at once when its row is not drawn, so the taught wait
  returned while the reply was still being drawn. The skill now teaches what `aterm help` does:
  `turn typed=1 settle=submitted`, then `await agent idle,prompt,question,wall
  since=<agent_rev>`, whose verdict reads Claude Code's window title beside its screen. `aterm
  ctl`'s note on a pattern split at a space gives `Do.you.want.to.proceed` as its one-token
  example instead of the footer hint.

- (developer tool) **`verify census` fails an `[Unreleased]` entry a release already shipped.**
  A branch that merged `main` before a release cut and merges it again after can bring an entry
  the cut rolled into `## [X.Y.Z]` back under `## [Unreleased]` word for word. Nothing read it
  as wrong, so the next release shipped it a second time in its notes, the Software Update
  window and the GitHub release, as 0.169.0 did with 0.167.0's mode-light entry. The census's
  `changelog-repeat` guard now fails each `[Unreleased]` entry whose whole text (its `- ` line
  and every indented line after it) matches an entry of a released section, or an earlier
  `[Unreleased]` one, naming the copy's `CHANGELOG.md` line and the section that already has it
  and saying to delete the copy from `[Unreleased]`. A follow-up that opens with the same line
  and says more passes, and so do repeats among released sections.

## [0.171.0] - 2026-11-07

### Added

- **`aterm harness accounts stats` shows the limit resets left.** A new `resets` row, and the
  `resets` object in `--json`, show the limit resets aterm last saw the account had, their
  kind where Claude Code named one, the time Claude Code said to use them by, and when and on
  which machine they were seen: `resets 1 weekly left · use by Thu Nov 12 16:40 (in 28d) · as
  of 3d (limit-reset, here)`. Only aterm's own limit reset (`[harness] limit_reset`, off by
  default) records the figure, from a reset confirmation or a used-reset line it read whole; a
  reset you take yourself records none. With none recorded the row says why: `no offer read
  yet`, or that the limit reset is off, and `--json` says `no-grant-read` or `limit-reset-off`
  with every value null, never 0. From its use-by time on it reads `passed` (`state: void`).
  The next date a reset is available is not read, so `next_available_at` is null. The
  weekly-limit notice (`Weekly Claude limit nearly used`) now names, in its detail, the resets
  that give the week back (weekly, full or Fable) each listed account was last seen to have,
  with the day they were seen (`Limit resets left: cedar 1 weekly (seen Oct 12, use by Nov
  12)`). The notice is otherwise unchanged and is never raised anew for it: a change in the
  counts alone updates it in place, at most once every ten minutes.

### Fixed

- **The standing go-ahead stops after three tries, and never hides a NEEDS YOU of yours, when
  the agent's turn is taller than the screen.** Where the agent parked in an earlier message of
  a long turn, above what the screen showed, the harness typed the go-ahead at every turn end
  without counting it, so its limit of three never ran out and the need never came back up for
  you. And where that earlier message made one of the last message's `NEEDS YOU:` lines yours
  (`I can't push to main without your GitHub token.` above a line asking to push), the go-ahead
  hid that line from the menu bar and the window border as if it had answered it, and it stayed
  hidden after the agent's next reply.
  Each go-ahead now counts, and it hides only the lines it answers, the same ones whether it is
  typed at once, by the Enter of a line it left unsent, or in place of a move (to another
  account, back to the model, onto another sign-in) that waits for a quiet moment; a move made
  in its place puts them back.

## [0.170.0] - 2026-11-07

### Added

- **`aterm harness accounts stats` shows the Fable and Sonnet weeks Claude Code last said.**
  When a session's screen shows Claude Code's own warning that the Fable week is filling
  (`You've used 85% of your Fable limit · resets …`) or its Fable or Sonnet wall
  (`You've hit your Fable limit · resets …`), the stats keep that figure and its reset with
  the source `warning` or `wall`, and `--json` shows it in that week's window. A wall that
  names no reset reads `100%, no reset given`, with `resets_at` null and the new `void_at`
  saying when the figure stops counting: at the reset an earlier reading of that week named,
  and never later than a week after the wall. A newer reading of the same week replaces it,
  and a limit reset used on the week clears it. These figures are for reading only: the
  harness decides nothing from them, and recording one alone starts no accounts check.

### Changed

- **Each account's usage readings are kept as a history, not only the last week.** The
  readings file the accounts outlook reads for each account (`stats/u-<label>@<machine>.jsonl`
  in the harness state folder) used to be cut back to its newest eight days. It now keeps every
  reading for 7 days, the last reading of each hour and a summary of each ended five-hour
  window for 90 days, and a summary of each ended local day and weekly window for 400 days
  (a window's peak, when it ended, how many readings it had and whether it reached its limit),
  with a row each time another login signed in to that Claude Code home. Each file stays under
  2 MiB, the harness compacts it once a day, and a file with nothing in it from the last 400
  days is removed. The outlook, its card and the week chart read the same week as before. The
  history is a record only: the harness decides nothing from it.

### Fixed

- **`aterm db alab import` settles a moved machine name in one run, and `aterm db alab merge`
  folds the two rows of a Mac the roster calls by another name.** A name a table or the roster
  moves from one machine row to another now moves in one plan, written so that a run cut short
  leaves no moved name on two rows (two rows trading names aside, which the next run finishes),
  and a name a source states beside a host or node the same run writes on its row stays there. A
  replica's machines a Mac has not joined count as covered also where another source of the same
  import wrote them first, and turn `active` once the Mac publishes its principal; `adopt`, which
  finds rows by name, no longer turns one `active` before then. A phone label an earlier import
  made up, for a number a phones or emails sheet or a replica's emails table gave with no label,
  gives way to the one a replica's phones table states, under `--fill-only` too. The replica is
  imported again before it can be deleted, since this changes what `covered` means. `aterm db
  alab merge` now also folds a Mac's own row, bound to its node under the label it registered
  with, and the row an import gave the roster's name for it before it joined, which share no
  name; it sets a row an older import called `active` and no Mac has joined back to `planned`, so
  its Mac takes that row on first registration instead of making a new one under another label,
  and moves a preference a Mac wrote on a row since merged; a merged row a Mac's facts name holds
  every preference whose `merged_into` passes it until that Mac's facts show it rebound along the
  merge.

- **A credential request the vault's admin Mac never answers reaches you.** Once a Mac posts its
  credential requests to the lab, a missing mailbox password or GitHub token it would have asked
  you for before waited there, "open", for the vault admin's aterm to decide it, which an admin
  Mac that stays off, or runs a release with no custodian pass, never does, so nothing said it
  was missing. When 96 hours pass (the lab's 72 to answer, and a day for the admin's aterm to
  reply) with no answer and no Mac offering it, a mailbox password or GitHub token that this Mac
  can show no other Mac holds now goes to you with the same `NEEDS YOU` line as before. Any other
  request says the admin's aterm wrote nothing on it in 96 hours, names the `aterm secrets set`
  step on the admin Mac, and files one note for later: set each of them there. Running that step
  ends the request once this Mac syncs, whatever the admin Mac runs.

- **A credential you are asked for after 72 hours names the Macs that never answered.** When the
  lab's 72 hours to answer a request ran out before every Mac had looked, the `NEEDS YOU` still
  said the credential "is on no Mac the lab can reach", so you could mint a new deployer key
  while a Mac that was off held a good one. It now names the Macs that did not answer and says a
  copy one of them holds is the file to set, before you make a new one; once each of them has
  answered without one, it says so. A Mac whose aterm recovered its lab writer counts as one
  Mac, so a request it makes never names itself. If one of them comes back and offers it, the ask
  names that Mac's copy, which the vault admin's aterm takes over the LAN, and `aterm secrets need
  ls --all` shows the offer.

- **A Claude Code reply drawn under a status line reads busy in the tab's state.** Under a
  status line (aterm's usage tap is one) Claude Code's footer has no `esc to interrupt` and,
  on 2.1.311, its spinner row goes once the reply's first line is drawn, so `aterm ctl
  status`'s `agent=`, `await agent`, `survey`, the menu bar and the tab's dot read a reply still
  being drawn as idle. They now read the program's own window title beside the screen: `◐`/`◑`
  over a reply the screen shows no sign of says `busy`, and the word turns idle when the turn
  ends, a quarter second after the title rests unless the turn's closing timing line is
  already drawn. A shell running under that reply no longer reads as a turn resting beside
  its background work. A finished turn, a box, a limit, an interrupted turn and a turn that
  rests beside work it handed off read as before, and so does a tab whose Claude Code shows
  no status in its title. Muse Code's spinner title holds its idle composer busy the same way.

- **`aterm ctl rewind check` no longer fails a faithful replay of a tab whose program changed its
  reported state.** Codex and Grok Build tell aterm whether they are working, waiting on you or
  done (OSC 7501). Once such a report had changed, for example from working to waiting on a
  permission box, `rewind check` and `rewind check export` answered
  `verdict=fail:WitnessMatches` at the next screen they compared, although the replay drew the
  same screen: the comparison included where each engine had numbered the report, and a replay
  numbers it afresh. It now compares the report itself, and answers `verdict=pass`.

## [0.169.0] - 2026-11-07

### Removed

- **The `desktop_alerts` setting is gone.** aterm posts no desktop notification of its own, so
  the key decided nothing you saw. A `desktop_alerts` line already in your `aterm.toml` loads,
  whatever its value, and every other setting loads as it would without it. A value other than
  `true` or `false`, such as `desktop_alerts = "on"`, used to stop the file loading: the
  window's settings outside `[harness]`, `[ai]` and `[amacs]` started at their defaults, under a
  `Couldn't load your settings` band. It no longer does, so the rest of your settings now take
  effect. The line stays in the file: Reset All leaves it. aterm's message log, not a banner,
  says `desktop_alerts does nothing: Desktop alerts was removed; safe to delete`;
  `aterm --window --validate-config` passes with that one warning, `aterm ctl settings set` and
  `unset` answer with the same sentence, and Settings ▸ Modified lists it as Desktop alerts
  (removed), No effect. A program's own notifications are unchanged: `allow_notifications`
  still decides them.

### Fixed

- **The mode light and the top-effort key no longer press into a Claude Code reply drawn under
  a status line.** In a Claude Code session with a status line (aterm's usage tap or your own),
  Claude Code shows no busy sign while it draws a reply: the footer drops `esc to interrupt`,
  and the spinner goes once the reply's first line is on screen. A click on the mode light could
  press Shift+Tab into that reply, and the top-effort key could type its `/` there. Both now
  read Claude Code's window title with the screen: while its `◐`/`◑` says the turn runs, the
  mode light holds its next press, and the top-effort key types nothing more and says Claude is
  working, even beside a background shell's pill. The turn's closing timing line still ends the
  turn, and a tab whose Claude Code shows no status in its title reads as before.

- **A NEEDS YOU line the standing go-ahead answers stays off the menu bar when Claude Code
  wrapped it.** Where a long `NEEDS YOU:` line wrapped onto a row that opens with a capital
  (`… with the small fix` above `Claude Code needs.`), the harness read the whole line as the
  need but answered only its first row, so the line Land's instruction or the go-ahead had
  answered still went up on the menu bar and the window border, the answer said `Needs on
  screen`, and it stayed up until a reply said `NEEDS YOU: nothing`. A need whose first row asks
  for a go-ahead but whose whole line does not got the go-ahead anyway. Both now read the same
  words, at a turn's end and at a break of the agent's background work, in its last message and
  in an earlier one read from the history above the screen.

- **The harness reads a Claude Code reply drawn under a status line as a live turn.** Under a
  status line (aterm's usage tap is one) Claude Code draws no `esc to interrupt` and drops its
  spinner once a reply's first line is up, so only its window title's `◐`/`◑` says the turn
  runs. The harness held such a reply only where it read the turn's end; everywhere else it read
  the reply as idle, so an act it had typed went untaken beside a background shell's pill, and
  `aterm drive phase` said `idle` mid-reply. It now reads the title sent with each screen beside
  the rows: the act is taken, the wait for the turn's end is on the session log where the tab
  keeps one (else the next read once the screen settles), and `aterm drive phase` says `busy`
  with `reason title: running`. A reply that stands unchanged a minute under a running title is
  read as it shows, with a note, even while its status line keeps refreshing, so a title stuck
  running never holds the harness. Claude Code's critical-memory banner beside such a reply is
  no end of it either: the memory restart waits for the reply's last line instead of cutting it
  short. A turn stopped with Esc is judged on its interrupt, never on the frame drawn after it.

- **A fleet_db replica edited after its import reports what it no longer says, and a word the
  registry cannot hold keeps the replica uncovered.** A link, mailbox, phone, note, service,
  preference or machine fact that this replica's own import wrote, and the edit removed, is now listed
  by column and left in the registry, in either mode. The replica stays uncovered until the owner
  settles each cell with `aterm db emails set` (and `computers`, `phones`, `ai-accounts`). Before,
  the old values stayed and the replica read as covered. A status or provider word no registry cell
  has, a cell a guard refuses, a phone cell holding more than one number, a tier the registry has no
  column for, an `active` beside a held `banned`, a `suspended` that only restates a note disabling
  another vendor, and a machine row no source lists now are reported instead of being dropped
  silently. A note on a row that holds no account goes on its address. A protected address is no
  mailbox's login, whether an alias's root, a receiving mailbox, a correction or `--mailbox-toml`
  names it. A replica row finds its Mac by its mesh id, and a rekey keeps the import's record.

## [0.168.0] - 2026-11-07

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.167.0: `alab claude harness 0.22`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

### Added

- **`aterm ctl @self status` names the `syspolicyd` it read and how long it has run.** When
  macOS's program check (`syspolicyd`) crashes, launchd starts another, and `status` read
  `syspolicyd=ok` with nothing to show that the daemon had changed. Now `status` (and
  `aterm ctl program-check`) carries `syspolicyd_pid=` and `syspolicyd_up_ms=` after
  `syspolicyd_full_ms=`: the `syspolicyd` the stuck check's last look read, sampled once a
  minute on macOS, and how long it has run. Both read `-` before a look reads one and once
  none runs; a look that reads nothing keeps the pid with no age, since no look says that
  `syspolicyd` still runs.

### Fixed

- **A live upgrade no longer restarts Claude Code in the middle of a reply drawn under a status
  line.** Under a status line (aterm's usage tap is one) Claude Code drops `esc to interrupt`
  from its footer and, once a reply's first line is drawn, its spinner row too, so the upgrade
  read that reply as a finished turn and could restart the tab, or let the ⬆️ press restart it,
  before the reply ended. The upgrade now reads the tab's window title beside its screen: while
  the title's `◐`/`◑` says a turn runs that the screen does not show, the restart, the ⬆️ press
  and the upgrade's notice wait for the turn to end, and the ⬆️'s label says `at turn end` where
  it said `now`. The turn's closing timing line ends it whatever the title says, and a tab whose
  Claude Code shows no status in its title reads as before.

- (developer tool) **`lab halfdraw scan` and `lab idle-points` read a Claude Code reply under a
  status line as the turn it is.** Under a status line Claude Code draws its reply with no busy
  row, so `halfdraw scan` saw no busy state in such a cast and reported `busy gaps: 0` as if it
  had looked, and `idle-points` opened a turn's end at its first mid-reply frame. Both now read
  the window title the cast set beside the rows, as the harness does: a read is busy by its busy
  row or where it reads busy under a running title, and the scan reports `busy states: N`, with
  `(blind: …)` when it is 0. A gap is still the busy row gone mid-turn, which `await gone` answers
  on whatever the title says, or, where no busy row is drawn, the titled busy read gone; a cast no
  title runs over is counted by its busy row alone, as before. A turn's end opens at its done
  frame (Muse Code's where its title rests), and the title's rest is still timed from the frame
  that drew the end.

- **A bash rc's `DEBUG` trap now runs only for your own commands, as in bash alone.** Under `set -T` or
  `extdebug` it still ran for the commands of aterm's prompt hooks, about 78 times a line on bash 5.3 and
  48 on macOS's bash, so with a trap that starts a program Enter took about 245 ms and 114 ms on a busy
  Mac; it now runs once a line and Enter takes about 11 ms and 7 ms, where bash alone takes 2. With no
  flag it also ran for aterm's own prompt and `PS0` entries, two or three times a line, and now runs
  once. With bash-preexec's current master on bash 5.3, bash-preexec itself still runs your trap for
  aterm's hooks, as before.

- **A bash in posix mode (`set -o posix`) no longer prints `-: command not found` after every command.**
  Bash 5 reports an unset `DEBUG` trap as `-` there, and aterm ran that as your trap.

- **A bash rc's `DEBUG` trap that prints, such as one that sets the window title, is no longer lost.**
  aterm read your trap's text while the trap itself ran, so what the trap printed became part of that
  text, and aterm dropped the trap.

- **An rc that leaves `set -a` on no longer exports aterm's own state to every program.** About 440 of
  aterm's variables and functions, 28 KB, went into each program's environment, among them the line you
  typed and the key that tells aterm's own marks from a program's.

- **Under `set -T`, a bash prompt that runs a command in `$(…)` no longer leaves a phantom command
  after every line.** aterm's own trap reached the prompt's `$(…)` and recorded another command there,
  your last line again or the prompt's own, which never finished.

## [0.167.0] - 2026-11-07

### Removed

- (developer tool) **`targo --unverified lab told-once` is gone.** It raised a NEEDS YOU set in a
  private window and counted the aterm.log line for each decision aterm made about telling you
  of it on the desktop, which aterm no longer makes, so every step of a run would now fail. The
  dev seam it set went with it: a `meta set harness_needs` that no self-claim admits answers
  `ERR denied` in every build.

### Fixed

- **The mode light and the top-effort key no longer press into a Claude Code reply drawn under
  a status line.** In a Claude Code session with a status line (aterm's usage tap or your own),
  Claude Code shows no busy sign while it draws a reply: the footer drops `esc to interrupt`,
  and the spinner goes once the reply's first line is on screen. A click on the mode light could
  press Shift+Tab into that reply, and the top-effort key could type its `/` there. Both now
  read Claude Code's window title with the screen: while its `◐`/`◑` says the turn runs, the
  mode light holds its next press, and the top-effort key types nothing more and says Claude is
  working, even beside a background shell's pill. The turn's closing timing line still ends the
  turn, and a tab whose Claude Code shows no status in its title reads as before.

## [0.166.0] - 2026-11-07

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.165.0: `alab claude harness 0.21`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

### Fixed

- **A model fallback no longer outlives the program it was made for.** After the harness moved a
  session onto its fallback model at a usage limit, a program you started yourself in the same
  tab was still held to that switch: when the limit reset, the harness ended your program and
  restarted it on the model the switch had left, and your program's own limit waited out the
  week instead of falling back. The switch now stays with the agent process its relaunch
  started and with every process the harness starts from it (a crash, stall or upgrade
  relaunch, a memory or lost-input restart, a relaunch whose continuation it owes). Another
  program on another conversation ends the switch, and a later loop reads that end from the
  approval ledger. While the tab's new process has not named its conversation, the return
  waits.

- **With `desktop_alerts = true`, codex's own notifications for its approval box are no longer
  dropped.** aterm posts no desktop notification of its own, but where it decided to tell you of
  a codex approval box it counted the box as told, and each notification codex then wrote for it
  with OSC 9, OSC 99 or OSC 777 while the box stood was dropped before it reached aterm's
  notifier. Each now reaches the notifier with its words.

- **A Commons founding that cannot go on until you change something now says so, and what to
  run.** On an open vault's only admin Mac, the pass that founds the vault's Commons failed its
  `sync.shared-data` row with "the next pass tries again" whatever stopped it, so a vault server
  that refused the publication (403 or 507) failed every pass with that promise. A refusal like
  that, and a condition the founding finds unmet as it runs, now waits for you instead of
  failing, and the row names `aterm secrets commons init`, which runs the founding by hand and
  shows the refusal whole. Only a founding that may pass by itself (another publish landed
  first, the vault did not answer, a lock was held) still fails with "the next pass tries
  again". Each reason the pass leaves a founding alone now says what changes it: `aterm secrets
  commons init` run on the vault's admin, `aterm secrets edit` to remove an opaque Commons
  control entry, or which file to move out of the way. A founding read back while this Mac's
  vault sync still holds the vault's state no longer fails: the row waits up to 5 seconds for
  it, and if the state is still busy it keeps what the founding said, marked unconfirmed.

## [0.165.0] - 2026-11-07

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.164.0: `alab claude harness 0.20`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

### Fixed

- (developer tool) **`verify` ends a program macOS's program check stranded COULD NOT RUN,
  instead of failing your tree three hours later.** When macOS's program check
  (`syspolicyd`) crashes, launchd starts another, and a program the old one was checking can
  stay held before its first instruction while `aterm ctl @self status` reads
  `syspolicyd=ok`. `targo --unverified verify` counted that wait as work: it printed nothing
  until the stage's 3-hour ceiling, then reported a FAIL against the tree. Now verify watches
  the programs its own stage started that have not run. One it saw held since before the
  `syspolicyd` running now started ends COULD NOT RUN, named on stderr with both pids, once
  that `syspolicyd` has run 10 minutes (the bound on a first exec) with a free thread pool and
  no program held since it started. Verify ends only its own stage child: it sends the group
  it holds SIGKILL (a started parent above the held program gets SIGTERM and its grace first),
  leaves the program's file in place and does not retry. A program held past 10 minutes under
  the running `syspolicyd` is said once on stderr and waited for, since its check is work in
  line. At the ceiling, a stage whose program never started, or one of whose programs (not
  one a test binary started) has been held past 10 minutes, now ends COULD NOT RUN instead of
  FAIL. Run the check again on the same tree; no restart of the Mac is needed. `aterm help
  permissions` (SLOW FIRST RUNS) explains it.

- **A tab no longer stays marked for a macOS permission dialog after `[privacy] observer = true`'s
  log stream ends by itself.** The mark came off when macOS answered the dialog or when the stream
  was stopped, but a stream that ended on its own (its `log stream` process exited, or its worker
  went) left it on until a later stop or the tab closed, though nothing could answer it any more.
  Every way a stream ends now takes its marks down.

- **A program worker's tab is named by its program, not by the line that started it.** A `spawn
  program=` worker has no agent to name it, so while its shell titled its tab by the line it typed
  (`'/opt/lab/bench' '--quick' < "$ATERM_TASK_FILE"`, a store binary's opening with its shim's
  environment words) or by its folder at a prompt, every message that placed it ("Autopilot set to
  land" among them), the Workers chip, the Overview and Next That Needs You named it `Workers ▸
  '/opt/lab/bench' '--quick' < "$ATERM_TAS`, and its Workers row read `the program` once it had
  stalled before its line ran. Each names it by its program's file name now (`bench`), never by its
  arguments, its environment words or its folder, also while its program has emptied the tab's
  title; a title its program gives the tab names it while that title stands, and the name crosses
  an update or a restart with its task. A program worker an older aterm carried across, whose
  record names no program, is `the program` everywhere, as its Workers row was.

- **Cruise's background wait no longer jumps ahead after its harness loop restarts.** A turn of
  real work starts Cruise's wait for an agent's background work over, but the harness's ledger
  did not say so, and a restarted loop read the gaps between its prompts as one wait growing:
  after a few prompts that each followed real work, the next quick answer waited up to an hour
  for its prompt instead of two minutes. Each prompt's ledger row, and the row of a go-ahead or
  a continuation Cruise types in a prompt's place, now says how far the wait had grown when it
