  went, and a restarted loop takes the wait up from the newest; rows an older build wrote are
  still read by their gaps.

- **Cruise's background wait starts over after a restart when it had started over before.** When
  a turn of real work, a message from someone else or a turn the harness could not see started
  the wait over, and the loop restarted before the next prompt went (a line of aterm's own went
  in the prompt's place, or a guard held it), the restarted loop took up the old wait, so the
  agent's next quick answer waited up to an hour for its prompt. The ledger now records each
  time the wait starts over, and a restarted loop starts it over from there too.

- **Cruise's background wait starts over after a restart in the middle of a turn.** A loop that
  restarted while the agent was working timed that turn from its own first look, so the last
  seconds of a long turn of real work counted as a quick answer, and a message another session
  sent the agent before the restart went unseen on Muse Code and agy: the wait kept growing,
  and the prompt at the turn's end waited up to an hour. A turn still running at the restarted
  loop's first look, or resuming from a pause before that loop has seen one settle, now starts
  the wait over, as a turn the harness could not see does. A turn that begins after a pause the
  loop saw settle, or that a background task's wake Claude Code shows opened after the loop's
  first look, is still judged by its own work. A turn that ends while no loop is watching still
  goes uncounted.

## [0.164.0] - 2026-11-07

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.163.0: `alab claude harness 0.19`, `alab agy harness 0.15`, `alab grok harness 0.18`, `alab kimi harness 0.16`, `alab muse harness 0.18`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

### Removed

- **`aterm ctl survey` content rows no longer print `need_ids=`.** The field named each need of an
  ask so another Mac could post one notice per need, and aterm posts no notices of its own any more.
  A content row is one field shorter, so a script that reads `need_ids=` needs changing. An ask still
  shows as `needs=ask` with its words in `attention=`.

### Fixed

- **A worker's first Autopilot message names its tab by its agent, not by the line that started
  it.** A shell titles its tab by its folder at a prompt and by each line it runs, and a worker's
  line opens with environment words, so "Autopilot set to land" named a just-spawned worker
  `Workers ▸ CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY=1 'c` while its landing, once Claude Code had
  titled the tab, named it `Workers ▸ Claude Code`. While its shell titles a worker's tab, every
  message, the Workers list and the Workers chip now name it by its agent (the one in front, else
  the one its task started), a busy terminal's too; a title the agent gives the tab names it from
  then on, Claude Code's own name and then its topic. A tab on the strip is still named as its
  chip reads it.

- **A worker sent with `aterm ctl --sock` to another aterm is booked where it runs.** A spawn
  from a tab into an aterm of another environment (a `lab instance`) named the tab's
  session as the worker's manager, a session that aterm does not hold, so each conclusion was
  recorded as "Worker mail not delivered", and wrote the worker's row on this Mac's board, whose
  keeper found no such session and closed the row as failed while the worker went on and landed.
  The client now names this shell's session (`from=`) only to an aterm that holds it: one a spawn
  addressed to that session reaches (an aterm refuses one for a session it does not host), or the
  one this Mac's socket folder records as its host, known by any path to its socket (a symlink, a
  hard link, another spelling of its folder); an explicit `from=` still goes. It judges from those
  files alone, probing no socket, and a spawn judged by its socket reaches that aterm on every
  connection, even if the `latest` alias moves between them. It writes a board row only for a
  worker its keeper reaches: in an aterm whose sessions this Mac's socket folder records (its own,
  or one bound elsewhere that mirrors them there), or on another Mac with `--host`.

- **A NEEDS YOU line written just before a usage limit or an API error now goes up.** The harness
  read no NEEDS YOU from a turn that ended on a limit or an error, and the turn its resume opens
  reads only its own words, so the need was never posted. A cut turn's NEEDS YOU lines now join
  the needs already standing; its words never take a standing need down, and a line the
  standing go-ahead answered stays off the menu bar unless the cut turn names it again.

## [0.163.0] - 2026-11-07

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.162.0: `alab claude harness 0.18`, `alab agy harness 0.14`, `alab muse harness 0.17`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- **Claude Code's vault token route is on in every build.** Minting, serving and the offer of an
  account's vault token now run wherever their gates hold (standing, identity, the claims ring, the
  usage tap's gate), with no compiled switch and no `off` fallback. Every launch path types aterm's
  token wrapper for a token decision, and a running Claude Code session moves between its stored
  login and its account's vault token at a turn end. `aterm doctor`'s accounts row counts token
  rows, `aterm help token` explains the route, and the session card, the Lab page, the state line
  and `aterm ctl status` show a session's token facts.

- **A fleet Mac starts its handshakes at once.** The automatic wait of up to two minutes before a
  member's first handshake, and its presence-only key probe, are gone; admission and the bounded,
  jittered retries at capacity are unchanged.

- **Full-screen programs redraw for less.** The alternate screen's archive serves a row nobody
  wrote since its last read without comparing it, finds each row with one lookup, and keeps its
  text end to end in chunks.

### Fixed

- **A Mac Setup failure no longer always says to run `aterm init`.** The remedy now follows the
  failure.

- **A setup run that has exited no longer holds the installer's custody**, so the next install or
  update does not wait on it. The install's quiet clock restarts after a harness wait, and a
  withheld claim no longer counts toward it.

- **`agh` screens a repository's private and effective git configuration before it runs git
  there**, and binds a replayed configuration to its access policy.

## [0.162.0] - 2026-11-07

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.161.0: `alab claude harness 0.17`, `alab agy harness 0.13`, `alab grok harness 0.17`, `alab kimi harness 0.15`, `alab muse harness 0.16`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- **A build that needs more disk than its volume can give stops instead of waiting for ever.**
  A build's disk claim (`targo --unverified verify`, `ship trust run`, `ship release`, the lab's
  VM lanes) that needs more than its volume has free above the floor, once the build cache's pass
  and the window's disk watch have freed what they could, with no held scratch claim able to
  return enough room on that volume, now ends at once: COULD NOT RUN (NOT RUN in the lab). It
  names how much to free on which volume and what holds the most there, and, where the command
  has one, the way to start it anyway (`--admit now`). Before, it waited, a line a minute, for
  space that nothing it waited for would free, until it was killed. While another build marks
  its writes as scratch on that volume, it waits where those writes could give back enough room
  by the claim's end, then rechecks and is
  relieved again once it has ended. If the scratch remained, that second look refuses the build
  instead of waiting again. A claim the relief brings within the room still waits for the builds
  ahead of it and starts once they leave it room; `aterm pkg capacity` still marks a claim beyond
  the room `unservable`.

- **Turning on Allow programs to show desktop notifications in Settings is what asks macOS.** On a
  bundled aterm macOS's question came only from a program's first notification, and only with the old
  `desktop_alerts` key set; otherwise nothing asked, and a program's notifications were held for good.
  Your own click or key on the Settings ▸ Security row now asks, once. A program can no longer raise
  that dialog, and neither can a line in `aterm.toml`, `aterm ctl settings set`, `aterm ctl act` or a
  screen reader's press: with the setting on and macOS never asked, a program's notification is held,
  `aterm.log` says so, and turning the row off and on yourself asks.

### Fixed

- **`aterm db alab import` no longer makes a second row for a Mac it already knows, and a repeat
  of the same import plans nothing.** A machine in a replica, a sheet or the roster now matches a
  row by its fleet node, then a host, then its label or an alias, and a name two rows answer is
  reported rather than given a third row. `aterm db alab merge` folds duplicates an earlier import
  made into the row their Mac is bound to: the Mac's current name stays its label and the old one
  an alias, its preferences move with it, and `--dry-run` shows keys, labels and columns, never a
  value; it reads the roster for that name and refuses on a Mac with no copy of it. A replica's
  machines a Mac has not joined now stay `planned` and count as covered.

- **A bash rc's `DEBUG` trap under `set -T` or `extdebug` no longer runs for every command of aterm's
  helpers.** Under those flags bash hands the trap to each function, so one line ran it about 310 times on
  bash 5.3 and 160 on macOS's bash, and a trap that starts a program made Enter take about 860 ms and
  440 ms to give the prompt back, where bash alone takes 3 ms. Most of those helpers now run with the flag
  off: about 80 and 50 runs, 260 ms and 120 ms. The trap still runs for the commands of the prompt hooks
  themselves, and in your own `PROMPT_COMMAND` as it did.

- **`aterm ctl await task` wakes on every new ask, not only the first.** While one ask stood
  on a worker, a second one (a permission box beside a standing NEEDS YOU, codex-alab's own ask
  over a worker stalled at startup, or a new need joining the worker's set, even one hidden
  behind the same `(+1 more)` text) left its task record unmoved, so a lead's background wait
  slept on until it timed out. Each new ask now wakes it once, and so does one taken down and
  raised again; a need taken down, the same needs written again (after a seamless update too)
  and a usage-limit wait do not.

- **A lead hears when the harness has tried all it can at a worker it started.** When Autopilot
  stopped at a point only a person can answer in a worker a lead had spawned (a request refused
  after repeated tries, a context wall compaction cannot shrink, a model with no reset, a limit
  that answers each try the same, or the same reply held), the worker's task record stayed
  `working` and `aterm ctl await task` slept until it timed out. After two minutes with nothing
  moving the worker is now `stalled why=held`, its attention quotes the point (`it needs a
  person: …`), and the stall ends when its screen, input or transcript moves, not when the point
  is merely lifted. A point Autopilot recovers from by itself, such as a refused go-ahead it
  answers with a change of approach, wakes no lead.

- **One credential the vault admin's Mac cannot publish no longer holds up the rest.** When the
  vault admin's aterm could not publish a copy of a credential (another publish held the vault,
  or its server was out of reach), it dropped every other decision it had made in that pass, so
  requests that needed a person were never handed to one and old requests never lapsed, for as
  long as the publish kept failing. Those decisions now go through, and only the request the
  publish carried waits for the next pass, which `aterm secrets need pass` names with its error.
  A need ledger the admin's Mac cannot read no longer stops it deciding for the other Macs
  either.

- (developer tool) **A check waiting behind a hung lab run is ended after 15 minutes.** A
  `verify` check waiting for the Linux lane behind a `lab linux exec` whose guest had hung, or
  waiting for disk or memory behind a lab boot, a verify run or a `ship trust run` that had
  stopped working, waited for ever: the holder's own once-a-minute measure of its disk, and on
  the Linux lane lima's own idle program, made it look busy. Now a holder works only while what
  it runs, its VM included, keeps a quarter of a core busy or writes a MiB a minute, so after
  15 minutes without progress the waiting check reads NOT RUN, naming the holder, which nothing
  signals. A guest command that only waits for 15 minutes (a `sleep`, a stalled download) reads
  as stuck too. A holder that is itself waiting its turn for a lock or for room counts as stuck
  only once what it waits behind does.

## [0.161.0] - 2026-11-06

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.160.0: `alab grok harness 0.16`, `alab kimi harness 0.14`, `alab muse harness 0.15`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

### Fixed

- **A session on an AI account another Mac holds also pauses while a limit reset on that
  account is being taken.** With `[harness] limit_reset` on, no session moves off an account for
  up to ten minutes after one of its sessions took the reset Claude Code offers at its usage
  limit. A session on that account whose own account another Mac's claim held had Cruise's or
  Land's next prompt typed in at its turn ends all that time, whether or not it had a free
  account to move to, so both Macs used the account. It now pauses at its turn end, and is asked
  again within about a minute, until the move can be made. The pause now says that the session
  cannot move off the account yet, where it said that no other account could take the session,
  which was not true while one could (`F19`).

- **A session waiting at a usage limit whose limit record is not written yet, or whose
  account's limit reset is in flight, no longer records that wait as "another account can be
  used then".** Its journal now names the real reason, and that it is asked again shortly.

- **Muse Code's refused API requests are no longer retried as an outage.** A Muse Code
  `◆ model failed: API error` whose status refuses the request (400, 403, 404, 422, and every
  other 4xx except 401, 408, 409, 429 and 451) was read as a server error, so the harness sent
  the same request again on doubling waits, with no end, though each try met the same refusal.
  It now takes the ladder Claude Code's refusals take: tries after 1, 30 and 120 minutes, then
  the harness stops and records a refused-request exception for you. That exception's reason,
  the action it asks of you and its title in the exceptions digest named Claude for every
  program; they now name the program whose API refused the request. Server errors, rate limits
  and connection failures wait as before.

- **A build ending as another reads the capacity ledger no longer fails the read.** `aterm pkg
  capacity`, or a build deciding whether it may start, could stop with "No such file or
  directory" or "checkpoint anchor was copied or replaced" when another build's claim was
  retired while it read the ledger. A claim retired during the read is now skipped, since it no
  longer reserves anything.

- **A credential request the lab let lapse is asked for again.** When a Mac's aterm stayed shut
  for 30 days, the lab retired its open credential requests as lapsed, and `aterm secrets need
  ls` said the next pass would ask again. Nothing did for a request made with `aterm secrets
  need <want>`, so it ended quietly while the credential was still missing. The Mac now posts it
  again as soon as it reads the lapse, under a new request every Mac reads at once; one that was
  waiting for you comes back to you with the lab's next answer.

- **A typed `turn`'s rest is now its keys' own bytes, never a paste.** A `turn typed=1` that
  stopped pressing keys one at a time (past `cap=`, or once its time ran short) still pasted the
  text between the Tabs and line breaks of its rest, and a program may take a paste otherwise
  than typing: fish escaped the quotes of a paste inside a quoted word, so `'fix it'` was left as
  an open quote and the Enter never ran the command. Each run of the rest now goes in one write
  as the bytes its keys send, so the program sees what typing every key would have sent, in any
  keyboard mode. The verdict's `pasted=` still counts that part.

- **`lease release force` now stops the turn it preempts.** A turn whose lease was force-released
  kept typing its text and pressing its Enter behind the turn that took its place, mixing the two
  texts. It now writes nothing more, even while its guarded Enter waits to be sent; one stopped
  before its Enter answers `OK 0 turn skipped reason=preempted`, with `typed=` and `pasted=`
  saying what of its text stands, and one stopped after an Enter went only presses it no more. A
  plain turn halted by a `hold` after its paste now says its text stands too (`typed=0
  pasted=<n>`).

- **A turn's guarded Enter no longer overtakes the text it follows.** A `turn submit=guarded:…`
  could press its Enter while the program was still being sent the turn's paste, ahead of the
  end of the text, and judged its guard before that text had been written. The Enter now waits
  until the text has been written and judges its guard then. A program still drawing a long text
  at that moment can make a guard on the text itself miss, which presses nothing and leaves the
  text typed (`reason=guard`). Every write with a fence waits too: `key if=…` and `send
  if=…` answer `ERR busy sink` meanwhile, a footer slash press does not begin behind it and types the rest of
  its command and its Enter once it has gone (or stops at its deadline, saying what it left
  typed), and a worker's first line waits for it.

- **A typed turn whose first `cap=` characters are all control characters keeps to its
  `timeout=`.** Such a turn types no key before its rest, and it sent the rest of its text even
  when no time was left for it to be submitted; it now writes nothing then, as any turn whose
  first key does not fit. One whose only write was its Enter is also no longer stopped part-way
  by its caller going, and one whose guarded Enter wrote nothing gives its `id=` back, so a retry
  is judged again rather than answered `dup=1`.

- **aterm's setup runs a new clone's git hook installer only from that clone.** A link put in
  place of the new clone while its dependencies were fetched made the setup run the installer of
  the folder it pointed to, and a required dependency checked out at `scripts` made it run that
  dependency's installer. Neither runs now, and the setup's row says why. What an installer printed
  is quoted on the row, with control and right-to-left characters escaped and the escaped line cut
  short, so it cannot reorder the row, flood it or pose as another clone's outcome.

## [0.160.0] - 2026-11-06

### Fixed

- **Founding a vault's Commons no longer fails on its own publication.** The founding's publish
  wakes this Mac's vault subscriber, which holds the vault's state for a moment while it applies
  the new version. The founding read its root back at once, met that hold, and failed with
  "published Commons control is not visible after sync" although the root was published. It now
  waits up to 5 seconds for the subscriber. A window's founding and a person's `aterm secrets
  commons init` on the same Mac could also run at once and publish over each other. Each now
  holds `commons-foundation.lock` from its read of the vault through its publication: the
  window's pass founds nothing while the command runs, and the command waits for the window's
  founding to end. A founding whose publication loses a race with another publish now reads the vault
  again. If a Commons root landed, it finishes that root. If not, it says another publish landed
  first, and the next try publishes the same kept attempt.

- **Two aterm launches at the same moment no longer cost one its control socket.** A launch
  that checked the socket while another was checking it could read it as in use and run
  without one, so `aterm ctl` could not reach that window.

- **The row naming the agents that did not come back after a restart always appears.** With
  many tabs reporting at once, or many other messages waiting, the newest row, the one that
  names every tab, could be dropped.

- **`install.sh` no longer promises the ALab toolset when `aterm.toml` names a `[packages]
  prefix` aterm ignores.** aterm installs no toolset there, and the plan now says so.

## [0.159.0] - 2026-11-06

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.158.0: `alab claude harness 0.16`, `alab grok harness 0.15`, `alab kimi harness 0.13`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- (developer tool) **`lab told-once` checks told once in a real window.** It opens a private
  window with desktop alerts on, raises one NEEDS YOU set in a background tab, re-orders it,
  re-counts it and adds a need, and reads the herald's own `aterm.log` lines: one decision to
  notify for the set, `not queued: told once` for each repeat and one for the new need; with told
  memory off (a debug-build seam) every step notifies. No banner can reach Notification Center.

### Removed

- **`aterm ctl chrome` no longer prints the `presence rim= pressing= pill=` line.** The window's
  needs border and the tab-strip and titlebar pill it reported had stopped drawing, and their code
  is gone. The chrome reply is one line shorter, so a script that counts its lines or reads that
  line needs changing. What needs you is still in the menu bar, the tab's hover, Overview and
  `aterm ctl @<sid> status`.

### Fixed

- **A typed `turn` now sends the part it pastes as typing it would have.** When a
  `turn typed=1` pastes the rest of its text (past `cap=`, or once its time ran short), a Tab in
  that part was pasted as text, so a shell completed nothing where the typed keys would have, and
  a text ending in a literal `\n` had it turned into a line break: a second Enter where the
  program had no bracketed paste, and lost text where it had. The pasted part now goes exactly as
  written, with each Tab or line break in it pressed as its key between the pastes. A plain
  `turn` no longer turns a trailing `\n` into a line break either; it submits with its own Enter.

- **A new clone's git hook installer can no longer ask for the Command Line Tools.** On a Mac
  without them, the installer aterm's setup runs in a new clone (clean's runs `python3`) could
  bring up Apple's "install the command line developer tools" dialog part-way through the setup,
  which installs the tools only after its clones. There the installer now runs with no developer
  directory to ask for, so such a step fails at once and the setup's row says so.

- **On a busy Mac, an account renewal that aterm stops is no longer recorded as a failed
  renewal.** When aterm ends a sign-in program it runs (because its sign-in service is
  unavailable, or because the work was cancelled), macOS refuses the signal to the program's
  process group for the short time the program takes to end. On a loaded Mac that time was
  0.2 ms at the median and up to 20 ms (`docs/measured/capture-terminal-exit-2026-11-06.md`).
  aterm took a refusal in that time as a program it could not stop, so a renewal waiting on an
  unavailable service was recorded as a failed renewal instead of being put off for a later
  try. aterm now judges the refusal once it has collected the program's exit.

- **A screen reader reads a terminal again.** Since v0.157.0 a terminal window showed a screen
  reader an empty document of no height, in one pane or in a split, on every platform. It now
  holds the text on screen, as it did before. A terminal's document now reads the terminal itself
  rather than the last frame's cells, so it keeps its top rows under a tab strip, a tab that comes
  to the front reads at once, and a window that cannot present still tells a screen reader what
  changes in its terminal. What aterm paints over a terminal is now its own element: a tab's menu is
  a menu a screen reader can press, the session name field holds its focus, a paste question on Linux
  holds the lines it asks about, a close question says what the answer ends, and a hovered link's
  destination and a rewound pane's age are read.

- **On macOS, a file aterm watches stays heard when it or its folder appears as the watch
  starts.** A folder made at that moment could leave the watch listening one folder too high,
  and a file made at that moment could leave it with no listener of its own. Either way aterm
  stopped noticing that file, so an open document kept its old text and the title kept the
  old machine name.

- **Autopilot Land no longer carries a relaunch that had nothing to resume as the session it
  replaced.** When aterm restarted an agent afresh because there was no conversation to resume, a
  message you sent before aterm next read the agent's screen was carried as the old session's
  work. It now opens a fresh exchange of your own.

- **A `turn` whose sender goes still submits its text to a program that is not reading.** When
  a program had stopped reading its input for a while, as a loaded worker can, and the `aterm
  ctl` that sent it a `turn` went away while the turn's paste waited for the program (interrupted,
  or ended by whatever ran it), the turn ended there: the whole text reached the program later,
  with no Enter after it. A turn that has begun writing now finishes whatever its sender does:
  into a session that is not in front, as a worker's is, its paste waits up to 30 seconds for
  that session's input to take it, and its Enter follows; `aterm ctl @<sid> history` records
  whether it was submitted. A paste not all taken in those 30 seconds is still left queued
  without its Enter, and the turn answers `ERR paste delivery failed`. A turn whose sender is
  already gone when it would first write writes nothing.

- **A fenced typed `turn` no longer pastes a digit ahead of what its program has shown.** A
  `turn typed=1` fenced on a composer box (`if-rows=`) types each digit only once the program
  has drawn the keys before it, so a permission box that appears meanwhile cannot take the digit
  as its answer. The part it pastes after the typed keys (past `cap=`, or once the time left ran
  short) skipped that wait; when it holds a digit it now waits too. A program slower than the
  turn has time for stops the turn there, the typed part left standing, as it does before a
  typed digit.

- **A package update whose switch-over fails now says why.** When the last step of an update
  (pointing a program at its new build, laying its commands, or checking that a Trust toolchain
  bundle's libraries resolve) failed, every pass reported only that the switch-over failed and
  was rolled back, so on 2026-11-04 a Trust update retried for more than five hours with nothing
  saying what stopped it. The update notice, `packages.log` and the program's status row now
  name the step that failed and its own error, then the group members that were put back. A
  member whose rollback could not put it back is named with what failed rather than as rolled
  back, and the notice then says not every member is back on its previous version.

- **Peers coming and going no longer count as this Mac's network moving.** Every aterm window and
  node job names its `_alab._tcp` advert afresh, so on a fleet LAN some peer starts or ends one
  every half minute, and the browse took each name it had not heard as a move: the converge
  pass, account upkeep and the fleet heartbeat ran at the move detector's 30-second floor, 20
  to 46 times an hour, instead of on their schedule. The browse now tells a move only for a
  member it hears after every member was silent for two minutes, as when this Mac comes back to
  a LAN.

- **Unfinished setup reopens vault and repository steps when their evidence changes.** A
  completed step still observes its subscriber, private inventory, token and credential helper
  while another step waits, then rechecks readiness and resumes any work that is needed.

- **Background fleet recovery starts with the direct member handshake.** A window's recovery
  pass no longer looks up the HTTP vault before trying native admission. Unconfirmed joins and
  offline sources retain their retry state instead of reporting a failed join, and confirmation
  stays with the subscriber. A Stop or changed setup choice is checked again before publication.
  A successful native admission also starts the fleet and fabric setup pass while the vault's
  HTTP request is still waiting, including with no window open.

- **A new usage limit after a long background break is told as a new one.** When an agent
  worked past a usage limit and its turn ended while its own background work ran, the next
  limit it hit, even hours later, was taken for the first one hit again: its notice was not
  counted as a new escalation and the person's wait on it went unmeasured. The break the turn
  ends at now ends that first limit's retry, so the next limit is a limit of its own.

- **A continuation a compaction owes no longer tells the agent to proceed over a question
  the person kept.** With aterm's answers to questions off, the continuation a `/compact` owes,
  at a break of the agent's own background work or at its turn end, still said that the agent's
  own reversible work is never a NEEDS YOU line, over a reply that waits on the person's
  go-ahead. It leaves that sentence out there now, as aterm's carry at such a reply already did.

- **`aterm secrets need` reaches the lab's table while an aterm window is busy with Commons.**
  The need verbs (`need`, `need ls`, `need retire`, `need pass`, `need give`) and the window's
  own `sync.requests` pass said "lab table: not reached (… another local journal writer is
  active)" whenever the window's Commons runtime held the journal's writer through a repair
  exchange for more than 2 seconds. A pass now waits for the window's writer for up to one repair
  exchange (30 seconds) before it says the table was not reached, and it waits without holding
  Commons custody, so the window and the Writer read are not held up behind it. A credential
  handoff inside the window's own exchange keeps the 2 seconds. The ledger still keeps every need
  until a pass reaches the table.

- **A sign-in that the Mac slept through ends when the Mac wakes, for every CLI.** A sign-in's budget ran on a clock that stops while the Mac sleeps, so a Claude renewal that began just before sleep, or in a dark wake, held the Mac's sign-in lock for hours (6.2 h and 3.4 h were measured), and every other sign-in waited behind it; a Codex, agy, Grok Build or Kimi Code sign-in, whose budget is up to 15 minutes, could hold it across sleep the same way. Every sign-in's budget now also counts the time the Mac slept, so such a sign-in ends at its first look after the Mac wakes; so does the window `aterm harness accounts browser` opens, and a Codex sign-in that ran out of time that way says so instead of reporting a failed sign-in. A network request already in flight when the Mac sleeps, or a wait capped at a minute or less, still runs out its own timeout, mostly 30 seconds or less: a Kimi Code token refresh request now takes 30 seconds at most, and a Google mail grant's renewal retries a grant store another process holds for 30 seconds at most. A Proton mailbox's sign-in through its mail owner can still run on for what was left of the budget while it waits for that owner (`docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, ATERM-KI-1105-14).

- **On a busy Mac, aterm's windows no longer wait on the disk walker.** The window read each
  new disk-size result from a queue that, when it met a result part-way through being written,
  waited for the background thread writing it, yielding the processor 10 ms at a time. macOS
  may keep that thread, aterm's lowest class, off the processor for a long time while other
  work runs, and every window stopped drawing and taking keys until it came back. The window
  now takes the newest result when one is ready and otherwise goes straight on; the walker
  wakes it again once its result is written. (The freeze needs that thread stopped inside a
  few instructions, so it was rare; its length on a real machine was not measured.)

- **Cruise's background wait keeps growing when the harness answers a box in the turn.** A wake
  or an answer to Cruise's prompt that asked a question, or ran into a box the harness answered
  (a recommended option picked, a call declined with a reason, a selection approved), counted
  the harness's own Enter as a message from someone else, so the wait started over and the
  prompt went at once after every such turn. The harness now counts its own answers, and the
  lines aterm types for it, as its own, and an Enter on an option already chosen as sending
  nothing; a message you or another session sent in the turn still starts the wait over.

- **Cruise's background wait keeps growing after an answer too quick to see.** An agent that
  answered Cruise's prompt within a second or two, before the harness looked again, left the
  next wake of its background work timed from that prompt instead of from the wake's own start.
  A wake of a few seconds more than two minutes after the prompt then counted as two minutes of
  work, so the wait started over and the prompt went at once. A wake is now timed from its own
  start: from the first look that shows it where Claude Code draws it, and for another agent
  once the break the quick answer left has settled. An answer the harness sees still counts
  from the prompt.

- **The harness waits out a Claude Code reply that keeps drawing past a minute.** Where it
  waits on the window title for a reply to end (Claude Code's under a status line, as aterm's
  usage tap is one, and Muse Code's), it gave up a minute after it first held the reply and
  acted on it while it was still being drawn. The minute now counts from the reply's
  last change, so the harness gives up only on a reply that stood unchanged for a minute while
  the title still said the turn runs; a status line or a panel's timer that refreshes is no
  change of the reply. The note it leaves then says the reply stood unchanged 60 s.

- **A Claude Code reply is no longer cut short when the harness's wait for it starts over.**
  A wait on a turn that started over (after a lost connection to the window, closing the usage
  panel, a switch to Off and back, or a usage limit's reset) forgot that it had seen the reply
  run. A read in the moment between Claude Code's title resting and the frame that draws the
  reply's last line was then taken for the turn's end, and the harness acted on a reply short
  of its last lines: under Land, a `Nothing left:` reply judged before its `NEEDS YOU` lines.
  The wait now keeps the run the turn's earlier reads saw and reads the screen once more after
  the title rests, as an unbroken wait does.

## [0.158.0] - 2026-11-06

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.157.0: `alab claude harness 0.15`, `alab grok harness 0.14`, `alab kimi harness 0.12`, `alab muse harness 0.14`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

### Added

- **A checkout's `trust.lock` names the Trust build it compiles with.** In a tree whose
  `trust.lock` names a build, plain `targo` and `targo --unverified verify` compile with that
  build rather than the store's newest, so a Trust update that lands in the middle of a build
  changes no compiler. A locked build this Mac lacks is installed once, beside the newest, which
  stays. `aterm pkg install trust --build <N>` installs one build that way by hand, and adding
  `--retry` downloads a build held back after a failed install again now. `aterm help rust` says
  which build the lock names and whether plain `targo` honours it, and verify refuses a `RUSTC`,
  `CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC` or `build.rustc` that would take the locked compiler's place.

- (developer tool) **`atpkg-publish adopt trust=<N>` moves a checkout to another Trust build.**
  It writes the new `trust.lock` on its own branch, runs the checks `publish/config.sh` names
  for a compiler move with that build, and commits the lock only when every one passes.

- **Mail gets through a Mac's node key change.** With the mesh on, mail a Mac's sessions sent
  before its node key changed still reaches each other Mac once, a Mac that was cut off at the
  time included, once it is back. Mail that was waiting on that Mac for one of its own sessions
  reaches that session once, even across more than one key change, and a reply to it reaches
  the session that asked, on that Mac or another.

### Fixed

- **A write cut short no longer stops a vault's Commons being founded.** A Mac killed or
  powered off while it wrote its Commons lease or device custody left a temporary file
  (`.device.age.tmp.<pid>.<salt>`) in the vault's `commons` folder. Founding read that file as
  history the vault does not describe and refused, on every pass and at `aterm secrets commons
  init`. Founding now takes such a leftover as its own. Any other file there still stops it, as
  before.

- **A lasting account-preparation refusal is logged once, not on every pass.** While the
  Commons kept refusing this Mac's native account preparation (this installation excluded from
  control, or control not visible to it), each accounts upkeep wrote the same line to
  `aterm.log` again, about 120 times an hour, until those lines filled nearly half the log and
  pushed older history out of its rotation. aterm now logs such a refusal when it first appears
  or changes, and again only after a pass that got past it.

- **A test binary verify did not let run is NOT RUN, not a failed test.** When verify could not
  start a test binary, or something outside the binary ended it (an interrupt, a stuck holder it
  waited behind), the test row read FAIL against your tree, and the log named that binary a
  failed target with `could not execute`. Each such binary is now a NOT RUN row of its own,
  naming the binary and why. The binaries that ran decide the test row, and the log names only
  those that failed as failed targets.

- (developer tool) **`verify` no longer waits forever on a stage program that outlives its
  SIGKILL.** When a stage's program ran past its ceiling, or waited behind a stuck lock holder,
  `targo --unverified verify` sent its process group SIGKILL and then waited, with no limit, for
  the program to exit. A program macOS's program check holds before its first instruction may
  not die of that signal, and the whole run then hung. Verify now waits at most a minute after
  the SIGKILL. A program still there then is left as it is, and the stage's report names its pid.

- **A toolchain whose programs the system will not run is no longer installed.** Before
  installing a toolchain, aterm runs each program it provides once. A program the system refused
  to execute was handed to the shell, and the shell's own exit passed it, so the toolchain was
  installed and every build with it then failed. Now it is refused at install. A refusal that
  comes from this machine (a mount that forbids running programs, or a security policy) is
  tried again later rather than refused until `--retry`.

- **A Commons member Mac that was never given a shared account no longer logs a failed native
  account preparation on every upkeep pass.** The automatic discovery of the accounts prepared
  for this Mac treated an account activation table that no Mac had set up as an error, so each
  pass logged `native account preparation: application table is not initialized`. Each pass
  also took this Mac's exclusive Commons control writer just to look, and the other Commons work
  that needs that writer refused while discovery held it. Discovery now reads first. When no
  current decision names this Mac, it finds nothing and takes no writer; only a decision for
  this Mac takes the writer that its permit needs.

- **Automatic LAN joining starts at the first eligible network use.** Setup no longer waits
  a minute for its Local Network page to be visible. Native LAN requests feed authenticated
  member handshakes directly, and a route change can retry admission while the vault is still
  holding a long poll. A completed member admission returns without waiting for the HTTP vault;
  its subscriber carries on syncing. Existing privacy choices and macOS's permission dialog
  still apply.

- **A need withdrawn by hand says so.** `aterm secrets need retire <want> --note …` recorded
  "not needed: by-hand's check no longer lacks …", resting on "the requester's own check",
  though nothing was checked and the credential may still be missing. A need withdrawn by hand
  now reads "not needed: withdrawn by hand on this Mac (<host>)", rests on "withdrawn by hand on
  <host>" on the lab's table too, and keeps its note there. `need ls` shows a retired need's
  note on its own line, and `--json` gives its `evidence` and `note`. A control character in a
  note (a newline) is kept as a space, so the table takes the record; before, it failed every
  later pass on that Mac, and a note an earlier build kept that way is cleaned when it is read.

- **A new Mac can join through a nearby member before finding the vault server.** Default
  setup tries the native handshake first, verifies the expected fleet authority, and keeps
  retrying after an offline start or an interrupted reply. Checking setup changes nothing,
  and Stop, sharing and sync choices continue to hold automatic work.

- **aterm started with `CI` set reads your vault before another Mac may drive it.** A window or
  node service started with `CI` set, or a release build started with `ATERM_STATE_HOME` set
  (which a release build does not read), took itself for scratch state and read no vault while
  it served your Mac's own fleet key: a Mac the swarm's deny list names was let in, the
  membership log held out no key, a drive grant, `"*"` included, admitted beside a fleet taken
  under another vault, and a toolset download dialled Macs the deny list names. Which vault the
  window, the node service and toolset downloads read now follows where their state is kept:
  scratch state (a lab instance, a test) reads none, and your Mac's own state reads your vault,
  whatever `CI` says. A window on scratch state now turns away a Mac asking to rejoin the vault
  over the fleet, as the node service already did, rather than judge it by no vault and then
  serve it on the vault in its home folder. A window on your Mac's own state whose vault cannot
  be found (no home folder) now admits by no grant, as the node service then refuses to serve.
  No Mac could drive such a window before either (on macOS it has no state folder and so no
  fleet key; elsewhere it never reads its deny list, so its handshake turns every Mac away), but
  it no longer offers to be driven, its status line no longer says every fleet member may drive
  it, its sessions' remote holds are lifted, and its log says once why no grant admits
  (`docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, ATERM-KI-1105-10).

- **A Mac with no aterm window open keeps its updates right by itself.** The background node
  service replaces its update check if that check stops answering, and it restarts to follow
  a changed "Check for updates automatically" instead of keeping the setting it started with.
  After an update is rolled back, it restarts into the build put back, not the one rolled
  back. It no longer restarts into a release that was withdrawn. A second copy of the
  service, started while one already runs, now exits before it installs a waiting update or
  counts a start against one.

- **A sign-in that the Mac slept through ends when the Mac wakes, for every CLI.** A sign-in's budget ran on a clock that stops while the Mac sleeps, so a Claude renewal that began just before sleep, or in a dark wake, held the Mac's sign-in lock for hours (6.2 h and 3.4 h were measured), and every other sign-in waited behind it; a Codex, agy, Grok Build or Kimi Code sign-in, whose budget is up to 15 minutes, could hold it across sleep the same way. Every sign-in's budget now also counts the time the Mac slept, so such a sign-in ends at its first look after the Mac wakes; so does the window `aterm harness accounts browser` opens, and a Codex sign-in that ran out of time that way says so instead of reporting a failed sign-in. A network request already in flight when the Mac sleeps, or a wait capped at a minute or less, still runs out its own timeout, mostly 30 seconds or less; Kimi Code's token refresh, a Google mail grant's renewal and a Proton mailbox's sign-in can run on for what was left of the budget (`docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, ATERM-KI-1105-14).

- **A page that changes in a covered window reaches the screen reader.** A file reloaded under
  an open page changed nothing a screen reader could read until the window presented again, so a
  selection it made then fell on the wrong text. aterm now sends the page without waiting.

## [0.157.0] - 2026-11-05

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.156.0: `alab claude harness 0.14`, `alab agy harness 0.12`, `alab kimi harness 0.11`, `alab muse harness 0.13`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

### Added

- **A person's post reaches a session on another Mac.** With the mesh on, `aterm fabric post
  to=@<sid>@<node>` to another Mac's session is now carried there instead of refused. The
  session sees it as yours, `trust=human`, from `<you>@<your Mac's node>`. Your Mac seals the
  post with a person key of its own. The node service makes that key and has your Mac's node
  key vouch for it, with nothing to set up. The other Mac takes the post as a person's only once
  that seal checks out under your Mac's node key, so no other Mac can pass off its mail as your
  post. On your own Mac, as before, any process of yours can post as you. A post your Mac does not
  carry is said in your `aterm fabric inbox`, with why.

### Fixed

- **Automatic LAN joining starts at the first eligible network use.** Setup no longer waits
  a minute for its Local Network page to be visible. Native LAN requests feed authenticated
  member handshakes directly, and a route change can retry admission while the vault is still
  holding a long poll. Existing privacy choices and macOS's permission dialog still apply.

- **A landed worker switched to Cruise opens its task again.** A worker's task record read
  `done` with its landing's result while Cruise, switched on from Land, typed into it and the
  worker went on working, and its next landing was never published, so a lead's `aterm ctl
  await task` never woke on it. The record now moves to `working` before Cruise types, as it
  did when the harness restarted first, and a switch made while the land check runs decides
  how its `LANDED` is read, so Cruise never types into a record that reads `done`. The next
  landing is published with its own result.

- **A finished turn's status line no longer takes in a separate line under it.** aterm read
  Claude Code's `✻ … · done …` line in a box narrower than the window, with cells to spare,
  where Claude Code draws it to the window's edge, so a line of its own under it whose first
  word would have ended in the last four cells of the status row read as the rest of the status
  line. It is now read where Claude Code wraps it, as the text under its `⎿` mark already is,
  and a status line Claude Code wrapped in a narrow window still reads whole. A wait for
  background work is read as before: no capture shows where Claude Code wraps one.

- **Caps Lock setup verifies the key's effective mapping.** Setup reads native, user and
  vendor keyboard mappings, preserves other keys' behavior, and verifies the live result.
  Activation belongs to the console user and exact keyboard, with the complete mapping state
  rechecked before each write to detect changes from other apps. Composite keyboards' secondary
  keyboard-capable interfaces are included, and newly attached services receive the accepted
  mapping automatically while explicit device choices, Stop and Restore remain respected.

- **GNU Git bundles retain their runtime paths after installation.** The producer builds from
  pinned source, and staging checks the actual ELF architecture and GNU libc requirements.
  Incompatible managed builds leave native Git eligible; publication checks never mark a
  foreign build ready on the producer.

- **Automatic Git commands use their account's ready managed build first.** An older system
  Git no longer shadows the updated managed tool. Checkout, credential and hook-installer
  commands select the executing account's build and retain native fallbacks when it is absent.
  Waiting for Git no longer asks to install Apple's developer tools just for cloning.

- **Required dependencies repair from local commits while offline.** Setup fetches an older
  clean dependency's exact recorded commit only when it is missing locally. Metadata reads
  cannot start an implicit partial-clone fetch, and Git that lacks the required local-read
  capability leaves the dependency unfinished without a network fallback.

- **Interrupted automatic setup upgrades recover on the next launch.** An older partial
  setup can expand to the base Mac plan before joining a fleet. If the process ends between
  publishing that plan and its progress, recovery now admits the exact expansion, preserves
  the configured vault and earlier grants, and retains Stop and Restore decisions.

- **Setup attention labels read correctly for every row name.** Cards, group summaries and
  the status menu use the same “Needs you” wording for singular and plural subjects.

- **Automatic setup retries failed and unfinished work.** Setup waiting for Git to finish
  installing resumes without another vault change or restart. Failed and unfinished
  background passes retry quietly with a bounded backoff instead of waiting half an hour.
  Settled work clears the retry, and a running pass or Local Network hold still prevents
  overlapping work.

- **A worker whose first reply comes at once is carried on under Land.** A worker started with
  `aterm ctl spawn agent=claude` whose first turn ended before Claude Code had written its task
  into the conversation's transcript was read as a session nobody had asked anything: Land typed
  nothing there, and with the screen at rest it never looked again, so the worker stood idle
  until someone typed to it. At a worker's first reply aterm now goes by the task its launch
  carried, not by a transcript that can trail the screen, and continues the worker there as at
  any other reply; if aterm could not read the worker's task at that moment, it looks again
  shortly. Later replies still go by the transcript, so a worker whose conversation was cleared is
  not typed into. In any tab, where only the transcript says nobody has asked anything while the
  screen shows a conversation, aterm reads the transcript again a moment later before it settles
  on typing nothing, so a transcript that trails a reply no longer leaves a Cruise tab, or a
  worker's later reply, waiting for good.

- **A Claude account renewal that the Mac slept through ends when the Mac wakes.** Its 300-second budget ran on a clock that stops while the Mac sleeps, so a renewal that began just before sleep, or in a dark wake, held the Mac's sign-in lock for hours (6.2 h and 3.4 h were measured), and every other sign-in waited behind it. The budget now also counts the time the Mac slept, so such a renewal ends at its first look after the Mac wakes. Codex, agy, Grok Build and Kimi Code sign-ins still count only awake time, up to 15 minutes (`docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, ATERM-KI-1105-14).

- **Text in Claude Code's side panel is no longer read as the conversation's.** Claude Code
  2.1.310 and later can draw a panel beside the conversation. Panel text beside the status line
  was read as part of that line: text saying a shell or a workflow still runs read as the agent's
  work, which holds a dropped line's restart, an ellipsis read as a turn still running, and an
  ellipsis beside a wait for workflows hid that wait. The status line is now read up to the
  panel's edge. So is Claude Code's network retry row, which beside the panel was never read as
  one: a turn the Mac slept through in that retry now gets aterm's Esc with the panel open too.
  Panel text that said `Still working` beside a row under the status line no longer reads as
  Claude Code's hint of a turn still running, which kept a finished turn from being continued.
  Nor does panel text beside a workflow's end row count that workflow as completed, which could
  read the work an earlier wait still waited for as ended. A status line too long for the space
  beside the panel, which Claude Code wraps onto a second row, is read whole: its first row alone
  could hide work still running that it names at its end. Where Claude Code compacted an idle
  conversation beside the panel, the line that ended the turn above that compaction is now read
  as it is with no panel: background agents it named as still running had read as no work, so a
  line the agent dropped could be restarted over them. A question the agent asks beside the panel
  now reads as a question: the row's padding and the panel's edge after its `?` read it as a
  finished turn, and with the panel's divider beside it an earlier row read as the agent's last
  words. The agent's last words aterm reads, the prompt a turn answered and the turn's line in
  aterm's journal no longer carry the panel's edge or its text, and a finished `/login` beside
  the panel reads as finished. A usage-limit or error notice a turn ended on beside the panel is
  read as its own words: its message took in the padding, the panel's edge and the panel's text,
  though its kind and reset read right. A hint Claude Code draws over the composer beside the
  panel (the goal mark, the critical-memory warning, usage credits in use, a login about to
  expire) is read against the panel's edge: it went unread there (the goal mark was read only
  where the panel's own text ran its row out to the window's edge), and panel text reaching that
  edge read as such a hint. A question you declined with Esc beside the panel is read as your
  stop, not as a turn that ended by itself. A row holding an emoji such as ✅ or 🚀 is read up to
  the panel's edge too: aterm counted such an emoji one column wide where it draws two, so it
  missed the edge on that row and a question there read as a finished turn. So is a row holding
  an emoji written with its variation selector (✅️), joined to others (👩‍💻), with a skin tone
  (👍🏽), a flag (🇯🇵), a keycap (1️⃣) or a letter with a combining accent: aterm counted the
  selector, the joined emoji, the skin tone, the flag's second half or the accent as columns of
  their own, where its grid draws each in the columns of the character before it, and now counts
  a row as its grid lays it out. So is a row holding an emoji or a CJK character whose
  text-style selector narrows it to one column (✅︎): aterm's grid reads the column it leaves
  blank back as a space, which aterm counted on top of the two columns the character took. The
  usage limit a cancelled auto-continue leaves beside the panel now reads the same kind, reset
  and place as with no panel: a limit notice in the panel's text, or Claude Code's word there
  that it continued by itself, read as the newest limit or as the auto-continue's end, so the
  cancel was read as leaving no limit. Its message no longer takes in the notice's separate
  `/upgrade to increase your usage limit.` line after it, beside the panel or in a window 81 to
  87, 43 to 49 or 38 to 40 columns wide, nor does the line aterm reads as the tab's last words
  where that line is the last thing said: aterm read the text under Claude Code's `⎿` mark as
  wrapped short of the window's edge, where Claude Code draws it to the edge, so a line that fit
  on the notice's last row read as the rest of it. Only where that line cannot fit on the
  notice's last row (72 to 80 columns, and 41 and 42, where a row of the notice is exactly full)
  are its rows the very ones a single wrapped line would draw, and both still take it in. A file
  name with a combining accent (as macOS writes `é`) on a row drawn to the window's edge no
  longer makes aterm read the window as wider, which in a narrow window could leave a limit
  notice unread, the tab idle where it was walled, or a finished `/login` unread. Where no status
  line shows over the composer, the conversation is read as ending above the rows blank up to
  the panel's edge: they read as conversation, so the report of a worker's turn ran on through
  those rows of padding and edge. Claude Code's rating cards, its drafted bug-report card, its
  transcript-share ask and a rating's thanks are read as cards beside the panel too: the
  conversation was read as running on through them, so an Esc you pressed above one read as a
  turn that ended by itself, and an open rating card read as none. A worker's report beside the
  panel holds the conversation's words up to the panel's edge: each of its rows carried the
  padding, the panel's edge and the panel's text, so a manager read the panel's words as the
  worker's. Rows the report takes from aterm's record of rows that scrolled off still carry the
  panel's edge and text: that record does not say which rows were drawn beside the panel, so a
  table's own `│` there could be taken for the panel's edge. A turn you sent that wraps onto a
  second row beside the panel is found as the report's start, on the screen or in that record,
  also once the panel has closed or its edge has moved, and the ledger finds it there to size its
  reply: the panel's edge on its first row hid it, so the report said it found no start and ran
  from the top, and the ledger said the turn's row was not found. A change in the panel's own
  text, such as its list of changed files, no longer reads as the agent moving on: it read as a
  new point in the turn, a sent message's turn drawn, a conversation that moved, and new words
  from an agent held busy by background work, which started over aterm's count of how long that
  agent had been stuck.

- **aterm no longer blanks a native page for a screen reader when you act on a control.**
  Acting on a control in Settings or another native page could send the screen reader an empty
  page, moving its focus to the window until the next frame. A load change repainting the page
  could do the same, and so could a press that opened a page or brought a hidden tab back.
  aterm now sends the page as it stands, without waiting for a frame.

- **A screen reader no longer hears another tab's text as the tab it just switched to.** Until
  the next frame, a switched-to terminal read out the previous tab's screen under its own name.
  A terminal's text now reaches the screen reader only from a frame composed for that layout.

- **A Muse Code turn stopped by its own fault now reaches a person.** When Muse Code ends a
  turn on a fault notice such as *A configuration problem stopped this turn. Fix it in
  /settings.*, Cruise and Land used to leave the tab idle with nothing said. They now list
  that notice once under the menu bar's Needs you, and still type nothing into the session.
  That holds when the fault answers aterm's own continuation at once, and a person typing at
  that tab is left their grace before it is listed.

- **Autopilot Land no longer carries an agy relaunch that started a fresh conversation as the
  session it replaced.** An agy relaunch aterm refused as started fresh, or one whose
  conversation has moved on since, is now read as a fresh start, as a new launch in the tab is,
  though aterm's relaunch line still names the old conversation.

- **Autopilot Land no longer carries its task into an agent started fresh in the tab.** When you
  cleared the conversation, started a new agent, or aterm's relaunch of one started fresh while
  Land was still carrying the old session's task, your first message to the new one was carried
  as that task's work, and Land then asked the new agent to land work it never saw. That first
  message now opens a session of its own, as a new session's opening message does.

## [0.156.0] - 2026-11-05

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.155.0: `alab claude harness 0.13`, `alab agy harness 0.11`, `alab grok harness 0.13`, `alab muse harness 0.12`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- **A repository aterm's setup clones into your home gets its own git hooks.** Right after it
  clones one, the setup runs the clone's `scripts/install-git-hooks.sh` where the repository
  has one, as trust and clean do, so a new `$HOME/trust` has its push gate and its git tuning
  without a separate step. The setup's row says what the installer printed, or how it failed.
  A failing installer never fails the setup, and the setup never runs one in a folder that was
  already there.

- (developer tool) **`lab forever` judges Cruise as continuous forward runs it.** A Cruise
  chain whose agent repeats one report (HC) passes when aterm paces it on the short back-off
  ladder, asks for a different approach after the ladder's wait, and decides the answer to that
  request as the ladder's next step; it fails a hold (`STOPPED FOR GOOD`), a park after the
  request, a gap shorter than the ladder's step and more acts an hour than the ladder allows.
  Cruise's other wants follow: N4 wants no tab pressed for attention, F18 judges the person's
  prompt answered at once on the ladder instead of wanting it left to them, `switch-over-held`
  switches a Cruise tab at its repeated report, and `--mode ladder` reads each wait before a
  request for a different approach as a step. Land's same-reply hold, a person's hold and a
  claim's custody keep their wants. The lab reads a tab's "driven by" line by the words the
  window writes it with, codex-alab's own `codex-alab autopilot (…)` line included.

### Fixed

- **Fleet setup acquires required repository dependencies automatically.** The private vault
  inventory selects required submodules; each checkout's tracked gitlinks supply their exact
  commits. Setup repairs missing or outdated required dependencies in existing checkouts as
  well as new clones, preserves personal work, and counts a repository ready only when its
  required dependencies are ready too. A saved conflict is rechecked locally so correcting
  the checkout lets automatic setup resume without changing credentials or running init again.

- **A failed automatic setup pass retries after connectivity returns.** Vault subscribers and
  mesh nodes retain unsuccessful runner outcomes and retry unchanged inputs with a bounded
  backoff, instead of waiting for the half-hour healthy recheck. A successful pass clears the
  retry, and a running pass or Local Network hold still prevents overlapping work.

- **System State's Stop reaches its active Mac Setup installer.** Cancellation verifies the
  current installer's private receipt and process identity, then interrupts that exact CLI.
  Its attached wait forwards the stop to its own sudo child so the authorized run can finish
  its current step and release custody. Replaced programs are preserved, and Stop opens no
  replacement password prompt.

- **Vault discovery no longer conflicts with this Mac's own hostname.** Proxy advertisements
  stay on their actual LAN interface, including on a Mac with one network, instead of also
  claiming loopback and causing Bonjour to append a number to the hostname. A missing or
  invalid interface cannot broaden the advertisement.

- **Setup checks debugger authorization as well as developer mode.** An enabled mode still
  needs the console account's missing membership; existing administrators and developers need
  no extra grant, and an unreadable membership causes no speculative group change. Name status
  also recognizes automatic repair through the existing naming rule instead of asking for
  another Mac password.

- **On a busy Mac, a tab's reader no longer gives up its turn after handing the window its
  screen.** When the window wanted a tab's screen while its reader was taking in output, the
  reader handed the screen over and then yielded the processor. macOS sets a thread that yields
  aside for a whole 10 ms scheduling turn whenever other work is waiting, so the output that came
  next could reach the screen up to that much later. The reader now watches for the window to
  take the screen, for at most a fifth of a millisecond, and goes straight on. (The 10 ms is
  macOS's turn, measured for yields elsewhere in aterm; this reader's delay was not measured.)

- **The Macs of a vault this Mac left no longer drive it by the grants made there.** After `aterm
  secrets join` of another vault, or `aterm members join` with a person's phrase, the new vault's
  log binds none of the old vault's Macs, so fleet admission judged each by this Mac's book, and
  every one the book bound that held this Mac's fleet secret drove it by a drive grant made under
  the old vault (`"*"` or a named one). That included a Mac the old vault had removed or denied.
  It lasted until a fleet sync moved this Mac to the new vault's fleet, and for good where that
  vault publishes no default fleet code, or the fleet was joined by hand or is one this Mac
  issues. Now each fleet records the vault it was taken under (`fleet-vault` in the state
  directory), and while this Mac is in another vault, or none, no drive grant lets any Mac drive
  it. The grants stay in aterm.toml. `aterm fleet peers` says on a `Drive:` line why none admits
  and how to take the fleet under the vault this Mac is in, and `aterm fleet allow drive` grants
  nothing until then. A sync of that vault's default fleet code takes the fleet again with its
  default grant; a join of the fleet held does it too, and names the old grants it takes out. The
  issuer of the vault's default fleet takes it again at its sync; the issuer of another fleet runs
  `aterm fleet init --rotate`. A fleet is recorded under the vault configured when the join began
  or the sync read its code, so a move to another vault while a join dials leaves no grant
  admitting. A signer rotation, a mirror added or a host renamed is the same vault. A fleet joined
  by an older aterm, or with no vault, records the vault the first heartbeat, peers read or sync
  finds configured. A Mac that moved before upgrading therefore keeps its old grants, through a
  join of the same fleet again too, until it moves to another fleet, leaves, or `aterm fleet
  allow content` takes the grants out (`docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, ATERM-KI-1105-10).

- **A worker whose first reply comes at once is carried on under Land.** A worker started with
  `aterm ctl spawn agent=claude` whose first turn ended before Claude Code had written its task
  into the conversation's transcript was read as a session nobody had asked anything: Land typed
  nothing there, and with the screen at rest it never looked again, so the worker stood idle
  until someone typed to it. aterm now takes a worker's task from the task its launch carried,
  not from a transcript that can trail the screen, and continues the worker at that first reply
  as at any other.

- **Repository downloads survive unrelated vault updates.** Setup keeps a completed download
  when another vault entry changes, while still checking its credentials, repository inventory
  and the vault's admission before publishing it. Forks and archived repositories also leave
  active repositories' destination folders available.

- **Setup keeps your choices and reports current evidence.** Joining the fleet expands automatic
  setup plans while preserving deliberately disabled groups. Control status keeps unread
  permissions and missing repositories pending even when an earlier setup run finished.
  Stop and newly disabled repository groups also take effect within an active clone batch.

- **`[harness.agy] enabled = false` keeps aterm's own agy sign-ins off.** Switching agy's harness off stopped the window signing agy accounts in, but `aterm ai` with nobody at the Mac still ran aterm's own agy sign-in, and its reports did not name the switch. Both now read agy's own table as they read Claude Code's and Codex's.

- **Reports name the setting that actually keeps aterm's own sign-ins off.** When something in aterm.toml stops aterm signing accounts in by itself, `aterm harness accounts`, `aterm ai` and a sync's receipt now quote that setting: `[swarm] enabled = false`, `swarm = false`, `harness = false`, `[harness] logins = false`, or a `harness` key filed below another table's header, which they show as `theme.harness.accounts = "off"`. They used to name `[harness] accounts = "off"`, `[harness] enabled = false` or `[harness] logins = "off"`, which the file did not contain. An aterm.toml that cannot be read, or that its reader refuses (one other users may write, say), is reported as such rather than as `[harness] enabled = false`, on the `rotation off:` line too, which used to name a setting in the refused file and offer a fix that changed nothing. One that is not valid TOML is reported as not valid TOML, read line by line, with where the parser stopped. The `rotation off:` line also quotes a master or agent switch, or a `harness = false`, filed below another table's header (`theme.harness.enabled = false`), which it used to name `[harness] enabled = false` or `[harness.codex] enabled = false`, and names every setting that turns rotation off where two do.

- **Fleet setup acquires your repositories automatically.** Once the vault delivers its
  credentials and private repository inventory, setup clones missing repositories even when
  no earlier init recorded unfinished work. Fleet and account setup finish before long clones,
  and Stop or a changed repository setting holds later clone steps.

- **An incomplete repository inventory never earns a green check.** Counts include every
  intended repository, including destinations blocked by existing folders. Unknown readings
  stay unfinished, and a saved completed setup is checked against the repositories on disk.

- **A shared account sheet does not require Claude on every Mac.** A new Mac without a Claude
  assignment still sets up its other assigned AI tools. Invalid or conflicting assignments
  remain errors, and a later Claude assignment is picked up automatically.

- **A closed tab's leftovers keep their proof when aterm restarts.** aterm kept what it knew of
  each closed tab in memory only, so after an update or a quit and relaunch, what a closed tab
  had left running read as an orphan with no token in `aterm ctl sys left scope=aterm`, and
  `aterm ctl end` could not reach it. aterm now keeps each closed tab's record in its state
  folder (the last 512 closes, none older than 30 days, of this boot), and a tab still open when
  aterm quits counts as closed at the quit. An aterm that starts again offers each such process
  with the same proof and token the aterm that saw the tab close would have, and records the
  close's "Tab 2 closed and left …" message once: again only where the aterm before never
  recorded it. A tab an update hands to the new aterm stays that aterm's open tab, and a server
  its agent started before the update is named there, not offered.

- **A typed `turn` no longer leaves half its text in the prompt when its time runs short.** A
  `turn typed=1` whose keys went slower than its `timeout=` allowed, such as one sent over a
  drive to a busy worker on another Mac, stopped part-way with `reason=deadline typed=<k>` and
  left those keys in the worker's prompt, and each retry added another piece. It now types only
  while the rest still fits as one paste before the timeout, at the pace the keys are actually
  going, then pastes the rest and submits the whole text. A turn whose first key does not fit
  writes nothing and answers `reason=deadline typed=0 pasted=0`. A turn into Claude Code whose
  Enter went but was not yet seen taken when its time ran out now says `pressed=<n>`, as other
  unverified Enters do, so whoever sent it can tell an Enter went before typing the text again.

- **A sign-in no longer leaves `claude auth login` running.** When aterm quit, updated itself,
  crashed or was killed while an automatic or `accounts renew` sign-in waited, Claude Code's
  sign-in stayed behind, waiting days for a code that never came. It now ends with the aterm that
  started it, including an update that replaces aterm in place, and with its renewal on every
  other way the wait stops; a renewal that runs out says so in `aterm.log`, as before. Another
  CLI's driven sign-in and a person's `accounts login` end with aterm the same way. A window still
  running after an update replaced its app starts no sign-in, since it could not end one; the
  updated aterm signs in.

- **A walled tab's next account is signed in again by itself when its login has gone.** When a Claude account meets its limit and the account the tab would move onto has lost its login on this Mac (its login directory removed, or written over by a `/login` on the default login), aterm now signs that account in again by itself, provided a session on this Mac ran on it within the last week, no other Mac holds its claim, and your sheet does not give the account to other Macs alone. Where this Mac cannot tell whose the account is (the sheet is only on the network, a source or the lab cannot be read here, or the Mac has no name), it leaves the account for `aterm harness accounts renew <label>` and says which of these it is. Until it is signed in, the tab waits for its own reset. A login no session here has run on for a week still waits for `aterm harness accounts renew <label>`. For each row that waits, `aterm harness accounts` and a sync's receipt name the reason aterm does not sign it in, and the receipt promises a sign-in by itself only for a row with a route that needs nobody at the Mac.

- **Account reports stop promising a sign-in that will not happen.** A row no session on this Mac runs on, or ran on within the last week, now says it waits for `aterm harness accounts renew <label>`, in `aterm harness accounts` and a sync's receipt, and the settings help says when aterm signs a login in by itself: a login that ends or comes due within a week of a session here running on it, unless another Mac holds it or this Mac cannot tell whose it is. A second account still takes a person's first sign-in, so a report no longer reads as if one is on its way.

- **Text in Claude Code's side panel is no longer read as the conversation's.** Claude Code
  2.1.310 and later can draw a panel beside the conversation. Panel text beside the status line
  was read as part of that line: text saying a shell or a workflow still runs read as the agent's
  work, which holds a dropped line's restart, an ellipsis read as a turn still running, and an
  ellipsis beside a wait for workflows hid that wait. The status line is now read up to the
  panel's edge. So is Claude Code's network retry row, which beside the panel was never read as
  one: a turn the Mac slept through in that retry now gets aterm's Esc with the panel open too.
  Panel text that said `Still working` beside a row under the status line no longer reads as
  Claude Code's hint of a turn still running, which kept a finished turn from being continued.
  Nor does panel text beside a workflow's end row count that workflow as completed, which could
  read the work an earlier wait still waited for as ended. A status line too long for the space
  beside the panel, which Claude Code wraps onto a second row, is read whole: its first row alone
  could hide work still running that it names at its end. Where Claude Code compacted an idle
  conversation beside the panel, the line that ended the turn above that compaction is now read
  as it is with no panel: background agents it named as still running had read as no work, so a
  line the agent dropped could be restarted over them. A question the agent asks beside the panel
  now reads as a question: the row's padding and the panel's edge after its `?` read it as a
  finished turn, and with the panel's divider beside it an earlier row read as the agent's last
  words. The agent's last words aterm reads, the prompt a turn answered and the turn's line in
  aterm's journal no longer carry the panel's edge or its text, and a finished `/login` beside
  the panel reads as finished. A usage-limit or error notice a turn ended on beside the panel is
  read as its own words: its message took in the padding, the panel's edge and the panel's text,
  though its kind and reset read right. A hint Claude Code draws over the composer beside the
  panel (the goal mark, the critical-memory warning, usage credits in use, a login about to
  expire) is read against the panel's edge: it went unread there (the goal mark was read only
  where the panel's own text ran its row out to the window's edge), and panel text reaching that
  edge read as such a hint. A question you declined with Esc beside the panel is read as your
  stop, not as a turn that ended by itself. A row holding an emoji such as ✅ or 🚀 is read up to
  the panel's edge too: aterm counted such an emoji one column wide where it draws two, so it
  missed the edge on that row and a question there read as a finished turn. So is a row holding
  an emoji written with its variation selector (✅️), joined to others (👩‍💻), with a skin tone
  (👍🏽), a flag (🇯🇵), a keycap (1️⃣) or a letter with a combining accent: aterm counted the
  selector, the joined emoji, the skin tone, the flag's second half or the accent as columns of
  their own, where its grid draws each in the columns of the character before it, and now counts
  a row as its grid lays it out. So is a row holding an emoji or a CJK character whose
  text-style selector narrows it to one column (✅︎): aterm's grid reads the column it leaves
  blank back as a space, which aterm counted on top of the two columns the character took. The
  usage limit a cancelled auto-continue leaves beside the panel now reads the same kind, reset
  and place as with no panel: a limit notice in the panel's text, or Claude Code's word there
  that it continued by itself, read as the newest limit or as the auto-continue's end, so the
  cancel was read as leaving no limit. Its message there can still take in the notice's
  `/upgrade` line after it, as it does in a window that narrow with no panel. Where no status
  line shows over the composer, the conversation is read as ending above the rows blank up to
  the panel's edge: they read as conversation, so the report of a worker's turn ran on through
  those rows of padding and edge. Claude Code's rating cards, its drafted bug-report card, its
  transcript-share ask and a rating's thanks are read as cards beside the panel too: the
  conversation was read as running on through them, so an Esc you pressed above one read as a
  turn that ended by itself, and an open rating card read as none. A worker's report beside the
  panel holds the conversation's words up to the panel's edge: each of its rows carried the
  padding, the panel's edge and the panel's text, so a manager read the panel's words as the
