  until you had been at the Mac 30 seconds since your first touch after the question, and every
  other answer held it until the re-probe heard it. On macOS 26 and 27, aterm now also ends the
  hold on an Allow the re-probe cannot hear, and on any answer before the re-probe hears it: it
  watches, from a background thread, which windows UserNotificationCenter (the process that
  draws that alert) has, reading only window owners and numbers and whether each is on screen,
  so it needs no Screen Recording permission. Once the alert it saw come is gone and
  UserNotificationCenter has no window left, on screen or off, at a read made while you are at
  the Mac, System State goes on at that read. The watch reads every quarter second for the first
  half minute after the question, so an alert you answer at once is still seen. A read made while
  you are away never counts: after that first half minute the watch reads every 5 seconds while
  you are away, and a quarter second after each read once you are back. When it sees no alert
  come (macOS asked aterm before, or the alert came and went between two reads) or another
  UserNotificationCenter window is still up, aterm still waits your 30 seconds at the Mac. The
  question macOS asks at aterm's first local-network use outside System State's step (Commons or
  a converge pass, before you press Turn On macOS Access…) is not watched yet and still holds
  System State for your 30 seconds. aterm never presses the alert's buttons.

- **`aterm_policy::Response` exposes `strictness_rank` and `is_at_least_as_strict_as` in the public
  API, and Linux/POSIX QoS and sandbox probes no longer pass vacuously or fail on tight `RLIMIT_NOFILE`
  ceilings.** Policy consumers can now compare `Response` strictness (`Drop > Warn > Rewrite > Ask >
  Execute`) directly without duplicating ranking tables; `aterm-gui`'s Linux EEVDF slice probe reports
  `COULD NOT RUN` instead of silently passing on pre-6.12 kernels and stages its launcher stub in
  `aterm_tempfile`; `aterm-sandbox`'s binding `RLIMIT_NOFILE` probe adapts when a host's hard ceiling
  is `<= 8192` and reports `COULD NOT RUN` under root; and `aterm-agent` folds two helper subprocess
  stages out of the `#[test]` namespace.

- **A planted file no longer hangs aCaffeine's start.** Before the mug runs again from a copy
  of aterm it already ran from, aCaffeine stamps that copy. A FIFO named `exec` in the copy hung
  the mug's next start while it held its lock, and a link there was written through, truncating
  the file it named. The stamp now goes only into a regular file with no other name, and nothing
  is truncated until that is known: a FIFO is refused at once rather than waited on, and neither
  a symbolic nor a hard link there is written through.

- **aCaffeine leaves another Mac's Enable at Startup.** With a network home that two Macs
  read, aCaffeine on one Mac removed the Enable at Startup login items whose aterm was missing
  there, among them one for an aterm in another Mac's /Applications: at each aterm launch, at
  `aterm acaffeine start`, when Enable at Startup was turned off, when the mug started and in
  the pass aterm runs at login with no window. Its retirement of old `aterm caffeine` login
  items also ran this Mac's aterm at the path another Mac's item names, to ask whether it still
  had the old verb. On a home that is not on a disk of this Mac, aCaffeine now judges only a
  login item whose aterm lies inside the home. An old Caffeine login item outside it stays and
  its aterm is not asked, even where this Mac's aterm there is 0.145.0, which fails at each
  start. aterm's log names each item kept so, once per launch, and where this Mac's aterm there
  is this release or a later one, the item's own run at login says why it kept it. A kept login
  item of either name whose aterm is missing on this Mac is unloaded from this Mac's launchd,
  which cannot run it, until the next login, unless the item's process still runs here (a mug
  that runs from its own copy of that aterm, which outlives the app): that item stays loaded
  while its process runs. The line aterm writes for an old Caffeine item says which it did.

- **Windows ConPTY `build_command_line` no longer doubles trailing backslashes on `argv[0]`, and
  `Parser::restore_carry` rejects unreachable subparameter masks and colon carries.** `aterm-pty`
  now quotes `argv[0]` with literal backslashes (`append_argv0_units`) while keeping MSVCRT
  backslash doubling for `argv[1..]`, fixing round-trip command-line parsing when a quoted program
  path ends in `\`; `aterm-parser` now rejects `subparam_mask` bit `0` on `params[0]`, empty-list
  `last_was_colon`, and `subparam_mask != 0` or `last_was_colon` outside `CsiParam`/`CsiIntermediate`;
  and `aterm-json` moves `json_const_helpers_round_trip` into `tests/json.rs` so it executes in the
  test suite.

- **The accounts report, `accounts use` and a launch now say the same thing about every Codex, Grok
  Build and Kimi Code CLI pool.** A roster of this machine's own login alone, at its limit, reports
  `next: main (limited until ...)`, since a launch runs on that login at once, instead of waiting
  for the limit to end. The report judges rotation as a launch does, so `[harness] enabled = false`
  and `[harness.codex] enabled = false` show as `rotation off:`, and `aterm ai review` takes the row
  a launch takes under those switches too. For each row a codex-alab session can run on, the report
  says where a session there moves at its weekly limit in an `at a weekly limit:` line, because
  `next:` is what a new launch takes, and `accounts use` points there. That line is the row the
  session's own handoff would take: none while a pin stands on another row (the session reads
  nothing from the provider and stays put), none where the only other row has little left or
  `relaunch`, `resume_limits` or a warning in `aterm.toml` keeps handoffs off, and a pin on the
  session's own row ends at that limit. A Codex build that runs only this machine's own
  login no longer moves a running session to a row it would never run. `accounts use` of a row it cannot pin now names only a step that can end the refusal: the
  Mac that holds the row, a root's shared renewal, what Codex's keyring store does, the step a
  stopped sign-in left, and `aterm pkg install` first where the program is not here; on a Codex
  build that runs only this machine's own login, it offers no sign-in of a row that build never
  runs.

- **Signing in an account pool stops doing work it cannot finish.** A sign-in of a row held for
  another Mac, or of a CLI that is not installed, starts nothing and says why. `aterm ai login codex`
  no longer signs in a healthy row when the signed-out row has no email: it names that row's
  `accounts login`, or says the pool needs no sign-in. A `codex login` that exits nonzero now counts
  as not signed in, whatever a status read after it finds; quitting `agy` after `aterm ai login agy`
  does not. The report says aterm signs a row in by itself only where it does: not under `[harness]
  logins = "off"`, not on a Claude Code row with no route to sign in with nobody at the Mac, and not
  before the CLI it needs is installed.

- **`aterm ai doctor` rates what it finds more truly.** A roster refused whole is now `refused`,
  with its fix, rather than `ok` or `signed-out`, and `aterm ai status --fleet` counts such a Mac. A
  launch refused until a person changes a pin or roster says so on a row whose login is due or at a
  limit too. Claude Code's accounts report and `accounts use` read its default row's login the way
  the doctor does, and a review's login error now ends a Claude Code login kept in the keychain.

- **A roster that names one account twice is harder to reach and easier to fix.** The first lab sync
  of a Codex pool lists this machine's own login under its lab label, where the lab knows that
  account, instead of beside a second row for it, and a login kept in the OS keyring is not read
  from a leftover `auth.json`. `accounts renew` of a row with no email no longer
  suggests an address that would refuse the whole roster, and the refusal of two rows naming one
  account says which to remove.

- **Fewer false messages from account sources.** A machine with no Commons account catalog no longer
  reports one as unavailable. Naming the `alab` source under `[alab] roster = false` says that
  setting turned it off. Automatic pool messages record a stopped sign-in or a sheet conflict as a
  fact for later, without asking anyone to act.

- **A review that ends on a login error no longer marks a row signed out** when that row never held
  a login. Why a driven sign-in stopped is now said whole, and the `accounts sync` report says how
  many rows the lab prefers on this Mac.

- **A worktree that keeps merging a fast-moving main no longer fills the disk with dead build
  caches.** Below the disk watch's floor, aterm now removes a live worktree's incremental compiler
  caches and old-compiler build outputs once nothing has written them for an hour, rather than
  three days, including while a session is supervised. It takes what nobody uses first and stops
  once enough space is free, unless a run short of room asked, which gets all it may. A running
  build still keeps its whole build directory.

## [0.152.0] - 2026-11-03

### Fixed

- **Restored terminal checkpoints with omitted `xterm_keyboard` fields now default to mode `0`, and
  `DamageTracker` ignores out-of-range `u16::MAX` columns.** `XtermKeyboardState::default()` now
  matches `XtermKeyboardState::new()` and `reset()` (`modifyOtherKeys = Some(0)`, `DECRQM 1036`
  enabled), preventing omitted `#[serde(default)]` checkpoint fields from restoring in the
  explicitly disabled `CSI > 4 m` state; `DamageTracker::{mark_cell, mark_wide_cell}` reject
  `col == u16::MAX` instead of saturating to `[65535, 65535)`; and `AltArchiveBudget::{total,
  min_share}` plus `Terminal::block_eviction_read_count` are exposed on the non-test API.

- **Automatic dialog answers no longer overtake input whose read is unproven.** When the harness
  holds a continuation the worker has not drawn, a dialog's Enter or Esc now waits while no clear
  input read proves the worker consumed the held line, including pending, typeahead or unknown
  status. That proof stays valid across later reads; the ordinary input gate still holds later
  pending or typeahead before the dialog takes the key, without releasing the line's custody.
- **`aterm fabric doctor` dispatches remedies over a closed `WarningKind` grammar, drop-overlay
  border geometry is unified in `aterm-gpu`, and the web predictor stores an injected per-instance
  clock.** `aterm-link` now pairs every warning emitted by `fabric::gather` and `enable::doctor`
  with a structured `fabric::WarningKind` matched exhaustively by `enable::fix_for`, giving
  failed session control-socket queries and unreadable `rendezvous.toml` files explicit remedies
  instead of falling back to prose substring matching; `aterm-gui` reuses
  `aterm_gpu::{drop_border_px, scaled_border_px}` for drop-target glow borders; and `aterm-wasm`
  replaces its thread-local predictor test clock with an injected per-instance clock on
  `PredRows` paired with pure `predict_*_at` methods.

- **Verification now fails closed when its shared subprocess admission pool is unavailable.** A
  saturated, missing, malformed or unsupported configured pool refuses the affected live test
  before it spawns descendants; it no longer returns a usable non-exclusive lease or falls back
  to an independent process-local pool. Pool initialization failures likewise mark the test stage
  COULD NOT RUN before any test child starts. Re-entrant leases are bound to the opened pool
  directory's identity, including Windows file IDs, so re-entrant reuse of a replacement and a
  replacement detected during acquisition are refused.

- **A program in a tab can no longer change aterm.toml's owner keys, or press Settings ▸
  Security's macOS access buttons, through aterm's accessibility tree.** Every program in a tab
  reaches that tree with aterm's own Accessibility access, so aterm cannot tell its request
  from a screen reader's. An edit made through it to the aterm.toml in force now marks the
  buffer as a control client's edit does: a Save that would change `[harness]`'s `occupancy`,
  `occupancy_source` or `occupancy_rule` is refused until Discard Changes and Reload from Disk,
  and so is such a Save pressed through the tree. The macOS access buttons now take only your
  own click or key: an accessibility request, or a control client's key or click, is refused
  them, as `act` already was.

## [0.151.0] - 2026-11-03

### Fixed

- A VT510 program that asks DECCOLM to keep the screen no longer keeps stale margins, line
  sizes or cursor position with it. DECNCSM now suppresses only the screen clear; the
  column-mode transition still performs its other resets and homes the cursor, while preserving
  the program's tab stops as DECCOLM requires.

- **Native agy sign-in now finishes after its CLI exits successfully on macOS.** macOS reports
  permission denied when the unreaped CLI's private process group contains only exited processes;
  aterm treated that normal state as a process failure and discarded the new grant. It now
  confirms every member has exited across two complete group readings before accepting that
  result, while still refusing an incomplete reading or any live, unknown, or newly appeared
  member.
- **Verification test runs share one capacity-aware subprocess pool across concurrent test
  binaries, Seatbelt `sandbox-exec` wrapping is unified on `aterm_containment::sbpl`, and the
  timeline's upgrade column reads an injected awake clock.** `aterm-verify` now sizes a shared
  `ATERM_TEST_SUBPROCESS_SLOTS` lock-file pool from the stage's granted CPU share so live
  headless `aterm` instances and multi-worker `aos-search` coordinators stay bounded across
  concurrent test binaries without widening one-minute hang detectors; `aterm-pty` delegates
  macOS `sandbox-exec` profile validation and argument wrapping to `aterm_containment::sbpl`;
  and `SessionTimeline` and `upgrade_status::Row` accept an injected awake-clock reading so
  upgrade-dwell checks stay deterministic across host sleep and load.

- **State, launchd, fleet, fabric, converge, VM, translation, and archive helpers validate owned
  non-symlink directories and regular files before reading, writing, or unlinking.** Update
  sentinels, service image digests, consent markers, fabric handler tallies, `fabric-off` records,
  fleet membership state, converge history and records, `acaffeine` records and `launchd`
  `LaunchAgents`/log trees, VM run directories and disk keys, native restart observations,
  `<state>/upgrade` harness records, stamps, build caches, model lists, and ledgers, and
  `private_file::remove_private` now verify that their state directories are plain directories owned
  by the current user rather than symlinks or foreign directories before opening, replacing, or
  removing files inside them; `aterm-lexicon` bounds `.mo` and `.po` translation reads to regular
  files up to 64 MiB opened without following symlinks or blocking on FIFOs; `aterm-keeper` rejects
  embedded NUL bytes and `.`/`..` segments in marker directories; and `aterm-forge` validates
  pristine cache directories, rejects conflicting or duplicate PAX/GNU tar extension headers, and
  requires tar trailer padding to be all-zero.

- **An update on a busy Mac no longer misses its first try to hand your tabs over.** To hand
  your tabs to the new aterm, the running one first stops each tab's reader. On a Mac busy
  with other work that took 10 ms a tab however promptly the reader stopped, so three tabs
  missed the first 20 ms try and the update had to wait half a second to try again: aterm
  checked on each reader by yielding the processor, and macOS sets a thread that yields aside
  for a whole 10 ms scheduling turn whenever other work is waiting. aterm now sleeps until each
  reader's end (and, with Rewind on, its recording's last write) wakes it. The capture that
  follows, and the check for Vim's insert indicator as you type, now also wait for a busy tab's
  screen by sleeping between tries rather than yielding, so they catch the fifth of a
  millisecond in which the tab's other work hands the screen over.

- **A line the harness typed that the agent never showed is no longer typed twice.** When an
  agent took a line the harness wrote and showed none of it, aterm used to badge it `typed, not
  submitted` and, once the screen moved, could write it a second time behind a copy the agent
  still held. The harness now holds that line, with no badge or question: nothing more is written,
  at a turn end or at a break of the agent's own background work, and aterm types none of its own
  lines (a relaunch's carry-on, the ask to free disk space, an upgrade's notice) nor restarts the
  agent for an upgrade, until the agent shows it (it is then sent once, as the harness's own
  line), your own typing follows it, or a turn runs after which the agent reads its input clear;
  background work alone is no turn, and a line shown during it counts as shown though it is
  cleared before the work ends. When Claude Code read the line and still shows none of it a
  minute later, at rest, the harness restarts it in place once and the resumed session gets the
  line once; while its background work runs the restart waits for the work to end, and a restart
  the window puts off is asked for again later. Where no restart is made (any agent but Claude
  Code, `[harness] relaunch = false`, a supervisor with no window to make one, a restart the
  window refused, or a second loss), the session waits for one of those, writing nothing, and an
  upgrade that comes due may still restart the agent onto its new build.

- The harness now confirms Claude Code's "Claude in Chrome" intro, which left Chrome-using
  workers stalled at startup. That includes panes 20 to 24 columns wide, where the intro is
  taller than the rows the harness reads at first.

- With no terminal tab open, pressing Install no longer retries the update's pre-install check
  dozens of times a second while the check waits for an update check to confirm the signer.
  The press now stops and says it is waiting for that update check. With automatic install on,
  the update then installs by itself; with it off, press again after the check. If the
  pre-install check fails, a window that can relaunch itself relaunches to check again, as
  before. If it ends without an answer (for example, because another aterm holds the update
  lock), the next press checks again instead of repeating the old answer for ten minutes, and
  a window that can relaunch itself relaunches. A press waiting on the pre-install check now
  shows as installing, says how it ended, and is no longer refused while the check is running.

- **`verify appkit` reports `COULD NOT RUN` naming the missing display on a closed-lid Mac.**
  When CoreGraphics lists no active drawable display (such as a MacBook with its lid closed and
  no external monitor attached), `objc_window_drive`, `objc_toolbar_drive`, and
  `objc_frame_clock_drive` now exit `NOT RUN` before opening a window or waiting out a 60 s
  display-link timeout, and `verify appkit` quotes the driver's `NOT RUN` reason directly in its
  `COULD NOT RUN` summary instead of reporting an empty `available_monitors` finding.

- **`aterm harness accounts --cli codex|grok|kimi` names the account the next launch takes.**
  With no pin, `next:` treated the active account as one in use and named another, while
  `accounts use --auto` and the launch itself took the active one; where no other account could
  serve it said `next: none` though a launch ran. `next:` now names the account a launch takes,
  and no account is called "the account in use". A pinned account this Mac may not use now is
  listed under `not next:` as held for another Mac's warm set, leased elsewhere until its claim
  ends, or not this Mac's to claim, in the words `accounts use` prints; Claude Code's report and
  the refusal of a held pin under `[harness] accounts = "off"` say "held for another Mac's warm
  set" too, where they said `held-elsewhere`.

- **The accounts report's `active:` line says when a launch would not take the active account.**
  With no session running, it named the recorded active account alone while a Codex, Grok Build
  or Kimi Code CLI launch took another or none; it now adds the account a launch takes, or that a
  launch does not take this one, as `next:` says.

- **`accounts use` and `next:` say when Grok Build or Kimi Code CLI is not installed.** They said
  a launch takes the pinned account while `aterm ai status` said not installed. With no copy of
  it here, neither aterm's nor one on `PATH`, they now say it is not installed, with
  `aterm pkg install grok` or `aterm pkg install kimi`, as for Codex. A copy on `PATH` that aterm
  does not manage still runs where a launch types the program's word, so there they still name
  the account a launch takes, though `aterm ai status` says not installed by aterm and
  `aterm ai review` skips that copy. With no Codex to start, `next:` no longer also says
  accounts are not next for what a Codex build would run, nor prints a `this Codex build:` line.

- **`aterm harness accounts use <label> --cli codex|grok|kimi` names the sign-in that ends its
  refusal.** A signed-out account and one with no login made here were both told "its login is
  not made yet". Each now names its sign-in at a terminal (`aterm harness accounts login|renew
  <label> --cli <id>`, the command `accounts add` names; Codex's own `aterm ai login codex` for
  this machine's own login on a Codex build that runs only that login), and an account held for
  preparation only is not sent to a sign-in.

- **`aterm ai login codex` at a terminal names the pin a launch still needs.** On a Codex build
  that ignores `CODEX_AUTH_PATH`, with the pin on an account of its own, signing this machine's
  own login in said `signed in` and exited 0 while every launch stayed refused. It now says the
  launches stay refused, names the step that ends it (the pin on that login's account, `aterm
  harness accounts use <label> --cli codex`), and exits 1.

- **`aterm ai login codex` no longer says Codex is signed in where aterm cannot see its login.**
  With Codex's login kept in the OS keyring, it refused because "Codex CLI is signed in" while
  `aterm ai status` said it could not tell; it now says aterm cannot see whether Codex is signed in
  and names Codex's own `codex login`. Where no Codex login is stored, the sign-in no longer warns
  that it revokes Codex's current login first.

- **`aterm ai status` no longer says no route of aterm's signs a CLI in where `aterm ai login`
  runs one.** Under a switch that keeps aterm's own sign-ins off, the person's `aterm ai login`
  at a terminal can still run aterm's renewal; the health line now says the sign-in is one aterm
  does not make unattended.

- **An accounts report on a machine with no Commons catalog set up prints no catalog error.**
  Every report ended with "Commons account catalog unavailable" when
  `~/.config/aterm/secrets` did not exist; a catalog that is set up and cannot be read is still
  reported unavailable.

## [0.150.0] - 2026-11-03

### Changed

- **A new Mac on the home ALab LAN gets into ALab by proving itself to a member there, and
  only so.** Being on the LAN is the approval: the member lets it in on that same connection,
  with no Allow, phrase, admin Mac or approver in the path. A Mac's plain request to join,
  from any network, the home LAN included, now waits for a person's Allow. A member no longer
  passes a LAN Mac's request on to the vault's join queue, the vault's server no longer marks
  a request with the network it heard it on, and an admin Mac's approver no longer lets a Mac
  in for asking from the home LAN; it still reads past the marks an aterm 0.148 or 0.149
  server lists, and admits nothing by them. `aterm secrets requests --json` drops
  `lan_observed`.

- Capability files must be owner-only regular files for every reader, including
  supervised bridge startup. Startup and setup leave refused files unchanged,
  even inside a private folder. OS access failures do not authorize replacing a
  ring. On-demand fabric diagnostics name the refusal; automatic compatibility
  narrowing and its Messages notices are removed.
- **Direct mail from another Mac is sealed on disk.** A session's direct fleet mailbox
  (`<state>/fleet-mail/<session>.toml`) is now encrypted at rest under the one `key` beside
  every mailbox in that folder, 0600, left out of Time Machine backups and never in the
  Keychain, so a backup or a copy without the key holds no message or reply text. It does not
  need the bus: direct mail seals with the fabric off. When aterm starts, it seals every
  mailbox an earlier aterm wrote, a closed tab's included, and removes the plaintext
  temporaries a crashed write left; a live session's is sealed by its next read or write. An
  earlier aterm cannot read a sealed mailbox. A mailbox moved to another session's name does
  not open there. A missing or damaged key refuses direct mail, `inbox fleet` included, and
  leaves the mailboxes as they are; no new key is made while any of them is sealed. Put the
  key back, or move the sealed mailboxes aside to start empty ones. Bus mail is untouched, and
  `inbox` marks the direct part `fleet_error=unavailable`. Linux has no backup mark, and
  aterm's log says so when it makes the key. It does not protect mail from a process of your
  own user or a copy of the whole folder.
- **Tabs that are applications look like it.** System State, Settings, About, Mail, Markdown, the Editor and Recovery wear their icon on a small tile in the theme's colours and have a bold title, selected or not. Terminal tabs keep bold for the selected tab. System State has its own icon.
- **Harness versions since v0.149.0: `alab claude harness 0.9`, `alab agy harness 0.9`, `alab grok harness 0.9`, `alab muse harness 0.9`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- **`yolo` wears the rule's colour, and a click on it turns it `lame`.** On Claude Code's
  rewritten mode row, `yolo` (bypass permissions) is drawn in the ink of the rule it sits on
  instead of red. Clicking `yolo` (or `auto`) presses shift+tab until Claude is in manual mode,
  which the row now calls `lame`; clicking any other mode goes back to yolo or auto. Hovering a
  mode says what it does, Claude's own name for it, and where a click goes.
- **The Autopilot chip names a mode as you click to it, then fades the name.** Land and Off now
  rest as their glyph alone (`⤓`, `○`), like Cruise's `∞`. Each click on the chip brings up the
  mode it reached after the glyph (`∞ cruise`, `⤓ land`, `○ off`), holds it for a second and
  fades it out; the glyph stays in place, so clicking through the modes keeps hitting it. The name
  only takes room the rule can spare (a hover title may shorten for it; no fact moves), and Reduce
  Motion removes it without the fade.

- Fabric bridges reuse a current session list across post batches. Session arrivals,
  removals and identity changes force a new read; a reply without a roster generation
  still requires a fresh lookup.

### Added

- **aterm no longer checks AI accounts' usage on a timer for accounts nobody is using.**
  Claude Code's `/usage` check runs only at a turn's end, and only once a turn has run since
  the last check; Kimi's background refresh is gone (`aterm harness accounts refresh` still
  reads it when you ask); a Codex launch reads the account it is about to start on, and
  another only if that one cannot serve, three at most; agy reads at a launch and once at a
  limit wall (again after an hour if the wall still stands), and the agy and Muse Code
  footers read once per session. `accounts stats` asks no provider and shows what this Mac
  last recorded, with its age.
- **Each Mac now keeps a journal of the accounts it uses, shared with the lab.** When the
  harness sees an account start or end a session, sign in or out, hit or clear a limit,
  rotate, or read a new quota figure, it notes one short line in a local spool, with the
  account's key and a few fixed words, never an address, link or reason text. Noting it
  takes no lock and allocates nothing, so typing never waits on it. About once a minute the
  Mac that runs the shared database packs what waits into one record of the lab's weekly
  journal table, keeping to its fixed share of the week (a few records at once, then spread
  over the week, in records and in bytes; nothing is lost, it just waits, and a Mac that
  has nothing to send reads the table only every few hours), and each week it restates every account
  it used in the last six months, so the lab can still say who last used an account, on
  which Mac, after the week that held it is gone. Macs relay each other's last-use news in
  16 buckets so every account stays covered as Macs come and go, and each Mac keeps what it
  heard from the others for 120 days. A Mac with no room for the table keeps its journal
  local and `aterm db alab check` says why. Each check of an account's usage that remains is
  noted too, with why the account was in use (a launch, a running session, a limit wall, or
  you asked); agy's and Muse Code's checks name no account yet and are not noted. On first
  start the Mac also notes its last 30 days of local account history, from the app or the
  background job only, and again on a later start if it stopped before that history was saved.
- **Each Mac now registers itself in the lab's shared table.** After a repair round of the
  shared database, a Mac finds its own machine row and writes one small row about itself under
  its own key: its label, its computer and local host names, model, chip, core counts, memory,
  disk and macOS version, read on the Mac itself. It finds its row by a reinstall's hardware
  hint, then its fleet node, a host name, then a placeholder with its label. A Mac with no row
  writes a new one only after a round with a Mac that already holds the table, and never beside
  a row that already has its label. The hardware identifier is never stored, only a hint keyed
  to your lab, so a cloned virtual machine is reported for you to look at, never merged. A Mac
  restates its row only when something about it changed (at most daily) or once a month, stops
  at its share of automatic writes, and stops writing, with a finding, when you retire the row
  it is bound to. `aterm db alab check` shows what this Mac's registration decides and why.
- Mail now watches the active folder in the background. IMAP accounts use IDLE
  notifications, Proton checks every two seconds, and switching folders cancels
  old work without interrupting foreground reading or sending.
- Authentication email reads share the native Proton connection with Mail and
  preserve sign-in link targets. Gmail waits keep one TLS IMAP connection, batch
  message headers, and wake on IDLE notifications instead of repeated logins.

### Changed

- **A release build cannot be told where it is by an environment variable.** The lab's switch
  that scripts where a Mac is on the network (`ATERM_DEBUG_NETPLACE`) is read only by debug
  builds, and `verify census` now fails any change that names it in code a release build
  compiles, which every way of reading it needs.
- **A member this Mac cannot reach on its own network is told apart from a privacy setting.**
  `aterm fleet peers`, `aterm ctl survey --fleet` and the menu bar now judge a "no route" by the
  member's address. A member on the network this Mac is on that cannot be reached while another
  member's Mac there answers, even only to refuse the connection, is that Mac's own problem
  (asleep, off or moved), and its row says so. Only when nothing on this network answers do they
  point at Local Network privacy, and then wherever this Mac is, a phone hotspot included. A
  member on another network that cannot be reached never blames the privacy setting, whatever
  network this Mac remembers.
- **The internet is checked again when the network comes back.** When this Mac's network
  drops and comes back on the same network, or the Mac wakes from sleep, aterm checks the
  internet once more with the same API check it makes after a move, so the network state no
  longer shows the answer from before the drop or the sleep. Nothing polls for it: the Mac's
  own path and wake notices start the check. Like the check after a move, it runs in a window
  whose harness carries an agent session (with `harness.probe_api` on, the default): the
  window's network watch starts with that session's first look, and a window that never
  carried one makes no API checks at all.
- **A Mac asking to join ALab says what will let it in where it is.** On the home ALab LAN
  System State's Secrets note, `aterm doctor`, `aterm members status` and
  `aterm members join --no-wait` still say ALab lets it in automatically. Away from that LAN
  (another network, a phone hotspot, a cellular link, or none) nothing lets it in by itself,
  so they now say what does: a member's Allow and `aterm members join` on this Mac, or its
  return to the ALab LAN. A Mac that was a member says instead that it proves itself to each
  member it reaches, which lets it back in by itself. Where aterm cannot tell (a Mac that was
  never a member has no ALab LAN to compare with), they say both. `aterm init`'s waiting line
  and the vault sync's peer step say the same now. Being away is never an alert or a request.
- **The vault and the network place agree on where this Mac is.** ALab's automatic admission of
  a new Mac on the home LAN now reads this Mac's network from the same place every other report
  does, rather than from a second record of its own. A member calls a network its home ALab LAN
  no more readily than before: it still takes at least three members that proved their keys to
  it in the last ten minutes, on this very network and behind the router in use, over Ethernet
  or Wi-Fi, and never on a phone hotspot, a cellular link or a network whose path aterm cannot
  read. Each member's answer counts
  only for the network it was heard on, even where this Mac moved between two networks numbered
  alike without aterm telling their routers apart, and only where the heartbeat that heard it ran
  under this Mac's membership log: a test, lab or CI job that reads no vault never counts. Back on
  the home LAN from a phone hotspot, the vault no longer goes on calling the network "expensive"
  for up to 30 seconds: it reads the path again as soon as the route changes. Two things are
  stricter: members heard before this Mac went away and came back no longer count, and neither
  does a network the place only remembers as home. The vault's own `home-lan` file and the second
  copy of the fleet heartbeat's notes it took are gone; the vault's record of where it last looked
  for the ALab vault is now kept against the place's network id, so a record from before this
  change is dropped once and the next look rebuilds it.

### Fixed

- **A refused Commons repair says what refused it, once.** aterm's log named the step that
  refused Commons repair (`custody`, `transport`, …) but not the error the step gave, and warned
  again whenever the refusal came back after the owner's tries had passed through another state,
  as they do when each try is refused at its first poll. The warning now carries the error, as
  in `transport: <the error>`, and appears once for each cause in each aterm process: later
  refusals for the same cause log at debug until the cause changes or the refusal lifts
  (Commons repair runs for 30 s, starts again on changed local state, or is switched off). The
  `control endpoint` step had also dropped its error, and with it the fact that another local
  process was writing the vault: that contention is now a retry, as it is at every other step,
  not a refusal that backed off and warned with no reason.
- **Proton address-list discovery fails closed on unknown address types, `aterm db alab check`
  reports owner disagreements, and `aterm db alab import`, `aterm db table`, and the lab journal
  harden file, save, and spool guards.** An unrecognised or missing Proton address `Type` is treated
  as the account's own login and marks the listing incomplete so it cannot enter Commons,
  `mailbox-obs` readers verify that each row's key prefix matches its `mailbox` cell,
  `aterm db alab check` reports ambiguous observations and owner `mailbox` links that disagree with
  discovery, discovery passes that run out of quota or lack a valid clock log at `info` in release
  builds without spending a record, mailbox discovery keeps a newly born target address in the
  `mailbox-obs` address list even past the 64-address cap and resolves `alab-mailbox-keys.json`
  across an account's own twin addresses, `aterm db alab import` strips Windows path prefixes on
  harness sheets, propagates RNG errors instead of recording empty mailbox keys, and refuses
  duplicate mailbox births even when unlanded local mailbox keys already exist, `alab`
  self-registration does not start its six-hour rest or spend drained-round evidence when a host
  probe transiently returns nothing, generic table checks deduplicate repeated dangling references,
  `aterm db table` reads grid files and baselines without following symlinks or blocking on FIFOs
  and reports `born` and `retired` keys only when `apply` actually wrote them, and the lab journal
  leaves its first-start backfill unmarked until a harness state directory exists, opens spool and
  heard-archive files without following symlinks or leaving loose modes, recovers `sum` counters
  after a torn book, binds `relay` rows to their key bucket, and joins any in-flight journal pass on
  owner step-down.
- **`agh` asset downloads, rate-limit books, GUI need scans and worker pages, publication
  transcripts, and machine key registration harden symlink, resource, slot, UTF-8, and
  duplicate-key edges.** `agh` release and public asset downloads now inspect destination paths
  unfollowed (`symlink_metadata` + `O_NOFOLLOW`), refusing `.agh-part` names, directories, and live
  or dangling symlinks with usage errors before sending any HTTP request or renaming staged files;
  `RateSnapshot` and `RateBook` normalize `x-ratelimit-resource` names to lowercase
  `[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}`, reject malformed names, and cap per-identity book entries at 64 while
  evicting unspent entries before spent `PreRefused` guards; `aterm-gui`'s `agh` need reader
  filters `<key>.json` stems, checks current-UID ownership, and caps at `NEEDS_MAX` after parsing
  so non-need or corrupt files sorting earlier cannot starve real `Family::Agh` entries, while
  Workers pages scope action drains and revision updates to their own window instance and Overview
  aligns `Read Result` availability with `result_to_read`; `atpkg-publish` log trimming aligns kept
  tails on whole-line or UTF-8 codepoint boundaries and opens staging temp files with
  `create_new(true)`; and `aterm-machines` validates `AghFleet` GitHub logins up front, rejects
  zero key ids, reuses newly created key ids across host users sharing a public key, and
  deduplicates `revoke` key ids before `DELETE`.
- **Release status readers, site/tap/export checks, `atpkg` cache clearance, and `aterm ctl` waits
  harden symlink, XML, and framing edge cases.** `ship release status` now falls back to
  `latest-run` when an orphaned `running.child.<pid>` note carries no `logs` pointer, opens status
  and verification logs as non-blocking regular files without following symlinks, rejects relative
  log pointers and malformed `release-stage` titles, and scrubs control characters from text output,
  while `manifest_out` writes `aterm-appcast.toml` atomically without following symlinks,
  `Info.plist` readers and stampers ignore XML comments, handle `<string/>`, decode `&quot;` and
  `&apos;`, and reject unescaped `<`, `changelog` matches exact bracketed section headers,
  `ship harness-bump` detects untracked harness source files and updates an existing `[Unreleased]`
  harness-versions bullet in place, `ship site` and `ship tap` refuse symlinked roots and scan
  non-UTF-8 files, clean-tree checks catch `--skip-worktree` submodule drift, `--linux-worker`
  validates `user@host` destinations and expands literal `~/` paths, and export transforms strip
  pathless withheld `[[bin]]` targets, clear inherited `GIT_*` redirect variables, and refuse
  symlinked export roots; `atpkg`'s `ordinary_clearance` resolves the deepest existing ancestor
  before checking registered-cache overlap and `probe_cache` refuses symlinks and shared-writable
  files; and `aterm ctl await task` preserves caller target order across interleaved groups, waits
  for every group's baseline leg before finishing an `any` wait, and sets `task_news=1` on
  synthesized `state=closed` rows, `await edit` validates fallback URIs up front and stops on
  permanent post-cut server refusals, `--host any` reads `driven-any-hosts.tsv` as a private
  regular file and refuses sids advertised by multiple fleet peers, and `survey` rejects
  sub-nanosecond `--timeout` underflows and non-numeric `wait_gib` figures.
- **Service-image qualification, content-addressed service stores, and paginated GitHub listings
  enforce confinement and base-query invariants before execution.** `Qualification::validate` and
  `service_artifact::authenticate` reject whitespace-only platforms and non-relative executable
  paths while `image_digest` expands intermediate symlinks step-by-step relative to the image root
  so multi-hop chains cannot bounce above the root and re-enter or place a trailing slash on a
  regular file; `service_artifact::Store` checks ancestor paths against symlinks before creating
  directories and refuses symlinks or regular files at content-addressed image slots; and
  `github_pages::all` validates positive page bounds, unslashed API origins, non-empty unique base
  queries without pre-set `page` keys, and canonical positive `/repositories/{id}/{suffix}` aliases
  before issuing requests or following links.
- **`aterm secrets service-repair`, `aterm db alab` harness sheet parsing, `LabView`, `aterm keeper`,
  and `aterm acaffeine` enforce flag-boundary parsing, identity floors, and private non-blocking
  file guards.** `service-repair` normalizes `--json` and `--help`/`-h` only at standalone flag
  boundaries across both local and `--host` routes, rejects trailing options on `protocol`, and
  validates image hashes, nonces, and non-empty path flags before touching live paths;
  `Harness::stated` requires single-component `fleet-accounts.toml` or `ai-accounts-<cli>.toml`
  names for `SheetKind::FleetAccounts`, and `alab_view` reads `aterm.toml` through
  `fsx::read_aterm_config` and reads the `alab/settled` repair witness through
  `private_file::read_private`; `KeeperClient::status` enforces the client's `IdentityPolicy` floor
  and empty `WELCOME` invariant (`offers: 0`) across `aterm keeper status` and `start`, while
  `aterm keeper <verb> --help` exits cleanly and `--sock` rejects empty paths; and `aterm-acaffeine`
  validates single-component launchd labels, opens `acaffeine.trouble`, login plists, and bundle
  markers without following symlinks, strips XML comments in `plist_string` and `plist_strings`,
  rejects oversize files and signed `since` timestamps, scrubs control characters in `why`, and
  stages `.startup-off` (`0600`) inside a validated non-symlink `0700` session directory.
- **Linux VM boot-key, kernel, layer, and guest-agent checks, plus toolchain lease directories,
  harden durability and confinement.** `aterm-vz` flushes `key.img`'s parent directory durably,
  opens kernel and initrd inputs with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, refuses symlinked `root`/`baked`/
  `live`/`seed` directories, rebuilds empty `seed.iso` images, and flushes `seed.iso.made` durably;
  `aterm-vz-agent` rejects empty program names and interior NUL bytes in `Exec`, bounds and verifies
  regular unit files in `refresh_unit`, and rejects `gid 0` in `lane_user`; and `aterm-toolchain`'s
  lease directory narrows permissive owned `<prefix>/leases` directories to `0700` via an
  `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW` descriptor, refuses symlinks and other-user directories, decodes
  non-UTF-8 `who` lines lossily in `probe_file`, and reports non-regular `.lease` entries or
  non-`NotFound` `file_type` errors as `Holders::Unknown` rather than `Holders::Free`.
- **Network-place parsers, diskwalk bounds, theme CLI flags, converge journals, netlink RTT framing,
  Windows `file://` URIs, atomic saves, crash-restore tails, vault deny-list locking, `aterm-winsign`,
  `aterm-observe`, and `aterm-vitals` harden untrusted inputs.** `aterm-netplace` requires mandatory
  top-level keys, rejects duplicate keys and malformed IPv4 subnets in `record::parse`, sanitizes
  and bounds `InternetNote.endpoint`, and counts unterminated trailing lines, uppercase member keys,
  and unreadable or loose `heard` files as unread in `read_counted`; `aterm-diskwalk` rejects short
  `getdents64` `reclen < 19` records and guards 32-bit `Tree::name` offset overflow;
  `aterm theme import` refuses non-UTF-8 `--name=<bytes>` and unknown `-...` flags with exit code 2;
  `FileJournal` in `aterm-converge` narrows directory permissions via `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`,
  verifies current-UID ownership, and refuses non-regular `journal.1.ndjson` targets before
  rotating; `aterm-sysprobe` rejects interrupted, overrun, negative-errno, short, or malformed
  netlink `SOCK_DIAG_BY_FAMILY` dumps; `amacs-protocol` rejects mixed/backslash UNC prefixes on
  Windows `file://` URIs; `amacs-files` preserves target permissions via `fchmod` on the staged temp
  file and verifies current-UID save-lock ownership; `aterm-restore` validates tail headers before
  allocating payloads and uses fallible reservations; `aterm-secrets` and `aterm-agent` hold
  `state.lock` across initial vault deny-list admission; `aterm-winsign` stages atomic replacements
  and verifies `(dev, ino)` on reads; `aterm-observe` enforces exact fixed-frame wire lengths; and
  `aterm-vitals` saturates `Bucket` counts at `u16::MAX` and guards non-finite rates and clock
  backsteps.
- **Machine envelope windows, XML plist prologs, agent inbox walks, control-socket framing, mail
  protocols, D-Bus fallback, Markdown gestures, bus-log retirement, Bonjour polling, recovery
  ledgers, `atpkg` state files, bootstrap verification, shell integration, and `aterm-primer` reads
  harden remaining boundaries.** `aterm-machines` rejects inverted `expires < issued` envelopes and
  restricts `<!DOCTYPE` in `plist` to at most one DTD-subset-free prolog declaration; inbox writes
  require non-root dot-free absolute homes and reject symlinks at every path component; control
  session queries require newline-terminated bounded replies and deduplicate zero-PID graph entries
  by `sid`; `aterm-mail` hardens `Endpoint::parse` IPv6/scheme parsing, control-free SASL inputs,
  RFC 822 comment `Content-Type` parameters, `multipart/mixed` banner handling, IMAP flag and
  Modified UTF-7 folder parsing, and control-free Proton human-verification tokens; `aterm-dbus`
  validates transport/key tokens and requires a private non-symlink `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus` before
  fallback; `aterm-gui-documents` enforces user gestures on local images, non-empty URL authorities,
  and percent-decoded path confinement; `aterm-link` verifies bounded regular `.retiring`, log, and
  sidecar files; `aterm-net` rounds positive sub-millisecond Bonjour browse waits up to `1 ms`;
  `aterm-update` rejects duplicate keys and uncleaned tokens in `recovery_ledger` and flushes trims
  durably; `atpkg` hardens activation notices, `peers::turn_off`, five-file `packages.log` tail
  reads and compound-word redaction, and `quiet` package-name and durable-write checks;
  `aterm-bootstrap-verify` enforces non-blocking regular-file opens and `.`/`..`-free repository
  slugs; `aterm-shell-integration` refuses symlinked script-set roots and GC entries; and
  `aterm-primer` bounds skill and statusline file reads through `AsRead`.
- **A restart no longer doubles Cruise's or Land's next wait.** When a restart cut a turn that
  aterm had already seen running, that cut turn counted as one more short reply, so after the
  restart prompt's own short reply the next prompt waited one step longer on the back-off ladder
  (4 minutes instead of 2 in a measured Cruise run). Whether aterm happened to see the turn
  running decided it. A turn that aterm's own restart, or its own Esc after the Mac slept, ended
  now adds nothing to the short-turn count; real work in it still clears the count.
- **A line the harness typed that the agent never showed is no longer typed twice.** When an
  agent took a line the harness wrote and showed none of it, aterm used to badge it `typed, not
  submitted` and, once the screen moved, could write it a second time behind a copy the agent
  still held. The harness now holds that line, with no badge or question: nothing more is written,
  at a turn end or at a break of the agent's own background work, until the agent shows it (it is
  then sent once), your own typing follows it, or a turn runs after which the agent reads its input
  clear. When Claude Code read the line and still shows none of it a minute later, at rest, the
  harness restarts it in place once and the resumed session gets the line once. Where no restart
  is made (any agent but Claude Code, `[harness] relaunch = false`, a restart the host refused, a
  second loss, or a break of background work), the session waits for one of those, writing
  nothing.
- **A Mac that comes back to ALab with a new vault key keeps its seat and its label when it can
  prove it.** When m110 came back after a reset, the vault let it in at once as a new machine,
  m160, before it could prove it was m110, and seat m110 stayed behind. Now a Mac proves itself
  to a member before it asks anyone, and nothing lets a Mac in for asking alone, so a Mac whose
  seat its proof can move takes that seat back under its own label. A Mac that cannot prove it,
  such as another Mac using that name, gets a new seat under a new label by its own proof on the
  home ALab LAN. `aterm members list` lists each pair of seats that belong to one Mac, and each
  new seat that asked under another standing seat's label. No window shows an entry for a pair
  or asks anyone to act on it: a name does not prove which seat is gone (a second account on a
  Mac asks under that Mac's name too), and removing a seat that shares a node key with another
  would take both out.

- **Lab runs no longer ask the live ALab vault.** `lab commons-lan auto-join` asked the live
  default vault from a new identity on every run, its approver let each one in, and the run
  kept it, so it held `[everyone]`'s files and counted as a member. A Mac the vault lets in
  cannot take itself back out. The lane is gone with the approver path it used. Every other
  `commons-lan` verb refuses a folder of the live vault without
  `--live-alab-vault-keeps-member`, because running a host there keeps the member and adds it
  to the membership log.

- Monitor reports saved host contact history instead of treating cached state as live SSH
  connectivity. Never reached, failed contact, unreadable state and absent observations remain
  distinct, while a refused run does not erase the last successful contact.

- Idle inbox reads avoid fleet-mailbox transactions while the private mailbox is unchanged.
  Cached notifications recheck descriptor ownership, permissions and ACLs, and a ready bus
  reply answers before reading unrelated mailbox storage.

- Rolling-table inventory includes authenticated receive-only recovery data
  and identifies recovery observations. Counts now agree with detailed
  inventory when primary and recovery storage hold different records.
- **Codex browser sign-in journal cleanup, live-upgrade inline environment parsing, and route
  witness proxy checks enforce publication and POSIX environment rules.** `CodeExchange::persist`
  now refuses non-regular `auth.json` or `auth.json.refreshed` paths before spending a one-use
  authorization code and discards stale or corrupt `auth.json.refreshed` files with a directory
  flush once the new login is written; `inline_env_for` strips POSIX backslash-newline line
  continuations outside single quotes and recognizes quoted or escaped variable names before an
  unquoted `=`; and `witness::named` requires both `NO_PROXY` and `no_proxy` to spare a target when
  both are set while `muse_env_var` honors first-entry POSIX `getenv` precedence across duplicate or
  cleared environment entries.
- Release-credential `machine_roster` and `notary_profile` readers now parse single-quoted
  and commented TOML string assignments without copying the signing key, ignore nested table
  keys, and fail closed on empty, relative, non-string, multiline or duplicate assignments
  rather than falling back to another roster path.
- System State's `person-access.json` check now requires a readable hardware UUID,
  opens the record without following symlinks or blocking on special files, rejects
  files readable or writable by other accounts, preserves an older setup's permission
  approval across provisional plan upgrades, and keeps unverified older runs from
  gaining permission authority during an explicit `aterm doctor --apply`.
- **Mailbox component index stamps, route-scoped credential needs, signed `fleet_names`, Kimi
  credential guards, and `agy` wall-read budgets enforce ownership and freshness boundaries.**
  `mailbox_index` now verifies symlink-free parent directories, UID ownership, `0600` mode, and
  `file_stamp` equality before `read_mailbox_component` opens the vault; `mailbox_needs` scopes
  `http_url` suppression per route and refuses stripped unready `routed_for` views while Google
  authenticator challenges use a route's `totp_secret` even without a stored password; `SwarmCensus`
  resolves `fleet_names` by highest key-bound `signed.seq` across `fleet-peers` and
  `fleet-issuer-book` and invalidates cached local renames immediately; `connector::login_file`
  scopes `kimi-code-env-*.json` (and `.refreshed`) to `~/.kimi-code/credentials/`; and failed `agy`
  wall and footer reads now persist failure/wall budgets across cold stores and post-refill readings
  while `muse_usage_forget` honors explicit fact-menu refreshes on live Muse sessions, skipped or
  deferred Muse/agy vendor-revision upgrades survive same-build `agy` quota-wall model rotations,
  retry streaks, and exit relaunches, and `journal::backfilled` verifies a private `0600` regular
  marker file while `mailbox_seen::captured` restores its thread-local capture slot across unwinds.

- Rolling-table inventory now reports whether each window is subscribed or
  excluded and leaves excluded ring storage unopened. Detailed inventory and
  custody inspection also honor whole-catalog exclusions.
- Vault roster authorization keeps its source, membership history and key use under one
  state observation. Transient reads remain retryable, older caller logs cannot undo newer
  removals, and creation and bounded authoring reuse their existing lock ownership.

- **Account claims hold when a Mac's clock is wrong.** Every claims table is a day's table, so a
  Mac whose clock ran a day or more ahead or behind wrote its claims where its peers never read
  them, and read none of theirs: two Macs could use one Claude account. Now each Commons repair
  round carries the sender's clock beside the tables it lists, and every Mac learns how far its
  clock stands from each peer's. Peers from before this release are placed by the day tables
  they offer.
  - When most of the Macs it hears read its clock as off by more than 10 minutes, a Mac writes
    no account claim, keeps to its home accounts whatever its own view shows, and moves any
    other session at its next turn end. A one-line warning says how far off and against how
    many Macs, with the step: turn on automatic date and time in System Settings. It goes away
    once the Macs it hears read the clock within 5 minutes of theirs; a sleep, or a clock
    changed while no peer is heard, keeps it.
  - When its peers disagree among themselves (one liar beside an honest Mac), it claims and
    uses its home accounts only, and the warning names the Macs whose clocks disagree, so a
    person whose clock is right knows which ones to check.
  - A Mac that reads another's clock more than 2½ minutes from its own in a direct round keeps
    that Mac's home accounts for it for a day after the reading, and keeps the claims it can
    see live past their end by as far as that Mac's clock runs behind, so it does not take an
    account the other Mac may be using but cannot show. Naming a Mac's home accounts needs the
    swarm roster and `ai-pool.toml`. A Mac that has never had a round with the one whose clock
    is off, or whose own clock is off the same way, keeps nothing for it. A lone Mac, or one
    with no fresh reading that was not off, works as before.
  - One member can state only its own clock. A single liar puts an honest Mac that hears one
    other honest Mac in the split state (home accounts only), and off only when the liar is the
    only Mac it hears (`docs/DESIGN-fluid-swarm-2026-10-28.md` F22).
- Shared-table inventory remains readable when a ring's local state file is
  damaged or unreadable. Inspection uses the same window as replication
  readers and leaves state repair to the next writer pass.

- `aterm db commons-tables` now includes recovery and lab-journal rolling
  tables alongside account claims, with their retained record counts and
  period lengths.
- **Mailbox component routing, native Google mail selection, and Commons credential holder probes
  enforce route boundaries and private-file ownership.** `mailbox_component` now keeps top-level
  `[[mailboxes]]` entries alongside `[mailbox]`, `[ai.mailbox]`, and `[harness.mailbox]`, accepts
  `username` route aliases and `@` inside IMAP `userinfo`, and skips non-table route entries;
  headless native mail now inspects unstripped `[[mailboxes]]` routes before probing managed Google
  OAuth sessions and records missing second-factor or second-password components against the
  registered mailbox source home; and Commons credential holder sweeps now check private regular
  file metadata (`O_NOFOLLOW` symlink rejection, UID, `0600` mode, and size cap) before offering a
  secret while skipping blank optional `*_totp` files during contribution reads.

- **Mail exits account setup on second-account and reconnect flows, deduplicates mixed-case
  addresses, and restores the active folder watch after stale replies.** Connecting an additional
  account or reconnecting an existing account from `Add account` now returns Mail views from setup
  to the mailbox and resets setup scroll offset, worker and UI account tables reuse slots and
  deduplicate discovered addresses case-insensitively instead of creating duplicate sidebar rows,
  switching accounts clears the prior account's folder and open message immediately, and `MailApp`
  re-arms the background watcher on the active `(account, folder)` once a foreground `Send` or
  error clears `pending` after an ignored stale `Connected`, `Listed`, or `Read` reply.

- **Operational probes, Gmail OAuth callback listeners, and release status pointers enforce
  bounded, blocking, single-token inputs.** `operational` now arms control-socket read/write
  timeouts, rejects line-broken or empty control tokens before `AUTH`, and validates candidate
  hosts and pending join tokens before emitting recovery commands; Gmail OAuth loopback callback
  listeners clear inherited `O_NONBLOCK` on accepted sockets so delayed browser HTTP requests
  honor socket timeouts on macOS/BSD, drain queued callbacks before exiting on stop, accept
  `"client_secret": null`, and require canonical `--timeout` digits in `gmail connect`; and
  `ship release --status` bounds `latest-run` pointer reads to 8 KiB while summing rejected lines
  across verification and release logs.

- **Vault join proof exchanges bind the fleet channel's proved node key across stale fleet codes and
  reject zero clocks, shadowed LAN answers, and malformed join lines.** `vault-join` connections now
  enforce `Desk::begin_proof`'s channel-proven node-key check even when the channel proved a rotated
  fleet code or lacked drive admission, `reads_moved_seats` requires canonical `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`
  versions, `readmit` refuses unset clocks (`now_ms == 0`) and verifies the evaluator's bound node
  standing for every newly admitted key, `home_lan` shadows older home answers when a member has
  newer off-home evidence and fails closed on corrupted evidence files, and `members::wire` rejects
  duplicate keys and stray tokens in join exchange lines.

- **ALab registry verbs, self-registration, and signed service repair enforce retired-row,
  denied-roster, private-file, launchd GUI domain, and RPC job bindings.** `aterm db alab` now
  refuses `prefer` on retired machines or accounts even when named by key while still letting
  `unprefer` end lingering preferences on retired rows, excludes denied swarm-roster members from
  `import`, `adopt`, and self-registration enrollment timestamps, joins the self-registration worker
  thread when the Commons runtime stops, reads `alab-mailbox-keys.json` through `read_private`,
  rejects `--apply --review` and duplicate or non-canonical flags, and checks retired account
  identities and address mailboxes; signed service repair restarts macOS `gui/<uid>` launchd units
  in `Domain::Gui` instead of misrouting plists without `LimitLoadToSessionType` to `user/<uid>`,
  regenerates replacement units across changed bundle identifiers, cleans up failed store
  materialization scratch directories, rejects symlinked executables and `..`-reentering image
  symlinks, validates qualification and custody snapshots end to end, and binds remote `inspect`
  and `recover` replies to the requested service job.

- **Swarm window survey relays read large account rosters whole, `aterm email` preserves post-wait
  observations and healthy IMAP folder selections, and source-signing preflight requires 64-byte
  signatures.** `aterm node serve`'s window survey relay no longer truncates `survey` replies past
  64 lines or accepts duplicate or control-injected relay greeting fields, and
  `SwarmSurveyFacts::from_survey_reply` verifies the body's `account` row count against the
  `instance` header's `accounts=` field. `aterm email session` now runs the post-wait observation
  within its slack deadline when a polling wait or late `IDLE` notification reaches `wait_end` while
  skipping redundant searches after quiet `IDLE` timeouts, `aterm email watch` reuses cached Proton
  observations across unchanged polls and skips unchanged `IDLE` timeouts, and IMAP `EXAMINE` clears
  its untagged `EXISTS` banner notification and restores the active folder on nonexistent-folder
  refusals without dropping the session. Source-signing preflight now verifies full 64-byte Ed25519
  signatures and canonical OpenSSL major versions.

- **`aterm ctl survey` and `aterm ctl --host any spawn` clear expired `week_reset` utilization
  against each member's clock.** Cached survey account rows whose weekly reset timestamp has passed
  by the member's `at_ms` header no longer display or rank stale pre-reset 7-day utilization
  percentages.

- **Native Mail reconnects silently on the first IMAP `IDLE` drop, Google OAuth leases track sleep
  and grant re-registration, Proton clears single-use verification proofs, and IMAP `LIST`, `FETCH`
  and `run_until` handle literals, flags, inline bodies and deadlines cleanly.** Background folder
  watches now attempt one silent immediate reconnect before starting cancellable exponential backoff
  when an IMAP server closes an idle connection. Google OAuth sessions measure token lifetimes on
  the wall clock across system sleep, clear rejected status as soon as a fresh refresh token is
  registered, and treat transient proxy (`407`), early-data (`425`) and `temporarily_unavailable`
  responses as retryable while tolerating `null` optional JSON fields. Proton sessions clear
  human-verification proofs immediately after the retried refresh or request instead of re-sending
  spent headers on later API calls, validate system clock availability before rotating credentials,
  and ignore blank `Retry-After` headers while treating signed non-digit values as unparsed
  deadlines. IMAP folder listing keeps literal alignment across `\Noselect`, `\NonExistent` and
  untagged lines without falsely skipping selectable folders whose names contain `\Noselect`,
  ignores non-numeric `{...}` text in status lines, preserves inline quoted and `NIL` `FETCH` bodies
  without leaking body text into flag or `UID` parsing, rejects leading-zero or signed `UID` inputs
  before issuing wire commands, and bounds `Reader::wait` to `Reader::run_until` deadlines while
  restoring the stream's active deadline on exit.

- Background vault services stop without sending a stray connection to another
  local service that has reused their port.
- Background vault services detect app replacements made during startup and
  restart on the updated copy.
- **`aterm fleet init` and `join` stop looking at a port another fleet holds.** After writing a
  new key, either verb looks at this Mac's `[fleet] listen` place until it proves itself there.
  When another fleet's listener held that port and no aterm or node job here could read the
  key, the verb kept dialling it for three seconds, and each look was a refusal in that
  listener's log. It now stops once a second look still finds nothing here to read the key (an
  aterm here between two versions answers nothing for a moment) and says who holds the port.

- **A test, a lab instance or any other private aterm no longer reaches your fleet port.**
  A private aterm, whether a test, a lab instance or a debug build under a scratch home, could
  dial or take the default fleet port on your Mac, and each dial it hung up was a refusal in your
  own aterm's log. It no longer listens on or dials that port, whatever named the place, and its
  automatic join takes another port.

- Commons table repair prepares outgoing batches within the send's existing
  custody and membership check, reducing duplicate admission work while
  preserving the final policy check before sending.

- Shared-table edits that need several causal merge records now check the
  complete batch before writing. A rejected edit no longer consumes remaining
  table space with merge records when its payload or batch exceeds a limit.

- Fleet discovery tries other addresses when a remembered address now belongs
  to a different Mac. Remote control still retries a temporarily busy endpoint
  when another address answered as the wrong Mac. Rejoining keeps newer
  authenticated contact details learned during the join. Once an enrollment
  proof may have reached a member, a connection failure does not resend it to
  a second member in that attempt.

- macOS close and quit confirmations stay in the terminal window, avoiding the
  native glass-alert teardown crash after System Settings requests Quit & Reopen.
  Cancelling keeps aterm open; confirming preserves the requested restart.

- **A colour-space id is read as one wherever the first colon falls.** `38;2:cs:r:g:b`, and its `48`
  and `58` forms, took the id for red and ran the blue as an SGR code, so `38;2:3:10:20:9` drew
  (3, 10, 20) crossed out; it now draws (10, 20, 9), as xterm and ITU T.416 read it.
  `38;2;r;g;b`, `38:2::r:g:b`, `38:2:cs:r:g:b`, `38:2:r:g:b`, `38;2:r:g:b` and the palette forms draw
  what they drew. These spellings changed:
  - A trailing colon is now an empty element, as a trailing `;` is an empty parameter, in xterm and
    T.416 too: `38:2::255:128:` draws (255, 128, 0), where it drew (0, 255, 128). So `38:2:r:g:b:`
    reads `r` as an id, as they do, `38:5:` is palette 0, `4:` turns the underline off rather than
    on, and `1:` and `0:` are ignored rather than applied.
  - A sub-parameter is never an SGR code. `38;5:n:x` no longer runs `x`; CMY and CMYK after `38;3:`
    and `38;4:` no longer leak; `4:3:9` no longer crosses out. A code that takes no sub-parameters,
    like `1:4`, is ignored whole, as xterm ignores it; aterm set bold and an underline.
  - Some choices differ from xterm: `38;5;9:4` and `38;2;r;g;b:4` no longer underline, where xterm
    runs that `4`; `38;3;c;m;y` and `38;4;c;m;y;k`, in all semicolons, change nothing, where xterm runs
    their values as codes; and xterm ignores `4:`, as it ignores every styled underline `4:n`.
  - A group too short for its colour, `38;2:r:g`, names none, where it took the next parameter for
    blue.
  - Past aterm's limit of 24 parameters, a colour that loses a value it needs names none, where 19
    parameters before `38:2:cs:r:g:b` read the id as red.

  `58` has no xterm or T.416 reading to follow, and takes the same rule as `38` and `48`.

- **A `turn` into a Claude Code that has not read its line no longer reports a submit nobody
  saw.** When a starved Claude Code left a typed line unread for 5 seconds, `aterm ctl turn`
  stopped looking for it in the composer, pressed Enter and took the next thing the screen drew
  for the submit, so it could answer `submitted=1` for a line that was still sitting there. It
  now presses once the composer shows the line, waiting as long as the line stays unread and 5
  seconds past the first look that finds it read, up to a minute after the typing and never past
  `timeout=`, and the line leaving the composer is what verifies it.

- Usage readings retain the matching login's provider identity when several
  accounts are configured. A login change is also recognized when its usage
  percentages stay the same, so the prior account's quota history is not reused.

- Capability-file reads now require an owner-only regular file (0600 or tighter).
  Readable files, symlinks and FIFOs are refused promptly with corrective guidance.
  Running bridges keep their held ring, and `fabric on` leaves refused files intact.
- **Headless `aterm email` normalizes account listings, accepts Proton URLs without a trailing
  slash, and honors explicit non-Gmail IMAP overrides.** `aterm email accounts` now case-normalizes
  and deduplicates discovered and OAuth-registered addresses, Proton webmail URLs without a trailing
  slash (`https://mail.proton.me`) route to native Proton, explicit non-Gmail IMAP URLs take
  precedence over stored Google OAuth sessions, and empty credentials fail fast before dialling.

- **Headless vendor sign-ins treat profile contention from another aterm launch and browser spawn
  failures as automatic recovery, and `proven_pid` rejects signed PID tokens.** `VendorApprover`
  now classifies `ProfileLock` contention from another local aterm sign-in (`Holder::Aterm`),
  lock-file errors, and headless browser spawn or pipe failures as `Approval::NotRun` rather than
  raising a person `NEEDS YOU` alert while still surfacing external browser locks (`SingletonLock`)
  for the person, and `self_claimed::proven_pid` rejects leading `+` signs in `codex-alab@<pid>`
  status tokens.

- **Daylight-saving reset times in a repeated or skipped hour no longer miss the second pass or
  wake an hour early.** `reset_in_zone` now checks both passes when clocks fall back so a reset
  whose first pass has already gone by lands on the upcoming standard-time pass (`1:00 PST`), and
  pushes a clock skipped by a spring-forward jump across the transition (`3:30 PDT`) instead of
  placing it an hour early (`1:30 PST`).

- **Muse Code route inspection respects `--preset` profiles, partial `-c endpoint_transport`
  merges and `--provider` flag precedence.** `launch_endpoint` now treats `--preset` and non-empty
  `-c preset` profiles as unprobeable transport gaps, preserves earlier `proxy`, `ca_bundle`,
  `auth` and `base_url` fields across partial `-c endpoint_transport={…}` overrides, resolves
  `${VAR}` in `endpoint_transport.proxy` and `ca_bundle`, and keeps `--provider` ahead of
  `-c provider` regardless of argument order.

- **Native authentication mail waits preserve fleet mail relay, local ProtonMail Bridge and
  missing-password fallbacks.** Native Gmail and Proton authentication waits no longer intercept
  mailbox polls that lack a non-empty password, configure a local ProtonMail Bridge or loopback
  IMAP server, or rely on the fleet mail relay (`relay_enabled`), and CDP webmail waits record
  target-scoped OTP consumption when a native read succeeds.

- **`aterm fleet census` counts live account walls from `limited` heartbeats and clears expired
  ones.** Swarm census walled-account counts and shortfall supply now match the `"limited"`
  condition word emitted by survey heartbeats, lift walls whose `walled_until` has already passed,
  and ignore unenrolled account rows.

- **Outage probes and route witnesses match IPv6 endpoints and strict `NO_PROXY` rules.**
  Equivalent IPv6 base URLs (`[2001:0db8::1]` and `[2001:db8::1]`) now share one canonical
  route and probe target, `NO_PROXY` matches bracketed and unbracketed IPv6 literals with
  optional ports, and malformed `NO_PROXY` entries (`host:`, `:0`, `:99999`, `*suffix`, `.`)
  no longer bypass a configured proxy.

- **Autopilot's next prompt waits after the short reply to a restart's restore line.** The line
  a restart types when the resumed build warned something was lost is a restart prompt like the
  others, and a short reply to it now gets the same pause before Cruise's next prompt, instead
  of that prompt arriving straight away when the line had been held behind a draft or under Off.

- Commons membership repair verifies the cached vault's signature, configured
  name and signing-key handoffs before trusting another log signer. Unrelated
  or damaged cached envelopes and forged predecessor keys no longer establish
  trusted lineage; valid signing-key rotations remain accepted.
- **Membership stays quick when Sybils flood the log with quorum removals.** Working out which
  quorum removals take effect weighed each pair of them with a membership check of every Mac,
  so keys a removed Mac had let in could slow every membership read, and with it every vault
  entry read, to minutes near the log's size limit by signing removals at many points in the
  log. Each pair now re-checks the Macs its voided records can change, or every Mac where
  working out which would read more than checking them all, and never more Macs than before.
  On these floods the checks now grow with about the square of the log rather than its cube:
  Sybils that each remove the one before (4,416 checks where there were 139,173, at 323
  records); many Sybils repeating one Mac's removal, with that Mac let back in never, once or
  after every removal (7,956 to 9,232 where there were about 200,000, at 356 to 457 records);
  Sybils that each remove one Mac at each of its names (2,966 where there were 72,789, at 358
  records); removals of one Mac at 256 points (11,917 where there were 704,154, at 1,029
  records); and Sybils that each let a removed Mac back in (7,801 where there were 137,700, at
  408 records). Still slow: a flood in which a Mac let back in after its removal signs again,
  such as letting a new Mac in after each return, re-checks about half as many Macs as before
  (134,282 where there were 264,132, at 557 records) and still grows with the cube of the log;
  so can another flood whose removals settle nothing about the Macs they reach.

- **`aterm db alab import` tracks provenance per cell and records source rows for seat vacations.**
  Cells and set elements added by `ai-account-logins.csv` to rows born from `ai-accounts.csv` now
  carry the logins sheet's source instead of the vault sheet's, so re-importing one sheet alone no
  longer retracts the other sheet's mailboxes or services; header-only sheets that vacate seats
  still write their `source` row; Windows sheet paths strip `\` basenames; and swarm-roster entries
  with uppercase hex nodes or inadmissible hostnames are normalized or skipped without aborting the
  import plan.

- **Filtered `aterm db table edit` sessions keep stale rows on reopen, and typed table guards and
  readers close credential and address leak paths.** Editing a collection with `--where` no longer
  drops a stale row (`⚠ mine ‖ theirs`) on reopen when a concurrent peer edit moved that row outside
  the filter. Vault references, foreign-key references, cell primary keys and set elements now
  enforce credential-shape and element-type guards while keeping legitimate vault entry names and
  hex digest keys; unchecked set cells, non-boolean set writes and unknown set columns stay masked
  across `scan`, `get`, `history`, `check` and `export`; and `aterm db table` and `aterm db alab`
  option, verb, collection, filter and row-lookup refusals never echo addresses or credentials.

- Registry seeding reserves the quota for each batch and its causal merge records,
  including pending merges from an interrupted attempt. A batch that cannot fit
  is refused before adding records; another machine with room can still supply the rows.

- Undoing an edit in a shared typed table now honors automatic-write quotas
  when comparing and restoring values. Writes past a machine's quota no longer block an undo,
  supply its restored value, or become undo targets.

- Account sync and local discovery no longer identify a Mac from its current
  login or from email-address tags. A Mac without a local machine identity cannot
  inherit another machine's account roster; existing logins are preserved.

- **Temporary IMAP connection limits, long SMTP OAuth tokens, split MIME headers, Proton CC/BCC
  recipients and Bcc-only drafts behave per RFC.** Native IMAP authentication now distinguishes
  transient server and connection-cap responses (`[UNAVAILABLE]`, `[INUSE]`, `[SERVERBUG]`,
  `[LIMIT]`, `Too many simultaneous connections`, `BAD`, `* BYE`) from credential rejections and
  tolerates untagged server lines before an `AUTHENTICATE XOAUTH2` continuation challenge. Outbound
  SMTP now splits oversized OAuth2 bearer tokens across `AUTH XOAUTH2`'s `334` continuation (keeping
  command lines within 512 bytes), completes `334` OAuth error challenges to surface the real `535`
  code, accepts bare 3-digit `250\r\n` reply lines, and omits an empty `To:` header on Cc-only or
  Bcc-only drafts. MIME and Proton body projection now coalesce multi-byte UTF-8 characters split
  across adjacent RFC 2047 encoded-words (including RFC 2231 `*lang` tags), strip the CRLF belonging
  to multipart boundaries, ignore HTML comments and nested `<head>`/`<style>`/`<script>` blocks,
  include `CCList` and `BCCList` recipients in `Message.to`, and project parameterized `text/html`
  and `multipart/*` Proton bodies to readable text.

- **Leftover git merge-conflict markers in release notes and tracked docs are caught before they
  ship.** Both `verify census` (`conflict-marker`) and `ship release`'s changelog gate now refuse
  leftover `<<<<<<<`, `|||||||`, `=======` and `>>>>>>>` markers in `CHANGELOG.md` and non-Rust
  tracked files.
