- A Mac whose names carry no `m<N>` no longer takes another machine's accounts: account sync never reads the machine id from the vault's shared `~/.aterm/machine.toml`, which named `m22` on every Mac.

- Rapid Mail folder switching keeps only the latest pending selection, avoiding
  accumulated snapshots while a server is slow.

- **A webmail mailbox ends the ask for its password.** Once the lab was asked for a Claude
  account's mailbox password, only a mailbox aterm reads without a browser (a folder, IMAP, HTTP
  or the fleet's mail relay) ended the ask, so `NEEDS YOU: <label>'s mailbox password …` stood
  beside a webmail mailbox that every automatic sign-in of that account went on to use. A
  webmail mailbox with a password the sign-in would use now ends it too, with a headless
  browser here to read it or not; one with no password is still tried beside a headless browser
  and leaves the ask standing.

- **A vault command no longer runs on for minutes after its change has landed.** Once a server
  stored the new version, `aterm secrets approve` (and `set`, `unset`, `revoke` and the other
  admin commands) sent its membership records to the vault's servers one after another, and
  waited up to two minutes on each server that took the connection and never read it, as the
  server of a Mac whose aterm has hung does. With several such Macs on the LAN, an approve whose
  version had applied in under a minute went on for many more. It now sends them to every server
  at once, skipping a server that never answered the new version itself, and every records send
  that follows the landed version shares one two-minute limit, however many servers hang and
  however many rounds of sends follow. Opening the vault before the change, and reading
  the servers' versions before a mirror, now ask every server at once too, so hung servers cost
  one short wait rather than one each. Those reads, the background sync's reads of other
  servers, the look a Mac joining the vault takes at every server it finds and the check made of
  each server before a join request is left there (by the Mac joining, or by a Mac in the vault
  passing one on) take at most two versions longer than 256 KiB whole at a time besides the one
  at the vault's own address, and the sync's reads of membership records from other servers take
  at most two answers longer
  than 256 KiB whole at a time, each checked before another is read in its place, as the vault
  server's own reads do. A host on the LAN that advertises many servers can no longer make a
  command, the sync or a join hold hundreds of megabytes of answers before it checks them, nor,
  by answering slowly, keep a joining Mac from finding the vault at its own address. Removing a Mac
  (`aterm members remove`), undoing a removal and the vault's own background passes send to
  every server at once as well, each send within two minutes.

- **`brew install` and `brew upgrade` by formula alias or former name keep the resolved formula's
  request and pin state, and multi-hop tap redirects are refused.** Installing or previewing a
  formula through an alias or `oldnames` entry (such as `python3`) previously compared the requested
  token against the resolved formula's canonical name, marking the poured keg as an unrequested
  dependency, skipping pinned-dependency checks, and missing already-installed, outdated-linked and
  pinned state in `Cellar`. Alias and former-name requests now bind to the resolved formula across
  dry runs, preflight, receipts, pin checks, upgrades and dependent passes, deduplicate aliased
  edges in the dependency plan, and inspect every hop of a git tap redirect without panicking on
  non-ASCII warning prefixes.

- **After a network split heals, Macs find each other again on their own.** A Mac's background
  check-in with the fleet skipped every member it had failed to reach during the split for as
  long as three others answered, so once the split healed those Macs could stay out of touch
  until someone ran a survey or `aterm fleet peers` on one of them. Each check-in now also tries
  up to three of the members it missed, starting with those other Macs have heard from since,
  and stops at the first that still does not answer, so the two sides usually reach each other
  again within a check-in or two (a few minutes). A member that is really gone costs a check-in
  one short try at most.

- **Automatic vault join checks a member's newly synced removal or roster deny before
  challenging possession.** When an answering fleet member pulled newer vault records during its
  pre-possession check and those records removed that member, rotated its `[everyone]` epoch out,
  or denied the joining Mac in `aterm-swarm-roster`, the member previously checked only `decide`
  again and still issued the possession challenge before refusing, stopping `aterm fleet join`
  from trying the next healthy member or falling back to a plain ask. All pre-possession checks
  now run again on the newly synced records before any challenge is sent.

- **Accents and emoji selectors land on the right cell.** UTF-8 C1 controls no longer
  enter a cell as accents. After a carriage return or a cursor motion, combining marks stay
  within the current row and left margin; they still reach the glyph just printed, across a left
  margin it was printed up to or a window resize that wrapped it to the row above. Emoji
  selectors respect the right margin and a double-width row's edge, and widening a glyph blanks
  an overwritten wide glyph's other half with the current background. The VT oracle compares the
  marks too.

- **A Claude tab resting over a shell it left running is told as that, not as a screen aterm
  does not recognise.** When a turn ended with a shell or a monitor still running, the stall
  record at 90 minutes, and an error in `aterm.log` each time it climbed, said Claude's title had
  read idle "over a screen this build does not recognise". The record now says Claude's own
  background work has run that long under words that stood still, as it already did for agy and
  Muse Code, a warning rather than an error. A background agent or a workflow, whose title runs,
  and a screen that names no work keep their reading. aterm also reads a turn's end through
  Claude Code's idle compaction: the compaction's notice no longer hides the done row above it,
  and its `Task "…" still running in background` row no longer stands in for the agent's last
  words. An automatic update's restart reads that done row too, so background agents it names
  still running hold the restart, as they do with no compaction drawn.
- A Mac aterm with no terminal tab open installs a downloaded update by itself at once,
  instead of waiting for a tab and installing it under you.

- **A worker whose prompt redraws as it starts no longer stalls.** A worker's launch stalled
  for good (`stalled why=shell`) when its shell redrew its first prompt in the instant between
  aterm seeing that prompt and typing the worker's line, as a new tab settling its size or an
  asynchronous prompt (pure, powerlevel10k, starship) can make it, although nothing had been
  typed and the shell still waited at its prompt. The launcher now looks again and types the
  line once the prompt has held still for a quarter of a second, still only once. A person who
  uses the tab first still stalls the task at once, and a prompt that never holds still is
  stalled `why=startup` two minutes after the spawn, like any worker that did not start.

- **A build into an existing target folder cargo made starts again.** Since 0.148.0 refused
  unregistered explicit targets, a worktree whose `--target-dir` or `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` folder
  was made before registration, or by a build that bypassed atpkg, stopped with `explicit build
  target is unmanaged or unsupported` until someone moved the folder away, which also left it
  outside cleanup. On macOS, atpkg now records such a folder where it stands once it proves
  cargo made it as its build directory: cargo's own `CACHEDIR.TAG`, which cargo writes into a
  build directory only as it makes it, beside the `.rustc_info.json` a build leaves, in a
  private folder of yours with no source and no other cache's custody. It does the same for a
  registered target that such a build made again after it was removed. Nothing in the folder
  moves and its builds stay warm, but it becomes a disposable cache like any other atpkg
  registered: once every workspace that built into it is gone and nothing has written it for a
  day (sooner when the disk runs low), atpkg removes the folder whole, anything put in it since
  included. Any other existing folder is still refused.

- The harness now confirms Claude Code's "Claude in Chrome" intro, which left Chrome-using
  workers stalled at startup.

## [0.149.0] - 2026-11-02

### Changed

- **Harness versions since v0.148.0: `alab claude harness 0.8`, `alab agy harness 0.8`, `alab grok harness 0.8`, `alab kimi harness 0.8`, `alab muse harness 0.8`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

### Added

- **Private member discovery for first-run labs.** `ATERM_LAB_MEMBER_SERVICE` selects a
  per-run `_alab-lab-<nonce>._tcp` service for the phrase lab. Invalid values refuse the
  browse instead of falling back to live members.

- Native Proton Mail can use a private headless session when API verification
  cannot complete. It reuses that session for native API reading and sending,
  without opening a browser window. Message reads are cached, and the active
  folder refreshes automatically with backoff after network failures.

- **aterm says where this Mac is on the network.** Every place aterm reports on the network
  now says, in the same words, where this Mac is. The places are `aterm ctl @self status`, `sys
  net` (and `--json`), `aterm fleet peers`, `aterm ctl survey --fleet`, `aterm secrets
  status`, `aterm members requests`, `aterm doctor`, the network band and the menu bar. It
  reads one of five places:
  - on the ALab LAN;
  - on another network (a phone hotspot, another LAN, cellular, a VPN);
  - offline;
  - still checking;
  - on a network, with no ALab LAN to compare it with (a Mac in no fleet, or in a fleet of
    fewer than three).

  Whether the internet answers is said apart, with how that is known: a reply an agent got, an
  API check, or only the path. Beside them come how many members it reaches and since when it
  has been away. A network counts as home only once at least three members have answered on it
  with their keys. So a hotel, a travel router or a phone hotspot never becomes home by
  accident, and a Mac's first run says "checking" rather than "away". Members going quiet at
  home because Local Network is turned off, or because they refuse this Mac's key, never make
  home read as elsewhere. A fleet read that nobody answers from a hotspot now says the Mac is on
  another network, not that a privacy setting is to blame, unless the member it could not reach
  is on the same network. aterm reads no Wi-Fi name and sends nothing to the LAN to work this
  out; the internet is measured by the API check aterm already makes, once after each move
  (`docs/DESIGN-network-place-2026-11-01.md`).

- **Off the ALab LAN, aterm says so plainly and the LAN features wait quietly.** When this Mac
  is on a phone hotspot or another network, aterm puts one quiet fact in its exceptions digest
  (no alert, nothing on the menu bar's "needs you"): it is off the ALab LAN, since when, and
  whether the internet works. A Wi-Fi blip of under two minutes, and being offline at home (a
  router restarting), raise nothing, and the fact goes the moment the Mac is back. Meanwhile
  the features that need the LAN wait instead of dialling Macs they cannot reach:
  - the fleet heartbeat dials only the members this network reaches, and every member once on
    each network and once every half hour;
  - the fleet glance and the vault's subscriber ask again every 30 and 15 minutes, not every
    minute;
  - a package download races only the members on this network.

  Being away blocks nothing: no secret, no join and no vault serving waits on it. Back on the
  ALab LAN, every lane catches up at once, as soon as the network is read rather than half a
  minute later. A Mac coming back alone, after more than ten minutes elsewhere, does not wait
  out the spread that keeps 40 Macs from calling at once after a router reboot, and a router
  reboot still spreads them, even when they fell back to a guest network meanwhile. The API
  check measures the internet again after each move, and keeps measuring while it reads down
  for up to ten minutes; a measured answer stands for 15 minutes. With no window open, the
  vault's own jobs keep track of the network place.

- **ALab's machines, accounts and seats are tables every Mac shares.** The lab's
  providers, Macs, login addresses, mailboxes, accounts and seats (`m2.2` is seat 2 on
  m2) now live in one table in aterm's shared database, which every Mac in the lab holds
  and repairs over the local network: no server, and nothing polls a provider. Edit it as
  a spreadsheet in amacs with `aterm db table edit alab/registry account` (or `machine`,
  `seat`, `address`, `mailbox`): edits to different cells never collide, and a cell two
  people changed shows both values until you pick one. Import your accounts CSV with
  `aterm db alab import`: it reads the vault's `ai-accounts.csv` and your
  `ai-account-logins.csv`, shows what it would write (`--review` opens a private review in amacs, removed once
  you close it, that never shows a credential-shaped cell) and writes only with `--apply`, on a Mac
  that already holds the table (`--apply --first` for the very first import). It reads the sheet the way the harness does (a
  bare Kimi `1` waits for a region, and a note such as `kimi banned` pauses each account
  the harness would skip for it), copies no notes or free text into the shared table (only where in the sheet they are), keeps
  mailbox logins out of it, and never overwrites a cell you edited since the last import:
  it lists those instead. Running it again on the same sheets writes nothing; a service, Mac or mailbox
  the sheet no longer names is withdrawn the same careful way, and an account it no longer
  lists is reported, not deleted. `aterm db
  alab check` reports seat, label and login problems, and `aterm db alab adopt` matches
  the Macs the vault knows to their rows by fleet node.

- **Typed lab tables (groundwork).** aterm's shared database learned a typed table
  format for the lab's machines, accounts, addresses and sign-in routes: each column
  is its own replicated cell, so two Macs editing different columns of one row never
  overwrite each other, and a real conflict stays visible until someone resolves it.
  Values are checked before they are written: a password, token or similar secret is
  refused (only a reference to the vault is accepted), an address goes only in an
  address column, and no refusal ever repeats the value. A row a Mac writes about
  itself counts only at its own key, and a Mac removed from the lab keeps its rows.
  For the lab's coming usage log, the database can also give each Mac a fixed share
  of a log table, so one busy Mac's entries wait for the next table instead of
  crowding out the others. Nothing uses either yet.

- **The lab registry table.** aterm's shared database now defines the lab registry,
  the one table for the owner's providers, AI command-line tools, plans, Mac models,
  machines, login addresses, mailboxes (by name only: their logins stay in the vault),
  phones (last four digits only), accounts, sign-in routes and seats. It always gets
  its own storage slot, so a new Mac can hold it however many other shared tables
  came first. Each build carries the six providers, the AI tools and the plan names
  the tools report, and `aterm db alab import --apply` writes them first, only where
  the table has nothing yet, so it never overwrites the owner's edits; a Mac that writes too many automatic rows has the
  extra ones ignored by every reader. One parser now reads every machine label
  spelling the lab uses (`M109`, `m40-3fa2`, `m27-2`, `m3.2`, `m106-m38`). Nothing
  writes to the registry on its own yet.

- **The lab journal's weekly tables.** aterm's shared database now keeps a weekly
  journal table beside the claims and recovery tables, with its own storage slots: each
  Mac holds last week's, this week's and next week's, and deletes older weeks on its own.
  Each Mac gets a fixed share of a week's table, so many Macs joining mid-week cannot
  overfill it. A Mac with no storage slot left keeps its journal entries on the Mac and
  says `journal: no storage slot` instead of failing. Shared tables declared by others
  now get 38 storage slots instead of 47. Old claims tables from every earlier
  generation (`claims.2` to `claims.6`), not just the first, are now retired, so none of
  them takes a slot on a new Mac. Nothing writes journal entries yet.

- **`aterm db table`: read and edit the lab's typed tables, in amacs's spreadsheet.**
  `aterm db table ls` shows each typed table's records and bytes against its caps, the
  automatic records this Mac has left, ignored records, conflicts and schema versions;
  `schema`, `get`, `scan` (`--where col=val`, `--tsv` or `--json`), `history` (who
  changed what), `check` (conflicts, dangling references, repeated unique values, a Mac
  that has used up its automatic records, and when the table should move to a new one)
  and `revert` work on any of them. Addresses show as `ab…@…` everywhere unless
  `--show-addresses` is given, and no error repeats a value. `aterm db table edit
  alab/registry machine` opens the collection in amacs as a spreadsheet (a private file
  in a scratch folder that is deleted afterwards) and writes what changed when the tab
  closes: only the cells whose text changed, and each only if nobody else changed it
  since it was opened. A cell someone else changed in the meantime is never overwritten:
  the sheet reopens with that cell showing both values, yours first. Columns whose
  header starts with `=` are read-only; a conflicted cell shows `⚠ a ‖ b`, and typing one
  value resolves it; a new row with its pk left empty gets its key from its columns (or
  a random key for a mailbox or phone); a deleted row is retired (a seat's ends), so its
  history stays. A bad value reopens the sheet on that row with nothing written.
  `export … --tsv <file>` and `apply <file>` do the same round trip through a file you
  keep.

### Fixed

- **`aterm ctl tab` numbers match the Cmd-1 through Cmd-9 shortcuts.** Selection, close, move,
  inspection indexes, replies and errors are all one-based: `tab 1` selects the first tab, and
  tab 0 is a usage error.

- **Kimi Code's device login works unattended and enrolls correctly.** Email-less rows can use
  the headless device-code approver, and the harness accepts both `credentials/kimi-code.json`
  and the current `credentials/kimi-code-env-<id>.json` form instead of reporting a successful
  login as having left no login in staging.

- **Claude Code's automatic sign-in uses a proven browser profile before a webmail-only
  mailbox.** Direct mailbox access remains first; where only webmail is configured, an existing
  vendor session can now approve the login instead of unnecessarily taking a fresh sign-in
  through Cloudflare.

- **Old `aterm caffeine` login items are retired after a restart even when no window opens.**
  When `Enable at Startup` had already started the `aCaffeine` mug at login, the background
  converge pass (`sync.awake`) saw the mug running and skipped cleanup, leaving an old
  `com.aterm.aterm.caffeine` login item whose `aterm` was gone or `0.145.0` failing in
  `launchd` every ten seconds until a window opened. `sync.awake` now retires those dead or
  `0.145.0` login items directly without restarting the mug or overriding a `keep-awake` or
  `Enable at Startup` off choice, while leaving any `0.144` or earlier login item alone.

- **A vault server's membership records file holds finished records only.** A record that
  arrived before the record it builds on used to be written to the server's records file
  anyway, and a server that restarted then held it forever, waiting on a record that might
  never come. The file now gets a record only once everything it builds on is there, in that
  order. A post of such early records writes nothing and wakes nobody; a post that finishes
  records adds just those to the end of the file instead of rewriting it, and rewrites it
  whole only when the file is not exactly what the server wrote (cut short by a crash, or left
  by an older build). A file swapped for another of the same size is now noticed, and the
  members waiting on a full store no longer read the file again each time they wake. A post of
  records the server already has costs it no copy, no signature check and no write, and posts
  check their signatures without holding up each other. A restart forgets the early records,
  so each server now names its run in every records answer, and a member that hears a new name
  from a server missing its records sends it the whole store again, at most once an hour per
  server. The stores members send carry finished records only. A server that cannot read its
  records file for a moment answers a post with an error and reads the file again next time,
  instead of writing over records it did not read, and an early record that arrives beside the
  record it builds on is kept even when the server is full.

- **Semicolon-joined go-ahead parks (`Ready to commit and push; waiting on your sign-off.`)
  receive the standing go-ahead.** When an agent split pending reversible work and its consent
  wait across a semicolon in the same paragraph, sentence splitting hid the work from the wait
  clause. Pending own reversible work before `;` now pairs with the wait after `;` (setting
  `Park::lands` when the prior clause names a commit, push, merge, rebase or land), while
  completed past-work summaries, stage/phase asks and separate sentences stay plain.

- **Muse Code sign-in walls and custom TLS endpoint settings are classified accurately.**
  Muse Code's expired saved-login notice (`your saved login is no longer valid`), token-refresh
  and missing-login notices wrapped under `model failed:` or `model failed after N attempt(s):`
  now read as authentication walls with Muse Code's own login remedy rather than plain replies or
  retryable server errors, singular `model failed after 1 attempt:` notices read as walls, and
  launches configuring `-c endpoint_transport.auth` mTLS or `TBH_CA_CERTIFICATE` /
  `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `SSL_CERT_DIR` on `https://` targets stay off the direct endpoint probe.

- **Shallow submodules fetched more than one commit deep no longer hold a landing.** When a
  submodule was fetched with `git submodule update --depth N` (`N > 1`) at a commit no
  remote-tracking branch reached, Autopilot Land's repository check saw the commits above the
  shallow boundary as unpushed work in that submodule. Commits that `FETCH_HEAD` records as
  fetched from one of the submodule's configured remotes, and their ancestors, now count as on a
  remote; local commits made on top of that checkout, or fetched from an unconfigured local
  folder, still hold the landing.

- **Accents and emoji selectors land on the right cell.** UTF-8 C1 controls no longer
  enter a cell as accents. Combining marks stay within the current row and left margin,
  selectors respect the right margin, and widening a glyph blanks an overwritten wide
  glyph's other half with the current background. The VT oracle compares the marks too.

- **Standing go-ahead answers keep bot-branch merges for you and no longer stall on background
  notices or bare file names.** Autopilot's standing go-ahead now leaves a merge of a
  bot-prefixed branch (`renovate/…`, `dependabot/…`, `snyk-fix-…`) waiting for your own decision
  even when the reply names no bot or pull request. Earlier in the same turn, Claude Code's own
  background-task, monitor, hook and tool-group rows (`⏺ Background command "Build and tag the
  release" completed`), and bare source or config file names such as `release.rs` or
  `deploy.toml`, no longer read as an outward plan of the agent's that withholds the go-ahead.

- **Account usage warnings and usage-credits resets across a daylight change keep the reset's
  offset.** Claude Code's footer usage warnings (`You've used 85% of your weekly limit · resets …`)
  and usage-credits start notices (`Your 5-hour limit resets …`) recorded for an account used the
  Mac's UTC offset when the reply was answered rather than the offset at the reset's own instant,
  placing an unzoned reset across a spring-forward or autumn-fallback change an hour off. Both now
  resolve the local offset at the reset's instant.

- **agy's footer account, model and API route follow its real provider, gateway and `--settings`
  rules.** Having `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in the environment without
  `"modelProvider": "gemini"` no longer hides a Google sign-in account and its weekly quota in the
  footer, while selecting a model provider, `AGY_LLM_GATEWAY_URL`, Vertex AI or a newer
  non-consumer auth record in `cli.log` clears stale OAuth account state rather than falling back
  to an earlier log head or previous reading. Relative `--settings` files are now resolved against
  the session's working directory for both footer account display and outage witness routing,
  `AGY_LLM_GATEWAY_URL` is treated as its own gateway route ahead of `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`, and
  a right-column footer model read cut short mid-repaint no longer reads as a model switch at a
  limit wall.

- **An Autopilot or recovery edge that reads a torn frame decides at the next look.** When an
  Autopilot switch, a reach recovery, a witness or an account update re-decided a resting or
  waiting point and its screen read caught a one-read frame of another point, the consumed edge
  previously waited on the point's distant timer or the screen's next move; it now re-decides as
  soon as the next look finds the point back on screen.

- **`aterm init` now installs the aterm primer and skills for your coding agents.** On a Mac
  set up from a terminal, `aterm agents status` showed the primer absent after `aterm init`
  until `aterm agents install` ran, because only an aterm window laid it. Each `aterm init`
  run from the installed aterm.app now brings every detected agent (Claude Code, Codex, …) up
  to date, as the window does, unless `agents_auto_prime = false` is set. A file it cannot
  write stops none of the others and is named in the result. The primer also says that
  `aterm agh` reads GitHub with the vault's credentials and needs neither git nor gh, and when
  a plain `sudo` raises aterm's password sheet and when it is refused (`aterm help sudo`).

- **A Mac in no fleet no longer reads "100.0% joined".** `aterm fleet census` printed
  `0 heard 7d, 100.0% joined` when it had heard from nobody; it now says `none heard`. Its
  JSON is unchanged.

- **A join refused at this Mac's own name that another Mac answers for says what works.** When
  `aterm fleet join` used this Mac's `.local` name and that name led to a different Mac, the
  advice to pick another `--port` could not help, because the fleet would still reach the
  other Mac. The advice now names `--host` with this Mac's LAN address. Two members on one Mac
  still get the `--port` advice.

- **A vault edit made during a split no longer reverts when the Macs meet again.** When a Mac
  was removed on one side of a split, the Macs on the other side still counted it, and an edit,
  a new entry or a deletion made there could be sealed with the key that Mac had just made.
  Once the two sides met, that key stopped counting and nothing opened it, so on every Mac the
  edit went back, the new entry vanished and the deleted entry came back. Members that hold
  that key now still read those writes after the heal, also when the Macs had earlier undone
  another Mac's removals by a quorum. The removed Mac's own writes stay out, and no Mac seals
  anything new with its key or hands that key to a Mac it lets in. A Mac that cannot open that
  key leaves those entries alone until a Mac that holds the key seals them again under a new
  key, which one Mac now does on its own once the Macs meet, and it never writes its older
  values over them when it removes a Mac or saves, also after they are sealed again. Until then
  `aterm secrets status` on a Mac without the key says how many writes wait for one that has
  it; afterwards, on the Mac that sealed them again, it names the entries the removed Mac could
  read while it was out, so you can change them where they came from. This holds once every Mac
  of the fleet runs this version: a Mac on 0.147 or earlier can still put its older values back
  over those writes when the Macs meet.

- **Recording a pane that floods output costs less.** Rewind's recorder used to wake for every
  16 KiB a busy pane printed, and its rekey replays stored and compressed scrollback they then
  threw away. The recorder now takes what queued while it was busy as one batch, and a rekey
  replay drops those rows without storing them: its replays of a 64 MiB flood take 118 ms where
  they took 197 ms. A recorded flood parsed at 0.92 to 0.95 of an unrecorded one's speed on the
  Mac measured, and now parses at about 1.0. Each recorded event keeps its own Rewind state, as
  before.

- **A Mac under load keeps answering its fleet.** The background job that answers other Macs ran at
  the lowest priority macOS has, and with half its connection slots, so on a busy Mac they could
  connect and then wait out the 3 seconds with no answer. It now runs at a normal background
  priority with every slot. A command that drives another Mac tries again if that Mac was only
  busy, stopping in time to leave room for its answer, and `aterm fleet peers` names this job as
  a likely cause of a stall, rather than only blaming another program.

- **A new Mac's request reaches ALab's members.** A new Mac first tries to prove itself to each
  member, and in current source the first member with a window to refuse it ended the round, so
  its plain request never went out and nothing forwarded it for automatic admission. A member now
  gives any refusal that proof could not change before the Mac proves anything, such as for a Mac
  it knows nothing of or one a person must decide on, and the request follows at once.

- **A copy or a restore of the fabric's state folder no longer passes as already on disk.** Since
  0.146 a bridge that follows another in the same boot has skipped rewriting the run record and the
  mirror floor when a link beside each file showed its full flush had finished. `tar`, `ditto` and
  `rsync -aH` copy that link too, and `cp -R` and `cp -a` write into the linked file and leave the
  link standing, so a state folder copied or restored in the same boot looked flushed when it was
  not, and a power cut soon after could lose the record or the floor. The mark is now an empty file
  whose name says which file of which folder the flush covered and when that file last changed, a
  time any later write moves and no copying tool sets back, so a copy or a restore by any of these
  tools writes both again. The first handoff after this update writes them once more, about
  17 ms on the Mac measured.

- **A Mac let back in after a split keeps the label it was approved under.** When the other
  half of the fleet had changed the fleet's roster settings during the split, a Mac an admin let
  back in came back under a new `m<N>` label. It now keeps its own label and name whenever no
  other Mac took that label and nobody denied it.

- **An approval also survives when a second admin on the same side published after it.** When
  two admins were on the side of a split with fewer changes and the second one published
  anything after the first one let a new Mac in, the first admin's Mac took that newer version as
  proof the approval had been kept and stopped watching it; when the halves met, the approval was
  dropped for good. The approving admin's Mac now keeps watching until the new Mac has its own
  place in the membership log, or someone removed or denied it.

- **An admin's approval no longer disappears when two halves of the fleet meet again.** If
  the fleet split (a network outage, or a laptop away from home) and an admin let a new Mac in
  on one side while the other side published more changes, every vault server kept the side
  with more changes once the two met and dropped the approval, so the new Mac lost its access
  and nothing asked for it again. The approving admin's Mac now keeps a private copy of the
  last vault version it published (`vault.published`, readable only by you), notices when the
  version the servers kept no longer lists a Mac it let in, and publishes a version that lets
  that Mac back in with its name, its roster entry, its approval and its access, and nothing
  else from the older copy, so secrets and entries the other side deleted stay deleted. It
  does not let back in a Mac that an admin on aterm 0.145 or later removed or denied since (a
  Mac an older aterm let go, or one retired by its key alone, can come back), and keeps
  watching until the Mac can read the newest secrets every Mac shares, even if another admin
  re-keyed those at the same time; secrets shared only with some Macs are not watched. A carry
  that cannot finish is not tried again until something changes.

- **A sign-in left open over a usage limit no longer keeps the agent from resuming.** When
  Claude Code's `/login` was opened in a supervised tab and left at its method picker, its
  browser sign-in or its error, it covered the prompt, so after the limit reset neither aterm
  nor Claude Code itself could continue the work: one tab sat 33 hours past its weekly reset.
  With Autopilot on, aterm now waits for the reset (or, where your accounts have another one
  ready, moves at once) and, once the sign-in has also gone 30 minutes without a key of yours,
  closes it with its own Esc; the resume follows. If three Escs leave it open, aterm stops
  pressing and tells you once, at once, to close it. That holds even when aterm starts watching
  the tab more than a day after the reset, or with no earlier record of the limit. A usage footer
  that still shows an old reset time beside `Continuing shortly` now counts as a reset that has
  passed, so the resume is no longer put off to the next midnight.

- **A Mac that cannot read its deny list no longer lets every Mac in.** After an upgrade, a
  vault lock an older aterm had left readable by other users (mode 644) was refused, so the
  list of removed Macs could not be read until the next vault sync, and a Mac that had not
  read it yet treated it as empty: a removed Mac that still held the fleet's secret could
  join, read the book or drive. Reading the deny list or the roster now tightens such a lock
  to 600 itself when it belongs to you (a lock owned by another account, a symlink or a
  hard-linked one, or one in a folder other users can write, is still refused). And until a
  Mac has read its deny list once, it turns away every Mac that dials it as busy, so older
  Macs try again later too rather than take it for a Mac of another fleet, and dials, joins,
  drives and shares with no one; its log says why it has no list (the vault's error, or a sync
  that has not finished) and says again when it has one. Once it has read the list, it keeps
  using the last one it read while a vault sync is under way or a read fails. Commons
  replication keeps the last roster it read through a vault sync and checks the deny list even
  when it cannot read the roster.

- **A new tab no longer starts its shell on a terminal macOS has just taken away.** On a very
  busy Mac, macOS could remove a new tab's terminal device just as the tab opened, and the shell
  in it started with no terminal it could use: it printed nothing and took no typing. aterm now
  checks the terminal before it starts the shell and again the moment the shell takes it, and
  when the terminal is gone, opens a fresh one and starts the shell there. If the fresh one is
  gone too, aterm says it could not open the tab, and why, instead of opening a tab with a dead
  shell. If macOS takes the terminal away after the shell has started, the shell still ends.

- **Explicit build-target cleanup reaches `targo clean`.** The ownership guard no longer
  rejects cleanup of an unregistered target. Cleanup and built-in queries leave cache
  registration alone; explicit targets used to produce build output still require managed
  ownership. Newly registered caches receive the standard cache tag before publication, so
  the build tool can clean them normally. Interrupted setup flushes existing parent folders
  again before publishing output.

- **A stuck credit-claim tab now goes away by itself.** A worker that aterm starts to claim a
  free Claude credit could sit on a permission box or a sign-in screen forever, and its 30-minute
  limit often never ran. The limit now runs on a timer, not counting time the Mac sleeps, and
  starts again when you type in the tab or aterm restarts. When it passes, the worker is asked to
  end, and made to if it is still running two minutes after that request reached it; its tab
  closes about 30 minutes later, once its last reply has had time to be read. A tab on screen in
  the aterm window you are using is left alone, and so are a tab that is held or driven, any
  program running there other than Claude Code, and anything you run in front in the tab once its
  worker ended, Claude Code included, also after aterm updates, restarts or recovers from a crash;
  the tab then stays open 30 minutes after that ends, for its output to be read. A job you leave
  in the background there ends with the tab, as it does when you close a tab yourself. A Claude
  Code you start yourself in the worker's folder, in a tab opened from its tab, is not taken for
  the worker after aterm restarts. In a window's last tab the worker still ends, but the tab stays
  open.

- **A server that cannot take a Mac's own records no longer sends it records it cannot take
  every third pass.** Such a server says on every pass that it lacks records the Mac named, and
  the Mac took that as the server having lost its note, so it forgot the note and downloaded
  everything it could not take again. It now forgets the note at most once an hour per server.

- **In a large fleet, a Mac remembers what each nearby server sent that it could not take.**
  A Mac or vault server kept that note for only 68 servers and dropped the oldest note first,
  so in a fleet larger than that (ALab has about 86 Macs) each note was gone before that server
  was asked again, and its records came again on every visit. It now keeps notes for up to 256
  servers, drops the one used longest ago, and never drops the one for the vault's own server.

- **A member that could not read every membership record no longer lets a Mac back in by
  proof.** When a vault server or a nearby Mac held a removal that this Mac's aterm could not
  read (it came after a record only a newer aterm writes), this Mac still counted its download of
  the newest records as complete, and could let the removed Mac back in when it proved its old
  key. A download that leaves records behind now counts as incomplete, so this Mac declines and
  another member decides.

- **A Mac that cannot take some membership records stops downloading them again on every
  pass.** When a vault server held membership records this Mac could not take (a kind only a
  newer aterm writes, or past the 4,096 records a Mac keeps), every records pass pulled all of
  them again, up to 64 MiB from the vault server and from each of up to 16 nearby servers, and
  dropped them; vault servers did the same to each other on every tend pass. Each now
  remembers, for an hour of awake time or until it restarts, what a server sent that it could
  not take, and asks that server only for what is new past it. A record only a newer aterm
  reads also no longer keeps the records beside it from this Mac: it takes every record it can
  read from the same download.

- **A device that copies a member Mac's greeting no longer gets in the way of a join.** Any
  device on the network could repeat what a member Mac says to a new Mac asking to join, so
  the new Mac saw that member twice and asked you to pick one by its address. Now each
  member signs its answer to every new Mac's ask, and the new Mac sets aside an unsigned
  answer from a device that claims to be a member that signs, whatever that device answers,
  and counts one member reached over both Wi-Fi and Ethernet once. When an older member Mac
  that does not sign yet and a newer one both show a phrase, it still asks you which one's
  phrase you typed.

- **A join whose secrets never reached the new Mac can be allowed again at once.** If the
  connection dropped just after the member Mac sent the new Mac its secrets, the member
  counted the Mac as let in and its entry lost the Allow button until the new Mac asked
  again. Now the new Mac confirms that it received what it was sent and checked that it can
  use it, before it writes anything, and the member closes the entry only then; otherwise
  the entry keeps its Allow button, and the member's log says the secrets were sent but not
  acknowledged. That includes a new Mac that turns the secrets down, for example because it
  joined another vault since it asked. Macs from before this change join as before.

- **A member Mac busy syncing no longer spends the join phrase.** When the new Mac sent
  the phrase while the member Mac that showed it was in the middle of a vault sync, the
  member used up the phrase and told you to press Allow again for a new one. Now the member
  answers "busy" before it touches the phrase, the new Mac says once that the member is busy
  and keeps trying by itself every second or two while the phrase lasts, and it gets in as
  soon as the sync ends, with the phrase you typed once. If the sync outlasts the phrase, the
  new Mac stops when the phrase runs out and tells you to press Allow again.

- **Autopilot's account check no longer leaves `/usage` standing in an agent's prompt.** When an
  agent was slow to show the `/usage` that aterm types to read the account's usage (the tab then
  says `/usage was typed and not sent`), aterm gave up its check before the text appeared, and the
  `/usage` that showed later stood unsent, read as something a person had typed: Autopilot typed
  nothing more into that tab until someone sent or cleared it. aterm now treats that `/usage` as
  its own: it sends it once it shows, however the agent's screen moved before then, closes the
  panel it opens, and goes on. A line Cruise or a note leaves unsent no longer reads as a person
  typing either. A person's own typing still holds Autopilot, and a `/usage` aterm finds standing
  after a restart is treated as a person's draft: Autopilot waits out the person's two minutes
  before it sends it, then closes its panel.

- (developer tool) **`lab turn` types only into a composer that stands ready.** `lab claude`
  returns once Claude Code draws anything, its banner or a folder-trust dialog, and `lab turn`
  sent its text at once, before any composer existed: on Claude Code 2.1.312 the first turn after
  `lab claude` failed ("does not stand in the composer"), and a second one worked. `lab turn` and
  the prompts `lab forever` types into a tab now share one routine. It waits for the agent's
  empty composer (a hang detector: a minute in which the screen did not change), fails at once
  without typing on a draft or an editor no one typed, sends the text only then, and presses Enter
  once the text stands in the composer. A placeholder no one typed is an empty composer: one
  drawn dim (Codex's hint, Claude Code's grey suggestion) or in the agent's hint colour (Muse
  Code's prompt hint, 676c74, no dim), read by the harness's own rule, and `lab forever`'s start
  gate, mid-chain prompt gate and notice gate read it so too. A composer whose cell gives no
  reply after Enter is no turn taken. The wait for the text to stand is now a one-minute hang
  detector in `lab turn` too, where it gave up after 5 s.

- **A restarted agent starts working again.** A restart of a Claude Code, agy or Muse Code under
  Autopilot `cruise` or `land` now ends with one restart prompt per relaunch, typed at the
  relaunched agent's first rest: it says the agent was restarted, that work it ran inside its
  own process (subagents, workflows, background shells) ended with it, and to read its handoff
  and carry on; codex-alab carries itself on. Autopilot's own turn-end prompts go on after it,
  as they do after any turn, so under `cruise` a short reply to it is followed by the usual
  continue two minutes later. An agent that restarted itself from a running tool call used to
  sit waiting for a person: Claude Code restores the cut call as `Interrupted · What should
  Claude do instead?`, and the harness read that as a question and as a person's Esc. The prompt also waits
  behind a draft in the composer where it used to give up, however long the draft stands, comes
  under `land` as under `cruise`, comes ahead of Autopilot's own prompts, and is never typed under
  `off`, after a person's own message (a key or a click is not one), or into work Land finished
  or the agent defended as landed. The relaunch is seen at rest as soon as it is, where a restored
  row cost it 15 seconds.

- **A dialog aterm cannot read now tells you, and leaves Autopilot free once it is gone.** When an
  agent showed a dialog of no kind aterm reads, such as Claude Code's
  `--dangerously-skip-permissions` warning, the harness was refused its own attention entry:
  the menu bar and window border said nothing while the dialog waited, and the refused take-down
  was tried again every 2 seconds for the rest of the session. While that went on, a turn too short
  for aterm to see the agent working was never judged, so Autopilot typed nothing in that
  session. The entry now goes up while the dialog stands and comes down when it leaves, an entry
  an earlier loop left comes down the same way, and a take-down that cannot be delivered stays
  owed without holding back the next turn's end.

- **A restart prompt that was held no longer brings the next prompt straight after it.** The
  short-turn back-off after a restart prompt now runs from the agent's reply to it. It ran from
  the turn before the prompt, so a draft or Autopilot `off` that held the prompt used the back-off
  up, and Autopilot's own prompt followed about 30 seconds later. A prompt held by your keys is now
  looked at every minute until they stop: past a third look it waited five minutes more, with
  Autopilot's own prompts held behind it.

- **An accounts sync whose list trades labels among this Mac's rows publishes.** When the
  account list gave the default login's account a label another row on this Mac held (a sheet
  that swapped `m3` and `m3-2`), every `aterm harness accounts sync` refused with "the previous
  roster already uses that label", so `aterm init`'s `base.ai.accounts` stayed open. The sync
  now moves each account's record, renewal binding and sessions to the label the list gives it,
  along any swap or cycle of labels, and gives each row a login directory that holds nothing or
  its own account's login, as the profile in it says. An account that leaves the list and
  comes back finds its own login again when that login is in the directory named for the label
  it comes back under; one whose login a swap left under another label's name is given a new
  directory and signs in again. An account listed under another address for the same
  provider identity keeps its row's login, and a directory the sync cannot read stops it with
  a message naming the directory to make readable. A relabel outside the default login's still
  drops the account's record and can leave a renewal's login under its old label
  (ATERM-KI-1028-6).

- **A worker whose shell is slow to its first prompt starts all the same.** A worker's launch
  gave up for good if its shell had drawn no prompt 20 seconds after the launcher began to
  wait, as a long startup file or a heavily loaded Mac can make it: the task said
  `stalled why=shell`, and the prompt that came later went unused. The launcher now waits for
  the prompt with no clock of its own. A shell that ends, or a person who uses the tab first,
  still stalls the task at once, and a shell with no prompt two minutes after the spawn stalls
  it `why=startup` like any worker that did not start, with the tab's foreground program
  named. A launch no longer writes over a task a lead or a deadline has already marked.

## [0.148.0] - 2026-11-02

### Added

- **Linux names commands too short for a sample.** On Linux 6.6 and later, aterm now
  listens to the kernel's process connector (one listener for the whole app, on its own
  thread, needing no root or capability) beside the foreground sampler, so a command that
  runs for a millisecond and prints nothing, such as `/usr/bin/true`, can read its program in
  `status detail=` and the session log instead of `-`. The listener counts only after the
  kernel acks its subscription and it hears a test program of its own start; inside a
  container, Flatpak or another user namespace, on an older kernel, or wherever that fails,
  it stays off and the sampler alone names commands, as before. A program that exits before
  aterm reads it can still be missed. `aterm ctl status` says which source a session uses
  (`exec_watch=kqueue`, `sampler` or `connector`) and, for the connector, why it is off
  (`exec_watch_why=`, such as `no-ack` in another user namespace).

- Developer setup installs the secret scanner required to publish a release. Release
  commands find the managed scanner without a shell PATH change.

- **amacs opens directories.** `amacs DIR` shows a read-only directory listing,
  including hidden files. Press Enter or `f` to open an entry, `n`/`p` to move,
  `^` to visit its parent, `g` to refresh, and `q` to close. Refresh keeps the
  selected entry when it still exists.

- **The survey says where each agent works.** `aterm ctl survey` now gives each agent
  session a `work:` line: its branch, how many files the branch changes, how many commits
  it is behind its repository's main branch, and how old that reading is
  (`feat/x · 12 files · 3 behind origin/main · 40s ago`). `--json` and `--sid` carry the
  repository, the worktree, the base commit and the names of the changed files (up to 64,
  with the full count). aterm reads it with git when a worker first shows up and at its
  turn ends, at most once every 20 seconds per session, offline and under the same rules
  as its other repository checks: no fetch, no hooks, no diff drivers, no file contents,
  nothing inside a folder macOS guards, and no new git at all while macOS's
  program check is full or stuck (the last reading stands and its age grows). A session
  that lands shows none until its task opens again. Fleet peers see it only with a
  content grant. `lab git-starts --read` measures what one such reading costs.

- **`aterm ctl status` says whether this instance keeps a session log journal.** The journal
  that lets `log` and `brief` answer for a closed session after a restart had no status key, and
  `ctl help log` said a headless instance never keeps one, though a lab instance with the restore
  seam does. `status` now prints `log_journal=` (`on`, `armed`, `paused`, `stopped`, `handed` or
  `off`) and `log_journal_why=` (why it is off, such as `disabled`, `no-restore` or `no-desk`, or
  what paused or stopped it, such as `full`), beside `log_seq=`; `journal=` is still the crash
  journal's.

- **`aterm harness versions` shows what each harness is running.** It lists the harnesses
  built into aterm, each installed harness package (codex-alab, grok-alab and the other `-alab`
  harnesses) with the version aterm recorded when it installed that build, or the checkout a
  dev link points at, and each live harness session with its own version and its agent's. A
  codex-alab session, which does not announce a version, shows the version of the build its
  process runs. `--json` prints the same rows as one array. `aterm ctl ls` and `status` carry
  the live claim's two versions as `supervisor_version=` and `supervisor_vendor=`, and
  Settings ▸ Harness ▸ Harness updates lists the installed harness packages.

- **`aterm ctl pointer move item=<n>` aims at a palette or Overview row.** Over an
  open palette or Overview it moves the pointer to the centre of the card's row for
  item `<n>` (the palette's filtered row as `menu` counts `selected=`, the Overview's
  item as `controls overview` counts it) in the frame the next capture shows, where a
  person's pointer selects that row, and says `ERR item <n> is not a row the card
  shows` when the row is scrolled off.

- **The footer says whether your accounts last the week.** Where you keep a roster
  of accounts, the Claude Code footer's account now reads as one unit: who you
  are, then this week as a small bar (`━` used, `╍` the use expected by the reset
  at today's pace, `─` left), its reset, the 5-hour window (a figure read now
  only), and the outlook: `continuous 7d` when your rotation
  covers the week, `⧗ stop ~Wed 22:30–Thu 09:00` when it runs out before a
  reset, or `then pool1 ?` when it leans on an account aterm has never read. The
  outlook replays aterm's own rotation over what it has already seen, with
  every other account filled in (an account never read says `never read`,
  never a number), and refuses to project from a figure that is too thin, too
  old or cut by a reset. It never alerts, makes a sound or moves anything: the
  words change in place. Narrow panes drop the 5-hour part, shorten the words,
  then drop the bar, before the account's name is cut; the narrowest keep a
  stop beside the name, and never lose the name to the outlook. Times are said
  on your clock as it will read then, past a daylight-saving change. A pane
  whose account aterm cannot confirm shows no outlook. The Accounts card shows
  each account's bar and the chain over the week from the outlook the footer
  already holds. `aterm harness accounts` prints the same outlook, replayed
  under the rotation the window runs (`rotation off` with the harness off),
  and `--json` adds it as `outlook`, with a `fresh` and `projection` beside
  each figure.
- **`aterm ctl @self sys left` shows what a closed tab or a dead verify run left
  running, and what macOS's program check is holding.** Each row says why aterm
  believes the program is this user's own (`proof=`: its environment named the tab's
  session and it was born while the tab lived, or it was born into a dead run's stage),
  and how far that proof reaches (`tier=offer`, `auto` for what the next verify run will
  end itself, `name` or `never`), with the token `aterm ctl end` takes. A program
  holding a listening socket, or leading its own group with no terminal outside every
  run's folders (a daemon such as `trustd`), is only named, and so is anything the program
  check holds. `scope=aterm` lists every tab's rows and needs the owner's access. It is
  read-only: nothing is ended from it.
- **`aterm ctl end <token>…` ends the leftover processes you name.** Each token is a `sys
  left` row's `end=`; there is no `all`, no wildcard, and a bare pid is refused. Just before
  each signal aterm reads the process again and judges it as the view did, and refuses it if
  it is another process by now (`refused <token> why=stale`) or nothing proves it a leftover
  any more (`why=not-proven`); otherwise it sends `SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` after 10 s. The reply says what each token
  came to: `OK 1 end term=1 gone=1 killed=0 refused=0`. The owner can end any row; an agent
  in a tab ends only its own session's rows, and a request naming any other is refused whole
  before anything is signalled. If you press Ctrl-C, no token after the one being ended is
  ended. The message log records each process ended, each tab close that left processes
  running that `end` can take, once ("Tab 2 closed and left 3 processes: ugrep ×2, tail"), and
  each process a verify run ended on its own, with the proof each was ended on.
- **The message log says when aterm's Developer Tools grant did not take.** Once aterm has had
  macOS ask about it again after you switched it on, macOS should check none of the programs
  aterm starts. If the program check still holds one aterm started after that (outside a tab
  an update handed over), the message log records it once: "macOS's program check is holding 2
  programs aterm started after its Developer Tools grant took", "so macOS still checks the
  programs aterm starts: look at aterm's row in the Developer Tools list". Programs started
  before the grant are not counted: they may still wait.
- **`aterm ctl text @s-…` reads that session.** `aterm ctl` takes a read's session
  after its verb as well as before it: `aterm ctl status @s-ab12`, `aterm ctl text
  s-ab12 tail=5` (the sid as `aterm ctl ls` prints it) and `aterm ctl search @s-ab12
  needle` are `@s-ab12 status`, `@s-ab12 text tail=5` and `@s-ab12 search needle`,
  over `--host` too, and `read` is `text` beside a selector (`aterm ctl read
  @s-ab12`, `aterm ctl @s-ab12 read`). Each was an error, but for a bare
  `status @s-ab12`. A wait (`await`, `ready`, `wait`), `subscribe`, a write such as
  `send`, and `hold s-ab12 on` keep their words where they are, and so does a word
  that names no session: `aterm ctl search s-ab12` still searches for that text.

- **System State shows a turning spinner while setup works.** A working line's mark
  turns at 12 steps a second while a step runs and the page is in front in a focused
  window. It keeps turning in place under Reduce Motion, stands still under Low Power
  Mode, Serious Mode or load shedding, pauses while you type (until 2.5 seconds after the
  last key), and draws nothing while the page is hidden or another window has the focus.
  Each step repaints only the spinner's own pixels, without rebuilding the page, and
  VoiceOver never reads it out.
- **A supervised agent hears when macOS is still checking programs its tool calls started.**
  While macOS's program check holds programs one of the agent's tool calls started (or that a
  call left running), aterm ends the next prompt it types anyway (a continuation, a done check,
  a land act) with one sentence, once until none waits: `(aterm: macOS's program check is
  holding 2 programs this tab started (pid 72955, pid 72960), the oldest for 19 m; a retry
  waits in the same line)`. It names counts, pids and the wait, never a program's name or
  arguments. With `[harness] stuck_break_note` on, the same sentence is typed as aterm's own
  line at a break of the agent's background work; `[harness] facts = false` turns both off. The
  Harness page counts these under `program-check`.
- Root-approved Google and Meta API keys can be prepared for AGY and Muse without
  copying a browser login. Separate signed execution assignments control which
  machines may use them; automatic assignments wait and resume without a manual
  per-machine selection. OAuth and native browser-profile support remain separate.
- Root-approved shared AI accounts can prepare their first local login
  automatically, preserving existing selections and keeping account use subject
  to separate execution assignments.
- Shared account setup can cover current and future fleet members, with automatic
  recovery for interrupted preparation while its authorization remains current.
- **An untouched window can rest.** With `idle_rest_secs = 30` in `aterm.toml`, after 30
  seconds with no key, click, scroll, pointer move, focus or new output in its tab, a
  window holds a blinking caret solid and draws its stats deck as a background window's:
  still, with a reading every 5 seconds. The GPU then goes quiet between readings, and a
  window's memory falls by about 195 MiB, to 100 to 135 MiB, for most of that time. The
  first touch or output wakes the window at once. It is off by default for now: the first
  key after rest takes as long as an awake window's at the median but slower in its
  tail (up to 5.2 ms against 2.9 ms).

- `aterm db network-state` shows each peer's last authenticated service address
  and its observation age. Retained addresses do not imply current reachability.

- `aterm db commons-custody --table <digest>` inspects a table's retained recovery
  evidence, including when its directory binding fails. It checks the receipt prefix
  separately and leaves the claim, data, writer identity and rights unchanged.

- (developer tool) **`lab git-starts` measures how many git processes a busy Mac starts.** It
  only reads: for a set number of minutes it lists your own processes ten times a second (each
  one's start time and program, never its arguments or environment) and reads each local aterm's
  `survey facts` (no screen text, no command lines) every second. It prints process starts and git
  starts a minute, how often agent sessions end a turn, and how many git starts a per-session work
  record read at turn ends, at most once every 20 seconds, would add. A survey read that a local
  aterm did not answer counts as unanswered, and a run that no survey read answered fails rather
  than report no turn ends. It starts no process and opens no window.

- (developer tool) **`lab grok` runs the real Grok Build against the lab's own stand-in for
  xAI's API.** It launches Grok Build inside the lab's jail with a scratch home and a lab key.
  Both of Grok Build's API addresses point at the lab's local stub, which now answers xAI's
  model list and chat requests, tool calls, held and streamed replies and xAI-shaped errors.
  The launcher refuses to start Grok Build unless the jail first shows that it blocks
  `/usr/bin/open`, so no sign-in page can reach a browser. It never uses an account.

- (developer tool) **`lab kimi` runs the real Kimi Code against the lab's own stub.** It runs
  inside the lab's sandbox, with a throwaway home and a fake key aimed at the stub's new OpenAI
  Chat Completions routes, so no sign-in happens and no Moonshot server is reached. It refuses the
  login, update and server subcommands. The lab's sandbox now also blocks reads and writes of
  `~/.kimi*` and `~/.grok`. Kimi Code 2.4.0's screens, measured with it, are in
  `docs/measured/kimi-forever-2026-10-29.md`.
- (developer tool) **`lab forever --mode sysmsg` plays its outages under Land and an expired
  login.** Its overload, server error, rate limit and dropped connection now also run under
  Autopilot Land (`sys-land-overload`, `-outage`, `-rate`, `-drop`) on Claude Code, agy and
  Muse Code: Land's first act meets the outage, and the run fails if Land types its own
  instruction, nudge, check or answer into it, if the wait is not told or resumed once, or if
  Land does not carry on to its landing afterwards (a hold where every act was answered cleanly
  fails). A new expired-login stand-in
  (`sys-login` under Cruise, `sys-land-login` under Land) answers each program as its real
  service answers a lost login, with each agent in a throwaway home whose browser only logs what
  it was asked to open. On Claude Code the run wants `/login` typed at most once, the sign-in
  method left for the person to pick, the browser never opened by aterm and one quiet need; on
  agy and Muse Code nothing typed and one quiet need that says how to sign in again. Claude Code
  signs in with a stored fake subscription login, the case where aterm once pressed the sign-in
  method itself (`--token-login` runs it on an environment token instead). The lab then plays the
  person (on Claude Code, picking the sign-in method, which the browser must log, and leaving the
  dialog once the stand-in signs in; the real sign-in ends at a host the lab cannot reach), and
  the tab must go on once, by the back-off the policy gives it. A run whose browser log, band or
  sign-in picker went unread passes nothing.
- (developer) **A landing's journal records what aterm checked.** When Autopilot Land lands,
  the session's journal (`drive/<sid>.journal.jsonl`) follows the landing's `DONE …
  rule=land@v1` note with a `RECEIPT` line: `RECEIPT seq=<n> rule=land@v1 head=<12 hex>
  on=origin/main leg=on-main check=land-check@v1 repo=<percent-encoded path> branch=<HEAD's
  branch>`, then the agent's defense line and the lines after it, on one line of at most 240
  bytes. `check=land-check@v1` says the landing stood on the agent's `LANDED` answer to Land's
  land check, and the words are then the defense that check audited (`check=-` where none was
  answered). Its `leg=` is `pushed` where no `origin` main was there to check against,
  `no-remote` for a repository with no remote, `no-repo` (with `head=- on=- repo=-`) where no
  repository was checked, and `gone` (with `repo=` the folder) where the session's folder was
  deleted. A restarted loop reads the receipt back with the landing, and a landing its own wake
  kept writes it again under the new note. `aterm drive ledger`'s page lists the line. codex-alab's own landing writes none,
  because aterm ran no check there. Each landing costs one more in-process call and one more
  journal line.
- **A landing says what aterm checked, wherever it shows.** Once Autopilot Land lands a tab, the
  chip's hover, the menu bar's Done for you row and worker row (their tips), the Settings ▸
  Harness state line and the Messages record name the commit aterm's `git` check read and where:
  `aterm checked 3f9a1c2e4b7d on origin/main in /Users//me/src/proj; nothing uncommitted,
  untracked or unpushed, and no stash on main`, then what the agent said (`it answered the land
  check that nothing is left, after it said “…”` where the landing stood on the land check). A
  repository with no remote says `committed; this repository has no remote`, one with no
  `origin` main `pushed; no origin main to check against`, a folder with no repository aterm
  read `no git repository checked (a plain folder, or one aterm does not read)`, a deleted
  folder `the folder is gone (…)`, and a landing with no receipt (codex-alab's own, whose check
  aterm did not run, or one from before receipts) `aterm has no record of checking this
  landing`. The chip's hover says it in brief (the commit, `origin/main` and the folder, without
  the agent's words), so it shows beside the agent's footer from no wider a window than the
  sentence it replaces; its screen-reader description says it in full; the state line wraps
  rather than cutting it; the Messages record cuts a long quote before its closing mark; the
  chip at rest still reads `✓ landed`. The folder, branch and ref pass the same sanitizer as the
  agent's words, so hidden characters in a folder or branch name reach no surface. `aterm ctl
  status` gains `landed_head=`, `landed_on=`, `landed_leg=` and `landed_repo=` (`-` off a
  landing), and `task`, `task mark done`, `await task` and `result`'s header carry
  `checked=<head>@<ref>`, `pushed`, `no-remote`, `no-repo` or `gone`. None of it raises an
  alert, a sound or a `NEEDS YOU` line, and nothing is drawn per frame.

- **`sys jobs` names a program that never started and reads stopped or traced.** A program
  of yours whose one thread has not run 20 s after it started, while macOS reads it stopped or
  a debugger traces it, was read as started: one that read stopped showed only as `finding
  kind=stopped`, as every stopped process does, with nothing to say it never ran, and one only
  traced showed nowhere. `aterm ctl sys jobs` now also prints it as `finding
  kind=stopped-unstarted pid=… exe=… stopped=yes|no traced=yes|no for_ms=…` (`--json`:
  `stopped_unstarted`), its time running on while a debugger attaches, so a program macOS's
  program check holds that reads either way shows what it read. The Messages log records it
  once under `program-check.not-started` ("it has not started, and it reads stopped and
  traced"), an aterm with no window reads again within 30 s while one stands, and a tab's
  `sys jobs` lists one outside every job that a group-mate's environment ties to that tab. It is
  never counted as held at the program check, and aterm signals nothing because of it.

### Changed

- **A system message or your own turn no longer lengthens Autopilot's pause.** Cruise and
  Land pause after a run of the agent's short answers to their prompts (2 minutes, doubling
  to an hour). A prompt cut short by an outage, an overload, a rate limit, a dropped
  connection or an expired login used to count as one of those answers, and so did a turn you
  typed in the tab yourself: after you signed in again, the next prompt could wait 8 minutes
  instead of 2. Now neither counts. The agent's own short answers before and after still add
  up, a turn of real work still ends the run, and an outage that cuts prompt after prompt
  counts each one past the first, so the pause still grows rather than Autopilot prompting
  every few minutes for as long as the outage lasts.
- **A prompt an agent draws late is sent once it shows, and Land goes on from it.** When an agent
  leaves what aterm typed unread for more than a minute (the tab then says `typed, not
  submitted`) and draws it later, aterm presses its Enter as soon as it shows and counts it as
  sent: under Land, the agent's `Nothing left:` then gets the land check, never the instruction a
  second time.
- **The harness journal names a program that has not read what aterm typed.** When aterm types
  a prompt into an agent and the screen has not moved 10 seconds later, it reads the tab's
  `status` once and journals one line, `NOTE seq=<n> rule=<rule> the program has drawn nothing
  of the text written to it 10 s after the write: input=pending input_bytes=565
  input_wait_ms=10004`, so a program that leaves its input unread no longer reads as a slow
  aterm. It is one line per prompt, never per wait, nothing more is typed, and the read changes
  nothing aterm decides.
- (developer tool) **`lab forever` times Land's `land@v1` by aterm's own share.** The at-once want
  takes the first point to the Enter aterm pressed, less the time the program demonstrably held
  the text unshown, which it says beside it (`typed +3.6 s land@v1 decided +3.5 s, drawn +3.6 s
  (held 0.0 s), Enter +4.1 s`). It also wants land@v1 never typed twice in a row and one held-text
  note where the first look past the write saw nothing move. The lab starts its tabs one at a
  time and prompts each only once its program has drawn its composer and read every byte written
  to it; `--no-ready-gate` runs it as before, so Land writes behind unread input.

- **The stats deck's needle moves on the display's refresh.** The dial's needle is drawn on
  the screen's own vsyncs, from a clock that follows the window to whichever display it is on
  (120 Hz on a ProMotion panel, 60 Hz elsewhere), and each frame shows the needle where it
  will be when that frame reaches the screen. A sweep now steps once per refresh period, where
  it waited two before, and the clock stops on the frame where the needle comes to rest, so a
  still deck asks for no frames. It runs at two periods while the deck's frames wait for the
  GPU, and in Low Power Mode. Macs before macOS 14 keep the cursor trail's cadence (half the
  panel's rate on Apple silicon).

- **A still stats deck costs nothing between readings.** A reading now redraws only the
  windows that show the stats bars on screen: never a hidden, minimised or covered window,
  and none with the bars off. Each frame tells the renderer which version of the deck it
  carries, so the renderer no longer compares the whole deck with what it last uploaded on
  every frame (about 0.84 MB per frame at the default window size, including every frame of
  the cursor trail), and a live frame uploads only the rows it changed.

- **Cruise no longer stops when a session repeats itself.** A session that gave the same
  reply with no work used to stop being typed to after the second repeat. Autopilot Cruise now
  waits out its back-off (at most an hour by default, and never faster than `continue_per_hour`
  where you set one), then asks the session to change approach or pick another useful task.
  Land still stops on a repeat, and Cruise still stops at a spent usage wall or within an hour
  of your typing. No alert is shown; each stop is a note in Messages.

- **The fabric's bus log is sealed on disk.** `bus.log` is now encrypted at rest under a
  `rest.key` beside it, left out of Time Machine backups and never in the Keychain, so a Time
  Machine backup or a copy of the log without the key reads nothing. Linux has no such mark: a
  backup tool there must be told to skip `rest.key`, and aterm says so. A log from before is
  sealed once, at the broker's next start. A missing or damaged key refuses to open the log and
  says what to do: put the key back, or `aterm link broker --retire-log <log>`, which keeps the
  old records aside and starts a new log. It does not protect the log from a process of your own
  user or a copy of the whole folder. A broker's start on a log near its 256 MiB budget takes
  about 0.45 s longer; one set under load could not resolve a change in latency or bursts on the
  shipped ordered bus. `aterm fabric` has an `at-rest` row, also while the broker is down, and
  `aterm fabric doctor` says `at-rest=sealed` or `at-rest=plaintext`.

- **An agent's ask returns sooner.** Each ask or task used to rewrite two whole state files
  before its sender got its answer. It now makes one append to a journal of its own, so an ask
  is released as soon after the bus accepts it as a note: about 0.2 ms rather than 0.6 ms on the
  shipped ordered bus, measured on a loaded machine. A deadline that was answered while its post
  was held is no longer armed again by the next bridge after a crash, short of a second crash
  before that bridge retries the post. Rolling back stays safe: a stop still writes the old
  `asked` and `deadlines` files, and this build picks up what an older build wrote there.

- **Land contradicts a `Nothing left:` that is not true.** When an agent under Land answers
  with `Nothing left:` while `git` still finds work no remote main has, or repeats a defense
  Land's check already heard while its own list of what is left still stands, Land's next prompt
  opens with the contradiction instead of its usual words: `Still landing: your last reply says
  Nothing left, but git shows work no remote main has (…/land-c: 1 untracked (wip-notes.txt)).
  Commit, merge and push it to the remote main; never delete work.`, or, for its own list, `…
  but you said this is left: “The docs PR is still open.” Finish it and land it on the remote
  main; never delete work.` Land's own closing words follow, the sentence on files no repository
  holds and the `NEEDS YOU:` line for what only a person can give among them. It asks only that
  the work be landed, never that it be ignored or moved, and it is still Land's nudge: one prompt
  per point, under the same back-off, counted as a nudge everywhere a nudge is counted. Codex
  (codex-alab) keeps Land's usual nudge until its fork reads the repository's facts.

- (developer tool) **`lab claude-measure` and `lab codex-measure` judge a new transcript or
  rollout key by what the step fold reads and what the run exercised**, so a new Claude Code
  build is measured, not left partial for a person to admit by hand. A key or record kind no
  measured build showed is only noted on a row the fold does not act on (an attachment, a
  `tools-used` record), still refuses `NEW-KEY` when the fold reads it, and is otherwise admitted
  only once the second run, expecting the build exact, wrote a row carrying it and passed every
  check; the note names each admitted key with the run, the row and the check. A key is judged
  by the rows it was shown on, so one noted on an attachment is still new on a user row, and
  `GONE` reads only the rows the fold acts on. The keys and words the fold reads are now one
  list held to the fold's own reads, and the Claude Code session ends four Bash calls four ways
  (granted once, granted for the session, declined with Esc, and run sandboxed with no box),
  each call's end read off the screen and held to the transcript's. `lab codex-measure` now
  holds each run's reductions to the privacy oracle as `lab claude-measure` does, refusing
  `TEXT` when one keeps text of its rollout.

- **Land's hold quotes the agent, and Land keeps it resolving before it holds.** While Land
  holds a tab, its state line, the chip's title, the tab's hover and the worker's row now say
  what the agent itself listed as left, in its own words and in quotes (`not landed yet: open in
  its report: “The docs PR is still open.”`), in place of the family words aterm read off its
  report, and name the files `git` found (`1 untracked file: wip-notes.txt`, at most three).
  An item the agent rewords refreshes the quote. Land's prompt after the agent's list asks it to
  resolve each issue it can; Land holds only when the agent gives the same answer again, and the
  hold quotes that answer. A hold that only a person's need holds says `waits only on you:
  <the need>` on every surface instead of `not landed yet: needs you`, and the hover and the
  worker's tip no longer repeat the need under the need's own line. While a hold is shown, the
  chip's title and its screen-reader description leave Land's own acts (`⤓ landing`, `⤓ nudged`,
  `⤓ land check`) out of `last:`, which the hold's `landing since` already says.

- **A session waiting out an API outage now resumes as soon as another session on the same
  route gets an answer.** When one supervised session's turn on a route (the same program
  talking to the same endpoint) finishes with a real reply, every other session waiting out an
  overload, a server error or a lost connection there types its one *has cleared* line within
  about 20 seconds, instead of waiting up to an hour for its next blind try. Only a turn the
  model answered counts: a reply drawn as an error, or a turn whose wall aterm confirmed, does
  not. A route is the program and its endpoint's full base URL, path included, so two gateways
  on one host are two routes. A resume like this happens once per outage, never into a route
  aterm measures as down, and never at a rate limit, which belongs to the account rather than
  the route. The reachability probe now also reaches the endpoint each session's own launch
  names: Muse Code's `--base-url`, agy's `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` when agy runs on a Gemini API
  key (not when it is signed in with Google or on Vertex AI), and Claude Code's
  `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. A launch that names none is logged as a gap, and that session waits as
  before; an environment aterm could not read yet is read again at the next wait. A rate limit
  whose message names its wait (Muse Code's `Please try again in 150s.`, agy's per-minute quota
  and its `retryDelay`) gets its first try after that wait, at most an hour, instead of two
  minutes in. Claude Code's rate-limit message names no wait, so it is tried on the usual ladder.

- **Switching a stopped tab to Land asks once more.** When aterm has stopped typing
