  free credit waiting for your account (the $250 cloud session credit, or the API credits
  your Max plan includes), a window supervising a Claude Code session starts one worker tab
  that opens the offer's claude.ai link in your own Chrome, through Claude in Chrome, and
  claims it. The worker never enters payment details, buys anything, turns on extra usage,
  changes your plan or signs in anew; it stops if the page asks for any of that, and ends
  with one `Nothing left:` reply saying `CLAIMED:` or `NOT CLAIMED:`. The harness only
  approves the worker's Chrome actions on the vendor's claim pages (each once, never for the
  whole site), declines every other box it raises, leaves its questions, and any Chrome action
  off those pages, to you, and stops it after 30 minutes. Each offer is tried once, and again
  at most once a week later if it still stands; the digest names the offer and the worker's
  tab. Feature of the week is never claimed (claiming it turns on extra usage), nor are guest
  passes. Turn it off with `[harness] claim_credits = false`.

- **An open vault's admin founds its Commons by itself.** On a vault made before Commons
  that has one admin and lets in every machine that asks (as the ALab vault does), the admin's
  converge pass now publishes the Commons control entry that only `aterm secrets commons init`
  published before, under the same authority, and approves every machine in the vault for
  Commons by the vault's open policy, so each one enrolls over the LAN with nothing typed. A
  machine on a `code-only` line is left to approval by code. A closed vault, or one with two
  admins, is still founded by `aterm secrets commons init` alone, and `[commons] enabled =
  false` or `aterm secrets agent off` keeps the pass out. While macOS has not let aterm use the local network, the pass
  waits and does not ask. It also waits while the admin Mac's vault approver (its secrets
  subscriber, such as a held snapshot) runs a release before 0.145.0, which shares Commons
  with no machine the open vault lets in later, and the row names that program and its
  release: `aterm secrets agent on`, or `agent on --program` with aterm 0.145.0 or later,
  lets the next pass found it, and `aterm secrets commons init` founds it at once, leaving
  each Mac the old approver lets in afterwards to `aterm secrets approve`. The wait shows in
  the pass's `aterm.log` line.

- `aterm ctl text --json` now carries the program's window title as `"title"` (the OSC 0/2
  title `aterm ctl title` prints, `""` when the program set none), read in the same hold as
  the rows, so a reader sees the title and the screen as one snapshot. Under a status line
  Claude Code hides its `esc to interrupt` hint and stops drawing its spinner once a reply's
  first line is up, so its title's `◐`/`◑` is then the only sign on screen that a turn still
  runs. A reply from an older aterm has no `"title"`, and readers take that as saying
  nothing. The title is the last one set in the tab, so it can outlast the program that set
  it.

- **A Mac asks the lab for a credential it lacks, or says why nobody can give it.** A Mac
  missing a credential (the site deployer's key, the notary profile, a Claude account's mailbox
  password) now raises a need: `ship provision` raises one for a missing deployer key, and the
  sign-in ladder raises one for a row with no mailbox. Needs live in a ledger beside the vault's
  state, and once Commons runs they go on a table every Mac reads. Each Mac checks whether it
  holds the credential and says so; taking a copy from that Mac comes in a later release, and
  until then the need's line names the command a person with that Mac's copy runs. The vault's
  admin Mac copies a credential the vault already holds into the asking Mac's own section, and
  only that entry. A credential no Mac holds
  goes to a person as one `NEEDS YOU` with the one step that gives it, and the ask comes down when
  the credential arrives or a person declines. A credential that cannot be given at all is retired
  at once, with the reason (the paper master is on paper only; a vendor login is made fresh on
  each Mac). `aterm secrets need` lists, raises, retires and runs a pass by hand, and `aterm
  secrets status` gains a `needs:` line (docs/DESIGN-credential-requests-2026-10-27.md).

- (developer tool) **`lab claude-measure` measures the installed Claude Code build in one
  command**: a session under a private lab before and after, the reduced transcript, the
  standing tests and the `docs/measured` note, or a named refusal that leaves the checkout as it
  was. The Claude Code builds the session log reads exactly are now the builds whose reductions
  are committed, read when aterm is built, as for codex-alab; until a build is measured its
  transcript is read as partial.

- (developer tool) **`aterm ctl dims` names the content the window's last present drew**
  (`presented_seq=`, `"presented_seq"` in `--json`): the session grid's content clock, the one
  `aterm ctl await match` answers with, in the frame the window's own last successful present
  drew, or `none`. A present a capture forces does not move it. The Windows lab's modal-resize
  row now waits for a present that drew its echo instead of any frame after it.

- (developer tool) **The lab stub's log names a scripted tool call that does not fit the tools
  its request declares.** An agent refuses such a call itself, often with nothing on its screen
  to say why: agy 1.4.10 answered every argument its closed schemas do not name with a tool
  result, and the lab's legs that called them saw no task run. A `tool` or custom mode's call
  now logs `misfit='…'` after its row when the request declares no tool of that name, or the
  tool's schema requires an argument the call lacks or is closed and does not name one the call
  gives: `misfit='run_command: undeclared Cwd, undeclared toolAction'`. It reads Gemini's
  function declarations, the Messages API's `input_schema`, and the Responses API's `parameters`
  (Muse Code's namespaced tools among them), each at its top level only.

### Changed

- **Every Mac in ALab can drive every other, admin Macs included.** A Mac that joins the
  default fleet by sync, a vault admin's too, and the admin Mac that forms that fleet now let
  every member drive them (`drive_from = ["*"]`), and the node job's default is the same on
  every Mac. Admin Macs were held at `facts`, so a Mac the open vault let in could not drive
  the Mac holding the vault's keys. That exemption goes now that no Mac gets in without an
  Allow. A level you set with `aterm fleet allow` stays as you set it.

- **An open vault no longer lets in a Mac just because it asks.** A Mac joins with a
  member's Allow and its phrase (`aterm members join`), the vault's join password, or an
  admin's approval by code. The fleet port now answers callers without the fleet secret
  only for the join request (`ask`); survey and drive still need the secret.
- **After a network move, each Mac waits a few seconds of its own before it reaches the
  fleet.** When a Mac's network moves (back on the LAN, onto another Wi-Fi), its fleet
  heartbeat, converge pass, account claims and fleet glance now start at an offset of up to
  8 seconds that stays the same for that Mac (from its fleet node id, else its host name), so
  ~35 Macs coming back together do not all reach one Mac at the same instant. The wait is
  sized to the fleet: about a quarter second for each other member, up to the full 8 seconds
  for a fleet of 35, and none for a Mac in no fleet or alone in one. macOS's Local Network
  answer for aterm, and the harness's check that the Claude API is reachable again, still act
  at once.
- **Another Mac's window opening no longer reads as this Mac's network moving.** A member that
  disappears from the LAN and reappears under the same name within two minutes (as a Mac does
  when its window opens or closes) no longer wakes this Mac's fleet heartbeat, converge pass
  and account claims. A member back after longer, or a new one, still does.
- **amacs is the default editor in aterm's tabs.** A new tab sets `EDITOR=amacs` when
  neither `EDITOR` nor `VISUAL` is set once your shell's startup files have run, so
  `git commit` and an agent's Ctrl-G (Claude Code's included) open the file in an aterm
  editor tab beside the tab that asked: C-c C-c hands the text back, C-c C-k aborts.
  An `EDITOR` or `VISUAL` you set yourself, in your startup files or in aterm's own
  environment, always wins, and aterm never sets `VISUAL`. zsh, bash, fish and PowerShell
  make the choice in aterm's shell integration, so an agent started in a tab inherits it;
  a `-e` command and cmd.exe get it as they start; any other shell, or one with
  integration off, gets none, since its startup files would run after it. Settings ▸
  Terminal ▸ "Use amacs as the default editor (EDITOR)", or `[amacs] default_editor = false`
  in aterm.toml, turns it off for new tabs, as `[packages] exclude = ["amacs"]` does; a
  contained session never gets it, and an aterm started from an aterm tab decides again
  under its own settings rather than keeping the outer tab's `EDITOR=amacs`.

- **Every ALab vault member serves, servers replicate to each other, and `alab-secrets` needs no
  lease.** Every active member of the ALab vault now runs the keyless vault server by default (the
  user LaunchAgent aterm installs for it, which leaves the Mac free to idle-sleep, or a LaunchDaemon
  on an always-on desktop `aterm machines` enrolls, unless turned off with `aterm secrets server
  off`), advertises `_alab-vault._tcp` under its own label, pulls newer verified heads from browsed
  peers (`?after=<held seq>`), and receives every admin publish across all candidate servers at
  once. Empty servers adopt `alab` from a peer only when `alab` is pinned. A held pre-0.146 ALab
  server job, whose store holds the ALab vault, moves onto the new build with the arguments it had,
  by converge or the window's mend, and counts as moved only once it is seen serving that vault at
  its own address; otherwise it is put back. `alab-secrets.local` is claimed after 90 s of silence
  without a lease (yielding to an answering holder, settling two holders it hears by highest `seq`
  then lowest label, and letting the name go when mDNS keeps it for another server), and vault
  publishes keep the 0.145 header grammar without `parent:` lines so 0.145 Macs keep reading
  throughout migration.
- **`aterm ai` never tells a person to run what aterm runs itself.** The health line used to
  end "next: ask a person to run aterm ai doctor" whenever an agent ran it. It now names
  what `aterm ai doctor` fixes by itself (installs, and sign-ins through accounts v2's or a
  pool's renewal), and only a sign-in no aterm route can make goes on a `NEEDS YOU:` line,
  with the command that starts it. `aterm ai doctor` and `aterm ai login` now make aterm's own
  fixes under an agent or with no terminal too; a CLI's own browser sign-in still waits for a
  person at a terminal. A signed-out row also says what aterm's last sign-in of it tried.
  A sign-in counts as aterm's only where it can run with nobody at the Mac: a Claude account
  with no mailbox and no browser profile of its own, a pool account whose last renewal stopped
  for a person, and any account while `[harness] logins = "off"` (or accounts off) are a
  person's, and the `NEEDS YOU:` line names the one step that person takes (for Claude,
  `aterm harness accounts browser <label>` once). With nobody at the Mac, a renewal runs
  without the terminal, so it never opens a browser on the desk, and it waits for the
  window's upkeep after a failed sign-in or Cloudflare's bot check is on record.
  `aterm harness accounts renew <label>` that runs nothing exits 1, so `aterm ai login`
  no longer reports such a run as signed in.
- codex-alab `0.166.0-dev.13766` is measured for its session log, so its harness
  status no longer reports its rollout as unmeasured.

- **Harness update labels show the running CLI's complete build.** Hover a shortened
  label to read codex-alab's product version or Muse Code's revision. An update's arrow
  names its target and the work it waits for; a held move explains its reason on the
  messages row. Pending arrows stay with their original program and source build.

- **Claude Code keeps its effort reading through background launches and updates.** The
  prompt rule retains the effort Claude's own hint showed, even when no frame was drawn
  before that hint disappeared. A resumed conversation keeps the reading for the same
  model; a fresh conversation takes its own hint. Narrow mode rows can clear a cut key
  hint while preserving the running jobs, and an account watch with no limit or inventory
  leaves the rule clear.

- **ALab's agent harnesses install with the rest of the toolset.** Once a harness such as
  `grok-alab` is published, `aterm pkg` installs it and keeps it current like every other
  program, instead of waiting for you to type `aterm pkg install`. To keep one off, list it
  in `[packages].exclude` or run `aterm pkg uninstall <name>`; either choice stays.

- **Macs in a fleet share toolset downloads over the local network.** When a Mac in your
  fleet (`aterm fleet`) downloads a toolset archive that another member already has, it asks
  that Mac for it while the download from GitHub runs and keeps whichever finishes first. A
  member's copy is used only when it matches the signed checksum. While aterm runs, each Mac
  in a fleet offers the archives it keeps for its installed builds to its fleet members on
  port 7487, and to no other machine. `aterm pkg doctor` says what this Mac shares and with
  whom. `aterm pkg serve-units --off` stops sharing and deletes the kept archives, until
  `aterm pkg serve-units --on`; `[packages] peers = []` stops asking other Macs.

- **The message bus (fabric) is on by default on every Mac.** An aterm window's converge
  pass, at launch and every 30 minutes, now turns the fabric on with `aterm fabric on`'s own
  steps wherever you never turned it off: the broker job, the node's grants and `[fabric]
  command`, with every running window attached. It asks nothing, posts no proof note into a
  session, and never runs from the vault's subscriber, headless, under CI or in a private
  state root. `aterm fabric off` now records your choice (`fabric-off`, in the fabric root and
  beside aterm.toml, so deleting the fabric folder afterwards keeps it off), and no pass turns
  the fabric on again until `aterm fabric on`; an off waits for a turn-on the pass is making,
  so it always lands after it. A fabric root an earlier `off` left reads as off too, and so
  does a `[fabric] command` you clear from aterm.toml after the fabric ran.

- **Harness versions since v0.145.0: `alab codex harness 0.5`, `alab claude harness 0.5`, `alab agy harness 0.5`, `alab grok harness 0.5`, `alab kimi harness 0.5`, `alab muse harness 0.5`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- **An admin Mac's held approver moves onto aterm once it can no longer approve.** When an
  admin Mac's vault subscriber or server runs a copy of aterm that a person pinned with
  `--program`, the window's mend, at launch and every 30 minutes, now moves the job onto the
  installed aterm only when that copy is too old to read the vault's admin locker (so it lets
  no Mac in) and the installed aterm, a release, reads it. A pinned copy that reads the locker is
  left as it is. To keep any pin, pin it with this release or later: `aterm secrets agent on
  --program <path>` and `aterm secrets server on --program <path>` record it, and no mend moves a
  job off a program you pinned that way; `agent on` or `server on` without `--program` unpins.
  On the ALab vault's admin Mac, a held approver older than this release that you did not pin
  moves too, even one that reads the locker: it would let in any Mac that asks and never the
  one you allowed.
  An `off`, `on` or pin you make while the mend works is never undone. If the job does not start
  on the installed aterm, it is put back on the copy it ran, and the mend tries again only at
  the window's next launch.

- **A Mac waiting on the ALab vault says what it waits for.** While the ALab vault has not let
  this Mac in yet, the window's converge pass (and its join) now says it is waiting for the
  vault's approver, which lets a Mac that asks in within seconds while it runs on the vault's
  admin Mac, or, if an admin closed the vault or let this Mac go, for the join password or an
  admin's approval by code. Another vault keeps the old words.

- **Every Mac now installs Grok Build and Kimi Code with the other agent CLIs.** aterm's
  package manager used to install Claude Code, Codex, agy and Muse Code on every machine and
  Grok Build and Kimi Code only when you ran `aterm pkg install grok` or `kimi`. Now its next
  update pass installs both from their vendors and keeps them current, like the rest. Nothing
  aterm runs by itself starts either one, and a signed-out `grok` typed in an aterm tab, even
  one typed while it was still installing, stops at aterm's sign-in step instead of opening
  xAI's page. To keep one off a machine, list it in `aterm.toml` (`[packages] exclude =
  ["grok"]`), or run `aterm pkg uninstall grok`, which stays in force. Until you sign in to
  Grok Build, `aterm ai` lists it as signed out and its check fails, the window shows it among
  the things that need you, and `aterm ai doctor` signs it in along with the others (opening
  xAI's sign-in page); set `[ai.grok] use = false` in `aterm.toml` if you do not use it. Before
  it lands, `aterm ai` shows it as `not-installed` with `aterm pkg install grok` as the fix,
  where it used to say `off`. `aterm ctl spawn` now installs any agent CLI that has not landed
  yet (a new Mac before the update pass gets to it) before it starts the worker, not just Grok
  Build; where you keep one off, or said no to installs as the update pass reads it (Settings ▸
  Packages with "Install ALab tools" or "Keep ALab tools up to date" off, that is `[packages]
  auto_install = false` or `enabled = false` in `aterm.toml`, or their retired spellings
  `seed_install = false` and `auto_update = false`, or `aterm pkg uninstall --all`), it installs
  nothing, the worker's launch line in aterm's log names what kept it off, and the worker runs
  your own copy if there is one.

- **Codex, Grok Build and Kimi Code accounts sync from the vault by default.** A Mac used to
  take its Codex rows from `ai-accounts.csv` (or `ai-accounts-codex.toml`) only if it already
  kept an `accounts-codex.toml`, so most Macs running Codex never got the rows the sheet assigns
  them and stayed on one login. Now `aterm init`, `aterm secrets` and the aterm window take this
  Mac's Codex rows from the sheet into `accounts-codex.toml`, as they always have for Claude
  Code. Your own Codex login stays the first row, and each new row gets an empty login folder
  of its own; no login is copied or moved. A new row starts signed out: aterm signs one in
  when a Codex session nears its limit with no other row ready, or you can run `aterm harness
  accounts login <label> --cli codex`. A Mac the sheet doesn't list gets no file at all. A Mac
  that kept an `accounts-codex.toml` and deleted it stays out of the pool while aterm still
  holds records of one of the rows it would add; `aterm harness accounts sync --cli codex`
  names that row. The rows then serve Codex as a kept `accounts-codex.toml` always has: new
  Codex workers start on a usable row where the Codex they run keeps that row's login its own
  (a codex-alab from its cd79a420c on; on any other Codex only your own login's row serves),
  and codex-alab sessions, which answer their own usage limits, are not moved. Grok Build's
  and Kimi Code's rows now sync from the vault by default the same way, on a Mac with no
  roster of theirs too; aterm signs no Grok Build row in by itself, so a new one waits for your
  `aterm harness accounts login <label> --cli grok`. `[harness] accounts = "off"` turns this
  off, and `aterm harness accounts sync --cli codex`, which you run yourself, still syncs.

- **`ship provision` no longer asks for your login password.** On a release Mac the Developer
  ID certificate and key now go into aterm's own keychain,
  `~/Library/Keychains/aterm-release.keychain-db`, instead of your login keychain. Provision
  makes it with a random password kept in `~/.aterm/apple/release-keychain.pass` (readable by
  you alone), sets it never to lock by itself, adds it to the end of your keychain search list
  (every entry already there stays, in its order), and lets `codesign` and `productsign` use
  the key by that keychain's own password, so no step asks for the login keychain's password
  or raises a keychain dialog. `ship release` opens that keychain and names it to `codesign`.
  A Mac whose Developer ID identity is already in its login keychain keeps signing from there
  exactly as before, and provision writes nothing to it. `ship provision` and the release
  audit show a `keychain` line that says what is missing and what to run; `ship provision
  --check` and a dry `ship release` only open the keychain and change nothing in it.

- (developer tool) **The real-Claude lab stands its own bus and tab strip, and launches by name
  as a person does.** `lab up --fabric` starts a private broker in the lab's jail and socket
  dir, mints the node's and an observer's caps, names the bridge in the instance's
  `aterm.toml`, writes the rendezvous file `aterm link` reads there, and returns once the
  bridge is connected; `down` ends it, keeps its logs and removes its keys, so the tag comes
  up with `--fabric` again. `lab up --tab-strip` gives the
  instance the one-row tab strip whose tab menu holds the session clause. `lab claude
  --by-name` (a `LAB_REROUTE=1` lab only) types `claude` at the prompt, the lab's environment
  as assignment words before it, so aterm reads the program a person runs. The codex-alab
  proof checks its worker after the legs a model's hold times, so a worker that never lands no
  longer makes the repository checks fail, and a late act says which leg held it.

- **The notary profile comes from `release-notary`, on release Macs with the tools only.**
  The vault subscriber used to run `xcrun notarytool` after every vault version it applied
  once a `notary` entry existed, on every Mac, with no check for Apple's developer tools, so
  a Mac without them would have put Apple's install dialog on screen. It now reads the entry
  `release-notary` (the old name is never read), and runs notarytool only on a release Mac
  (it holds the release-credentials profile and the release roster lists its vault name),
  only where xcrun has a developer directory with notarytool in it, and only when the entry
  changed since the last successful check. A Mac waiting for the tools says so once in the
  subscriber's log, and stores the profile on the first round after they arrive.
- **After a seamless update the fabric bridge reuses state already on disk.** The new
  bridge can now tell that its predecessor finished writing the run record and mirror floor.
  It keeps a link to each file's inode after the full flush succeeds, and a successor that
  finds the same inode skips writing that state again. A bridge restarted after a crash
  can reuse the same records; a missing or stale link keeps the full-write path.

- **ALab Commons holds 255 members, not 63, once every Mac heard this week runs 0.146.** A
  Commons roster now holds up to 255 Macs (a control node up to 256 facts; each member's key
  capsule bound to its measured 421 bytes, so a full roster fits the 256 KiB payload). 0.145
  refuses a control node past 64 facts, so the first roster past 63 members is written only
  once every member it keeps or adds that was heard in the last 7 days has reported aterm 0.146
  or later within those 7 days; a member not heard for 7 days does not hold it back, and once
  that roster exists nothing more is gated. After each completed repair round, two Macs now
  trade an 80-byte version report signed by each one's Commons writer key (0.145 neither sends
  nor reads it, and its rounds go on as before), and each Mac keeps a record of whom it heard,
  when, and on which version. A member unheard for 30 days (counted from when an admin's Mac
  first saw it on the roster, if it never heard it) leaves the Commons roster, never the vault,
  and is re-enrolled as soon as that Mac hears it again; one admin Mac checks this every 10
  minutes, leaving it to the admin on 0.146 with the smallest Commons key when it heard one in
  the last 15 minutes. Enrolling a Mac drops nobody. Until a Mac has watched for 7 days (30 for
  leaving), hearing peers with no gap of more than 6 hours, it opens no gate and drops nobody.
  A Mac now keeps address hints for 256 Commons peers, not 64, so it can dial every member.

- **A running command's program reaches the session log once it has started.** A `cmd`
  run's `open` record carries `detail=` only when the program was already seen running;
  otherwise one `amend` record (`src=status`) adds it as soon as it is, while the command runs
  or as it ends, and readers of `aterm ctl log` see it there. A wrapper or interpreter shown
  first (the `time` of `time make`, the `sh` of a script) is replaced once by the program when
  it is seen.

- **Rewind is now on by default, and an idle aterm uses less than half the memory it did.**
  Every new tab keeps its recent screens in memory (`temporal_recording = true` by default;
  Settings > Terminal > Rewind turns it off for new tabs), bounded by `rewind_budget_mb` (8)
  per pane and `rewind_total_mb` (128) across all panes. The pet-trick vocabulary is decoded
  when aterm is built instead of at every launch, three Settings preview caches no longer
  reserve their full size in every thread, and on macOS a compact slab allocator, startup
  code-page packing, stripped internal link symbols and deferred background helpers bring an
  idle instance with no window down to under 7 MB of private memory and about 24 MB resident
  (from about 23 MB private and 50 MB resident), with Rewind adding about 0.1 MB at idle.

- **An idle aterm window holds about 130 MB less memory.** The Mac's GPU driver keeps a
  separate block of working memory for copy work, and frees it only after a second or two with
  no such work. The copy that composed each frame for the screen counted as copy work, so any
  window that drew once a second kept the block: a blinking cursor, or the deck's live
  readings. That copy is now drawn like the rest of the frame. On an M5 Max, an idle default
  window's memory, the figure Activity Monitor shows, fell from about 410 MB to about 280 MB.
  First-frame, typing and present latency are unchanged.

- **The harness card links alab.systems, and Claude Code's startup announcement is ALab's.**
  The line under a decorated launch card now reads `✦ enhanced by alab claude harness v0.5 ·
  alab.systems` (agy's and Muse Code's name in place of `claude`) under every Autopilot mode,
  in place of `· autopilot ∞ cruise`; the mode still colours the card (Cruise's rainbow,
  Land's sunset, Off's white). Narrower panes step down to `alab claude harness v0.5 ·
  alab.systems`, `alab claude harness · alab.systems`, `alab.systems` and `alab`, so the link
  stays wherever it fits. The one announcement Claude Code shows under its card at
  startup (a credit offer, a feature of the week, the auto-mode notice, launch news such as
  `Get to finished work sooner with Opus 5.5`, whether or not it draws its accent bar, inline
  or in Claude Code's fullscreen layout, and news under a startup warning or the emergency tip,
  which themselves stay), and the `1 more notice hidden` row under
  it, are replaced on screen by `✦ ALab · aterm, the terminal
  that runs your agents · https://alab.systems`, shortened to `ALab · https://alab.systems`,
  `https://alab.systems` or `alab.systems` where the pane is narrow. Each `alab.systems` link
  is underlined and acts like the update-notice banner's: the pointing hand shows over it, a
  click (or Cmd-click) opens https://alab.systems once per double click, a click in an
  unfocused pane only focuses it, Shift and Option clicks select as before, and VoiceOver reads
  and presses it as a link. Copy, `aterm ctl text` and recordings still read Claude Code's own
  words. Claude Code's other notices stay as it draws them: its startup warnings, the
  emergency tip Anthropic pushes, an update notice the harness cannot read, and the status
  notices that take the same place (debug mode, remote control, channels, the tmux session,
  the model's source), which Claude Code draws with a faint bar. Where their colours cannot
  tell them from news, they are covered with it: with no colour at all (`NO_COLOR`) the tip
  and those status notices, and where faint text is drawn in the pane's own ink
  (`faint_opacity = 1`, or near enough to it) the tip in Claude Code's dim ink, unless news
  with a title stands under it. An announcement your organisation sets
  (`companyAnnouncements`) wears the same bar as Anthropic's news and is covered too.

- **`aterm fabric` warns of mail the broker's retention gave up.** What the broker let go of
  before it was read or handled was told to the sessions it was for (`given_up=`,
  `lane_given_up=`, a topic's `given_up=` in `topic ls`) and nowhere a person looks. Now
  `aterm fabric` lists it under WARNINGS, and `aterm fabric doctor` says what it means: this
  node's unread mail once per instance, with its ranges and counts, even when no session was
  there to be told, and each session's own lane and topics once for that session. `aterm ctl
  fabric status` counts the node's ranges since the instance started (`mail_gaps=`, the newest
  as `mail_gap=` and `mail_gap_count=`), and `aterm fabric status --json` carries the same
  fields.

- **`aterm fabric status` says how many held asks past their deadline it cannot judge.** It
  lists an ask as overdue only while the broker keeps every answer, report and ack its asker
  could have had since, because a reply the broker gave up may have been that ask's answer.
  It left such an ask out without a word, so an unanswered ask hid whenever a later reply to
  the same session had been given up. Now one warning gives their count, and `--json` carries
  it as `overdue_unjudged`. Such an ask is still never listed as overdue. `aterm fabric
  doctor` says under the warning where the asker's inbox shows the answers it had, and that
  only the broker letting those asks go clears the count.

### Fixed

- Claude account recovery names an account known to be signed out even when no
  sign-in attempt has been recorded, instead of showing only a generic wait.

- **Every NEEDS YOU line an agent writes reaches you whole.** Three ways a need never reached
  the menu bar and window border, or reached them cut, are gone. A turn that ends while the
  agent's own background work still runs was read by its last message alone, so a need written
  earlier in that turn was lost once Cruise carried the work on. A declared wake that came due at
  that moment typed its line before the needs were read, so even a need in the last message was
  lost. And a need that Claude Code, agy or Muse Code wrapped onto a second row starting with a
  capital letter, a backtick or a path was cut at the end of its first row (`grant aterm
  (dev).app the Accessibility permission in System`). Now such a turn is read whole, from the
  terminal's history where it began above the screen, as any turn end is, before anything is
  typed into it. A row is read as the rest of the line above it when the row above had no room
  left for its first word (counting the cell the program leaves under an exactly full row), unless
  the row opens another NEEDS YOU line, a list item or a code fence, or the line above ended its
  sentence. So a wrapped need is read whole, and the need after it stays its own. Cruise's own
  message at a break is also no longer read as the agent's words once the agent's answer scrolls
  its start off agy's screen, so a NEEDS YOU line in your standing rules that the message quotes
  is no longer raised as the agent's need.
- **Autopilot Land no longer lands with work left on another branch, in a submodule, or never
  pushed.** Land's repository check now counts a submodule commit the submodule's own remote
  does not have (a pushed record of it points the remote main at a commit nobody can fetch), in
  every submodule at every depth, however many there are; a shallow submodule's fetched commit
  is not counted. It counts the commits and stash entries a session left on another branch it
  used (the branches its own worktree moved through since it began, and the ones its commands
  created, never another session's), including one it pushed to `origin` and then deleted
  locally; and, where a remote is configured but nothing was ever pushed to it, every commit. A
  session that moved into a submodule is checked against the project around it as well as the
  submodule. A read of any of these that git refuses keeps the landing open. The hold's line
  names the submodule commits and the commits parked on other branches. The check reads only
  the local repository and fetches nothing.
- **Under Land, a relaunched Muse Code or agy no longer types "continue where you left
  off".** After a crash, an aterm restart or a stall, Claude Code's relaunch under Land types
  nothing and lets Land decide what comes next. Muse Code's and agy's relaunches typed Cruise's
  carry-on instead, which starts again work Land was wrapping up. Now they type nothing under
  Land either, and Land decides the point. Under Cruise, a relaunched Muse Code or agy whose
  last reply said the work was done gets Cruise's done check in place of the carry-on, as
  Claude Code does.

- **Under Land, a person's quick question no longer parks a session that worked under Off.**
  A session driven by hand under Autopilot Off and then switched to Land took the person's
  next quick question for the session's opening message. Land left it to them and rested with
  the work unlanded. The same happened to a conversation resumed with `claude --continue` in a
  new tab. Now a session that ran under Off, or a conversation resumed by its own launch, is
  mid-session, and Land carries the work on after the reply. A session switched from Off to
  Land during its very first exchange is still told apart: when the screen shows the program's
  start card above that one message, the message stays the person's. The reverse is fixed too. A
  program started fresh in a reused tab could get its first question sent before the harness
  saw its start screen, by typing ahead or with `claude "<question>"`. That question was
  taken as mid-session, and Land typed its instruction after it. Now it is that program's
  opening message, and it stays the person's.

- **Cruise and Land no longer leave an agent waiting on your go-ahead for its own work.** An
  agent that ended its turn waiting for you to say go (`NEEDS YOU: say "rerun the checks"`,
  `waiting only for your go-ahead`, `I won't start it again unless you ask`) before building,
  testing, committing or pushing its own branch to main could sit for days: Cruise answered it
  with its usual prompt, which the agent read as no go-ahead, and the agent's own hourly wakes
  kept restarting Cruise's wait. Now Cruise and Land answer such a turn with your standing
  go-ahead (`go-ahead@v1`), quoting the word it asked for, within 15 minutes of its last
  answer. The go-ahead covers only the agent's own reversible work: never anything that
  deletes, overwrites, force-pushes, releases, deploys, publishes, sends, spends money or
  touches another session's or person's work, and never what only you can give (a sign-in, a
  credential, a permission grant, a Mac restart), and none goes within an hour of your own
  message in the tab, which may have asked it to hold, nor before your next message when the
  one that started the turn held it (`don't push until I say so`). Your other `NEEDS YOU` lines
  stay on the menu bar. An agent still waiting after three such answers or an hour is put on
  the menu bar at once as refusing the standing go-ahead, and nothing more is typed to it; one
  that waits for memory or disk room as the answer told it is not. The primer and `aterm help`
  now say that a go-ahead for an agent's own reversible work is never a `NEEDS YOU` item, and
  that a decision to do anything irreversible still is.

- **A slow harness upgrade check leaves the idle point free to continue.** The check runs
  outside the point with one read in flight for the session. A newer package activation
  invalidates an older answer, so a late "no upgrade" result cannot consume its only look.

- **Land keeps an incomplete repository count unknown.** When Git refuses a work count or
  warns that it omitted reference data, the harness no longer treats the result as clean.
  A failed count over a branch with no commits needs a separate successful Git read to
  confirm that state, together with complete stash and remote-reference reads.

- **Read-only approvals follow shell paths and environment expansions more carefully.** The
  harness now holds relative paths, globs and recursive home-directory reads to the secret
  rules, and refuses expansions that can print credentials, including Zsh flags inside a
  braced expansion. A glob in one command no longer makes a separate command in its pipeline
  unproven. Awk options that macOS interprets differently from GNU awk are refused.

- **`aterm harness accounts use <label> --cli codex|grok|kimi` says what a launch does under the
  pin.** It said the supervisor moves Claude Code sessions to the account at their next turn end,
  which no other CLI's sessions do. It now says what a worker or launch aterm makes then does, as
  the launch decides it: takes the pinned account (under rotation off too), takes another account
  while another Mac's claim holds the pinned one, or is refused, in the launch's own words. On a
  Codex build that ignores `CODEX_AUTH_PATH`, pinning an account with a login of its own now says
  every worker is refused under that pin, and names the way back (`aterm harness accounts use
  --auto --cli codex`, `aterm pkg update codex`). `accounts use --auto` says what a launch takes
  once the pin ends, instead of when a session leaves the account. Claude Code's words are
  unchanged.

- **Under `[harness] accounts = "off"`, a launch refused for a pin another Mac holds names the way
  back.** Where the pinned account was not this Mac's to use (another Mac's claim held it, or
  this Mac could not record a claim on it), the refusal said so and stopped, with the claim's end
  in unix seconds. It now names `aterm harness accounts use --auto --cli <cli>`, after which a
  launch takes no account and runs on the login its starter carries, and gives the claim's end as
  a UTC time. The launch, the accounts report and `accounts use` say it alike, for every CLI.

- **Autopilot Land no longer lands with work left on another branch, in a submodule, or never
  pushed.** Land's repository check now counts a submodule commit the submodule's own remote
  does not have (a pushed record of it points the remote main at a commit nobody can fetch);
  the commits and stash entries a session left on another branch it used (the branches its
  own worktree moved through since it began, and the ones its commands created, never another
  session's); and, where a remote is configured but nothing was ever pushed to it, every
  commit. A session that moved into a submodule is checked against the project around it as
  well as the submodule. A read of any of these that git refuses keeps the landing open. The
  check reads only the local repository and fetches nothing.

- **A codex-alab turn too quick for a status sample is in the session log.** aterm reads a
  codex-alab's working and done reports every 50 to 250 ms, so a turn that began and ended
  between two reads had no turn in `log` and woke no `await log close=turn` unless its rollout
  was read. aterm now keeps when the last four turns began and ended, at the time their bytes
  arrived, and logs such a turn at those times (`src=engine conf=claim`), once, even beside a
  rollout that read it first. A claimed turn whose end was never kept closes `out=unknown` when
  the next one begins. Such turns share the 20-then-one-a-second allowance of the session's
  `program` marks, and more than four between two reads lose the oldest.

- **Under Land, a relaunched Muse Code or agy no longer types "continue where you left
  off".** After a crash, an aterm restart or a stall, Claude Code's relaunch under Land types
  nothing and lets Land decide what comes next. Muse Code's and agy's relaunches typed Cruise's
  carry-on instead, which starts again work Land was wrapping up. Now they type nothing under
  Land either, and Land decides the point. Under Cruise, a relaunched Muse Code or agy whose
  last reply said the work was done gets Cruise's done check in place of the carry-on, as
  Claude Code does.

- **Under Land, a person's quick question no longer parks a session that worked under Off.**
  A session driven by hand under Autopilot Off and then switched to Land took the person's
  next quick question for the session's opening message. Land left it to them and rested with
  the work unlanded. The same happened to a conversation resumed with `claude --continue` in a
  new tab. Now a session that ran under Off, or a conversation resumed by its own launch, is
  mid-session, and Land carries the work on after the reply. The reverse is fixed too. A
  program started fresh in a reused tab could get its first question sent before the harness
  saw its start screen, by typing ahead or with `claude "<question>"`. That question was
  taken as mid-session, and Land typed its instruction after it. Now it is that program's
  opening message, and it stays the person's.

- **Cruise no longer stops for good while the agent's own background work runs.** A turn
  that ends while a dev server, a monitor or a long workflow of the agent's runs is carried
  at that break, and four causes held the carry there long after they had passed. A Mac
  wake's settle never ran out at such a break. A usage limit stayed open after the agent
  resumed and worked past its reset. A context wall compacted while the work ran left its
  continuation owed, with no point to type it. A sign-in wall a supervisor told the disk-free
  ask stayed told after that supervisor ended, so the ask waited on a sign-in long gone. Now
  the wake's settle holds the carry only until it runs out, a limit past its reset and grace
  holds nothing and closes at the agent's first turn past it, the compaction's continuation
  is typed at the break in the carry's place, and a new supervisor's first turn end tells the
  window what holds the session now. A cause that still stands still holds.

- **`aterm ctl hwkey` reaches no clipboard.** `hwkey` posts real key events, which take the
  person's own key path with no mark of their own, so `hwkey v mods=cmd` reached Edit ▸ Paste
  (by its key equivalent, or the hard-wired ⌘V) and pasted the person's clipboard into a
  session the client could read, `hwkey c mods=cmd` copied a selection onto it, and a Copy or
  Paste binding, or an Editor's C-y, was open the same way. Now aterm records each key `hwkey`
  posts and tells it from a person's as it dispatches it: its dispatch, and a menu or toolbar
  item it chose, run as a control client's gesture, whose copy and paste are refused as the
  other control verbs' are. `hwkey`'s plain typing, and the person's own ⌘C, ⌘V, Edit menu and
  typing, are unchanged.

- **The stats lens copies nothing for `aterm ctl hwkey`.** A keyboard lens takes ⌘⇧C (its CPU
  diagnostic report) and ⌘C or a Copy binding (its sentence) before the Edit menu does, and
  neither copy asked whose key it was: `hwkey c mods=cmd,shift` with the lens open overwrote
  the person's clipboard. Both copies now refuse a control client's key. The person's ⌘⇧C and
  ⌘C in the lens are unchanged.

- **A key `aterm ctl hwkey` posted while a tab was starting reaches no clipboard either.**
  Keys typed while a new tab or window starts, a menu command is pending or an update
  finishes are held and replayed after, and aterm told an `hwkey` key from the person's only
  when it replayed it, by the event being handled then: a burst's Paste binding held behind
  its own New Tab could replay as the person's and paste their clipboard into the new tab,
  and the person's own held ⌘V could be refused. aterm now decides whose key it is as it
  arrives and keeps that with the held key.

- **`aterm ctl hwkey` stops posting rather than lose track of its keys.** aterm remembers each
  key `hwkey` posts until it handles it, so it can tell it from the person's. Past 40000
  waiting keys it forgot the oldest, which then ran as the person's, Paste included. Now a
  burst stops with `ERR hwkey: busy` instead, and a key the system took before aterm saw it
  (an input method's) no longer holds a place.

- **A control client's key or click no longer marks a session's news as seen.** A session
  with news the person has not looked at (its presence reads `story`) keeps that mark until
  they press a key or click in it, but an `aterm ctl hwkey` key or a `pointer` click counted as
  that press, so a driving agent could clear news the person never saw. Now only the person's
  own key or click does.

- **A key `aterm ctl hwkey` posted answers none of the person's questions.** A confirmation
  sheet (a multi-line paste of the person's clipboard, Quit or Close while a program runs, the
  sudo password sheet) took Return and Escape without asking whose key it was, so `hwkey return`
  could paste the person's clipboard into a session the client reads, or answer a Close. Now a
  posted key that reaches a confirmation, or the in-window paste and close questions, is
  dropped; the person's own Return and Escape answer them as before, and a control client
  answers a close with `confirm yes|no`.

- **A control client's C-s C-s in the Editor recalls none of the person's searches.** Each
  Editor view remembered one last search for every input, kept even when nothing matched: a
  client's `key ctrl+s` `key ctrl+s` put the person's last query (a token they checked for,
  say) in the minibuffer the client reads, and its search-next stepped to that query's matches.
  Now input without clipboard authority (a control client's) recalls only a search it accepted
  itself, as it keeps a kill ring and a keyboard macro of its own. The person's searches are
  unchanged.

- **A control client's Find Next in a terminal recalls none of the person's finds.** Find
  Next, and `^S` in an empty find field, recall the last find accepted, kept even when
  nothing matched, and one find served everyone: a client's `invoke` of Find Next opened the
  find bar on the person's last query. Now a control client recalls only a find it accepted
  itself, as in the Editor. The person's finds are unchanged.

- **A control client's C-x e in the Editor replays none of the person's keyboard macro.** A
  macro keeps the text typed while it was recorded, and every Editor view shared one macro: a
  client's `key ctrl+x` `key e`, or its `act` of call-last-kbd-macro, replayed the person's
  typing (a password, say) into a document it could read back, its keys while the person
  recorded joined their macro to run later with the person's authority, and its own macro
  replaced theirs. Now input without clipboard authority (a control client's) records and
  replays a macro of its own, as it keeps a kill ring of its own. The person's macros are
  unchanged.

- **`aterm harness accounts --cli codex` names the pinned account when a worker takes it.**
  Under a pin on an account that is signed in here, `next:` named another account and called
  the pinned one "the account in use", though a worker starts on it. It now names the pinned
  account, for Grok Build and Kimi Code CLI too. Where no Codex can start at all (no
  atpkg copy and no `codex` on `PATH`), `next:` says Codex CLI is not installed and gives
  `aterm pkg install codex`, as `aterm ai doctor` does, instead of naming an account.
- **A Codex build that runs only this machine's own login says what that login needs.** Under
  the owner's pin on an account with a login of its own, with this machine's own account signed
  out, `aterm ai doctor` called Codex `ok` and "signed in". It now reads `signed-out`, and the
  step it names, in its `NEEDS YOU:` line and in `aterm ai login codex` with no terminal, is
  that account's sign-in at a terminal and then its pin; `aterm ai login codex` says the
  sign-in alone does not end the refusal. Under a pin on an account of its own that is not
  signed in here, a launch, the doctor and `aterm ai review` give the refusal the accounts
  report gives (that build never runs such an account), not that account's missing sign-in,
  which would not end it. An account on this machine's own login with no login stored here
  (never signed in here, or its login removed since) is called not signed in here rather than
  signed out, and is not told its sign-in signs it in "again"; a stray capital in the advice to
  pin it is gone.
- **Renewing Codex's account on this machine's own login with Codex's login in the OS keyring
  gives a reason that fits.** The refusal said a sign-in would replace this machine's own login
  instead of making the account's, but that login is the account's. It now says Codex would
  write the pool's staged sign-in into the keyring, never into the home it stages, so that
  sign-in is not made, and that Codex's own `codex login` at a terminal signs the account in.
  An account with a login of its own keeps the earlier reason.

- **A fleet Mac reads its book while a heartbeat rewrites it.** A read of aterm's private
  state files (the fleet book, the issuer's copy of it, the fleet key) that opened one just
  before another write replaced it was refused as "it has another link", so for that instant
  the reader found the file empty: a session another Mac held could name its holder
  "node 4126e5cd" instead of "127.0.0.1 (node 4126e5cd)". Such a read now takes the file as
  it stood when it was opened; a file with a second link is still refused.

- **Joining ALab says what is true.** An invite's phrase sheet and `aterm members invite` now
  say 10 minutes (the phrase's real life; an Allow's is 5). A Mac a member allowed on a vault
  with no membership log says "Allowed into ALab … pending" until an admin Mac's approver
  records it, not "Joined". The approver logs each Mac by how it got in ("by a member's Allow"
  or "by the join password"), not "as the vault is open". `aterm secrets` no longer says an open
  vault lets in every machine that asks: since F10 a Mac joins by a person's Allow on any
  member (or the join password, or approval by code). A Mac waiting on, or removed from, a vault
  other than ALab is told an admin Mac approves its code, not to press Allow on a Mac in ALab.

- Pool supply and warm-account wall counts use the census's selected member heartbeats.
  Reports from denied nodes or labels, and reports superseded by a newer heartbeat, no longer
  remove an available account from supply or invent an account shortfall.

- **A clock correction cannot keep a swarm member online or its census cache fresh.**
  Future-dated contacts and heartbeat receipts no longer outrank known earlier evidence.
  A member with only future contact times remains admitted but unheard, and either census
  reader recomputes a cache generated ahead of this Mac's clock.

- Fleet reads dated after the current clock stay visible as older information and do not
  count or send notices. A clock correction also makes the next enabled Fleet poll due
  immediately and refreshes badges when polling is off; future-dated fabric needs show
  an unknown age.

- **A Mac that joins the fleet at any member reaches every member.** Until the vault's
  membership log reaches every Mac, only the Mac that minted the fleet's join code took in a
  Mac that joined somewhere else: a Mac that joined at another member while that one was away
  stayed unknown to most members, so `aterm ctl --host` to it and its drives of them were
  refused, and its `aterm ctl survey --fleet` listed a handful of Macs, with no end in sight.
  Every member now takes each signed entry it hears from another member's book, so a new
  Mac spreads member to member with no Mac gathering them. A Mac's `aterm fleet peers rm` of
  a member that another member still lists lasts until its next heartbeat; a new fleet
  secret, or the membership log, keeps a Mac out.

- **A fleet Mac's heartbeat no longer stalls on members that left.** Each heartbeat asked
  the members that last answered this Mac first, and gave each the whole round: two laptops
  that had answered last and then left cost about 6 s each, so every heartbeat reached nobody
  and never looked for members on the network, until those laptops came back. With every
  member up, each Mac heard the same three members forever. A heartbeat now passes over a
  member that stopped answering after one miss, gives each member a quarter of the round,
  keeps a quarter for members found on the network, and asks, beside the member that
  answered last, the members it asked longest ago, so it hears every member in turn.

- **A fleet heartbeat can no longer be held up by adverts nobody answers.** When a heartbeat
  looked for members on the network, it looked up each advertised host name in turn and
  waited as long as macOS did: about 5 s for each name nobody answers, so any device on the
  network could hold a heartbeat for minutes, and a laptop's heartbeat on rejoining a network
  was dropped meanwhile. The heartbeat now looks every name up at once and waits for them no
  longer than its own time allows.

- **NEEDS YOU reports keep earlier messages and wrapped words.** Three ways a need never reached
  the menu bar and window border, or reached them cut, are gone. A turn that ends while the
  agent's own background work still runs was read by its last message alone, so a need written
  earlier in that turn was lost once Cruise carried the work on. A declared wake that came due at
  that moment typed its line before the needs were read, so even a need in the last message was
  lost. And a need that Claude Code, agy or Muse Code wrapped onto a second row starting with a
  capital letter, a backtick or a path was cut at the end of its first row (`grant aterm
  (dev).app the Accessibility permission in System`). Now such a turn is read whole, as any
  turn end is, before anything is typed into it, and a row is read as the rest of the line above
  it when the row above had no room left for its first word, so a wrapped need is read whole
  while a line whose next word would have fit above stays its own. A space consumed after an
  exactly-full row still counts against the next row's room. A hard-broken token and separate
  words can draw identical screen rows, so screen-only reconstruction keeps word-wrap spacing
  rather than guessing a token's original spelling.

- **Disk cleanup keeps retired build folders while programs use them.** The old verifier's
  snapshots, cross-platform build folders, lock directory and snapshot Git metadata now
  receive the same active-process checks as other build caches. Interrupted snapshot
  cleanup resumes from a durable record of the exact directories it admitted; moved or
  replaced folders and work written afterward stay protected.

- **Setup that macOS's Quit & Reopen relaunched no longer stalls on the debugger row.** Pressing Quit & Reopen in Full Disk Access's dialog mid-setup relaunches aterm, and the relaunched window resumed the run without admitting it again. The debugger step counts only this window's own admission, so it waited for a press on System State for as long as aterm ran, and the run never finished. Now a startup that resumes an unfinished, unstopped run whose plan has aterm's own permissions offers that plan back to System State, after Quit & Reopen, an update's relaunch, or a heal or Restore that starts setup again. The page answers it by itself, as the first launch's does, while the run goes on. That answer is this window's own admission: nothing new is saved and the run is not held, and the debugger step goes on without a press, still after the run's Local Network step. A Mac whose debugger question was already asked is asked nothing again, and a revision whose debugger outcome an earlier launch recorded keeps it. A window that already admitted the plan itself, a Stop, or a choice made since lets the offer go.

- **agy's live upgrade reads agy 1.4.10's one-subagent row.** agy 1.4.10's `invoke_subagent`
  makes one subagent, and its row says `Created the following subagent:` where earlier builds
  said `subagents:`. The restart's transcript guard matched only the plural, so on 1.4.10 it
  never read a subagent open. agy's footer counts a working subagent, so its screen does not
  read idle while one works, and that held the restart in a live `lab agy-upgrade`; the
  transcript guard, one of the restart's witnesses of running work, was dead. The guard reads
  both spellings, and the lab's subagent leg now asks the guard itself, of agy's live
  transcript, whether it reads the working subagent open.

- **A control client cannot paste the person's clipboard.** `aterm ctl invoke Paste`, and a
  palette Paste row a client chose, put the clipboard into the front terminal, the find field
  or the rename field, where the client could read it back (`text`, `find status`, the tab's
  title), and the clipboard is where passwords go. Now a control client's paste reads no
  clipboard: it answers `ERR Paste: the clipboard is the person's own…`, logs the refusal, and
  every key, text, paste and mouse event a client sends is marked as the client's, so any paste
  it reaches refuses it. A client's `key cmd+v` was never a paste (the program gets it as a
  key) and still is not. The person's ⌘V, Paste binding, Edit ▸ Paste and right-click paste
  are unchanged. In a development build, `ATERM_DEBUG_PASTE_FILE` text (no clipboard) still
  pastes for `invoke Paste`, and `ATERM_DEBUG_PERSON_INVOKE=1` makes `invoke Paste` and
  `invoke Copy` the person's, as the Linux lab's clipboard rows now launch with.

- **A control client cannot write the person's clipboard.** `invoke Copy` copied the front
  terminal's selection, `invoke CopySessionId|CopyCwd` and the tab menu's Copy rows copied a
  session id or a directory, a client's `key enter` on an open fact menu's Copy path, Copy
  branch or recovery row copied it, and with `copy_on_select` on a client's double-click (`pointer
  click` twice, or an Owner client's `mouse press … count=2`) copied the word it selected, each
  over what the person had copied. Now none copies for a control client: the refusal is
  logged and an `invoke` answers with it, and the selection is still made. The person's ⌘C,
  Copy binding, Edit ▸ Copy and copy-on-select are unchanged, and so is the `copy` verb, which
  copies the selection on purpose under the `clipboard-write` grant.

- **A selection a control client started copies nothing when the person lets go.** With
  `copy_on_select` on, a client (an Owner client, a program in the front session, or a fleet
  member) could press with `mouse press` (a double-click's `count=2` included) and never
  release, or drag the person's own selection with `mouse move`. The person's next left
  release then copied the client's selection over their clipboard, and on Linux set PRIMARY to
  it, even a release that only ended a ⌘-click on a link or a click that closed a menu. Now a
  selection remembers that a client started or dragged it, and its end copies nothing on select
  whoever releases the button; the refusal is logged. The person's own selections copy as
  before.

- **A control client's yank in the Editor reads none of the person's kills.** Every Editor
  view shares one kill ring, and the person's C-k, C-w, M-w and grid copies go on it and on the
  clipboard. A client's `key ctrl+y` and `alt+y` inserted those kills, older ones too, into a
  document it could read back, and a client's own kills went on the person's ring for their
  next C-y. Now input without clipboard authority (a control client's) kills to and yanks from
  a ring of its own, so a client can still cut and yank its own text, and the person's ring and
  clipboard never see it. The person's kills and yanks are unchanged.

- **A control client's `act` on a native Copy button copies nothing.** About's Copy Build
  Information, Settings' copy-path button, Recovery's Copy Diagnostics and a Markdown view's
  Copy wrote the clipboard when a control client pressed them with `act` or sent the view a
  key. Now the view shows that the clipboard is the person's own, and the person's press
  copies as before.

- **Joined Macs keep their Fleet view current by default.** A member used to read in
  the background only with `[fleet] watch = true`, so its menu could keep an old snapshot
  until opened. Background reads now start with no watch setting, using the normal
  one-minute interval and existing backoff while peers are away. `watch = false` and
  `[swarm] enabled = false` stop automatic reads on every member; explicit refresh
  requests remain available.

- **`aterm harness accounts --cli codex` names the account a worker really takes, or says that
  none does.** With no account active, `next:` now names the row a Codex, Grok Build or Kimi
  Code CLI launch takes, instead of calling this machine's own login "the account in use" under
  `active: none` and naming another row. Where the owner's pin is on a row that is not signed in
  here, which refuses every launch, `next:` says none and why. A row in use that is signed out,
  not signed in here or at its limit says so in `not next:`, so a lone Kimi or Grok row with no
  login no longer suggests listing another account. Where Codex keeps its login in the OS
  keyring, `next:` says that a worker takes no row, the pin included, under every rotation
  mode, and the `rotation off:` line then names `cli_auth_credentials_store = "file"` rather
  than `"early"`, which would change no launch. An aterm.toml that is not valid TOML is named
  as such on that line, with where the parser stopped and why.
- **`aterm ai doctor` names a refused launch of a pooled CLI, and whose act ends it.** Before,
  it said such a CLI was plainly `ok`. Where the owner's pin is on a row that is not signed in
  here, the row now reads `signed-out`, and its fix is that row's sign-in (`aterm ai login
  <id>`), which aterm runs itself where it can. Under a pin on a row of its own on a Codex
  build that keeps only this machine's login, or a pin or roster that names no row a launch
  can take, the row still reads `ok`, warns and says why, and names what ends it as a
  `NEEDS YOU:` step (`aterm harness accounts use <label> --cli codex` where that does). A launch
  that another Mac's lease or warm set holds back ends by itself, so the row only notes it.
  `aterm ai login codex` gives the launch's refusal instead of saying the roster lists no email.
  Under `[harness] accounts = "off"` with no pin, the doctor judges this machine's own login,
  which a plain launch runs on, so its sign-out or limit shows, and `aterm ai review` skips that
  CLI where that login is recorded signed out or at its limit, where it used to run it there. A
  row the pool recorded signed out no longer counts as "signed in here", and its sign-out is
  quoted as recorded, with when, instead of being called a login wall. The accounts help now
  says that Codex's JSON report carries each row's email.
- **`aterm ai login` with no terminal names the step a refused launch needs.**
  Where the doctor's step for a pooled CLI is a change to the owner's pin or roster (a pin
  naming no row; on a Codex build that keeps only this machine's login, a pin on a row of its
  own), or the sign-in of the pinned row that the pool's own sign-in does not make, `aterm ai
  login <id>` run with no terminal told a person to run `aterm ai login <id>` at a terminal, a
  sign-in that does not end the refusal. It now names the doctor's step and the launch's
  refusal, and exits 2.
- **A long fact in `aterm ai` and `aterm ai doctor` is cut after a whole word, and says so.**
  The text cut each row's fact at 400 bytes, mid-word and unmarked, so a refused launch's
  reason could stop at `…refused: Thi`. The cut now falls after the last whole word that fits
  and ends in an ellipsis and a pointer to `--json`, which carries the whole fact.
- **Under a pin on a Codex row of its own, a refused launch no longer says when the walled
  row on this machine's login serves again.** On a Codex build that keeps only this machine's
  login, with the owner's pin on a row of its own and the row on this machine's login at its
  usage limit, the refusal said no Codex account could run until that limit ended, but the pin
  keeps refusing every launch after it. It now says that row serves once that pin ends and
  its limit ends: `aterm harness accounts use --auto --cli codex` ends the pin at any time, and
  that row's own pin (`aterm harness accounts use <label> --cli codex`) ends it once its limit
  has ended. Where that row is signed out, it says that its pin follows its sign-in.
  `aterm ai review` says the same.

- **A Mac installed without a window can ask to join ALab.** install.sh's windowless lanes
  (SSH, `--no-open`, Linux) run `aterm members join --no-wait`, which stopped at once with
  "this Mac's node key: fleet-peers's lock: … it is open to other users (want 0700)": the
  installer makes aterm's state folder readable by others, and a new home has none. The join
  now makes that folder private first, as `aterm fleet init` and `fleet join` do, so it asks
  every member and a person can press Allow.
- **aterm no longer freezes for seconds when the permission walk's helper panel appears.** The
  panel's aterm icon was made by macOS's icon service the first time the panel drew, on the
  thread that draws every window; on a busy Mac that took 7.76 s. The icon is now asked of macOS
  (or, failing that, read from aterm's own icon file) and drawn into plain pixels on a separate
  thread, in the panel's light or dark look so it keeps the system icon style (Dark, Tinted,
  Clear) and is made again when that look changes. It is made sharp enough for any screen the
  panel moves to. The panel shows at once with a plain rounded square where the icon goes, and
  the icon appears when it is ready; a drag started before then carries the square. aterm's
  alerts (the paste confirmation, the `sudo` password sheet, quit and close confirmations) show
  the same ready-made icon instead of asking the icon service as they draw.

- **Allow on a busy member tells the new Mac to Allow again.** When a member was busy
  publishing or applying the vault as its phrase was typed, the join waited up to a minute
  for it, past the three seconds the exchange may take: the new Mac read only "the other
  Mac closed the join exchange", and through the node job the member could even mark it let
  in while it wrote nothing. The member now waits a second at most and the new Mac hears to
  Allow it again once that pass ends.

- **On Linux, joining ALab says to name a member instead of finding none.** Linux has no
  Bonjour browse here, so `aterm members join` there always said no ALab member answers,
  and `install.sh` on Linux asked nobody and left nothing behind, silently. It now says to
  name a member with `aterm members join --at <host>`, and the install lane joins the ALab
  vault and starts the vault subscriber, as it did before the members verb, and shows why
  it asked no member.

- **A Mac set up with no window keeps asking ALab's members until one lets it in.**
  `install.sh` over SSH or with `--no-app` asked the members once and left nothing
  behind, so a member asleep, away or restarting aterm at that moment never showed the
  request, and when none answered the lane said nothing at all. It now also joins the ALab
  vault and starts the Mac's vault subscriber, which asks the members again every minute
  while the Mac waits, and says so when no member answered yet.

- **`aterm members join` no longer loops on a Mac that was already let in.** Run again on
  a Mac a member had let in, it said "press Allow on any Mac in ALab" and waited for good,
  while every member it had told refused an Allow for it. It now says the Mac was allowed
  and makes sure it follows the vault. A Mac that lost what a member handed it (a crash or
  a dropped network mid-join) shows its request again on that member, so an Allow there
  lets it in.

- **A Mac let in by the phrase with no window open keeps following the vault.** On a
  Mac set up over SSH, with `--no-app`, or on Linux, `aterm members join <phrase>` wrote
  `~/.secrets` but started no vault subscriber, so the Mac never took a later vault change
  while it said "needs no one here", and `aterm members status` said it "finishes by
  itself". The run now starts the subscriber (a person's Sync off stays off), and both say
  `aterm secrets agent on` when none runs.

- **The Fleet menu keeps a partly read Mac visible.** When a peer reports several
  aterm instances but the read covers only its primary, the menu says `1 of N aterm
  instances read` and keeps the Mac out of the quiet group. Known needs and working
  agents keep their counts; an unread instance does not create a new need.

- **With rotation off, a launch never starts on an AI account another Mac holds.** Under
  `[harness] accounts = "off"`, a session started on the owner's pinned account even where
  another Mac's claim held it, and its own claim was made after the start and its answer
  ignored. Now such a launch is refused with the reason (no worker is started), as it is
  where this Mac cannot record its claim on an account that is not its home, and the claim is
  recorded before the session starts.

- (developer tool) **`lab swarm partition`'s accounts plane judges production's turn end.** Its
  model let a session leave an account whenever another Mac's claim was senior, which is not
  what aterm does, so "one user per account after the heal" passed by the model's own rule. It
  now asks aterm's own turn-end advice under the Mac's `[harness] accounts` mode.

- **A Mac that sleeps, or whose aterm window quit or crashed, gives its AI accounts back to the
  other Macs within about two hours.** A Mac's account claims were given up only by its own
  window's look, so a Mac whose window had quit (its node job still answering on the LAN) kept
  its claims up to a day, and a sleeping laptop held its home account on every other Mac until
  it woke. Now the node job looks every 5 minutes while no window runs, and before the Mac
  sleeps the window gives up the claims it no longer uses and keeps the rest at most two hours.
  The first usage reading after waking takes them back, keeping their place.

- **A session on an AI account another Mac now holds leaves it at its next turn end, even with
  no other account free.** When two Macs used one Claude Code account across a network split,
  the heal settled which Mac's claim was senior, but the junior Mac's session moved off only
  under `[harness] accounts = "early"` and only when another account was free. Under `"wall"`,
  or with every other account at a limit, low or held, it kept using the account beside the
  senior Mac until a limit or the session's end. Now, under `"early"` and `"wall"`, it moves at
  its turn end to an account it may use (a low one too), and with none it waits: the harness
  types nothing into it, and asks again every few minutes, until an account opens or the
  other Mac lets the account go. `accounts = "off"` still moves nothing.

- **Adding to a set of `if-absent` secrets while another Mac removes the set no longer stops every
  Mac reading the vault.** Once the two Macs met again, the added entry pointed at an anchor that
  was gone: Macs on the new build failed every vault read, admin Macs' passes failed, and the next
  change an admin made reverted the other side's edits. The orphaned entry is now left out, so the
  set goes as a whole, and an admin that cannot lay the log over the vault text never writes that
  text over it.

- **A vault change whose publish was cut short still reaches every Mac.** When `aterm secrets set`
  was interrupted, or every server's reply was lost, after a server had stored the change, Macs on
  the new build waited for good on records only that Mac had and kept the old value, and admin
  Macs stopped letting new Macs in. The publishing Mac now keeps those records aside before it
  sends, takes them in on its next pass and sends them on, so every Mac gets the change by itself.

- **A secret two Macs changed while apart shows as a conflict, and removing a Mac never undoes an
  edit made elsewhere.** Removing a Mac seals every secret again under a new key. After a split,
  that on one side beat a real change or removal on the other about half the time, so a rotated
  token could revert or a deleted one come back; it no longer wins over a real change. Two real
  changes made while apart are no longer settled quietly by the next background pass: every Mac
  writes the same one, `aterm secrets status` lists the entry under `conflict:`, and `aterm secrets
  set NAME` picks the value, the one already in use included.

- **A revoked Mac can no longer change a secret on other Macs.** `aterm secrets revoke` (and
  `--stolen`) took a Mac out of the vault file but left it in the membership log, so a stolen Mac
  could still sign a new value for, or delete, a shared secret such as a GitHub token, and every
  Mac on the new build wrote it. Revoke now takes the Mac out of the log too, and nothing it signs
  afterwards counts.

- **A secret an admin outside a host list removes is gone on every Mac in that list.** An admin
  Mac that is not in a host list (the release ring, say) holds none of that list's keys in the
  membership log, so `aterm secrets unset NAME --for <hosts>` there took the entry out of the
  vault file but left it in the log: the list's Macs on the new build kept the file, and an admin
  inside the list put it back into the vault on its next pass. Each publish there also wrote the
  whole list again, which could undo a change made on another Mac while the two were apart. Such
  an admin now writes only what it changed in the list, a removal included, and nothing where the
  list did not change.

- **`aterm harness accounts login|renew` and `aterm ai login` judge the Codex a worker runs.**
  With no codex-alab from atpkg, a worker aterm starts types plain `codex`, which aterm cannot
  read before it runs, so it runs only this machine's own login; but a sign-in judged the
  `codex` in `~/.local/bin` instead, and where that was a newer codex-alab, `accounts renew` of
  the row on this machine's own login staged it a login of its own, after which no row was left
  that a worker could run. Sign-ins, their reports and the `aterm ai` facts now read the same
  program a worker runs, and refuse that row there as they do on any other Codex that keeps no
  row's login its own.

- **`aterm ai review` runs under the account a launch would take, and not at all where a launch
  is refused.** For Kimi Code CLI, Grok Build and Codex, a review picked its own row: with the
  pin on an account not signed in here, or on one the roster does not list, every launch was
  refused while the review ran on another account or on this machine's own login, and counted
  the outcome there; with this machine's own account held for another Mac, a launch took
  another account while the review ran on it. A review now takes the account a launch takes
  as the records stand (a launch's own usage read can still move it), and where that launch is
  refused it runs no reviewer and says why.

- **Membership records keep travelling when the log forks into hundreds of heads.** A seated
  key (a removed Mac's too) can sign records that each start a branch of the log. Each pull
  named every branch it held in its request, and past about 125 branches the request outgrew
  the URL limit, so every Mac's record sync and every server's pull failed on every server,
  with nobody acting. A pull now names the branches that fit, the ones that cover the most of
  the log first, and the server sends what lies past them.

- **Commons repair between Macs that already agree no longer reads the membership log over and
  over.** Each Commons exchange between two Macs holding the same records read, and checked
  every signature in, the whole membership-record file about a dozen times per side, and
  peers redial every few seconds, so the aterm app spent CPU continuously with nothing
  changing, more as the log grew. An exchange now reads the file once and again only after it
  takes records or signs some, and runs its second reconcile only when records moved.

- **Every Mac keeps ALab's membership genesis across a change of the vault's key.** A key
  change asks the next release to name the new key and retire the old one. Until a build checks
  the genesis by its digest, every Mac on that release refused the genesis the old key signed,
  lost the log-backed Commons and vault readers that need it, and erased it from its records
  file at the next save, for good. And a genesis signed after a key change was refused by every
  Mac still a release behind, which then downloaded and checked the whole log on every sync for
  nothing. A Mac now takes a genesis signed by the vault's current key, a key its build retired,
  or any key its own vault settings followed to the current one.

- **A vault server keeps ALab's membership genesis after the vault's key changes.** After
  `aterm secrets rotate-key`, servers hold an envelope signed by the new key, while ALab's
  genesis stays the one the old key signed. Until a build checks the genesis by its digest, a
  server that restarted (an app update, a reboot) or started after the change refused that
  genesis: it served no membership records, every Mac re-sent it its whole log on each pass,
  and its next write dropped the genesis from its file. A server now takes a genesis signed by
  any key its envelope's handoff chain names.

- **A vault server that cannot reach one of its peers no longer holds up its pulls from the
  others.** Each vault server pulls new versions and membership records from the other servers
  it hears on the network. It asked them one after another, so a peer that took a pull and never
  answered (a Mac asleep mid-answer, a stalled server) held every pull after it for its whole
  wait, and a peer that was gone was asked twice per vault. A server now pulls from all its peers
  at once, and asks a peer nothing more in that pass once a pull from it fails. It reads at most
  two peers' membership records at a time, so a machine that advertises itself many times
  cannot make it hold a large batch from each at once.

- **Commons repair between two Macs no longer waits on the vault server.** When an exchange
  between two Macs signed records to close a gap in the membership log, it sent them to the
