  vault's server before going on, and a server that took the request and did not answer (a Mac
  asleep mid-answer, a stalled server) held the exchange past its 30-second limit, so it failed
  and the other Mac did not get the records. The records now go to the server on the side, after
  the exchange has them.

- **A Mac with no membership log yet no longer keeps records from a host it cannot check.**
  Until a Mac holds the log's first record (a new Mac, and every ALab Mac until ALab's log is
  started), it can check nothing a vault server sends it, and any machine on the network can
  answer as one. Such a Mac kept whatever it was sent, up to about 63 MB of records written to
  its disk. It now keeps records only when they arrive with the first record they follow from,
  which is how a real vault server sends them. For a vault other than ALab that first record
  must also be signed by the vault's own key: a machine that signed one itself could otherwise
  tie the Mac to a log of its own for good.

- **A vault server that cannot take a Mac's newest membership records no longer trades whole
  logs with it on every sync.** A server can refuse a record a Mac holds (an older build, a
  full store). Each sync then had the server send the Mac its whole log, since it found none of
  the records the Mac named, and the Mac send the server its whole log back, up to 64 MB each
  way every half minute, for good. A sync now also names a few of the records before the newest
  ones, so the server sends only what lies past those, and a Mac sends a server that refused its
  log only the records it gains after that, and its whole log again an hour later. A server
  that was only too busy to read the log (or failed to save it) is sent it again at the next
  sync.

- **The cache preview reports candidate footprints, not promised freed space.**
  `aterm pkg machine cache` keeps observed lock failures visible and explains that cleanup
  rechecks eligibility; build and tooling cache removal also checks active use. A listed
  candidate may stay.

- **AI account claims never fill up.** Each Mac's account-claim row now goes into a table for the current UTC day, and every Mac deletes a day's table two days later, when every row in it has lapsed. Claims keep being recorded however long the swarm runs and through network splits, with nothing to reset. A day's table takes 7,680 rows (960 from one Mac) and then the next day's; a Mac past both keeps to its home accounts until 00:00 UTC. A Mac still on a development build with the earlier claim table is told that table is retired and keeps to its home accounts until it updates (`F19`).

- (developer tool) **`lab mac nux`'s ALab guard no longer reads a browse that never looked as
  no advert.** This Mac's `dns-sd` browse ran under `script`, which flushes its transcript every
  30 s, so stopping it after 3 s left the transcript empty and every row read "no production
  advert from guests". The browse now flushes each line, the guest's browse runs in the guest
  helper, and either browse fails the row unless its transcript shows it started
  (`...STARTING...`) with no failed call.

- **Every vault server now pulls from every other one on the network, not only the first 16 it
  heard.** With about 35 Macs serving, each server pulled membership records from, and each
  Mac's failover asked, the same first 16 servers it heard. A laptop that rejoined after its
  network name expired was heard last everywhere, so its new records reached no other server
  until an admin published again. Each pass now takes the next 16, so every server is reached
  within three passes (about 90 seconds).

- **A post of membership records to a vault server no longer copies the server's whole record
  store three times.** Any Mac on the network may post records to `/v1/alab/records`, and each
  post copied the store in memory once to try the records, again to take them, and a third time
  to write the file; near the store's bound that was several hundred megabytes per post. A post
  now takes its records into the one working copy and writes the file from it.

- **A Mac whose membership-record file grew past 64 MiB takes records and vault changes again
  by itself.** Before the record store was bounded in bytes, 64 records each carrying a 1 MiB
  value (which any seated key, a removed Mac's included, or before ALab's genesis any Mac on the
  network, can sign) made a `records` file the Mac then refused to read: from then on it applied
  no new vault version, synced no records and stopped Commons repair, for good. Such a file is
  now read up to 64 MiB, the records it holds are kept, and the next save rewrites it.

- **Membership records survive a reload after a Mac is admitted a second time.** Once a Mac
  was admitted again after it had signed a record of its own (as Allow again will do), reading
  stored membership records back (each sync, a server's start, a new Mac's first pull) put them
  in an order in which records by Macs admitted after it could not be checked, so about half of
  those were dropped, and the next save erased them on disk. Records are now read back in the
  order of their parents, and a second admission no longer upsets it.

- **Turning the node job off reports a refused stop and keeps its unit for retry.** Cleanup
  no longer says the job stopped after launchd or systemd refused it. An already absent job
  still removes cleanly, and an unreadable status does not count as absence.

- **Membership-log evaluation, founder-recipient squatting, and multi-round Commons record sync.** `Graph::unproved` in `aterm-secrets` no longer lets a removed member's cut-off or self-signed `Admit` squat an unproved Genesis v2 founder's recipient, `Graph::weigh` and `authorized` evaluate quorum and causal-past standing in quadratic bitset passes instead of cubic passes, and `aterm-db`'s multi-round `ALMR` control repair selects missing membership-log records in causal order from Genesis (with wraparound cursor) rather than raw SHA-256 digest order so seats and parent epochs always arrive ahead of child records on the first pass.

- **Automatic build-cache cleanup keeps programs still running from a cache.** A completed
  build's executable, working directory or open files now keep its cache even after Cargo
  releases its locks. The same check protects registered Codex build targets, provisioned
  tools and interrupted cleanup stages; an unreadable ownership scan keeps the cache too.

- **A crashed node job no longer leaves its ALab service advertiser running.** The
  registration helper now ends with the process that started it, including when
  that process is killed outright. Normal shutdown and network departure still
  stop and reap the helper.

- **A fleet dial keeps an earlier address's failure when its connect budget ends.**
  A later address that cannot start before the deadline no longer replaces an
  earlier refusal or proven busy response with a generic timeout. This also keeps
  a refused connection from being classified as listener capacity exhaustion.

- **Allowing a new Mac on a busy member no longer fails as "this Mac holds no applied vault".**
  The member gave up after 5 s when one of its own vault passes held the vault's state, said
  it had no vault, and the run's keyphrase was spent. It now waits up to a minute for the pass
  to end, and if one still holds the state it says so.

- **The node job (`systems.alab.aterm-node`) no longer widens grants, misreports a busy window, or holds the fleet port while it serves nothing.** An `aterm.toml` the job cannot read or parse now starts no fleet listener at all. Before, the job served every member at `drive` in place of what that file allowed, which is not what the window does. A window yields the fleet port only while the job actually serves it (a new `node-port.lock`), so a job with no fleet key yet, one that cannot bind the port, or one whose watch thread failed to start, leaves the port to the window instead of to nobody. While a window runs and takes no hand-over (busy, not yet serving, or silent), a survey or drive is answered `ERR busy: … ask again`, never `window=0` or "no window open", and a spawn opens no second window. A Mac that left a fleet and then formed or joined one gets its node job back (a leave's `fleet-off` stays through `aterm fleet init`). The job's plist now names the app its program belongs to, as that app's `Info.plist` says (`com.aterm.aterm`), as the `secrets watch` job's does, instead of an identifier no app has. `sync.node` rewrites and reloads a job whose plist an earlier build wrote, so a job installed before this fix gets it too. `sync.node` moves a job an SSH-only pass loaded in the background session to the login at the screen. It renews a job that runs a build an update replaced with `launchctl kickstart -k`, and reloads the plist only once launchd has let the old job go. If the login's session refuses the move, the job goes back to the background session rather than staying unloaded. Every `launchctl` call is bounded by a deadline and goes through one seam. The `open -g -a` that opens a window for a fleet spawn is bounded too (30 s), so a stuck `open` no longer holds the connection that asked.

- (developer tool) **`lab aos-repair`'s caret-move lag says when the present it timed is
  known to be the move's.** Its `lag` line's `present_after_move_ms` times the first present
  booked after the move, which can be a glow tick composed before the echo reached the grid
  (one in flight at the move, or one due before the echo arrived) rather than the moved
  caret's own. The line now adds `present_carries_move=`, read from the phase's trace. `true`
  means the first glow tick from a main-loop read just before the move carries the moved cell,
  so the present it timed showed the move; `false` leaves it unknown.

- **`aterm harness accounts` says what rotation off leaves a launch.** Under `[harness]
  accounts = "off"`, `next:` still named the account rotation would pick, for every CLI.
  Now it names the pinned account a Codex worker, or a Grok Build or Kimi Code CLI launch,
  takes then, or says `none` and why: with no pin, or with Codex's login kept in the OS
  keyring (the pin included), a launch takes no account and runs on the login its starter
  carries (this machine's own for a plain one); otherwise it says why the pin cannot be taken.
  Claude Code's report says no session moves, not even onto a pin. A `rotation off:` line
  names what in aterm.toml turns rotation off (`[harness] accounts`, a `harness.accounts`
  filed below another table's header, or `[swarm] enabled = false`) and, where it can, how to
  turn rotation back on. `not next:` and `list another:` are left out, and `aterm
  harness limits` says the same. The JSON report matches (`next.off`, `next.none`).
  `accounts --cli codex` also judges the Codex a worker starts, not the one a person's `codex`
  runs: with no codex-alab from atpkg that is plain `codex`, which runs only this machine's
  own login, even with a newer codex-alab in `~/.local/bin`. Other reports with rotation on
  are unchanged.

- **System monitoring keeps hardware capacity visible while utilization is unread.** CPU
  rows show the known core count before the first interval and while counters pause. `sys`
  keeps a GPU's measured name and core count when its busy reading is unavailable; a measured
  zero remains zero.

- **Agent sessions waiting out a network outage pick up again by themselves.** While a session
  waits at a network error, the window's harness probes api.anthropic.com every 5, 10, then
  15 seconds, and it watches this Mac's network path and routes, which sends nothing; when the
  path comes back or the routes move it probes at once, so a session on the default API route
  continues within seconds of the API answering. A session the probe cannot measure (another
  agent's endpoint, or a route of its own) holds while this Mac's network is gone, for up to an
  hour, and retries once it is back. Claude Code's `/goal` notice that the API was unavailable,
  with no error shown above it, is waited out like any other API error. `harness.probe_api = false`
  turns the probe and the watch off.

- **Cruise and Land no longer type into a network outage at a turn that ended without an
  error.** When this Mac's network path is lost, or the probe measures api.anthropic.com
  unreachable, at the end of a turn that showed no error, the harness now holds the
  continuation, the done check, the answer or Land's instruction, and the tab's state line reads
  `waiting: connection error`. It types the held words once the network is back. Cruise's carry
  at a background break waits for the network the same way. If the probe still reads the API
  unreachable an hour after the outage began, the harness types the words anyway, since the
  agent's last turn did reach the API, and later turns in that outage are not held again. Once
  the harness types at a turn, what it read of the network there no longer holds Cruise's carry
  at the background work that follows.

- **A login-PATH probe that runs past its deadline, or a spare shell aterm discards, no longer
  leaves a child behind that the shell was forking as it was killed.** On macOS a fork in progress
  as a group `SIGKILL` lands puts the new child in the group unsignalled; both sites now take
  `aterm_uds::process::kill_group_until_empty`, which re-sends until the group is empty.

- (developer tool) **A failed `aterm ctl` reply no longer stands in for a reading in eleven
  labs.** `lab forever`, `presence-flap`, `nudge`, `restore`, `seamless`, the codex-alab proof,
  `predict-live`, the Muse and agy upgrade legs and `forever`'s switch-flip read some baselines,
  final readings and guards from a reply whose exit code or `ERR` line went unread, so its empty
  output counted as zero, `None`, `-` or an all-`?` line. In 31 places that value could pass a
  check, or skip a guard, on a build that should fail: a `None` baseline that every count
  exceeds, a failed final `meta` read recorded as the latest look so a standing needs entry
  read as gone, a failed `metrics reset` that let whole-run wakes through END's idle window, a
  failed `meta set autopilot` write counted as the switch. A poll loop or recorder now skips a
  failed read and polls again within its one-minute hang detector; a one-shot reading the
  verdict counts from fails the leg (or says COULD NOT RUN, where that lab already reports a
  desk failure so) with the failed reply; and `lab forever`'s landed checks call "no task
  record invented" UNOBSERVED when no `task` read answered, where a recorder that skips failed
  reads would otherwise have read none as none invented.

- (developer tool) **`lab codex-alab-proof`'s person-exchange leg runs under Land.** Since the
  owner's rulings that Cruise never parks (2026-10-26) and that under Land a person's message is
  theirs only where it opens the session (2026-10-27), codex-alab (its gap 32, build
  0.166.0-dev.14175) continues a person's exchange under Cruise, as aterm's own harness does. The
  leg still ran under Cruise and failed five checks for codex-alab typing `continue@v1` there. It
  now runs under Land, where the person's message opens the session and is left to them
  (`left-to-person@v1`), and the Cruise checks no longer count it among their legs; the control leg
  stays under Cruise. The proof passed 122 checks on 2026-10-29 with that build.

- (developer tool) **`lab codex-alab-proof` no longer fails an unmeasured codex-alab build whose
  rollout opened a leg's every turn.** The rollout check asked each leg for a turn codex's own
  OSC 7501 claim opened, which no run can promise: since fix E1 a partial rollout that opened a
  turn first keeps it. A live run on 2026-10-28 failed the first leg, whose two turns were both
  the rollout's. The check now asks that the leg's log opened a turn, each by a claim or by the
  rollout read strong, that a rollout row reaches a turn, and that none reads exact. A failed
  `log` read fails the leg naming the reply, where it read as a log with no turns, and a failed
  `status` read is named where the leg reports no tap or a stuck one.

- (developer tool) **`lab agy-upgrade` and `lab muse-upgrade` judge the busy-turn leg by the
  agent's own record of the reply.** The leg looked at the screen every 500 ms and read an agent
  gone before the turn's end was seen as one restarted mid-turn. But a turn's end wakes nothing,
  so a correct restart can follow it within one look. A live agy-upgrade on agy 1.4.10 failed
  its leg 5 that way: the stub streamed the reply whole at 00:02:23.467, agy read idle 286 ms
  later, and the SIGTERM came within the second. The leg now reads the agent's own record of the
  turn, once at the landing and once after the restart: agy's `DONE` `PLANNER_RESPONSE` row
  holding the reply to the stub's last tick, and for Muse that reply's
  `assistant_message_committed` event and then its run's `terminal` record saying `completed`
  (Muse's end-of-turn gate runs about half a second between the two). It must be absent at the
  landing and present after the restart. A restart that cut the turn's reply, or Muse's run
  before its end, leaves no such record.

- (developer tool) **The agy labs call agy 1.4.10's tools as it declares them.** agy 1.4.10
  declares every tool with `additionalProperties: false` and renamed or reshaped most of them,
  so `lab agy-upgrade`'s background-task, subagent and daemon legs failed: agy refused each
  scripted call (`additional properties 'Cwd', 'toolAction' not allowed`) and no task or
  subagent ever ran. `run_command` loses `Cwd` and `toolAction`, `invoke_subagent` takes one
  subagent's `TypeName`, `Role` and `Prompt` in place of a `Subagents` list, and `lab
  agy-captures` calls `write_file`, `edit_file` and `ask_question` with the arguments 1.4.10
  declares, in place of `write_to_file` and `replace_file_content`. `lab forever`'s agy read
  call is 1.4.10's `read_file` in place of `view_file`, though no leg runs it (F3 is out of
  agy's reach).

- (developer tool) **`lab seamless`'s hwkey leg reads each key's marks only once the
  session's log has written the key.** A key that opens no burst and finds the session's
  timeline held (by a `log` read, or an events subscriber such as the bridge) is counted at once
  (`status human_seq=`) but written to the log, with any mark it makes, only when an entry next
  reconciles the person (delivered mail or another fabric fact, a control input), which a quiet
  shell tab may never make. A build whose third key wrongly wrote a mark could pass "counted,
  wrote none", and a correct build's second key could wait out the minute for its why=mail mark
  and fail. Once `status` counts the second key the leg adds a topic to the tab, and once it
  counts the third it drops it: each move is recorded under the timeline before its reply and
  writes a held key first, so the marks read after it include the key's. A failed log read now
  fails the leg rather than counting as no marks.

- (developer tool) **`lab forever`'s END no longer fails a resting desk for a status sweep
  a program's write just before the idle window was owed.** The window now waits 2 s after
  `metrics reset` and counts timer wakes, arms and fires from a `metrics` read taken then, while
  it still counts writes from the reset. Its L7 rows (This Mac's landing and landed counts, the
  page's Every session row) say UNOBSERVED when END found no window at rest, instead of
  comparing counts read while tabs still acted.

- **`aterm harness accounts --cli codex` names the account a Codex worker would run on.** On
  a Codex that keeps no account's login its own (OpenAI's, or a codex-alab from before
  cd79a420c), workers run only on this machine's own login, but `next:` still named the next
  account in rotation. It now names that row, or waits until the pool takes it again, or
  says `none` and why. Each account with a login of its own appears under `not next:`, which
  points to `aterm pkg update codex`, and a `this Codex build:` line says why. The JSON
  report matches (`next.only_default`, `next.none`). Claude Code, Grok and Kimi reports, and
  reports on a Codex that keeps `CODEX_AUTH_PATH`'s login, are unchanged.

- **An update keeps an unfinished table cell typed while the replacement starts.** If a cell
  changes after the update's first check, the final check waits with its text intact. Return
  keeps the cell and Escape drops it; the update can then continue.

- **A new Mac joins the ALab vault without waiting for aterm's own permission steps.** Once
  macOS has answered aterm's Local Network question, or this launch of aterm asked it, System
  State's vault join no longer waits behind the Full Disk Access or Developer Tools step aterm
  has on screen, and no longer holds those steps off while it waits for another Mac to approve
  it, so GitHub, publishing and AI credentials arrive minutes sooner on a fresh Mac. Until
  then, including after a relaunch that left macOS's question unanswered, the join still waits
  its turn, since its first look at the network can raise that question.

- **An Install… queued behind a macOS permission step waits until you stop typing.** Once
  the step ends, the Command Line Tools tab a queued press opens waits for 2.5 s without a
  key, as the automatic tab does, so it never takes keys you meant for the page.

- **CSV and TSV rows over 1,024 columns open as text even when the last quoted cell is
  unfinished.** Their contents stay intact, and unfinished cells within the limit remain
  readable in the grid.

- **A vault server no longer stops tending when a LAN name splits a character.** A
  `_alab-vault._tcp` instance whose name put a multibyte character just after
  `alab-secret` made every vault server that heard it panic in its tend loop, so it stopped
  pulling and settling `alab-secrets.local`. Such a name now reads as not a holder.

- **Claude Code's vim NORMAL mode stays dark after an Escape typed right after a letter.**
  When Escape followed a typed letter before the cursor trail had settled on it, the pause
  after Escape could take the letter's light back and hand the composer's row back to your
  typing, so NORMAL's motions (`h`, `l`, `w`) lit the trail. The Escape now settles that
  letter for good.
- **A key typed while the cursor trail weighs a redrawn letter keeps its effect.** When a
  program redraws the line right after a letter you typed (zsh's Ctrl-R search does), the trail
  waits for the cursor to rest before deciding whether to take the letter's light back. Taking
  it back put back how the trail read the row before the letter, which undid an arrow pressed
  in that wait, so the next keys on the row could stay dark. Now the cursor moving after the
  key keeps the letter lit, and a rest takes back only what the letter took, keeping what the
  key changed.

- **Computer monitoring reports measured disk and hardware usage consistently.** Reserved
  free disk blocks stay separate from occupied space and space available to your writes.
  Unread CPU counters add no utilization or history sample, load averages remain load,
  and remote memory or disk probe failures stay unknown. GPU utilization, model and core
  count remain visible independently when only some of them can be read.

- **Cruise recognizes a person's exchange completed before its harness restarts.** If you
  sent a message after the last background-work prompt and its reply reached another
  background-work break before a loop restart, Cruise could retain the old wait for up to
  an hour. The new loop now starts that wait over even when it first sees the completed
  break; a gesture before the last prompt still keeps the existing wait.

- **Computer monitoring keeps missing measurements distinct from zero.** A computer can
  show its CPU cores, total RAM and total disk even when usage has not been read, with
  unavailable usage and free space labeled as such. An unread local CPU sample no longer
  reports an invented 8% or adds it to the history; measured zero remains zero.

- **Tab Control agrees on how many AI CLIs are active.** Its fleet summary, computer
  counts and instance headers use the same observed phase, so a Claude Code or Codex
  waiting on a permission box or question is counted consistently. An unread phase or
  unclassified session stays unknown, and changing a row's display words cannot change
  its activity count.

- **Replacing or dropping the menu-bar semantic-font prewarm worker releases its background thread
  and retained renderer base.** Closing a window or switching fonts now wakes and exits an idle
  `aterm-semantic-font-prewarm` worker instead of leaving the parked thread and its cached font
  faces resident for the life of the process.

- **The permission walk starts by itself on a Mac set up from another.** A Mac moved over with
  Migration Assistant, or one of several Macs sharing a network home, no longer counts the other
  Mac's Full Disk Access or Developer Tools page as its own, so its first launch walks you
  through its pages, even when the other Mac ran aterm 0.145.0 or earlier. A second aterm bundle
  on the same Mac (a dev build beside the release) gets its own first walk too.

- **`aterm doctor` and `aterm init` open no second System Settings page beside the window's
  walk.** The window's `permissions walk now` answer names only the pages still ahead, and names
  a page your Not now holds back. Doctor leaves that page closed and says why, rather than
  opening it itself. A walk already under way takes back a page it had passed with no grant, so
  nothing else opens it beside the walk. An ask for Full Disk Access is no longer answered
  "declined" because of a Not now said to Developer Tools.

- **A walk that `aterm doctor` or `aterm init` asks for waits its turn.** While macOS has
  another question up, or one of aterm's own steps (the folder pass, the Local Network
  question), the walk opens its page only after that question ends. Doctor and init still get
  their answer at once. A Not now you say while it waits holds that page back. Pressing the
  page's own row in System State opens it at once.

- **`aterm init`'s Messages and FaceTime sign-out asks no Accessibility question past your Not
  now or beside the walk's page.** If you said Not now to Accessibility in the window's walk,
  the sign-out leaves macOS's dialog down and goes on to your own Sign Out click. If the walk is
  showing another page, the sign-out only reads the grant and says where to switch it on. A
  `doctor` or `init` that joins a walk already under way keeps your Not now going on, and the
  panel's `Step N of M` counts the page it added.

- **The walk's next page waits for your answer to macOS's Automation question.** Once
  Accessibility reads on, aterm asks macOS whether it may control System Events. The walk's next
  page (Full Disk Access or Developer Tools) used to open a second later beside that question.
  It now opens once you have answered. Nothing else of aterm's (the debugger step, the Local
  Network question, the folder pass, setup) starts beside it either.

- **A Mac whose person steps away before the first walk still gets that walk.** When aterm
  opened while you were away for a minute or more (a long `curl … | bash`, say), System State's
  own Full Disk Access step opened its page without the walk, and later launches then read that
  page as walked, so the walk never came. Its steps now wait for you to come back, and the walk
  starts then.

- **Pressing another permission row while the walk lists Terminal keeps the page you pressed
  for.** Before an empty Developer Tools page, the walk lists Terminal with `spctl`. If you pressed
  another row while that ran, its end brought Developer Tools up over your page and ended the walk
  you asked for. It now opens Developer Tools only while the walk is still waiting for it.

- **`aterm doctor` and `aterm init` run in another terminal send you to that terminal's switch.**
  Run under Terminal or iTerm2, they handed Full Disk Access and Accessibility to aterm's window
  walk, which turns on aterm's switch, not the terminal's that macOS holds responsible. They now
  hand those pages over only when aterm is that app. Elsewhere they open the page themselves and
  name the terminal to switch on.

- **A walk `aterm doctor` gave up waiting for no longer opens beside doctor's own pages.** When
  the window was too busy to answer doctor's walk request in time, doctor opened its pages itself,
  and the window then started the walk anyway, so two System Settings pages opened at once. A
  request its client gave up on now starts no walk.

- **Not now on the walk's Accessibility page holds after a relaunch.** A Not now there used to
  hold the page back from `aterm ctl permissions walk now` only in the window that heard it, so a
  relaunched aterm, or any program sending the verb a minute later, opened Accessibility again.
  aterm now keeps that Not now on disk the way it keeps Full Disk Access's and Developer Tools',
  and only your own press goes past it.

- **The first permission walk waits for macOS's Local Network question.** On a new Mac, the walk
  used to open System Settings' Full Disk Access page a few seconds after launch, while macOS's
  Local Network alert was still up. It now starts once that alert is answered, or once its
  30-second hold ends. If the question has still not come after a minute with you at System
  State and nothing else in the way, the walk goes first, and the question, and every permission
  step after it, the debugger's password dialog included, comes once the walk is over.

- **Moving the pointer no longer holds System State's permission steps.** The Local Network
  question and the steps after it waited for 10 seconds with neither the keyboard nor the pointer
  touched, so a hand resting on the mouse held them, and the first walk behind them, for as long
  as you stayed. They now wait only for 10 seconds without a key typed into aterm. They also wait
  while System Settings still has a question of its own up (its password window, or the Quit &
  Reopen sheet), also after System Settings moves to another Space or is hidden: aterm looks at
  System Settings while you are using it, so it knows that question even with aterm in full
  screen, and stops waiting once that window is gone. Ten minutes after you left it standing,
  the Local Network question and the debugger's password dialog no longer wait for it, but a step
  that opens a System Settings page still waits until aterm sees the question gone. On a Mac whose idle time macOS cannot
  read, a click or key in aterm shows you are there, and one click is enough for the first walk's
  minute of waiting, so setup no longer waits for good, and aterm.log says what holds the Local
  Network question while it waits.

- **After Full Disk Access the walk waits for macOS's Quit & Reopen question.** Switching Full
  Disk Access on makes macOS ask whether to quit aterm now. The walk used to open Developer Tools
  underneath that question, where the link was lost. Its panel now says to choose Later, and the
  next page comes up once you do.

- **The Developer Tools page no longer says Full Disk Access is missing once it is on.** Right
  after you switched Full Disk Access on, the page kept saying aterm could not see the Developer
  Tools list without it. It now reads the list again.

- **The permission walk goes on after Quit & Reopen.** Choosing Quit & Reopen after Full Disk
  Access used to end the walk, so Developer Tools and debugger access waited until you pressed
  Open in System State minutes later. The reopened aterm now picks the walk up at the next page.

- **Install… in the Developer Tools window goes ahead while a walk runs.** A press of the Command
  Line Tools install that came while `aterm doctor`'s or `aterm init`'s walk held the window
  waited behind the walk's page. Your own press now goes first, as every other press does.

- **The walk's `Step N of M` counts only the pages that come up.** Pages the walk skips because
  they are already granted or held back by your Not now no longer count.

- **`aterm ai login` and `aterm ai doctor` print why a sign-in did not start in full.** A
  refusal was cut at 160 characters, often before its reason or the step it named. With no
  terminal, `aterm ai login claude` and `aterm ai doctor` now say why Claude Code's sign-in
  cannot start (accounts.toml is refused or lists your own login with no email, aterm's
  account records cannot be read, or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` names a home of its own) instead of
  sending you to a terminal where it would refuse too. The doctor's `fix:`, `health:` and
  `NEEDS YOU:` lines then name what you do first, such as mending accounts.toml, and the window
  offers no Sign in for that row, instead of `aterm ai login claude`, which would only say why
  it cannot start; Settings still says Claude Code needs you, and its row names that step.
  Account records that cannot be read are no longer reported as a refused accounts.toml.

- **Autopilot Land keeps carrying a session across resumes aterm makes outside the turn-end
  loop.** When aterm resumes a conversation through a cold restore, `aterm ctl restart`, a crash
  relaunch, or a slow startup whose banner stays up past a minute, a message you send before its
  transcript finishes drawing no longer resets the session to a fresh opening exchange. Starting a
  new agent or clearing the conversation in place still opens a fresh exchange of your own.

- **aterm's ALab Commons networking waits for System State's Local Network step before it uses the
  local network.** Before, Commons opened its local network sockets as the window started, so
  macOS's "Allow aterm to find devices on local networks?" came up about a second after a first
  launch, before System State had even shown its plan. Commons now starts once System State's
  Local Network step has asked macOS. On a Mac where an aterm window outlasted the question, it
  starts at once. Where the step will not run, Commons asks by itself, at its first use of the
  local network, when no other macOS question of aterm's is up, and holds off the next one for 30
  seconds from that use. That covers a `[privacy]` switch or `[swarm]` off, Permissions left out of
  the plan, a Cancel or Stop, a network whose only IPv4 addresses are public (the step has nothing
  to ask with there), an aterm window that runs no first-run setup (one started over SSH, say),
  and a terminal session over ssh or `aterm node serve` on a Mac nobody is logged in at. Where
  Commons was about to ask by itself on a network with only public addresses but its first try
  did not reach the network, and the Mac then joins one the step can ask about, Commons waits for
  the step again. It does the same where aterm's notes say macOS asked or answered before but no
  aterm window on this Mac outlasted the question, for example an alert left unanswered when aterm
  quit, or a note another Mac or another copy of aterm (a dev build) left in a shared home folder:
  macOS asks each app on each Mac. A window that used the local network and outlasted the question
  keeps a note of it for its Mac and its copy of aterm, so later launches do not hold off again;
  one that never got to use it (another aterm had Commons) keeps none. A terminal session's use of
  the local network is not taken for aterm's, since macOS asks the app that holds the terminal.
  Until Commons starts, the network view and `aterm db network-state` say why it waits. In an aterm
  window, where aterm heard macOS refuse it the local network (at System State's step, or in a look
  for the ALab vault) and Commons' local network sockets fail, they say so and where to turn aterm
  on (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network), whatever Macs it heard before; where
  the Mac has no network address, they say that instead. A terminal session's or `aterm node
  serve`'s failed sockets say only that they failed, since macOS's switch for a terminal session
  is the terminal app's. Commons uses the local network again within
  seconds of you turning aterm on, with no restart. aterm's other early uses of the local network
  wait for the step too (next entry).

- **aterm's window no longer brings up macOS's Local Network question before System State asks
  it.** Four uses of the local network could still raise it on a first launch, ahead of System
  State's Local Network step. aterm's background setup pass, a few seconds after launch and every
  30 minutes, read which address this Mac uses on its network by opening a network socket toward
  the local network. It now reads that address from the routing table, which uses no network
  socket and asks macOS nothing. System State's Secrets step looked for the ALab vault on the
  network and joined it as soon as it was reached. It now waits for the Local Network step and
  goes on as soon as that step has asked; the setup line in aterm.log says why it waits ("waits
  for System State's Local Network question"). Settings ▸ Harness ▸ Tab Control looked for other
  computers on the network as soon as the page opened. It now looks once the step has asked, and
  the page says why it shows none until then. The window listened for other ALab Macs on the
  network (a Bonjour browse) from launch, to notice a change of network. It now starts listening
  once the step has asked. None of these waits where macOS answered or asked aterm before, or
  where an earlier aterm used the local network. None waits where the step will not run either:
  a `[privacy]` switch or `[swarm]` off, Permissions left out of the plan, a network the step has
  nothing to ask with (only public IPv4 addresses, or IPv6 only), or a window that runs no
  first-run setup, such as one started over SSH. An install with `--no-open` or over SSH
  still joins the ALab vault before any aterm window opens, and that join can still bring the
  question up first.

- **An early account move that could not be checked at once is still proven.** When aterm
  moves a Claude Code tab onto another account at a turn end, ahead of a limit, and cannot
  read where the relaunched tab landed right away (the accounts store busy, say), it now
  tells the tab's harness the move was made at the tab's next turn end. Before, the harness
  never learned of it: the new account was never proven by the turns it served, and every
  other early move on the Mac waited on it.

- **The usage tap reads a tab whose `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set but empty.** Claude Code
  then runs on its default home and login, but every usage reading from it was refused as
  another login's, so the account recorded no figures from that tab and moved nothing early.

- **A `/login` in one tab no longer books another account's limits onto the account it
  replaced.** Claude Code tabs go on naming the account they started on for up to an hour
  after a `/login` elsewhere replaces it. The accounts sync now books no transcript limit or
  answer across a `/login` to the account named before it, and after the newest one only to
  an account with a login on this Mac, so a row the `/login` replaced is not shown limited by
  the new login's wall.

- Vault reconciliation preserves authenticated Commons admission evidence across
  server partitions. Approved newcomers retain their existing control access after
  machine-name collisions are resolved; unapproved entries and primary exclusions
  stay outside Commons.

- A machine's first Commons approval survives vault reconciliation when another
  branch already listed its recipient without approval. Control exclusions for
  recipients previously approved on the primary branch remain effective.

- **System State's helper panel always has a way back to its page.** The panel beside System
  Settings now offers Open Developer Tools, Open Full Disk Access or Open Accessibility on each
  of its pages, as System State's own rows do. Before, once the Developer Tools list could be
  read, the panel offered only Not now, so a deep link that System Settings swallowed (behind
  its Quit & Reopen sheet over the Full Disk Access page) left no way to the list. An Open
  pressed while System Settings has a sheet or dialog up waits for it, says so, and brings the
  page up once it is gone. When macOS will not show the list, the panel says Show it tries again,
  and those words go once Show it does.

- **A press on System State never waits behind a panel the person cannot see.** The helper
  panel shows only while System Settings is in front, but it held System State's presses
  (Turn On…, Install…) for as long as it stood, so with aterm in front a click did nothing and
  nothing on screen said why. Now a press on the panel's own row brings System Settings and
  the panel forward at its page. A press on any other row has the panel give way: no Not now,
  nothing it had queued opens over the press, and the press goes on at once. A first launch's
  walk then starts again at the next quiet moment over the pages it never got past, and the
  folder warm-up still follows a Full Disk Access page nobody answered. A Local Network pane
  aterm opened no longer holds a press made back in aterm for its 30 seconds either.

- **`sync.peers` reads the Local Network answer once macOS has it.** The converge lane read
  `sync.peers` at launch and then every half hour, so a pass made before Local Network's
  question kept "macOS has not asked about local network" until the vault's join ran a fresh
  pass. Now the question going up, and the re-probe after it ending (whatever it heard, so on a
  network with no ALab vault too), wake every LAN reader of the window, the converge lane among
  them, which runs a fresh pass at once.

- **`aterm pkg capacity` shows what every claim reserves, memory too.** A held claim's line
  now says how much disk it still reserves against the claims behind it, as a waiting claim's
  did, and a claim of memory says what it reserves of it (`mem 16 GiB (…), reserves 8 GiB`:
  its peak less what its holder's tree and the processes credited to it use). `--json` gives
  every claim `reserved_mem` beside `reserved_disk`, and a `volumes` list with the free space,
  floor and room of each other volume a claim's disk is on, as `volume` has for the one read.

- **A build no longer claims disk by what it wrote into other directories.** Each run's
  measured footprint is now kept with the identity of the directories it measured, so from this
  build on, once a build's directories are re-pointed, what its runs wrote into the old ones no
  longer counts toward its disk claim: with no run measured on the new ones, it claims as a
  first run does. Runs kept before this build carry no such identity, so they still count
  wherever they were measured (the build cache's move among them) until they leave the last 8
  runs, as before.

- (developer tool) **`verify browser` no longer calls a slow page hung while it is still at
  work.** On a busy Mac, Chromium's software GPU page (SwiftShader) can take more than a
  minute to read its frames back, and the lane ended it at one minute as if it had stopped.
  Each lane page now tells the lane it is at work, at most once a second, while it renders or
  steps. The lane still calls a page hung after a minute in which it neither answered nor
  said it was at work.

- (developer tool) **`verify measure`'s sleeping-pet row no longer fails because the Mac is
  busy.** The stats deck's dial reads the Mac's own CPU, so the row's fixed bound of 20
  needle frames failed takes in which the CPU moved, at loads as low as 3.7. `ctl metrics`
  now reports the frames each reading's needle sweep owes the windows that draw the dial
  (`needle_sweeps`, `needle_frames_owed`, and `needle_episode_left` for a sweep still under
  way), and the row fails a needle that fires more often than its readings owed. The row also
  records the pet's state as its window opens, and refuses a take whose pet was not yet in deep
  sleep then (`trail status` now reports `pet_deep`) or whose window took any event other than
  a redraw (`ctl metrics` now reports `os_window_events`, and `os_window_events_by_kind` names
  each kind, such as `focus:2`, which the refusal quotes). A window that loses the focus and
  gets it back fades its pet in again over 0.30 s, about 18 frames on a 120 Hz display: the
  likeliest cause of one take that fired the cursor-effect lane 18 times with the pet asleep
  at both edges.

- Shared-table applications can open validated read-only sessions beside an active local
  writer. The replication probe uses that observation path to read retained data without
  enrolling storage, repairing an unfinished tail or taking the control writer's lease.

- Tab Control's stored session observations give the same counts as its deduplicated
  spreadsheet rows. Computers with matching labels and process IDs keep separate rows,
  headers and totals, and custom labels preserve each computer's fleet identity.

- **Rewind stays faithful across deep unscrolls and keeps scrollback images in pane traces.**
  When a program pulls lines back onto the screen from scrollback older than the 2,048 lines a
  Rewind keyframe keeps (via Kitty `CSI + T` unscroll, making a window taller, or reattaching a
  large scrollback after a width change), Rewind now takes a fresh live keyframe instead of
  marking later states `may differ` or failing `aterm ctl rewind check`. Exported pane traces
  also keep inline images across all 2,000 uncompressed scrollback lines, matching Rewind
  keyframes.

- Development-linked Codex packages show their selected package and client versions in
  Packages and AI CLIs. Packages reads the current link over an older installing record,
  and package verification identifies development links and unresolved links explicitly.

- Tab Control keeps unreported remote operating systems and session or AI counts unknown.
  Cached vitals and sessions enrich the canonical computer row, aliases share one session
  identity, and reports from a single aterm instance name their scope.

- Disk diagnostics include registered custom Rust build caches even when the broader
  folder search reaches its limit, so their sizes appear among the largest remaining
  holders. Stale receipts and replaced folders cannot lend their ownership to another path.

- Vault upkeep handed from a subscriber to the installed app now respects that app's
  Local Network permission before publishing fleet or Commons changes. A held subscriber
  copy that cannot hand off keeps using its own job's network.

- **The session journal loses nothing to a burst during a write that fails, and its full-disk
  pause ends once a reading finds room.** 0.145.0 said a burst of output during a journal write
  lost nothing the journal could still write; that held only for a write that landed. A burst
  while a write was under way dropped the records that write had taken, and when the write then
  failed (a full disk, an I/O error) the journal later said them lost (`gap why=evicted`). The
  journal now keeps the lines a failed write did not land, lets the in-memory log give those
  records up first since the journal still has them, and writes them again first, so a burst
  between two passes, during a write, whether it lands or fails, or during the pause after a
  failed one, loses nothing the journal could still write. And under the 1 GiB free-space floor
  the pause ended only when a write landed: once space was freed, with no new output to write,
  the "The session journal is paused" notice stayed up, Settings read `writer running; the disk
  is full`, and the next pause started at 60 seconds instead of 30. A reading that finds room
  now ends the pause at once. A write the disk refused (a full quota) still pauses until a
  write lands.

- **`aterm help fabric` says everything the session log puts on the bus, and how to read
  it.** THE SESSION LOG ON THE BUS said that every mark but a need's stayed on this machine,
  but a `clear`, a `seen` (which lifts a failure need) and an update's `handoff` mark cross
  too. The section now lists what crosses by each record's `op=` and `k=`, and gives the line
  `aterm fabric tail --json --bodies` hands a program: its fields, how they map to `aterm ctl
  help log`'s line, how `ms=` and a cover's `n=` show that nothing is missing, and what a
  snapshot carries. It no longer says a reader that joins anywhere needs at most 64 earlier
  records: a burst gets no snapshot until the bridge has taken all of it, and a quiet
  session's snapshot has no `open=` or `needs=`.

- **A Grok Build renewal you run no longer says aterm approves its page.** `aterm harness
  accounts renew <label> --cli grok` opened with "its page approved in a headless browser",
  though accounts.x.ai answers that browser with a block page and every such renewal stops for
  you. It now says so up front and names `aterm harness accounts login <label> --cli grok`, the
  step that signs the row in. The "sign-in needs you" notice for any pool no longer says a
  background sign-in stopped, since a renewal you ran yourself puts up the same notice and aterm
  starts no Grok Build renewal of its own.

- **A codex tab keeps its facts when you drive it by hand.** Turning Autopilot or the harness
  off for a codex-alab tab blanked what aterm read from its rollout: the context left, the model,
  its goal, `status rollout=` and the turns in its session log, though a Claude tab keeps its
  facts under Off. aterm now reads the same codex process's rollout on after its claim is given
  back, while that process runs in front of its tab, and follows its own session record to the
  thread it shows, so a `/new` or `/resume` you type is read from the new conversation. Nothing
  acts on that read: with no claim, aterm decides no exit, relaunches nothing and carries no
  resume line for it, as before. This lasts while aterm runs: after aterm restarts or updates, and
  for a codex-alab that never claimed, the facts come back at its next claim.

- **Codex, Grok Build and Kimi Code account pools say what they do, and their launches hold.**
  The `harness.accounts` setting's help claimed these pools move a running session at its
  limit; they act when aterm starts one, and the help now says so (no running Codex, Grok
  Build or Kimi Code session is moved). A worker `spawn` started under a pool is tried again
  when another aterm process holds the pool's records for a moment, and a Codex one is held
  (not stalled) while every account it may start under is at its limit: it looks at the pool
  again every minute, so it starts as soon as an account serves (one signed in, added or
  pinned, or rotation switched off) or the first limit ends. On a Codex build that serves only
  your own login's row, that row is the one account it may start under, so another account's
  sign-in does not end the hold. No Grok Build or Kimi Code limit is recorded, so their
  accounts are never skipped or held for one. A Codex login the provider refused twice
  (its refresh token expired, reused or revoked, and no other program's rotation of it landed
  meanwhile) is now recorded as signed out, so launches stop choosing it until it reads
  again; the machine's default Codex, Grok Build or Kimi Code login counts as signed in only
  while its login file is there, in the accounts report, stats, `aterm doctor` and the
  Account menu as in launches. A Codex tab a cold restore relaunches leaves an account that
  is now limited or signed out for the one serving, unless `[harness] accounts = "off"`.
- **A Codex refresh no longer loses the new login.** aterm's refresh of a Codex login takes a
  lock beside `auth.json` from its request to its write, so two aterm reads never spend one
  single-use refresh token, sends nothing with less than three seconds left for the answer,
  and keeps the provider's answer in a private (`0600`) file beside it until the write lands;
  a refresh whose write failed is published by the next read instead of signing the account
  out.
- **`aterm secrets` refuses AI CLI login files as vault entries.** The file each AI CLI
  keeps its login in (Codex's `~/.codex/auth.json`, Claude Code's `.credentials.json` in any
  folder, Grok Build's, Kimi Code's credential files and Muse Code's) and the logins aterm
  keeps for pool rows are refused by `aterm secrets set` and the vault editor with the reason
  (their refresh tokens are single-use, so a copy on a second machine signs one of them out).
  A vault that already holds one never writes it and applies the rest with nothing failed,
  naming the refused entry on each pass that applies.
- **aCaffeine's menu says a timed span ends in forever.** Since 0.145.0 a span keeps this Mac
  awake for good once it ends, as Activate Forever does, but the checked row read `Activate
  for 1 Hour — 52 min left` and the tooltip `keeping this Mac awake for 52 min more`. They
  now read `… 52 min left, then forever` and `52 min left of this span, then until you
  click`, and `aterm acaffeine --help` says the same of `on <span>`.

- **aCaffeine keeps this Mac awake when it cannot tidy its state file as a span ends.** At a
  span's end the mug saves `mode=forever` over the span; when that save failed (a full disk,
  a state folder it cannot write), it turned keep-awake off and quit, though the span left in
  the file reads forever to the next mug. It now logs the failure and keeps the Mac awake. A
  save that fails on a file that does not read forever still stops the mug, as before.

- **A click on aCaffeine as a timed span ends turns it off.** In the second or so between a
  span's end and the mug's next tick, the mug was still lit, but a click on it turned it on
  forever instead of off, and its menu checked no row. The mug now reads an ended span as the
  forever it ends in, as it does everywhere else, so a click turns it off and the menu checks
  Activate Forever. `aterm acaffeine --help` also says that `status`'s `until=` time is a
  span's end, after which it reads forever.

- **aCaffeine's open menu keeps up.** While its menu was open, a span's end, a wake from
  sleep or an `aterm acaffeine on|off` changed the mode but not the menu, so the checkmark and
  the time left stayed as they were until the menu was opened again. The open menu now moves
  its checkmark and its time left as they change.

- **A window opened as aCaffeine quits starts it again.** A window launched (or an `aterm
  acaffeine on` run) in the moment between Quit aCaffeine, or `aterm acaffeine quit`, and the
  mug's exit saved forever but found the ending mug still running and started none, so nothing
  kept this Mac awake until the next window; one launched just before `quit` could instead
  start the mug after it, set off, while `quit` answered `stopped`. A quitting mug now lets go
  of its lock before it reads the mode again, a window or `on` that finds it ending waits for
  its exit, and `quit` reads the mode again once the mug is gone and takes turns with a
  window's start, with `on` and with the quitting mug, so aCaffeine starts again when the mode
  was set on in that moment. `aterm acaffeine quit own`, which an uninstall runs, starts
  nothing.

- **`aterm pkg self-uninstall` says what to do about an old Caffeine that still runs.** When
  an older aterm's Caffeine (before 0.145.0) holds its lock, the uninstall keeps that mug's
  files; it now names them and the folder to remove them from by hand once that mug is quit
  from its menu or a logout ends it, where it only said that it kept them.

- **An update no longer turns aCaffeine back on.** When an update (by default applied on its
  own, with nobody asked) or a launch-record renewal restarted an open window, the new window
  started aCaffeine set to keep this Mac awake forever, undoing a click that turned it off or a
  Quit aCaffeine. Such a window now keeps the mode as saved, and starts the mug only when that
  mode is on; a window you launch still turns it on.

- **`--control-sock off` starts aCaffeine.** A window opened with `--control-sock off`, `0`
  or an empty value (no control socket, or the default one) was taken for a private lab launch,
  so it started neither aCaffeine nor the Commons runtime, while the same window opened with
  `--no-control-sock` did. Only a `--control-sock` naming a socket of its own keeps a window
  inert now.

- **Enable at Startup no longer holds back aCaffeine's tooltip.** Turning Enable at Startup on
  or off restarted the mug's minute tick, so each toggle could hold back the time left that its
  tooltip shows by up to another minute; the tick now carries on as it was.

- **An uninstall's dry run names aCaffeine's files.** `aterm pkg self-uninstall --dry-run` and
  `install.sh --uninstall --dry-run` said only that aCaffeine's files go once its idle lock is
  taken, and counted none of them. They now say what the uninstall does with them, under
  aCaffeine's name and Caffeine's: each file it removes once an aterm here confirms it stopped
  aCaffeine (with no such aterm, or with a lock a running mug holds, every file is kept), the
  lock it leaves (or makes, and leaves), and a copy macOS may still be assessing that it keeps.

- Automatic disk cleanup and build admission keep more free space on large build volumes.
  Their default reserve can now grow to 256 GiB, with warning at up to 512 GiB, so a nearly
  full multi-terabyte disk starts its existing safe cleanup before it reaches the old small
  reserve. Explicit disk settings still take precedence.

- (developer tool) The lazy-init census keeps proven dependency-qualified free calls
  in their own crate. Uncertain exports, aliases and borrowed cells retain conservative
  recursion checks.

- **Queued upgrade choices keep the build you saw.** If a session moves to a different running
  build while Upgrade Now, Not today or Skip waits to be saved, aterm refuses the old choice
  and lets you choose again from the current upgrade row.

- **Skip and Defer survive a managed Muse Code or agy update check.** A saved choice holds
  only its matching tab, conversation, source build and target build. Revision Skips survive
  reopening the saved record; an update already restarting continues to completion, and a
  build choice does not block an agy model rotation.

- Public export checks clear inherited HTTP authentication headers for the public
  release owner, including repository-specific settings, while preserving private
  repository authentication. Inherited Git command parameters cannot restore public
  headers or credential helpers. Unsupported header URL scopes are refused without
  printing configuration or credentials. Conditional Git includes also cause a named
  refusal, since they can add authentication when the export engine changes repositories;
  an incomplete Git key-list capture refuses instead of accepting its retained tail.

- Release signing refuses a release-keychain path that links to the login or System keychain
  before attempting to unlock it or change its key access.

- Vault discovery keeps looking after an unrelated advertised vault answers while a default
  address is asleep or unreachable. It records a network as holding another vault only when
  every default address answered that way.

- **A Mac whose vault subscriber runs a held copy of aterm now keeps in step with the
  installed app.** On a Mac whose vault subscriber runs a pinned copy of aterm (an admin
  Mac's snapshot, or a program `aterm secrets agent on --program` named), the subscriber's
  background pass ran that copy's own rules, so it and the aterm window's pass, run by the
  installed app, could keep undoing each other's work, and a fix in a newer app never
  reached the subscriber's side. The copy now hands its pass to the installed aterm.app,
  which runs it as itself, so macOS also sees any local network use as aterm.app's. An app
  too old to take the pass leaves the copy to run it, as before, and aterm.log says so.

- **Every aterm window runs its background pass, even while setup waits on you.** A window
  whose first-run setup was waiting on you (a permission you had not given yet, say), or had
  nothing to run this launch (the relaunch after an update, a Stop, a Cancel), never ran the
  pass that keeps the Mac in step every 30 minutes. It now starts with the window in all of
  those cases. While a setup run still has its Secrets step to do, the pass leaves
  joining the vault to that step. A first-launch review you closed without answering still
  starts nothing until the next launch.

- **The window's automatic vault join no longer turns sync back on after `aterm secrets
  agent off`.** If you turned the vault's sync off while the window's background pass was
  joining the open ALab vault, the join turned it back on and removed the record of your
  choice. Your choice now stays, and no sync process is started over it. Joins you make
  yourself, in System State or with `aterm init`, still turn sync on.

- **A background pass that cannot run now says why in aterm.log.** A pass refused outside
  your own login, or because its state folder could not be read, ended silently, since
  nothing reads the background runner's error output. It now writes one aterm.log line
  naming the build, what started it and why it did not run.

- **A Mac with no aterm window keeps its AI accounts in sync again.** The background pass
  that keeps a windowless Mac's accounts roster in step read a deleted roster as current
  and never rebuilt it, and never noticed a change to the Codex, Grok or Kimi accounts in
  the vault or the accounts sheet. It now checks exactly what its sync would do: a missing
  roster is rebuilt, and an account the vault adds to any of those pools is added.

- **`aterm secrets commons init` no longer marks open-vault machines as approved by you.**
  Run on an open vault, it recorded every machine it brought into Commons as one you had
  approved by hand, although the vault's open approver may have let each in with nobody
  approving it. It now records those machines as let in by the vault's open policy, which
  keeps them in Commons just the same; your own Mac and a machine let in by a code or a
  password are still recorded as approved by you, as is every machine on a closed vault.

- Command details no longer move file lookups onto the window thread if their background
  worker cannot start. They also respect executable shadowing on `PATH`: an empty or relative
  entry leaves later candidates unconfirmed. They identify the system `env` interpreter by
  its file, so a different program named `env` cannot confirm a command that did not run.

- Rewind keeps image memory accounted for after Kitty frame edits and deletions,
  accepts the same PNG and Sixel sizes as the live terminal, and preserves the
  start time of quiet Kitty animations when later output begins a replay slice.

- The swarm master switch also holds automatic System State vault discovery and joins,
  including the concurrent Secrets lane and Local Network grant probe. Explicit manual
  joins keep their existing behavior.

- **Loading a gallery of Kitty file thumbnails no longer pushes earlier screens out of Rewind.**
  Each image loaded from a host path (`t=f`/`t=t`/`t=s`) records a live keyframe instead of the
  path, and a pane keeps at most four keyframes, so loading four or more thumbnails in a row used
  to evict the screens before the gallery. Back-to-back live keyframes with no output, resize or
  host step between them now fold into one keyframe, keeping the earlier chains and carrying any
  command mark forward to the settled gallery screen.

- **A tab moved back onto the default login reads its usage again.** When aterm moved a
  Claude Code tab back onto the account of the Mac's default login, aterm's usage tap in that
  tab had every reading refused as another login's: `aterm harness accounts` stopped updating
  that account's figures from it, and its high figures no longer moved the tab to another
  account ahead of its five-hour limit. Readings in such a tab count as the default login's
  again.

- **A move onto another account counts as served when its first turn answers at once.** When
  aterm moved a Claude Code tab onto another account, it recorded that the account served only
  once it had seen the first turn under that account busy. A turn answered faster than aterm
  reads the screen was never counted: the move stayed open and the account was never marked
  proven. After a move at a usage limit, the account's next limit was then taken for the move
  failing, which undid the move in aterm's books although the tab had worked on that account;
  after a move ahead of a limit, quitting Claude Code in the tab struck the account as failed
  and relaunched the tab under the account it had moved off. The turn aterm asked of the
  account, answered on screen or in the conversation's record, and a prompt you typed after
  the move and saw answered, now count as the account serving.

- **A `/login` back to an account aterm had marked signed out makes it usable again.** When
  Claude Code's own `/login` switched the default login to another of the roster's accounts,
  aterm marked the account it had held signed out (it has no login on this Mac any more) and
  tried to sign it in, as it should. When a later `/login` switched the default login back to
  that account, aterm kept it signed out, with its failed sign-in, so `aterm harness accounts`
  listed it `signed-out` and `expired` and its sign-in was tried again although its login
  worked. The sync that sees the default login's new account now marks that account signed in
  and served, clears the stale sign-in error, and counts the default login's sessions as its.
  An account the default login merely still holds keeps what is on record: a login seen ended
  after the switch stays signed out.
- **A Claude account a `/login` moved onto no longer reads as signed out.** When a person's
  `/login` signed the Mac's default login in as an account whose earlier login had ended, and
  the roster already listed that account as the default login's, aterm kept the old sign-out:
  `aterm ai` said claude was signed out and `aterm harness accounts` showed the row
  `signed-out` while Claude Code ran on it. aterm now checks the default login once
  (`claude auth status`, which signs nothing in) and, signed in, records the account as
  working with its tabs on it. `aterm ai` also says when the sign-out was recorded rather than
  naming a login wall it may not have seen, and the account a `/login` moved onto takes over
  as the active one from the account it moved away from, so its tabs still move to another
  account ahead of a usage limit.

- **System State on a Mac outside ALab says it is set up.** Since 0.145.0 every Mac sets
  up the credentials vault, and on a Mac with no ALab vault on its network the page's
  headline stayed at `1 step waiting: Secrets vault` for good, its kitty village never
  settled, and `setup=` in `aterm ctl @self status` never read `done`. Where no ALab vault
  answers on your network, the Secrets vault row now reads `Not joined` in place, whatever
  else you set up and also when aterm reopens before it asks again, still saying what aterm
  heard there (`The ALab vault did not answer on this network`, `No vault on this network`
  or `Local Network is off for aterm`), with no Turn On Sync button. The headline reads
  `Permissions are set up` once your permissions are (`This Mac is set up` where you set up
  more and that is in place too), and `setup=` reads `done`. GitHub repositories there now
  read with this Mac's own GitHub token, as setup clones them with it, instead of waiting
  for the vault for good; only a Mac with no token of its own waits for the vault's. aterm
  still asks that address again by itself, and joins the vault if it answers there later. A
  Join you typed the vault's password for still waits for the ALab vault while aterm keeps
  that password for another try; stopping setup or quitting aterm ends that wait.

- **Claude Code 2.1.312's limit-reset lines no longer read as a usage limit.** 2.1.312 calls the
  five-hour window the `5-hour limit` where earlier builds said `session limit`, so its lines
  after a reset (`5-hour limit reset · next reset available …`, `Couldn't reset your 5-hour limit
  right now`, `Resetting your 5-hour limit…`) read as a fresh five-hour wall. They now read as on
  2.1.311, whose words still read too, and 2.1.312's own five-hour wall (`You've hit your 5-hour
  limit · resets 3pm`) still reads as one. Its usage warning (`You've used 92% of your 5-hour
  limit`) is kept in the account's stats again, the reset named where usage credits start (`Your
  5-hour limit resets 9:43am`) is placed in the five-hour window again, and a review run that
  stops at the five-hour wall is told as a usage limit. A 5-hour reset's spent line is read as
  spent, not as a failed reset, by 2.1.312's head (`5-hour limit reset`) as by 2.1.311's, now
  that the opt-in limit-reset step takes a 5-hour or full reset on 2.1.312 too.

- **`aterm ctl await task` no longer wakes on a limit a worker is waiting out.** It wakes when a
  worker is done, exited, stalled or needs you, but the harness's own wait at a usage limit it
  continues after (a `kind=wait` attention entry) also woke it, so a lead's background wait
  ended early with nothing to act on. A wait now never raises a task record's attention. The
  `attention=` of `sessions`, `task` and `await task` rows names a standing ask before a newer
  wait, and a wait written on a proven claim's connection goes when that claim ends or that
  connection closes, so a killed image's wait no longer stands in Waiting for good.
- **A session under Autopilot Land keeps working after you ask it something mid-job.** Land
  left the reply to any message of yours that the session answered within 10 minutes as yours,
  and typed nothing after it, so a worker you asked "are you working on anything?" stopped there
  with its work unlanded. Only the message that opens a session is left to you now; one later in
  the session, including after aterm restarts its supervision, interrupts the work, and Land
  carries it on after the reply until it lands. Autopilot Off is unchanged.

- **Autopilot Land treats a program you start fresh in a tab as a new session.** In a tab
  that had run another session, your first message to the new one was read as a mid-job
  interruption and Land typed after the reply; it is now that session's opening message, left
  to you. A session an older aterm left parked after your mid-job message now carries on under
  Land too.

- **Autopilot Land no longer takes a session it relaunched for a new one.** Where aterm
  relaunched a session itself (onto another account or model, or to free memory) and read its
  screen before the resumed conversation was drawn, it could take the banner for a program
  started fresh and leave the reply to your next message to you, as a new session's opening
  message. Such a relaunch is now the same session, and Land carries on after the reply; one
  that had nothing to resume is still a new session.

- **codex-alab gets aterm's skills.** `drive-aterm`, `supervise-agent`, `system-state`,
  `rust-in-aterm`, `aterm-themes` and `aterm-fabric` now load in codex as they do in Claude
  Code, from `~/.codex/skills`, so "run workers in parallel", "why is the Mac slow" or "Trust
  refused my build" finds them. `aterm agents install` typed in a shell that sets
  `$CODEX_HOME` writes them there instead; a window's automatic pass keeps to `~/.codex`,
  because aterm strips `CODEX_*` from the shells it opens, so a codex in a tab reads
  `~/.codex` unless your shell's startup files set it. aterm wrote codex only an
  `aterm-fabric` custom prompt, which codex stopped reading when it dropped custom prompts;
  `aterm agents` and each window's automatic pass now delete that file from `~/.codex` while
  it carries aterm's marker. A codex lead waits for its workers in the foreground with a
  bounded `timeout=`, as the `supervise-agent` skill and codex's primer now say, since
  codex's shell wakes no turn.
- **Each coding agent's primer says only what is true for it.** Every agent was told to run
  `aterm ctl await task` as a background Bash and `amacs --wait` in the background, which only
  Claude Code can do, and read Claude Code's `rm` box line, so codex read waits that never wake
  it beside its own. Those lines are now Claude Code's alone, each starting `In Claude Code,`,
  and codex's primer says to bound a foreground wait inside the tool call's own time limit
  (`await task @<sid>,… since=<rev> timeout=<ms>`), re-arm it with each worker's rev
  (`@<sid>:<rev>`), and open a file for you with `amacs --no-wait` and wait with `await edit
  … timeout=600000`. A file two agents share (`~/.codex/AGENTS.md` linked to
  `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`) carries both agents' parts, each said of the agent it names, so the
  Claude Code reading it keeps its `rm` box line and its background wait. The Autopilot lines
  now say where codex-alab's own Autopilot differs from aterm's harness: it leaves a reply to a
  person's message answered within 10 minutes to them under Cruise too, and under Land after a
  landing, unless it was carrying the work, and the prompt to check on your background work is
  the harness's. The primer's marker is v48.
- **`aterm ctl subscribe @<sid> events` pushes a codex's own report and acts.** A watcher got
  `EVENT <local> agent <word>` on every Claude Code verdict but nothing when a codex moved,
  since a codex's `agent=` stays `unknown`, so it had to read the `log` stream for program
  marks instead. Each move of the program's own report now comes as `EVENT <local> program
  state=<idle|working|blocked|done|error|-> [kind=<permission|question|auth>] rev=<id>`, and
  each act codex-alab records under its proven claim as `EVENT <local> act <act> rev=<id>`,
  `<id>` the row's `timeline` id; neither is ever an `agent` event. A state held back by a
  flap and written by the next second's status sweep now wakes the watch at once. The
  `supervise-agent` skill's marker is v19.
- **`aterm harness usage` in a codex tab shows your 5-hour and weekly windows.** Run inside
  codex-alab it printed `?%/5h · ?%/7d · acct codex · resets ?` beside the tokens and list
  dollars, where Claude Code's shows the plan's windows, the reset and how old the reading is.
  It now reads them from the newest `token_count` your conversation's rollouts carry for the
  `codex` limit, as in `gpt 43%/5h · 61%/7d · acct work · resets in 1h6m · rollout 12m`, where
  `rollout 12m` says Codex wrote that reading 12 minutes ago; `--json` gives each window's
  `used_pct`, `resets_at`, `age_s` and `"source": "rollout"`. A window whose reset has passed
  shows `?`, never the share it had. `acct` names the row of `accounts-codex.toml` whose
  directory holds the file `CODEX_AUTH_PATH` names (the row with none when it is unset) where
  the roster lists two or more accounts, judged by the path alone: no auth file is opened. It
  stays `acct codex` in a tool environment without the tab's `ATERM_PARENT_SESSION_ID`, since
  a `shell_environment_policy` that keeps that out (`inherit = "core"`, `include_only`) can
  keep out `CODEX_AUTH_PATH` too, which would read as the dir-less row.
- **`aterm ctl turn` into a codex-alab says `submitted=1` once codex itself took the line.**
  A follow-up with `turn typed=1 settle=submitted` was judged submitted on a codex tab by any
  redraw after Enter, such as a popup taking the Enter, so a lead could be told a line went
  when it had not, and a done task was reopened as working anyway. On a codex-alab aterm has
  proven that is between turns, the turn now waits within `submit_window=` for codex's own
  report to begin a turn and answers `submitted=1 … submit_by=claim`; when none comes, a
  press the screen showed is `submitted=0 … pressed=1`, Enter is not pressed again (it would
  pick from the popup) and the task stays done. Into a codex-alab in a turn, which takes an Enter into that
  turn or its queue and may begin another line's turn meanwhile, the screen judges the press
  as before (`submit_by=screen`). Every verified submit now names what showed it: a Claude
  Code turn's verdict says `submit_by=composer` and a shell's `submit_by=block`, with
  `submitted=` judged as it was.

- **`aterm agents remove <agent>` keeps a skill another agent still reads.** Where one skills
  folder serves two agents (`~/.config/muse/skills` or `~/.codex/skills` linked to
  `~/.claude/skills`), removing one agent's skills deleted the other's too; now each such row
  says `kept — claude reads it too` and names the `remove` that takes both.
- **A Grok Build sign-in shows you its code at once, without trying xAI's page in a headless
  browser first.** accounts.x.ai answers aterm's headless browser with Cloudflare's block page,
  so that try could never pass: each sign-in whose Grok row had an email and a browser profile
  or mailbox loaded xAI's page for nothing, and on a Mac with no headless browser it downloaded
  aterm's pinned one first. Had xAI answered with Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." check
  instead, the sign-in would have ended without ever showing you its code.
  `aterm harness signin --cli grok` now skips that try and downloads nothing for it, whatever
  your Grok row has (an email, a browser profile, a mailbox), and puts the code and the page
  up straight away (`NEEDS YOU: approve this Grok Build sign-in: code … at …`); the accounts
  ledger says why (`headless(skipped: …)`).

- **The message bus survives an app update.** After aterm updated itself, the step that
  restarts the bus's broker on the new build unloaded its launchd job and loaded it again
  at once, before launchd had let the old job go, so the load failed and the bus stayed
  down until you ran `aterm fabric on`. A job whose settings did not change now restarts in
  place, never unloaded on the way; if launchd refuses that restart, the job is left loaded
  as it was. One whose settings changed is unloaded, and its new settings are written and
  loaded only once launchd has let it go (up to 30 seconds), with one more try if that load
  fails. A job launchd never lets go is left loaded as it was, its settings unchanged. If
  the new settings still do not load and launchd holds no job of the bus, the ones they
  replaced are put back and loaded, and the error says which launchd step failed and what
  launchd said.
  This step runs for `aterm fabric on`, for the restart after an update, and when the bus is
  turned on by default.

- **The background upkeep brings the message bus back when its broker is down.** It read a
  bus whose broker was not running as healthy, so a broker the update left unloaded stayed
  down. Now, when no broker answers on the bus's socket (asked twice where a process holds
  it), the upkeep loads or restarts the launchd (or systemd) job `aterm fabric on`
  installed. It leaves the bus alone after `aterm fabric off`, under `--service none`, for a
  broker you started yourself, for a job you disabled in launchd or disabled or masked in
  systemd (its reason names the command that turns it back on), where launchd or systemd
  does not say what it holds, and in a login with no desktop session or systemd user manager
  to load the job in.

- **`aterm fabric on`, `aterm fabric off` and the background upkeep take turns.** A
  person's `aterm fabric on` ran alongside the upkeep turning the bus on, so the two could
