- **The join password is shown only to a person at a terminal.** `aterm secrets
  password show` writes nothing when its output is not a terminal or an agent runs
  it, and says to approve the new Mac with `aterm secrets approve <code>`
  instead; `aterm secrets password new` sets its new password there too but
  prints it only at a terminal. `aterm secrets join` without a terminal returns
  at once with that command instead of waiting ten minutes.

## [0.141.0] - 2026-10-25

### Added

- **First launch installs Apple's Command Line Tools.** On a new Mac, System
  State's GitHub repositories step waited on Apple's Command Line Tools (git, cc,
  the macOS SDK) and only said `Install Apple's Command Line Tools`. Now, once
  that step waits on them, System State is in front with no other step running and
  you have not typed for a moment, aterm opens a terminal tab that runs
  `aterm init --only base.clt`. Type your password there once, and setup carries
  on by itself within a minute of the install. aterm opens the tab by itself once
  per Mac: close it without installing and later launches leave it closed, and the
  GitHub repositories row's Install… opens it again whenever you press it. While
  the tab waits for your password, System State's headline says so; while Apple's
  installer runs, the row waits calmly, with no alert. An existing installer holds
  back another install tab, including one still spawning. A leftover marker alone
  does not leave the row saying Installing. Keys you type into System
  State while the tab opens stay there. A Mac whose
  Xcode builds C but lacks the Command Line Tools' git now counts them as missing.
  Closing the tab or pressing Control-C or Control-\ during the install lets its
  current step finish and then stops, instead of leaving a marker that made every
  later install fail, and the install says when it reads Apple's catalog and when it
  downloads, so it does not look stuck.

- **Grok Build signs in once per Mac, with no browser pages popping up.** Signed out,
  Grok Build opened accounts.x.ai in your default browser every time it started, so
  several Grok tabs opened several pages. Inside aterm a signed-out `grok` now first
  runs `aterm harness signin --cli grok --wait`: one sign-in for the whole Mac, run in
  a sandbox that keeps Grok from opening any page, with one need on the menu bar
  carrying the code and the page to open yourself (`NEEDS YOU: approve Grok Build
  sign-in, code …, at …`). Every other Grok tab waits for that one sign-in, and grok
  starts once it succeeds. `grok login`, `--help`, `-p`, the other one-shot commands
  and local subcommands such as `grok mcp` are not held, and `--no-harness` skips it.
  A Grok tab already showing its sign-in screen waits on the Mac's sign-in, or shows
  one shared need on the menu bar pointing at the code on its screen. A saved login
  Grok refuses (one it can no longer renew) counts as signed out, so the next launch
  signs in through the sandbox instead of opening a page.

### Changed

- **`spawn agent=grok` names Grok Build as a worker.** It was `ERR usage`. Until aterm
  reads Grok Build's turn end, the spawn is refused with the reason (`ERR spawn
  agent=grok: …`) before any tab opens, because nothing could mark its task done and
  `await task` would never wake on it. Once it starts, a worker with no usable Grok Build
  sign-in file (missing, empty, or one grok refused) is `stalled why=signin` before
  anything is installed, because
  signed out Grok Build opens xAI's sign-in page in your browser by itself. A missing
  `grok` is then installed by atpkg's verified install (naming it opts the Mac in;
  `[packages] exclude` or your own removal holds it back, and a hold or a failed install
  is `stalled why=install`). The startup deadline waits while it installs, and a worker
  whose task already stalled is never typed into later.

- **`aterm init` asks about a secrets vault only when one is there, and a vault join no
  longer holds it up.** With no vault configured, init looks for the ALab vault while it
  reads the Mac, and when it answers the join password is the only question. Off that
  network it asks nothing: the row says `aterm secrets join <url>` or the new `aterm init
  --vault <url|path>` joins yours. `--vault` checks that a vault answers there, asks again
  in place when none does, and asks you to trust an unpinned vault's key by its
  fingerprint. A look that heard no vault is kept for a day on that network, so the next
  run makes none. While macOS still asks whether aterm may use the local network, init
  says so in one line and waits for your answer instead of calling the vault absent. A
  join sent with the password waits at most 6 seconds for the admin Mac, then asks for the
  password again in place; one sent without it does not wait at all. Its row says
  "waiting" with the code an admin approves, and init exits 0 because the subscriber
  finishes the join by itself (it used to exit 69, and the next run 1). GitHub's sign-in
  waits for the vault row; when it is left waiting, init exits 75, and running it again
  once the join is approved finishes it. Ctrl-C during the wait ends only the wait, and a
  join now says two lines instead of eight.

### Fixed

- **Command Line Tools setup can retry after a marker write fails.** aterm now
  prepares the installer marker before publishing it, so a write or flush error
  cannot leave a partial marker blocking the next attempt. Existing files stay
  untouched.

- **Cursor trails continue after returning to a terminal window.** A focus
  change followed by a status-line repaint could make genuine typing count as
  program output, leaving gaps or suppressing the trail until Enter. Focus
  notifications now preserve the input row's ownership while clearing old
  classifier hints; unrelated output still cannot start a typing trail.

- **Config problem navigation respects the editor's active prompt.** F8,
  Shift-F8 and the problem buttons could move the document caret and viewport
  behind a command, search, buffer or Go to Line prompt. They now wait until
  the prompt finishes or is cancelled, then resume normal navigation.

- **Recovery reopens Settings in its own window.** Retrying a Settings page
  from another window could navigate the foreground page and disturb its
  unsubmitted field. Retry now opens or reuses Settings in the window that
  requested it.

- **A worker using its own login stays independent of pool budget damage.**
  Classifying an explicit login directory could fail because an unrelated
  account-pool budget file was malformed. Classification now recovers and
  checks the policy and login bindings separately from that budget read.
  Managed launches retain their full pool-state checks.

- **Switch Buffer selects the editor pane you requested.** In a split tab,
  `C-x b` could report a switch while leaving another pane focused, so typing
  and File > Save still belonged to that pane. The exact matching editor now
  receives focus, including in a zoomed split. Switch Buffer and Kill Buffer
  also refuse ambiguous duplicate views within one tab, as they already did
  across tabs.

- **Find honors configured Copy shortcuts.** With terminal Find open,
  Ctrl-Shift-C, Ctrl-Insert and other Copy bindings could be swallowed or move
  the query caret. They now copy the selected match through the same handler
  as Edit > Copy while preserving the query.

- **First launch no longer fills the disk with repositories.** Cloning your GitHub
  repositories went on until the disk was nearly full: a new 100 GB Mac ended in
  aterm's disk emergency with 3.7 GB free. Now a repository whose clone would take
  free space below the line aterm's disk watch keeps is left out, and the ones that
  fit are still cloned. System State's GitHub repositories row then says `Not
  enough free disk space for the rest`. Setup tries again by itself for about ten
  minutes; after that, free space and press Check again (or launch aterm again) to
  clone the rest. `aterm init` leaves them out the same way, and its plan says how
  many repositories have no room.

- **A yanked or removed grok-alab never breaks `grok`.** Once grok-alab was installed,
  typing `grok` handed the session to it whenever its command existed, so a grok-alab
  build that was yanked or revoked (whose command then only says why and exits) or whose
  build had gone made every `grok` fail. Now `grok` hands over only while the grok-alab
  command names a complete build, and runs Grok Build by itself otherwise.

- **A harness that only relaunches and updates its agent no longer hides that agent's
  boxes.** A harness's claim on a tab that takes only relaunches and updates (grok-alab's)
  counted as one that answers everything, so a permission box, a question or a wall on that
  tab raised no `Needs you` row. Now those still need you, as on any other tab.

- **A blocked background close keeps your working window active.** Closing a
  Settings tab with an unfinished draft could change aterm's input owner to
  that background window without moving OS focus. Its recovery choices now
  stay in the window that declined the close, while Edit keeps its foreground
  target. Deferred pane-close replay also keeps the originating window local.

- **Copy shortcuts stay inside inline tab renaming.** A configured Copy shortcut
  could commit the rename and copy a terminal selection behind it. Copy and
  Select All now follow the rename field's existing menu behavior, including
  held keys, without changing its draft or the clipboard.

- **Left and right margins behave as in xterm.** With DECLRMM (`CSI ? 69 h`)
  on and margins set by DECSLRM (`CSI Pl ; Pr s`), text that wraps on the right
  margin goes on at the left one, and a line feed, reverse index or wrap at the
  edge of the scrolling region scrolls only the rectangle between the margins.
  Carriage return, cursor left and right and tab stop at the margins unless the
  cursor already stands beyond them, CHA under origin mode counts from the left
  margin, and NEL or a newline-mode line feed from past the right margin scrolls
  nothing. Outside the margins, inserting or deleting characters or lines
  changes nothing, not even a pending wrap, and a wrap pending on the right
  margin survives a cursor save and restore. Full-screen programs that split
  the screen into side-by-side panes with these margins now draw as they do in
  xterm.

- **System State's signals agree with its rows.** A first-launch review you
  closed and opened again in the same launch reads `Setup has not started`, and
  its rows now say what Set up now will do instead of reading Needs you under that
  calm headline. The review of the groups an ALab
  Mac adds no longer hides a grant the setup already running waits on: Full Disk
  Access still reads Needs you, with Open, the tab's diamond and the menu bar
  line, and only the added groups read Will change. The review's line above its
  buttons now reads `Apply sets up what is shown; Cancel changes nothing.`, one
  line even in a narrow window. A step that failed keeps its reason on its row
  (`GitHub can't be reached`), and the page's note says only what comes next. The
  ALab notes name one fact one way: `This Mac is an ALab Mac`. While a newer aterm
  manages this Mac, each row keeps its note, and the vault's fields are read-only,
  as Join is.

- **A terminal beside a Settings or recovery view fits the window you move it to.**
  Window > Move Tab to Next Window left that tab's terminal at the old window's
  size until the new window was resized, so its prompt could sit below the
  visible rows and programs laid out for the wrong size. It now takes its place
  in the new window at once, as a terminal-only tab's does.

- **Closing a pane split off a terminal beside Settings no longer garbles its
  neighbour.** A pane closed within a quarter second of the split, by `close`, by
  its shell exiting, or by Cmd-W, made its neighbour shrink and grow straight
  back, which can leave Claude Code's screen garbled. The neighbour now waits out
  that quarter second before it grows back, as it does in a terminal-only tab.

- **The cursor glow beside a Settings view no longer takes its edges from another
  tab.** In a tab with a terminal beside Settings or a document, the cursor's
  bloom and fire shimmer were clipped to whichever pane the window's previous tab
  had focused, so they could vanish or end at an invisible edge. They now stay
  within the terminal you are typing in.

- **A failed Save leaves the document editable.** A busy file lock or another
  write failure could freeze an open document, even after a successful retry.
  Ordinary Save failures now preserve editing; a document already closing keeps
  its existing recovery guard and frozen sequence.

- **Palette Copy follows a pinned monitoring lens.** Its Copy row now uses the
  same summary owner as Edit and keyboard Copy. An unavailable summary disables
  Copy without borrowing a selection from the document behind the lens.

- **The ALab review's Apply never leaves System State stuck.** When the review of the
  groups aterm adds on an ALab Mac applied by itself and aterm could not widen your setup
  just then (you had pressed Stop, or another setup changed it meanwhile), System State
  kept showing a run with Stop that was not happening, every control stayed off, and
  nothing offered setup again until you quit aterm. Now System State goes straight back
  to your setup as it is. When another setup holds this Mac's setup records, the review's
  Apply waits for it as a choice does, saying `Waiting to apply your choice…`, and is
  applied once that setup finishes, unless your setup changed meanwhile. After you press
  Stop, aterm offers no ALab review for the run you stopped in that launch.

- **Cancel on the review after a Restore holds like any other Cancel.** Cancelling the
  review System State offered after Restore previous settings left every group as it was
  without saying setup was cancelled, and Set up now then did nothing. Now System State
  says `Setup was cancelled. Set up now applies the setup the review showed.`, and Set up
  now applies that setup. The settings Restore put back stay as Restore left them.

- **A vault path in a folder that does not exist says so.** `aterm secrets create`
  (or a publish) at a path whose folder is missing, mistyped or on a volume that is
  not mounted, failed naming an internal `.lock` file. It now names the folder and
  says to create it or check the path.

- **A busy Mac no longer fails a repository update that worked.** aterm's own git
  fetches and merges (System State's GitHub repositories step and
  `aterm init --develop`) start no automatic maintenance now. git's background
  maintenance fork could still hold the merge's output when git finished, and on a
  loaded Mac aterm then reported the finished merge as failed (`cannot run git merge
  in the checkout`). Your own git and its scheduled maintenance are unchanged.

- **Pointer commands acknowledge an action that already ran.** A click could open
  an editor prompt yet return an error because its resulting frame was unavailable.
  Such a command now replies `OK dispatched=1 readback=unavailable`, with an encoded
  reason and no invented position. Inspect the view or pointer status instead of
  repeating the action. Invalid targets and unavailable status reads remain errors.

- **The first launch shows what setup will do before doing it.** System State
  lists each setting as it is now and what Apply will change it to, under the
  headline `Review this Mac's setup`, with Cancel and Apply (30). Left alone
  while its tab is visible and active, it applies after 30 seconds; a click, a
  key or a scroll stops the countdown, and group and vault changes then wait
  for Apply. Cancel leaves this Mac as it is. One line above the buttons says
  so. While the review is open the headline is its only signal: the tab shows
  no attention diamond and the menu bar no System State line, and no row asks
  you to open a settings pane. Apply keeps its size once the countdown stops,
  and VoiceOver hears it as Apply, adding while it counts that it applies by
  itself in so many seconds.

- **The cursor pet no longer twitches late.** Once it settled beside the caret, the
  pet could slip a last pixel, hold a pose or puff a z up to most of a second late,
  whenever its window next woke for something else, and about one settle in four left
  it a pixel short of its place. It now lands exactly in place as its glide ends,
  changes pose and puffs each z when they are due, shows or hides a z behind text as
  the z moves, and keeps step with a typing rhythm instead of catching up in jumps. Its
  window wakes once more as a held pose ends, and draws frames while a typing rhythm
  carries the pet ahead.

- **The request to free disk space passes over tabs that are waiting.** A tab stopped at
  a usage limit, or at a question aterm has passed on to you, is no longer chosen while it
  waits there, however much of the disk its checkout holds: it cannot take the line until
  it is past. A chosen tab that stops at one goes back to the request at no cost, and can
  be chosen again once it is past; if it stops at one again after that, it is released, so
  the other tabs get their turn. Before, such a tab was chosen anyway, waited out half an
  hour and used up one of the request's choices, and a request whose only tab it was gave
  up for six hours. When every tab that could be asked is waiting like that, the request
  waits for the first one to be past instead of giving up for six hours, and the low-disk
  alert says so. A tab at a usage limit counts as waiting until the reset aterm itself
  waits for, including a later one that a weekly limit names after a session limit.
  `aterm harness disk why` and the next request's low-disk alert no longer name tabs that
  waited at an earlier request's limits as waiting. A tab you have put on hold or taken
  over, and a resting tab with text left typed in its prompt for a minute or more, are
  passed over the same way while that lasts; before, such a tab was chosen first, its line
  was refused at every turn break, and it used up one of the request's choices with
  nothing typed. When the request waits like that after a line already went and freed too
  little, the low-disk alert now says it is waiting, not that another session is being
  asked. The alert and `aterm harness disk why` now say what the tabs are waiting at (a
  usage limit, a question for you, your hold or take-over, or text left in the prompt) and
  what ends the wait (the limit passing, the hold lifted, the text sent or cleared); before,
  they always said a usage limit or a question, also for a tab on hold or with text left in
  its prompt. A tab at a usage limit is now recognised as one: aterm looked for a word the
  agent never shows, so such a tab was still chosen. A tab that aterm keeps from going on
  rather than spend usage credits (the default), a tab signed out of Claude, and a tab
  stopped at another error aterm waits out are passed over the same way, also while its own
  background command still runs, and the alert says what ends the wait (the usage limit
  resetting, signing in again, the error passing); before, such a tab was chosen, nothing
  could be typed into it, and a request whose only tab it was gave up for six hours.

- **The request to free disk space waits for people, and survives an aterm update.** The
  line is no longer typed into a tab where someone typed moments ago: it waits for that
  session's next turn break. A tab whose last turn was a person's own exchange with the
  agent, or whose task a manager is waiting on, is passed over for another session
  instead, and that uses up none of the request's tries. Each tab is checked at every turn
  break, even when it has not been chosen, and a tab passed over because it had no task, or
  had finished it, can be chosen as soon as it starts work on a new one. Before, a tab
  passed over once was never chosen in a later request. A seamless update no longer passes
  the request on as undelivered: the new aterm process takes over the chosen session, and
  any other aterm process now leaves it three minutes to do so. It takes the session over
  as its first disk check begins, not after the check has measured the disk, which can
  take more than a minute, so another aterm process no longer gives up on the session
  while the new one is still measuring. If the chosen agent exits
  during the update, the new process releases it at no cost; before, the request waited
  three minutes and then used up one of its choices. An update while the request is still
  choosing a session no longer makes another aterm process choose a weaker one, or give up
  with nobody to ask: it waits up to three minutes for the new process to put the session
  forward again, and the new process now takes that session's place over as its first disk
  check begins, so another process no longer chooses a weaker one while that check runs. A
  request waiting on a tab that is held up (at a usage limit or with text left in its
  prompt) no longer gives up for six hours during an update: the new process keeps that
  tab's place while its first disk check runs, though it cannot yet see what holds the tab.
  The note that asks an agent to retry after the disk filled up is no longer typed into a
  person's own exchange, or while someone is typing. A tab whose turns end with its own
  background command or monitor still running (a manager waiting on its workers) now gets
  the line once its turn is over, as at any other turn break, unless someone typed there
  moments ago (checked when the line would go, so a message you just sent the manager is
  not followed by the line), the tab is on hold, or text is left in its prompt. The line
  does not take the place of the harness's own last request to that tab, so an answer to
  that request is still read as one. Before, such a tab looked busy for hours, so its line
  was passed on undelivered after half an hour, and a request whose only tab it was gave up
  for six hours.

- **The request to free disk space keeps an accurate count.** The space a session frees is
  measured from the moment its line goes, not from a check up to a minute earlier. A line
  whose record could not be saved, because the disk was full, still counts as one of the
  request's two lines once it is saved, and the request goes back to waiting on that
  session's answer; a session chosen meanwhile whose line would be a third is not asked.
  The record is also saved when another aterm process has already ended the request
  because space came back. Before, that line was never counted, so the next shortage
  typed a second line instead of waiting out the six-hour pause. On Linux, changing the
  clock no longer makes a running aterm process look as though it had ended. A request
  that gives up with no line typed now says in `disk.jsonl` and `aterm harness disk why`
  that no session took its line, not that the agents asked did not free the space. When a
  request gives up, an aterm process raises the low-disk alert only if it reads the disk as
  short by its own limit; before, one with a lower limit than the process that opened the
  request raised "the home volume is still short" and cleared it again a minute later.
  Space that aterm's own cleanup frees after the line goes, in this aterm process or
  another, no longer counts as the asked session's, including a cleanup still running when
  the disk is checked. Before, the cleanup that keeps running while the disk is short could
  free a gigabyte and close the request in the session's name, and nobody else was asked
  for six hours. `aterm harness disk why` says how much of the space since the line aterm
  freed itself.

- **The request to free disk space no longer tells a worktree's tab that the main
  checkout's builds are its own.** A tab working in a git worktree inside another
  checkout (such as `~/aterm/.claude/worktrees/<name>` inside `~/aterm`) was credited
  with the enclosing checkout's builds whenever aterm's list of the largest builds held
  none of the worktree's own. Such a tab could be chosen ahead of the tabs working in
  that checkout, and its line called the checkout's shared builds "this tab's", which
  invited its agent to clean builds other sessions use. Each tab is now credited only
  with its own checkout's builds, and a tab whose folder has been removed (a worktree
  its session landed and deleted) with none. When the line has no room to name even
  the largest build as usual, it now names it with its folder shortened in the middle,
  still marked "this tab's" when it is; before, it said aterm had found no build it
  could size.

## [0.140.0] - 2026-10-25

### Added

- **First launch installs Apple's Command Line Tools.** On a new Mac, System
  State's GitHub repositories step waited on Apple's Command Line Tools (git, cc,
  the macOS SDK) and only said `Install Apple's Command Line Tools`. Now, once
  that step waits on them, System State is in front with no other step running and
  you have not typed for a moment, aterm opens a terminal tab that runs
  `aterm init --only base.clt`. Type your password there once, and setup carries
  on by itself within a minute of the install. The tab opens at most once per
  launch, and keys you type into System State meanwhile stay there. A Mac whose
  Xcode builds C but lacks the Command Line Tools' git now counts them as missing.
  Closing the tab or pressing Control-C or Control-\ during the install no longer
  leaves a marker that made every later install fail, and the install says when it
  reads Apple's catalog and when it downloads, so it does not look stuck.

### Changed

- **aterm reads Grok Build's own report of what it is doing.** Where a Grok Build tab
  reports its state with OSC 7501 (working, waiting on an approval, done or failed),
  `status`, `ls`, `task`, the survey and the menu bar show it as they show a
  codex's, only while Grok Build is the program in front. A subagent's report is
  not taken for the session's, and a report as long as the protocol allows (Grok
  Build's carries its session's title) is no longer dropped. aterm does not yet
  answer the protocol's support query, so Grok Build reports only where its own
  config sets `program_status = "on"` under `[ui.notifications]`. The report is
  shown only: a Grok Build tab showing one is not counted as a Codex by the disk
  watch.

- **aterm closes a sign-in it opened that nobody needs any more.** When aterm typed
  `/login` into a Claude Code tab and that login then came back in another tab, or was
  renewed and the tab restarts onto the new login, aterm no longer asks you to press Esc in
  the tab to close the sign-in. It presses the sign-in's own Esc itself, picking no sign-in
  method, and the tab carries on with its task, or restarts onto the renewed login. A method
  list still open after aterm's Esc gets the Esc again a while later, each time later than
  the last, instead of being left to you. A `/login` you typed yourself, and Console's menu
  you picked in aterm's sign-in, are never closed. Where the login came back elsewhere, aterm
  tells you that the sign-in can be closed only at Console's menu and at the message your own
  `/login` stopped on, not at your own method list or browser sign-in.

- **Cancel on the first-launch review holds until you ask again.** Cancel used to hold
  only for that launch: the next launch showed the same review again, and left alone for
  30 seconds it ran, aterm's own permission steps included. Now Cancel leaves every group
  at Leave as is for good, and no later launch shows the review. System State says
  `Setup was cancelled. Set up now applies the setup the review showed.` beside Set up
  now, with no Needs you, tab diamond or menu line for the permissions nobody approved.
  Set up now applies the setup the review showed; Set up on one group sets up that group
  alone. A Join or `aterm doctor --apply` replaces the Cancel as before, and a Restore
  after it never brings the review back.

- **Closing the first-launch review is "not this launch".** Closing the review's tab used
  to bring it back within a minute, over the terminal you had gone back to, each time with
  a fresh 30-second count that ran it once left alone. Now closing it records nothing and
  nothing offers it again in that launch: System State, opened again, shows the setup the
  review showed with Set up now and no countdown, and the next launch offers the review
  once more. A later offer never takes the tab you are in.

- **The ALab profile is never added without a review.** When aterm hears this Mac is an
  ALab Mac while the first-launch review is up, an untouched review now shows the whole
  profile in place, says `This Mac is an ALab Mac, so its profile was added.` and gives
  you 30 seconds again; a review you changed stays as you left it. When aterm hears it
  after its own setup already ran, it no longer widens that setup by itself at launch:
  System State offers the added groups as a review of their own, in its tab, without
  taking yours, and Cancel there keeps your setup as it is for good.

- **aterm closes a sign-in it opened for an account it signs in by itself.** When aterm
  typed `/login` into a Claude Code tab whose login ended before it knew that login was an
  account in your `accounts.toml` with an email, it no longer asks you to sign in to that
  account in your browser once it knows, also when it learns that only after the browser
  sign-in was asked for. At the sign-in's method list it presses Esc without picking a
  method; at a browser sign-in it already started (your browser may have opened) it closes
  the sign-in with Esc. A sign-in still open after its Esc gets the Esc again, each time a
  while later. aterm then signs the account in again by its automatic sign-in, and restarts
  the tab onto the new login where it can restart the tab; otherwise the tab waits, its
  record naming what keeps it off the new login. Before it types `/login` into a lost login
  no account names, aterm first syncs your accounts: where they come from a fleet source, a
  default login whose email Claude Code left on file becomes an account aterm signs in
  itself, and no `/login` is typed. A `/login` you typed yourself is never closed, also one
  you type after aterm closed its own. If you close the sign-in aterm opened, aterm waits
  for its own sign-in of the account instead of asking you to type `/login`. `aterm harness
  accounts sync --cli` now says that aterm signs an account it added in by itself once a
  session needs it, and that `aterm harness accounts renew` runs that sign-in now.

### Removed

- **Gemini CLI is no longer supported: agy replaces it.** aterm no longer reads,
  supervises, upgrades, relaunches or spawns Google's Gemini CLI. `spawn agent=gemini`
  (or `agent=gemini-cli`), `aterm agents install gemini`, a `[harness.gemini]` table and
  a saved session that carried a Gemini CLI relaunch are each refused or set aside with a
  note naming agy, never run as another agent. A `gemini` program in a tab is an ordinary
  program. agy keeps everything it had, its Gemini models, model pools and
  `aterm harness agy` included, and its primer stays in `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md`, which agy
  reads. aterm no longer writes `~/.gemini/commands/aterm-fabric.toml`, and the copy an
  earlier version wrote is deleted by `aterm agents install`, `aterm agents remove` and a
  window's automatic primer pass (a copy whose marker line you removed is yours and is left
  alone). (developer tool) The lab's Gemini CLI verbs and `--harness gemini` are gone,
  `lab autopilot-captures --baseline` takes its typing take on agy, and a lab an older
  aterm-lab brought up for Gemini CLI is refused by every verb but `down` and `ps`, never
  driven as Claude Code's.

### Fixed

- Automatic setup keeps verified settings and sign-outs when a later record save
  fails, so retrying does not undo a login you made afterward. Whole-profile
  `aterm init` also remembers widget changes deferred until Full Disk Access is
  granted and finishes them automatically after the grant.

- **Scrolling a terminal beside a Settings or recovery view no longer redraws
  unchanged frames.** Each wheel notch or trackpad scroll in such a tab redrew
  the whole window at the display rate for the glide's and bounce's
  in-between positions, which that tab does not show. It now redraws when a
  row moves, including a row step that lands after new output.

- **`metrics` no longer reports a fast echo as a slow one.** The echo figures
  (`echo_p50_ms` … `echo_max_ms`) started their clock only after aterm finished
  handling the key, so an echo that came back sooner was missed, and the key was
  instead timed to whatever the program printed next, often the next keystroke's
  echo. Each key is now timed from the moment its bytes went to the program to
  its first output, including output that arrives while aterm is still handling
  the key.

- **Disk conflicts update the editor without another click.** Reopening a
  file changed on disk under a local draft now refreshes Save, Reload and
  recovery guidance together. Conflict and recovery changes invalidate every
  view of that document, including hidden panes, without changing the draft.

- **Editor prompts keep their caret when the toolbar has focus.** Toolbar
  clicks and keyboard navigation retain the editor's text-input caret and IME
  position without moving control focus or adding an outer focus ring.

- **Revert, Done and Abort reflect the editor's current prompt.** The toolbar
  and palette disable them until the prompt ends. Abort also disables while a
  save is pending; Done can still finish that save.

- **Codex account moves recheck the login before returning a relaunch command.**
  A renewal, policy edit or new usage limit during command preparation now
  cancels the stale move, including when following an already active account.

- **The harness no longer cuts short a Claude Code retry sent after the network
  came back.** Since 0.135.0 the harness presses Esc on a Claude Code turn the Mac
  slept through in Claude Code's own network retry. Under "No response from the
  API", whose time is how long the try before it waited, not the one in flight,
  it could press on a retry sent once the network was back, which Claude Code
  gives up to ten minutes for a gateway that holds the answer back. It now
  presses there only when the same row was already up before the Mac slept, and
  never on a later try's row. After a wake, a first measure of the API that fails
  is taken again three seconds later, not fifteen, so the press comes sooner.

- **LAN database sharing reconnects after repeated restarts.** Failed listener
  addresses no longer reserve discovery slots just because they worked earlier.
  New listeners can be discovered while healthy connections keep their slots.

- **Account edits stop stale Codex, Grok and Kimi sign-ins.** Changing the selected
  account's identity, directory, browser or authentication settings now prevents
  an older sign-in from recording its result. Completed staged logins are kept
  for inspection, and edits to another account do not interrupt the sign-in.

- **Screen readers reach the message band over Settings and other native
  tabs.** While a Settings, System State or recovery tab was in front, the
  band's notices and their buttons, the find field, the tab list, the stats
  bars, the Rewind view, the harness chips and the Autopilot menu were
  painted but absent from the accessibility tree. They are now published
  ahead of the tab's content, as in a terminal tab; an open find field or
  menu takes the reader's focus.

- **Older sign-in attempts cannot replace a newer managed login.** Login and
  renewal now check the saved account generation before publishing a result,
  including when the replacement used the same directory and timestamp. An
  automatic Claude completion also checks the account it actually matched.

- **Screen readers read a terminal restored beside a recovery placeholder.**
  The accessibility tree of a tab that holds a terminal beside a native view
  now carries the terminal's text as its own document, in layout order, and a
  focused terminal is the focus VoiceOver reads instead of the bare window.
  The terminal text's reported position also follows the frame when the
  window is a little larger than the grid, in every tab.

- **Interrupted account renewals respect later logins when the clock moves backward.**
  Recovery checks which saved login a completion was meant to replace before
  adopting it. Completion files from older builds remain on disk, but are no longer
  automatically adopted without that evidence.

- **Clicking the editor preserves its input-method caret anchor.** Pointer
  focus now supplies the caret position without drawing the keyboard focus
  ring; typed prompts retain their own caret position.

- **Editor commands reflect an active prompt.** Go to Line and Commands are
  disabled in the toolbar and palette until the current prompt finishes or
  is cancelled, preserving its text and the document draft.

- **Deferred capture refusals report the observed state.** The error includes
  window presence, expected/current drawable identity, parking and cancellation
  state, preserving the existing capture cleanup and refusal policy.

- **System State uses the pane you clicked.** Right and middle clicks stop its
  startup countdown when they reach its body, without moving keyboard focus.
  Pane headers and sibling panes leave it alone. Accessibility's Show item
  action now stops the countdown too.

- **System State retries a GitHub refresh that could not start.** A renewed
  vault token stays due for a refresh until its reader starts successfully.

- **Stop keeps the Command Line Tools installer stopped.** Delayed requests
  and pending install commands must still belong to the current setup run.

- **Zooming a terminal restored beside a recovery placeholder no longer makes
  aterm panic.** Zooming that terminal (Cmd-Shift-Enter, or a zoom the restore
  brought back) panicked when its tab was the window's only one and froze the
  window otherwise; it now shows the zoomed terminal. Closing that terminal or
  its tab while a job runs now asks first, as any terminal's close does. Its
  output streak keeps moving while the placeholder has focus, and the tab no
  longer wakes for a scroll pill, word decorations or a kitty greeting it does
  not draw. A headless capture of a native or mixed tab shows the message band
  as of the capture, and `aterm ctl pointer` can aim at a mixed tab's native
  leaf.

- **System State's Developer Tools and Full Disk Access pages come up once for each
  setup approval.** A page brought up while no approval stood (after Stop, by
  `aterm ctl devtools hand-over` or `aterm doctor`, or by your press on a row) made System
  State drop its own step for that page, so approving setup again never brought the page
  up and the Permissions stage stayed waiting. A page shown within the last ten minutes
  could also cancel the step for the rest of the session instead of delaying it. The step
  now waits those ten minutes out and then asks, a page already shown for this approval is
  not shown again, and an `aterm ctl` request that came while the step waited is answered
  by its own rules once the step is done.

- **Permission notes survive a crash and a network home.** A crash while aterm wrote one
  of its notes about a settings page (that it opened the page, or your Not now) could
  leave the note empty, which lost your Not now or let the page come back too soon. On a
  home folder whose server refuses macOS's full flush, System State's access record and
  the access card's notes (your Not now, and where Full Disk Access was verified) were not
  written at all, so their steps and the card could come back at every launch. The notes
  are now replaced whole, and these records fall back to a plain flush there.

- **Accessibility focus supplies the editor's input method cursor position.**
  Native controls now show their focus indicator after an accessibility Focus
  request. The shared focus handler keeps the request bound to its original view.

- **Copy availability follows the past screen while rewound.** Selecting the
  past enables Copy in Edit and the palette; reopening it without a selection
  disables Copy even when the live terminal retains a selection.

- **The editor's buffer focus action now focuses the buffer.** Control,
  accessibility, pointer and keyboard activation use the live control's focus
  route instead of treating it as a document command. Focusing preserves text
  and selection, and an inactive or retired editor cannot redirect the action.

- **Scrolling a split reaches the pane under the pointer.** Native panes scroll
  without taking keyboard focus. Scrolling System State stops its automatic
  Apply countdown even while a sibling has focus, including small trackpad
  movements; scrolling another pane leaves the review alone.

- **A codex-alab tab counts as a measured build only when its package's two versions name
  one build.** aterm reads a codex-alab tab's turns from its session record only on a build it
  measured, named by the client version that record carries (`0.165.0-dev.13665`), never by
  codex-alab's own version (`0.1.0-dev.13665+codex.0.164.0`). A package whose recorded client
  version names another build than the package itself (another count or commit), or a
  codex-alab package of the new compound version that records no client version, is now read
  as unmeasured instead of as the build that string names.

- **Closing an edited pane keeps it available to reopen.** A pane closed after
  its save finishes now enters Reopen Closed Pane history. If its sibling
  closes while saving, the remaining document closes as a recoverable tab;
  other tabs keep their input target.

- **A terminal restored beside a recovery placeholder acts like one in its own
  tab.** When a session restore leaves a placeholder next to a surviving
  terminal, the terminal's link caption now follows output under a still
  pointer, and an untitled shell names the window after its working directory.
  A slow GPU now sheds effects in that tab too. The cursor cat and celebrations
  wind down instead of keeping the window redrawing for animation the tab does
  not show. Typing no longer arms predictive echo the tab never draws. A Settings
  tab also stops redrawing for a scroll pill it does not show.

- **A tab's first `sys disk` no longer reports zero.** The first time a tab (or
  `scope=aterm`) asked, before the disk walker had found its folders, the answer
  read `0 roots · 0 B exclusive`, as if the tab used no disk. It now lists the
  tab's working folder as still walking, with its size unavailable, and the
  total as a lower bound until the walk names every folder. `sys tab` reads the
  same way.

- **`sys disk` no longer totals a folder it cannot walk as zero.** When a tab's
  only folder was one aterm does not walk (too broad, like a home folder, or
  protected, another user's, remote or removable), the header read
  `1 root · 0 B exclusive`. It now reads `sizes unavailable(too_broad)`, and a
  total that leaves such a folder out beside measured ones is marked a lower
  bound that says why: `≥7.0 GB exclusive (1 not measured: too_broad)`. `sys tab`
  and the JSON say the same.

- **The first launch shows what setup will do before doing it.** System State
  lists each setting as it is now and what Apply will change it to, under the
  headline `Review this Mac's setup`, with Cancel and Apply (30). Left alone
  while its tab is visible and active, it applies after 30 seconds; a click, a
  key or a scroll stops the countdown, and group and vault changes then wait
  for Apply. Cancel leaves this Mac as it is. One line under the buttons says
  so. While the review is open the headline is its only signal: the tab shows
  no attention diamond and the menu bar no System State line, and no row asks
  you to open a settings pane. Apply keeps its size once the countdown stops,
  and VoiceOver hears it as Apply, adding while it counts that it applies by
  itself in so many seconds.

- **System State on a Mac a newer aterm set up no longer says Checking for
  good.** Its headline says a newer aterm manages this Mac's setup, the rows
  show their values as they stand, and Check again reads them anew; the
  groups, Set up now and Restore stay the newer aterm's.

- **System State says each thing once.** When aterm cannot read this Mac's
  vault settings, after a Join or the first launch's answer, the Secrets row
  says why and the page no longer repeats it in a line of its own.

- **A dozing cursor pet beside text stops waking its window for nothing.** For the
  ten seconds the pet breathes after it falls asleep below lines of text, its window
  woke about a dozen times a second to redraw z's the text hid, drawing nothing new.
  It now wakes only when the pet's picture changes.

- **The cursor pet no longer twitches late.** Once it settled beside the caret, the
  pet could slip a last pixel, hold a pose or puff a z up to most of a second late,
  whenever its window next woke for something else. It now stops where its glide last
  drew it, and changes pose and puffs each z when they are due, without waking its
  window more often.

- **An older aterm leaves a newer aterm's setup alone.** Running an older aterm beside a
  newer one (a development build, say) could take the newer one's saved setup for a
  damaged record, put your Mac settings back to Leave as is and drop its progress. The
  older aterm now changes nothing of it, and System State's headline says that a newer
  aterm manages this Mac's setup.

- **A first-launch Join no longer holds setup back while aterm cannot read the vault
  settings.** Answering the first-launch offer with Join then held everything back,
  aterm's own permissions included, and tried the same answer again every minute. Your
  answer now goes ahead without the Join: Full Disk Access, Developer Tools, the
  debugger, Local Network and every other group are set up, nothing is joined, and the
  Secrets vault row says aterm cannot read the vault settings and that `aterm secrets
  status` says why. The vault
  you typed stays in its field, so you can Join once the settings can be read.

- **A Join refused for unreadable vault settings is no longer a failure.** System State
  said "Setup failed. Set up now tries again." Its Secrets vault row now says calmly that
  aterm cannot read this Mac's vault settings and that `aterm secrets status` says why, with no Set up now,
  menu line or tab attention, and keeps the vault and password you typed.

- **A damaged setup record beside a newer aterm's no longer loops.** System State kept
  saying it would read the saved setup again and kept trying to set it aside, which the
  newer aterm's record never allows. Its headline now says that a newer aterm manages
  this Mac's setup.

- **The request to free disk space passes over tabs that are waiting.** A tab stopped at
  a usage limit, or at a question aterm has passed on to you, is no longer chosen while it
  waits there, however much of the disk its checkout holds: it cannot take the line until
  it is past. A chosen tab that stops at one goes back to the request at no cost, and can
  be chosen again once it is past; if it stops at one again after that, it is released, so
  the other tabs get their turn. Before, such a tab was chosen anyway, waited out half an
  hour and used up one of the request's choices, and a request whose only tab it was gave
  up for six hours. When every tab that could be asked is waiting like that, the request
  waits for the first one to be past instead of giving up for six hours, and the low-disk
  alert says so. A tab at a usage limit counts as waiting until the reset aterm itself
  waits for, including a later one that a weekly limit names after a session limit.
  `aterm harness disk why` and the next request's low-disk alert no longer name tabs that
  waited at an earlier request's limits as waiting. A tab you have put on hold or taken
  over, and a resting tab with text left typed in its prompt for a minute or more, are
  passed over the same way while that lasts; before, such a tab was chosen first, its line
  was refused at every turn break, and it used up one of the request's choices with
  nothing typed. When the request waits like that after a line already went and freed too
  little, the low-disk alert now says it is waiting, not that another session is being
  asked. The alert and `aterm harness disk why` now say what the tabs are waiting at (a
  usage limit, a question for you, your hold or take-over, or text left in the prompt) and
  what ends the wait (the limit passing, the hold lifted, the text sent or cleared); before,
  they always said a usage limit or a question, also for a tab on hold or with text left in
  its prompt.

- **The request to free disk space waits for people, and survives an aterm update.** The
  line is no longer typed into a tab where someone typed moments ago: it waits for that
  session's next turn break. A tab whose last turn was a person's own exchange with the
  agent, or whose task a manager is waiting on, is passed over for another session
  instead, and that uses up none of the request's tries. Each tab is checked at every turn
  break, even when it has not been chosen, and a tab passed over because it had no task, or
  had finished it, can be chosen as soon as it starts work on a new one. Before, a tab
  passed over once was never chosen in a later request. A seamless update no longer passes
  the request on as undelivered: the new aterm process takes over the chosen session, and
  any other aterm process now leaves it three minutes to do so. It takes the session over
  as its first disk check begins, not after the check has measured the disk, which can
  take more than a minute, so another aterm process no longer gives up on the session
  while the new one is still measuring. If the chosen agent exits
  during the update, the new process releases it at no cost; before, the request waited
  three minutes and then used up one of its choices. An update while the request is still
  choosing a session no longer makes another aterm process choose a weaker one, or give up
  with nobody to ask: it waits up to three minutes for the new process to put the session
  forward again, and the new process now takes that session's place over as its first disk
  check begins, so another process no longer chooses a weaker one while that check runs. A
  request waiting on a tab that is held up (at a usage limit or with text left in its
  prompt) no longer gives up for six hours during an update: the new process keeps that
  tab's place while its first disk check runs, though it cannot yet see what holds the tab.
  The note that asks an agent to retry after the disk filled up is no longer typed into a
  person's own exchange, or while someone is typing.

- **The request to free disk space keeps an accurate count.** The space a session frees is
  measured from the moment its line goes, not from a check up to a minute earlier. A line
  whose record could not be saved, because the disk was full, still counts as one of the
  request's two lines once it is saved, and the request goes back to waiting on that
  session's answer; a session chosen meanwhile whose line would be a third is not asked.
  The record is also saved when another aterm process has already ended the request
  because space came back. Before, that line was never counted, so the next shortage
  typed a second line instead of waiting out the six-hour pause. On Linux, changing the
  clock no longer makes a running aterm process look as though it had ended. A request
  that gives up with no line typed now says in `disk.jsonl` and `aterm harness disk why`
  that no session took its line, not that the agents asked did not free the space. When a
  request gives up, an aterm process raises the low-disk alert only if it reads the disk as
  short by its own limit; before, one with a lower limit than the process that opened the
  request raised "the home volume is still short" and cleared it again a minute later.

- **System State tells a passing failure from one you must fix.** A GitHub token the
  vault syncs that GitHub refused showed a red "Failed" row under a headline saying
  aterm would try again by itself. Now a step that fails for a passing reason (GitHub or
  the vault not answering, a change that did not take) reads "Will change" with its
  reason while aterm tries again, and "Failed" only once those tries are spent. A step
  only you can fix (a GitHub token to renew in the vault or add to it, Apple's Command
  Line Tools to install) reads "Needs you" with what to do. aterm stops retrying it, and
  reads GitHub repositories again whenever you return to System State, and by itself
  once a renewed token reaches this Mac through the vault. In every case the headline,
  the row, the tab mark and the menu line agree.

- **A failure aterm stopped retrying stays said.** Once setup had spent its ten tries on
  a step that kept failing (GitHub not answering on this network, say), switching to
  any aterm window started ten more tries a minute apart, and System State, the tab
  mark and the menu line went back to "waiting" until those failed too. Now the
  failure stays "Failed" until something it depends on changes, you press Check again
  or Set up now or make a choice, or aterm launches again. Coming back to aterm still
  looks again at once when a Messages, FaceTime or permission step is waiting for you.

- **System State no longer asks GitHub every minute while your token needs renewing.**
  While GitHub repositories read "Needs you", an open System State tab read every row
  again once a minute, GitHub included, for as long as it stayed open. Now it reads
  GitHub repositories again when you return to the tab, or once a renewed token
  actually reaches this Mac through the vault; meanwhile it only checks the vault's
  local files.

## [0.139.0] - 2026-10-25

### Added

- **Rewind for everyday use.** In a rewound pane, Option-Left and Option-Right
  step a second, Shift-Left and Shift-Right go to the previous or next command
  (from the shell's OSC 133 marks), Cmd-Left and Cmd-Right (or Home and End) go to
  the oldest or newest kept screen, and no step lands inside a half-drawn
  synchronized frame. The wheel and Page Up scroll up to 2048 lines of the past's
  own scrollback; a drag then Cmd-C, Select All and Cmd-F work on the past screen,
  not the live one. Click a cell and press B to go to the output that last changed
  it: the band says `row 18 col 42 changed 12.4 s ago: 37 bytes` and shows those
  bytes with control bytes escaped. A track above the band hatches the stretches
  that cannot be rebuilt or did not match the live screen. The tab menu's timeline
  rows open Rewind at their moment, screen readers see the band as a slider, and
  on macOS View > Export Pane History… saves the kept history as an asciicast file
  where a save panel says (nothing is written without it). Opening Rewind pauses the
  window's hosted effects and the band says so. `aterm ctl rewind` gains `step <n>
  by=sec|cmd`, `changed <row>,<col>` and `export`, and `aterm help rewind`
  describes it all. Tested, not proved.

- **Aos keeps the glow's recent history, repairs it off the main thread, and stops
  recording at a password prompt.** `aterm ctl aos repair` now replays the recording on
  a background thread and only commits on the main thread, so windows keep drawing while
  it checks (the answer ends `main_us=` and `off_main=true`). A new code, `code=safe`, is
  the shipped glow with a wake every frame while it is lit, so it cannot leave light
  behind. A watcher replays each finished stretch of the recording in the background and
  keeps any that break the glow's contract as a fault; `aterm ctl aos ls` lists them,
  and nothing pops up. `aos export` saves the live recording, or a kept fault, as a
  private file (mode 0600) in aterm's state folder, refusing a folder there that is a
  link, and `aos check <file>` replays one under this build and refuses a file another
  build recorded or one longer than a window records in one stretch (4096 inputs, at
  most 2 MiB). A key aterm does not see echoed stops the recording before the key is
  logged: one the terminal does not echo, one a program reads raw (as ssh, sudo with
  pwfeedback and Node prompts do) unless it is typed at a prompt of aterm's own shell
  integration, and any key under Secure Keyboard Entry. So recording also stops at the
  first key typed into a full-screen program or a shell without that integration. An
  attach after such a key starts the glow from rest, so the recording holds no instant
  or rate of it. A glow that wears Sparkle's paper gold on a light theme is not
  recorded, because the recording cannot hold that ink yet: `aos attach` refuses it, and
  putting the gold on stops the recording. Before this, a repair turned the gold to the
  usual light-theme ink until `aos detach`. Results are graded Tested, not proved.

### Changed

- **The stats deck says less and shows a strain gauge.** Each figure reads in its own
  unit, with words only while something is unusual; the header names its scopes, and
  "over max" shows only while a strip draws it. A gauge for the whole Mac takes the
  cores block's place left of the names (the per-core view stays in the CPU lens and
  the Cores row), and the folded deck every window draws unless Full is chosen shows
  the same gauge at its top left wherever it fits. The deck keeps its height, so no tab
  re-grids. This is a prototype: its words and its gauge icon are not final.

- **A sign-in menu and another CLI's wrong-account renewal ask no one either.** Should a
  Claude Code tab whose login is an account in your `accounts.toml` with an email show a
  sign-in menu where its prompt was, aterm no longer flags the tab with `the login is gone:
  sign in with /login`: it records that the account's login ended, signs it in again by
  itself and restarts the tab onto the new login, the tab waiting meanwhile, its record
  naming what keeps it off the new login. That holds too where the menu comes up after aterm
  moved the tab onto that account, and the restart is made at the menu itself, which has no
  prompt for it to wait on. agy's sign-in menu, and a login no account in
  `accounts.toml` names, are flagged as before. The Messages entry for a Codex, Grok or Kimi
  renewal that signed in another account now says aterm threw that sign-in away and signs
  the account in again by itself, and points at `aterm harness accounts --cli <id>`, not at
  `accounts login`.

### Fixed

- **Reopened System State accepts the first settings choice.** Closing a startup
  review now retires its request immediately, so a choice made after reopening
  reaches the setup worker without waiting for a timer tick.

- **Markdown's Edit action reports when its file cannot be opened.** If a file
  disappears after the reader opens it, Edit now shows the failure instead of
  staying at “Opening editor…”. The loaded text stays available, and restoring
  the file allows another attempt.

- **Reopening a closed tab keeps Paste in the front window.** When recovery
  restores a tab in another window, it now preserves the front window's input
  target. This also covers a closed pane reopened as a replacement tab after
  its original split location disappears.

- **Reopen Closed Pane returns to its original tab.** After switching to another
  terminal tab or Settings, reopening a closed pane now selects its tab and
  routes terminal input to the reopened pane. Retained panes and unrelated
  tabs keep their contents.

- **First-launch setup waits for review.** Apply counts down from 30 seconds;
  clicking, typing, shortcuts or scrolling stops the timer. Busy time pauses
  it. Settings and vault credentials stay together until Apply. Cancel ends
  the attempt before background ALab detection can start setup. Stopped
  retries release their pending work without interfering with a later Apply.

- **An accepted vault password is used once.** Another settings action can
  overtake Join without leaving its accepted password available for a later
  Join. A replacement password stays available for its own submission.

- **Idle windows stop waking themselves.** A background cursor check could
  keep a CPU core busy even while no work was due.

- **Reopening a file focuses its existing editor in a restored split.** A line
  jump now reaches that editor instead of moving the sibling editor's caret.
  The split and its zoom state stay intact, and no duplicate editor opens.

- **An obsolete save reply keeps newer Save requests intact.** It no longer
  clears a newer save's pending state, drops a later explicit Save, or cancels
  a pending Quit. The current save still writes the latest requested draft
  before Quit completes.

- **After an update, every tab fits its window again.** When an update changed how
  much of the window the system performance deck takes (0.135.0 made it compact), one
  tab took the new rows, but the window's other tabs kept their old size, leaving blank
  rows at the bottom when you switched to them. Once a restore has put every tab back,
  each one now takes its window's size. `aterm ctl resizes` books that re-grid as
  `site=restore`. A window still waiting for the size a maximize or full screen brings
  re-grids every tab once that size arrives (or a few seconds on, if it never does), so
  no tab is first resized to a size the window is leaving.

- **A tab with a Settings or editor pane beside a shell fits its window after a resize.**
  Resizing the window while such a tab was in the background left its shell at the old
  size even after you switched back to it.

- **A Stop of a widened setup stays stopped.** On a Mac where aterm found the ALab vault
  and widened its own plan, a Stop put the old plan back, but the next launch, or Set up
  now, widened it again. The plan your Stop put back is now yours, and nothing widens it,
  also when an earlier aterm put it back.

- **Your Stop holds through a damaged setup record.** After a Stop, and Restore previous
  settings, a damaged setup record let aterm set its permissions up again by itself; a
  damaged note that aterm had set records aside turned them off though nobody stopped
  them; and a Stop saved just as a Restore finished could miss a run nobody had started
  yet. Each now keeps exactly what you stopped, and nothing more.

- **An older aterm leaves a newer aterm's setup alone.** Running an older aterm beside a
  newer one (a development build, say) could take the newer one's saved setup for a
  damaged record, put your Mac settings back to Leave as is and drop its progress. The
  older aterm now changes nothing of it, and System State says in one line that a newer
  aterm set up this Mac.

- **Setup no longer stops for good on a damaged run counter.** If the record that numbers
  setup runs was damaged, no choice, Set up now or `aterm doctor --apply` could be saved
  again, so aterm's permissions never ran. aterm now rebuilds it.

- **System State takes your choices while it cannot read the vault settings.** With vault
  settings aterm cannot read (after `sudo aterm secrets …`, say), every group choice was
  refused while Secrets was at Set up. Your choice is now saved; the Secrets step waits,
  joining nothing, until the settings can be read. A Join still says why it cannot go on.

- **A first-launch Join no longer holds setup back while aterm cannot read the vault
  settings.** Answering the first-launch offer with Join then held everything back,
  aterm's own permissions included, and tried the same answer again every minute. Your
  answer now goes ahead without the Join: Full Disk Access, Developer Tools, the
  debugger, Local Network and every other group are set up, nothing is joined, and System
  State says the vault was not joined and that `aterm secrets status` says why. The vault
  you typed stays in its field, so you can Join once the settings can be read.

- **A Join refused for unreadable vault settings is no longer a failure.** System State
  said "Setup failed. Set up now tries again." It now says calmly that aterm cannot read
  this Mac's vault settings and that `aterm secrets status` says why, with no Set up now,
  menu line or tab attention, and keeps the vault and password you typed.

- **A Restore that waited for another setup shows that it is restoring.** Once the other
  setup finished, the Restore put your settings back while System State still said it was
  waiting and kept its groups live, and a group pressed then ran after the Restore
  instead of replacing it. The page now says "Restoring previous settings…" from the
  moment the Restore starts writing; a group pressed before then replaces it, having
  changed nothing. It also shows waiting from the moment it finds another setup holding
  this Mac's setup.

- **A damaged setup record beside a newer aterm's no longer loops.** System State kept
  saying it would read the saved setup again and kept trying to set it aside, which the
  newer aterm's record never allows. It now says in one line that a newer aterm set up
  this Mac.

- **The note that aterm set its saved setup aside goes once you answer.** Answering the
  first-launch offer with a choice of your own now takes it away, as any other choice
  does, and its exceptions digest entry goes with it.

- **A Restore waiting for another setup reads nothing meanwhile.** While another aterm or
  `aterm doctor` held this Mac's setup, a pressed Restore read your keyboard, trackpad,
  Desktop and Dock settings again every second. It now waits quietly and reads them once,
  when it runs.

- **`aterm doctor --apply` is not run again at the next launch.** Run while setup's offer
  still waited for its answer (after a Restore, or after a choice a quit cut short), it
  reset the Dock and signed out of Messages and FaceTime, and the next launch did both
  again. It now records what it did, also after you cancelled setup in an older aterm,
  and takes over that setup run unless you did.

- **An old Local Network "Don't Allow" no longer sticks.** Once aterm had heard macOS
  refuse the local network, System State read Local Network as Off for good, even after
  aterm asked again and you allowed it. The newest answer now wins, whatever the Mac's
  clock said when either was heard, and Check again looks again, without ever asking you.

- **The request to free disk space waits for people, and survives an aterm update.** The
  line is no longer typed into a tab where someone typed moments ago: it waits for that
  session's next turn break. A tab whose last turn was a person's own exchange with the
  agent, or whose task a manager is waiting on, is passed over for another session
  instead, and that uses up none of the request's tries. Each tab is checked at every turn
  break, even when it has not been chosen, and a tab passed over because it had no task, or
  had finished it, can be chosen as soon as it starts work on a new one. Before, a tab
  passed over once was never chosen in a later request. A seamless update no longer passes
  the request on as undelivered: the new aterm process takes over the chosen session, and
  any other aterm process now leaves it three minutes to do so. If the chosen agent exits
  during the update, the new process releases it at no cost; before, the request waited
  three minutes and then used up one of its choices. The note that asks an agent to retry
  after the disk filled up is no longer typed into a person's own exchange, or while
  someone is typing.

- **The request to free disk space keeps an accurate count.** The space a session frees is
  measured from the moment its line goes, not from a check up to a minute earlier. A line
  whose record could not be saved, because the disk was full, still counts as one of the
  request's two lines once it is saved, and the request goes back to waiting on that
  session's answer; a session chosen meanwhile whose line would be a third is not asked.
  The record is also saved when another aterm process has already ended the request
  because space came back. Before, that line was never counted, so the next shortage
  typed a second line instead of waiting out the six-hour pause. On Linux, changing the
  clock no longer makes a running aterm process look as though it had ended.

- **A choice made while another setup runs is applied, not dropped.** When another aterm,
  or `aterm doctor` in a terminal, holds this Mac's setup, a System State choice or
  Restore now waits for it and goes ahead when it finishes. The page keeps your choice
  showing and says "Another setup is running; aterm applies your choice when it
  finishes." from the moment it meets the other setup. A later press replaces the waiting
  one, a group pressed while a Restore waits included, and Check again stays live
  meanwhile. It is no longer shown as a failure.

- **Setup goes on when its saved records cannot be read.** An unreadable vault
  configuration no longer stops setup: the Secrets row says aterm cannot read the vault
  settings, and Permissions and every other group go ahead. A saved setup that cannot be
  read just now is one calm line while aterm reads it again. One that is damaged for good
  is kept beside itself as `<name>.unreadable`, and setup starts afresh, leaving
  your Mac settings as they are and setting up aterm's permissions by itself (on an ALab
  Mac the vault and repositories stay set up too), with one calm line on the page saying
  so and an entry in the exceptions digest, both gone once you make a choice or Restore.

- **System State says a failure only when you can act on it.** While aterm still retries
  a step, a reading or a whole setup run, the page counts it as waiting ("1 step
  waiting", "Waiting to try setup again…"), the row keeps its reason, and nothing marks
  the tab; once the retries stop, the headline, the tab mark and the menu line say it
  failed together. A row a run or Check could not confirm no longer shows a check mark:
  it reads "Not confirmed". A failed Check again says pressing it again reads the rows
  anew.

- **System State tells a passing failure from one you must fix.** A GitHub token the
  vault syncs that GitHub refused showed a red "Failed" row under a headline saying
  aterm would try again by itself. Now a step that fails for a passing reason (GitHub or
  the vault not answering, a change that did not take) reads "Will change" with its
  reason while aterm tries again, and "Failed" only once those tries are spent. A step
  only you can fix (a GitHub token to renew in the vault or add to it, Apple's Command
  Line Tools to install) reads "Needs you" with what to do. aterm stops retrying it, and
  rereads the row every minute while System State is shown, and whenever you return
  to it. A step no retry can change, such as GitHub repositories on a Mac with more
  than one user account, reads "Failed" at once. In every case the headline, the row,
  the tab mark and the menu line agree.

## [0.138.0] - 2026-10-25

### Added

- **Commons supports a stable empty network foundation.** Administrators with
  the same trusted authority can derive the same starting identity. Membership
  still requires signed approval, and competing first rosters remain visible
  as conflicts. New vaults bind this foundation in their first signed envelope;
  normal edits preserve the published root. Automatic enrollment is still being
  connected, and older unbound vaults require explicit migration.

- **Commons readiness has a local diagnostic.** `aterm db commons-status` shows
  vault availability, pending enrollment, inactive membership, control-history
  problems, reader/writer access and whether sharing is enabled. Application
  commands now name the unavailable vault boundary instead of conflating it with
  vault enrollment. A hidden control entry never becomes a prompt to reset a network.

- **Spreadsheet account candidates can share over ALab Commons.**
  `aterm db accounts-import-csv --file <csv> --request <nonce>` imports one bounded
  source atomically; `accounts-imports` shows the candidates and provenance.
  Email and machine labels remain unverified hints. Private notes, payment cells
  and phone values stay in the original spreadsheet; import never activates a login.

- **Account and contact proposals share over ALab Commons.** Enrolled machines
  can use `aterm db accounts-write`, `accounts-get`, `accounts-scan`,
  `accounts-history` and `accounts-revert` without choosing a database directory
  or running a sync command. The encrypted LAN table retains offline edits,
  conflicting values and each change's provenance. Mailboxes, explicit email
  aliases, phone references and machine assignment proposals stay separate from
  login activation and spending authority. Recovery restrictions also reach peers
  that missed the discarded history, so reconnecting cannot revive its old values.

- **Rewind a pane to see what was on its screen a moment ago.** With Settings >
  Terminal > Rewind (keep recent screen history) on, a new tab keeps its recent
  screens. View > Rewind Pane (Shift-Cmd-R on macOS) freezes the focused pane on
  the newest one; Left and Right step through the kept screens and Esc returns to
  live. While a pane is rewound your keys and clicks go nowhere, the program's
  output keeps arriving underneath, and a band at the pane's foot says when the
  screen was, how much output arrived since, and whether a live check matched it
  (`unchecked` until one has). `aterm ctl rewind` opens, steps, reads and closes the
  same view. Tested: the rewound pane draws the recorder's replay cell for cell, and
  an idle open view stays within the idle instance's timer-wake budget.

- **`aterm ctl aos` works in the shipped app.** Aos, the substrate that checkpoints,
  records and replays the typing-momentum glow, now answers in release builds:
  `status`, `attach`, `pause`, `repair` (with the shipped code it replays the recorded
  trace, checks that the live code reproduces the paused state and keeps the glow's
  contract, then resumes), `resume`, `detach` and `trace`. `publish`, `bundle` and the
  demonstration code still need a debug build and say so by name (`ERR aos publish
  needs a debug build`). Results are graded Tested, not proved.

- **Aos keeps the glow's recent history, repairs it off the main thread, and stops
  recording at a password prompt.** `aterm ctl aos repair` now replays the recording on
  a background thread and only commits on the main thread, so windows keep drawing while
  it checks (the answer ends `main_us=` and `off_main=true`). A new code, `code=safe`, is
  the shipped glow with a wake every frame while it is lit, so it cannot leave light
  behind. A watcher replays each finished stretch of the recording in the background and
  keeps any that break the glow's contract as a fault; `aterm ctl aos ls` lists them,
  and nothing pops up. `aos export` saves the live recording, or a kept fault, as a
  private file (mode 0600) in aterm's state folder, and `aos check <file>` replays one
  under this build and refuses a file another build recorded. A key the terminal does
  not echo, as at a password prompt, or Secure Keyboard Entry stops the recording before
  the key is logged. A glow that wears Sparkle's paper gold on a light theme is not
  recorded, because the recording cannot hold that ink yet: `aos attach` refuses it, and
  putting the gold on stops the recording. Before this, a repair turned the gold to the
  usual light-theme ink until `aos detach`. Results are graded Tested, not proved.

- **The Overview lists what sessions on your fabric's other machines need from you.** Its
  "On the fabric" group shows each session whose own log says it waits at a box or a
  question (◇), or is stuck on a failure, a limit or not responding (◆), with its machine
  and how old the reading is. It is read from the fabric's shared log, never from that
  machine, and a reading more than 5 minutes old is shown as older and not counted. Choosing
  a chip does nothing to the session. `aterm ctl controls overview` lists each chip. This
  shipped in 0.112.0, whose notes left it out.

- **`aterm fabric brief --json`.** It prints what `aterm fabric brief` folds as one object a
  program can read: each session's machine, its id on the bus, what it needs
  (`"need":"approval:bash"`), its open run and turn, its mail counts and how old its newest
  record is. Like the text brief it holds ids, closed words and counts only. This shipped in
  0.112.0, whose notes left it out.

- (developer tool) **`lab codex-measure` measures a new codex-alab build in one command**: both
  proof runs, the reduced rollouts and the `docs/measured` note, or a named refusal that leaves the
  checkout as it was.

### Changed

- **The aterm menu has fewer duplicate entries.** Updates, Packages, Messages
  and Open aterm.toml remain available inside Settings and through the command
  palette and control interface. Their separate application-menu shortcuts are
  removed; Settings and System State stay in the menu.

- **aterm signs your listed Claude accounts in by itself instead of asking you.** When a
  Claude Code tab's login ends and that login is an account in your `accounts.toml` with
  an email, aterm no longer types `/login` in the tab or puts a sign-in notice on screen:
  it signs that account in again by its automatic sign-in (ahead of every other account
  waiting for one) and restarts the tab onto the new login. That holds with a draft in the
  prompt, in a tab with no task, and where `relaunch` or `resume_limits` is off or aterm
  cannot restart the tab: the account is still signed in, and the tab waits, its record
  naming what keeps it off the new login. Your own `/login` stays yours. The Messages
  entries about your accounts (a signed-out account with no email, logins due for
  renewal, Codex, Grok and Kimi logins due too, none lasting past tomorrow, a renewal
  that signed in another account) now say what aterm did and point at `aterm harness
  accounts`, which shows each sign-in route it tried, never at `accounts renew` or
  `accounts login`. A failed automatic renewal of a login that is due now shows in the
  no-sign-in entry and in `aterm harness accounts` too, and a login signed in again in its
  tab no longer brings back an older failure once it comes due.

- **A landing no longer claims the work is on the remote main branch.** When Autopilot
  Land lands, the chip's hovered `✓ landed` title and the `Autopilot landed` record in
  Messages now say `it said nothing is left, and no repository check found work left to
  land; the harness types nothing more until someone else's turn`. They used to say `all of
  the work is on the remote main branch`, also for a repository with no remote, a folder
  that is not a repository or one macOS guards, and codex-alab's own landing, where aterm
  checked no remote main. `aterm help harness`, `aterm help workers`, `aterm ctl help task`
  and the agent primer now say what the `git` check reads and where it reads nothing.
  (developer) At a clean done claim the repository probe also reads which commit `HEAD` is,
