  whether the repository has a remote, and its main branch (`RepoRead::Checked`, taped as
  `{"at":{…}}`; an older tape's `null` still reads clean, and a read git refused names
  nothing). That costs one more `git rev-parse` per probe, and every decision stays the
  same.

- **`brew` compatibility uses atpkg without a Homebrew fallback.** Unsupported
  commands, recipes and flags fail with their missing native capability;
  `--real` and `ABREW_REAL` no longer run another package manager. Disabled
  managed wrappers and an unavailable atpkg also refuse the command. Existing
  managed wrappers are refreshed during repair. `brew bundle` and `abrew
  bundle` install native Brewfiles; installing a Homebrew bundle is removed.
  Old bundles stay unused until explicitly removed with `bundle remove`.

- **Settings ▸ Harness says its counts plainly.** In WHAT THE HARNESS DID, the row under
  `Kept going` reads `past “done”  3 today · 3 in 7 days`, the times the harness kept going
  past an agent's "done" (it read `of them  a done claim checked …`), and the row under
  `Approved` reads `no safe rule  2 today · 5 in 7 days`. `Needed you` and `Waited on you` are
  one row, `Waited for you  2 today, 14m · 5 in 7 days, 1h 2m`: the times the harness stopped
  and asked you, and how long it waited. `Needs told` is `Needs, carried on`. A count with none
  in the week is no longer a row of `0 today · 0 in 7 days`: each is named in one last row,
  `None in 7 days  declined · answered · resumed · …`, in the card's order. A session's day
  line and STATUS's today line use the same words (`today: waited for you once, 1m at 18:29 ·
  2 needs, carried on · 1 landed · 31 approved`, `waited for you 4m`), and a session's day line
  now says a wait that ran on into today from an ask raised before it (`today: waited for you
  3m · …`), as the page's row and STATUS's line count it.

- **The cursor glow's beams cost the GPU less.** The Rainbow Kitty ribbon and meteor
  trains, Bolt and the comet now lay a beam's one-pixel rows as ramps, one item for a run
  of rows, where they laid a quad a row. On Metal a frame draws its ramps in the effects
  stream where that measures cheaper than an instance a row, and draws the rows as before
  where it does not; a GPU backend with no measurement always draws them as before. Every
  frame is the same as before, byte for byte. On the effects bench (an M4 Pro), a typing
  flood presents 28–30 % faster at the p95 and plain typing 5–7 %, and the typing ribbon
  draws 639 GPU instances a frame where it drew 5,730.

- **codex-alab 0.1.0-dev.13665 is measured, so its tabs' session logs hold turns.** The
  first build on codex-alab's own version line (client `0.165.0-dev.13665`, OpenAI's
  codex up to Oct 23) showed nothing in its session record that the measured builds did
  not, so aterm reads its turns from that record, as it does for 13594.

- **The menu bar's This Mac row says `landing` for a held Land session, and the Overview says
  `landed` once.** A Land session that holds (Land's instruction typed, its work not landed yet)
  now counts as `landing` there, the word Settings ▸ Harness already says for it, where it
  counted as `resting`: `This Mac — 1 need you · 6 landing · 1 resting · 5 landed · 3 shells`.
  A need or a wait it carries still counts first, so This Mac's `landing` can be smaller than
  the page's Every session row, and a Cruise session at rest stays `resting`. The Overview's row of a
  landed task now ends `task landed 17m · 128 B · driven by aterm (land)`, where it said
  `(land, landed)` after `task landed`; the tab's hover, which has no task words, keeps
  `driven by aterm (land, landed)`. (developer tool) The forever lab's L7 judges This Mac's
  landing count against the Land tabs that hold at rest, less those whose need it counts, and
  `verify appkit`'s toolbar drive reads This Mac back off a real status item's menu.

- **Session recordings replay exactly and check themselves against the screen.** With
  `temporal_recording = true` (Settings > Terminal > Rewind (keep recent screen
  history)), each piece of output now replays at the clock reading it was first shown
  at, so a synchronized frame that timed out, bells close together and command
  timestamps come back as they were. While it records, the session also keeps
  snapshots of the real screen (after every 256 KiB of output or once a second, only
  when output arrives) and checks each replay against them: `aterm ctl temporal status`
  reports `witnessed=` and `diverged=`, and after a mismatch the recording starts again
  from the live screen. Replays also check shell-integration marks with the session's
  own key, as the live tab does.

- **Summarize also reads `aterm fabric brief` when the fabric is on,** so its brief covers
  what your fabric's other machines report; without the fabric its brief is unchanged.
  Summarize This Mac also reads `aterm ctl survey --brief`, what each session's log says.
  Both shipped in 0.112.0, whose notes left them out.

- **`aterm link broker` says what it no longer keeps.** A read below the oldest record it
  keeps answers `retained-from=<offset>` instead of quietly starting later (`aterm ctl inbox
  get @<offset>` says `ERR retained-from=<floor>`), and so does a read of unread mail it
  gave up past its 7 days or 64 MiB, so nothing it drops is dropped silently. It trims its
  log while it runs, and a crash in the middle of a trim leaves a log it opens again. This
  shipped in 0.111.0, whose notes did not say it.

### Fixed

- **Select All stays inside the focused terminal pane.** In a split scrolled
  into history, it could select and copy lines below the visible pane. It now
  uses that pane's own grid dimensions and keeps its scroll position.

- **Copy stays available for a selected terminal split after focus moves.**
  Edit ▸ Copy and the command palette now recognize a visible sibling pane's
  selection. A focused blank selection keeps ownership, and hidden panes or
  native-app focus do not supply another terminal's text.

- **After an update, every tab fits its window again.** When an update changed how
  much of the window the system performance deck takes (0.135.0 made it compact), one
  tab took the new rows, but the window's other tabs kept their old size, leaving blank
  rows at the bottom when you switched to them. Once a restore has put every tab back,
  each one now takes its window's size. `aterm ctl resizes` books that re-grid as
  `site=restore`. A window the restore maximizes or puts in full screen re-grids its
  tabs to the size that brings instead, so none of them is resized twice.

- **Reopen Closed Tab fits a split tab's panes to the window.** Each pane of a reopened
  split kept the whole window's size until the window was next resized.

- **Lost Commons state cannot silently become an empty history.** An independent
  local claim survives loss of the control directory and its pin. Reopening
  requires recovery of the recorded history, including when table files are the
  surviving evidence. Simultaneous opens serialize before inspecting custody;
  interrupted initial creation resumes under a separate pending phase. Intact
  older installations gain the claim on next open.

- **A Stop of a widened setup stays stopped.** On a Mac where aterm found the ALab vault
  and widened its own plan, a Stop put the old plan back, but the next launch, or Set up
  now, widened it again. The plan your Stop put back is now yours, and nothing widens it.

- **`aterm doctor --apply` is not run again at the next launch.** Run while setup's offer
  still waited for its answer (after a Restore, or after a choice a quit cut short), it
  reset the Dock and signed out of Messages and FaceTime, and the next launch did both
  again. It now takes over that setup run and records what it did, unless you cancelled
  setup in an older aterm.

- **A choice made after a Restore is kept even if aterm quits while saving it.** Turning
  a group back to Set up after Restore previous settings, cut short by a quit or a
  crash, was undone at the next launch. The next launch now offers your choice and sets
  that group.

- **Restoring an older aterm's setup keeps aterm's permissions on.** After Restore
  previous settings on a Mac an older aterm had set up, from System State or with
  `aterm doctor --restore`, aterm's permissions disappeared from System State until the
  next launch, and a choice made meanwhile signed out of Messages and FaceTime again.
  They now stay on, and nothing signs out again.

- **An old Local Network "Don't Allow" no longer sticks.** Once aterm had heard macOS
  refuse the local network, System State read Local Network as Off for good, even after
  aterm asked again and you allowed it. The newest answer now wins, and Check again
  looks again, without ever asking you.

- **aterm's permissions are not left for the next launch when setup is busy.** A launch
  that found another setup step holding setup's records skipped setting up aterm's
  permissions after a Restore until the next launch. It now waits for that step, quietly,
  and sets them up in the same launch.

- **aterm looks for the ALab vault at once after a finished setup.** A launch whose
  setup had finished could wait up to ten minutes, behind putting back the widget list
  once aterm had Full Disk Access, before it looked for the ALab vault. That put-back now
  waits on its own.

- **Vault signing-key rotation preserves Commons administration.** Commons keeps
  its authority key in the encrypted admin locker across vault rotations. Older
  lockers migrate without changing an existing network's root; missing or
  mismatched custody refuses instead of silently inventing a replacement key.
  Admin demotion refuses when Commons may already trust that admin's key, until
  an authority transfer is supported; deleting its control entry cannot bypass it.

- **Returning text keeps its cursor-trail age when typing resumes.** When a
  program briefly clears part of a line, then redraws it with newly typed
  characters, the original text keeps its existing rainbow instead of
  restarting the whole line's trail. Expired text still follows the normal
  revival rules.

- **System State recovery preserves Stop and permission choices.** Damaged
  progress no longer reuses old run history. Stop survives relaunch, and
  retrying interrupted recovery keeps newer choices. Setup retries workers
  that failed to start and repairs records damaged during a review.

- **Reopening System State keeps an Apply busy.** Restore, Check again and
  Join stay disabled until the pending Apply and a fresh reading resolve.
  Closing the page no longer loses that Apply's result.

- **Tab shortcuts retain their window.** New Tab, next/previous tab and direct
  tab selection use the window that received the key, including when its tab
  strip mixes terminals and editors and another window became frontmost.

- **The request to free disk space is no longer cancelled and restarted every minute.**
  When two aterm processes on one disk held different free-space floors, or free space
  sat right at the floor, one look opened the request and the next look ended it. No
  session was ever chosen, and `disk.jsonl` gained an opened row and an ended row every
  minute. Now a request stays open until free space is 5 GiB past the highest floor of
  the processes checking the disk, and, on a disk out of inodes, until free inodes are
  twice the 50,000 that count as out. `aterm harness disk why`, the line the session is
  typed and the low-disk alert all name that floor. A request that ran out, or that a
  session settled by freeing a little, no longer keeps a disk that stays near its floor
  from being asked about again: six hours on, a check that finds the disk short starts a
  new one.

- **A chosen session whose task finishes is released at once.** Before, a session that
  landed or exited after it was chosen to free disk space kept its line owed for 30
  minutes, and then used up one of the request's four choices. Now its window releases
  it at the next disk check, and the next session is chosen at no cost. The same holds
  for a chosen Claude Code that exits for good, one whose tab now runs another agent,
  and one whose directory is on another disk. None of them is typed the line.

- **The request to free disk space waits for people, and survives an aterm update.** The
  line is no longer typed into a tab where someone typed moments ago: it waits for that
  session's next turn break. A tab whose last turn was a person's own exchange with the
  agent, or that a manager is waiting on, is passed over for another session instead, and
  that uses up none of the request's tries. A seamless update no longer passes the request
  on as undelivered: the new aterm process takes over the chosen session, and any other
  aterm process now leaves it three minutes to do so. The note that asks an agent to retry
  after the disk filled up is no longer typed into a person's own exchange, or while
  someone is typing.

- **The request to free disk space keeps an accurate count.** The space a session frees is
  measured from the moment its line goes, not from a check up to a minute earlier. A line
  whose record could not be saved, because the disk was full, still counts as one of the
  request's two lines once it is saved, and the request goes back to waiting on that
  session's answer; a session chosen meanwhile whose line would be a third is not asked.
  On Linux, changing the clock no longer makes a running aterm process look as though it
  had ended.

- **Close shortcuts retain their window.** A configured Close shortcut or
  Cmd-W closes the originating window's focused content even when another
  window became frontmost before the key was delivered.

- **Terminal Find controls leave native search fields alone.** `find open`
  no longer opens an editor or Settings prompt that its other commands cannot
  drive. Edit → Find and `invoke Find` remain contextual.

- **A Claude Code that aterm restarts keeps its own updater off.** A restart,
  live upgrade, account move or a spawned worker starts the managed copy by its
  own path, which skipped the managed launcher's settings, so Claude Code's own
  updater could download a build of its own and re-point `~/.local/bin/claude`.
  A line aterm types that starts a managed copy by its own path now carries
  what the managed launcher would (`DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` for Claude Code, the
  one program aterm starts that way), and a line too long for the terminal
  drops the survey switch first, never the updater switch.

- **System State keeps retry limits during local read errors.** A temporary
  network, vault or subscriber read failure no longer resets the retry limit.
  Known changes to other inputs still let setup recover.

- **A choice made while another setup runs is applied, not dropped.** When another aterm,
  or `aterm doctor` in a terminal, holds this Mac's setup, a System State choice or
  Restore now waits for it and goes ahead when it finishes. The page keeps your choice
  showing and says "Another setup is running; aterm applies your choice when it
  finishes." A later press replaces the waiting one. It is no longer shown as a failure.

- **Setup goes on when its saved records cannot be read.** An unreadable vault
  configuration no longer stops setup: the Secrets row says aterm cannot read the vault
  settings, and Permissions and every other group go ahead. A saved setup that cannot be
  read just now is one calm line while aterm reads it again. One that is damaged for good
  is kept beside itself as `<name>.unreadable`, and setup starts afresh, leaving
  your Mac settings as they are and setting up aterm's permissions by itself, with one
  calm line on the page and an entry in the exceptions digest.

- **System State no longer shows a failure while aterm retries starting setup.** The page
  says "aterm could not start setup just now; it tries again by itself." with no failure,
  tab mark or menu line, and the exceptions digest notes it if it goes on for ten
  minutes.

- **A Restore that fails as a whole says so.** The headline reads "Restore previous
  settings failed" with the reason in plain words. A Restore pressed while a setup step
  holds the records for a moment now waits for it instead of being refused.

- **The ALab vault note goes when its run ends.** "aterm found the ALab vault on this
  network, so it is setting up the rest of this Mac." stayed on System State after that
  setup finished, until the next run started.

- **System State no longer calls a retry a failure.** A step aterm tries again by itself,
  such as joining the Secrets vault, is counted as waiting ("2 steps waiting: Secrets
  vault, GitHub repositories"), and its note says it did not finish this time and that
  aterm tries again by itself. The headline says a step failed, and the tab and the menu
  bar mark it, only once aterm stops trying. The village beside the logo now draws a
  failed step with its error look, even where the row reads in place, and a step aterm
  is retrying as waiting.

- **A Check again that failed is a note, not an alert.** It only read your Mac, and
  pressing it again is the fix, so it no longer marks the tab or adds a line to the menu
  bar; the headline says "This Mac is set up, as last read". A row a run or a Check
  could not confirm is counted in the headline ("1 row not confirmed: GitHub
  repositories") instead of "This Mac is set up".

- **Debugger access shows no dead Turn On… while macOS asks for your password.** The
  button is replaced by "Waiting for your administrator password in the SamplingTools
  dialog". The tab and the menu bar still say it needs you, since the dialog may be
  behind other windows.

- **System State's words read the same way everywhere.** Local Network, which macOS does
  not report, reads "—" with its note on every page state, and VoiceOver says "Local
  Network: unknown" before the note. VoiceOver reads the logo as "aterm ALab", without the
  dot. A Restore's summary names every row as the page does, without "the" ("Desktop,
  Widgets and Dock are as they were"). The manual calls the button by its name, Restore
  previous settings.

- **Local Network keeps newer permission observations.** An observation with
  an older timestamp can no longer replace a newer refusal in memory or on disk.

- **Trail-gallery cannot skip a requested rainbow that went dark.** Return
  measurements follow the final instance configuration, including overrides.
  Losing eligibility or live ribbon geometry is inconclusive; intentionally
  disabled or other trails remain outside that measurement.

- **Long control replies avoid repeated prefix scans.** Fragmented reply lines
  are searched incrementally while retaining the same framing and size bounds.

- **Repository setup resumes after a network change.** It now notices local
  interface changes after vault setup finishes or when using existing
  credentials, and resumes the unfinished step. A network or vault change
  during the final retry is also noticed before setup goes to sleep.

- **Autopilot puts off Claude Code's "Teach auto mode about your environment?" offer.**
  Claude Code 2.1.310 raises it at the end of a turn in auto mode and again at every
  turn's end until it is answered, and Land and Cruise sessions stalled behind it
  with "typed, not submitted". The harness now answers `Not now` at every `approve`
  level, in the inline and fullscreen renderers and in panes as narrow as 16 columns,
  the narrowest a split leaves, where Claude Code wraps the offer's footer (35 columns
  or narrower, onto as many as four rows) and its last answer (22 or narrower), never
  while you are typing, and records the answer in its ledger; `Not now` puts the
  offer off for a week and changes nothing else. It then decides the turn's end
  again, so its continuation is typed once the offer is gone.

- **A command stopped with Ctrl-Z stays `parked` while the next one runs.** `sys jobs` read
  a stopped job as parked only while the shell held the terminal, so a `vim` stopped with
  Ctrl-Z read `stop=held`, then `quiet` and in time `stuck`, once the next command ran,
  and so did `gdb` waiting at its prompt while the program it debugs sat at a breakpoint.
  Now a stop is `parked` when job control took the terminal from it, and a job whose own
  command runs in front is judged by that command; a build whose step stopped at the
  terminal (a `ninja` step at an ssh passphrase prompt, a `ninja &`'s too, also under
  `aterm -e ninja` or after `exec ninja`) still reads `quiet`, a Ctrl-Z'd `cargo nextest
  run` reads `parked`, and so does a `git pull &` stopped at its password prompt in a tab
  without shell integration. After `exec ninja` its build is one row that runs while its
  steps compile, after `exec python3` a REPL hung on a lock no longer reads as the shell's
  `read`, and after `exec zsh` the block ends at the new shell's prompt, also beside the
  `tee` a `.bashrc` logs the session through or from a `case` arm, after a comment or a
  here-document holding a quote, or past `ZDOTDIR=${…}/zsh`, and on macOS whatever the
  line says (a bash line kept out of history, which bash reports only in part), also when
  the first key at the new prompt opens a full-screen history widget (atuin's or hstr's
  Ctrl-R, `$(lf)`), so a background job's lines are its own again; `exec vim` back from a
  `:sh` keeps its row, its `:!make` included, also past vim's hit-enter prompt, when
  picked in atuin's full-screen search, and when kept to the main screen (`t_ti= t_te=`,
  as `exec psql` back from its `\!` is). A download pwsh runs in itself (`Invoke-WebRequest`)
  keeps its row, also after `exec pwsh`, beside a zsh it ran or between a loop's `docker
  exec`s, also one whose line a backtick continues, as does a `vared` prompt, and a build
  run by `exec cmake --build` or `out=$(ninja)` is one row as well, also when aterm saw its
  first process a moment before the command started, while one a pwsh `Start-Job` left
  running, by its steps (also those its `make` forks later in pwsh's group) or its lines,
  no longer keeps a later hung `git fetch` reading running, nor does a server
  `Start-Process -NoNewWindow` left printing there keep a deadlocked `dotnet test` running,
  nor one aterm may not read (`sudo log stream`) a hung `sudo mount`, also by the last line
  of one that exits or the lines of one that ran such a program in its place; a `dotnet
  build` in a pwsh run in pwsh, its profile writing the prompt's marks, reads running, as
  does a cmdlet it runs itself or a build printing through its `Tee-Object`, also after a
  command typed ahead with that `pwsh` or right at its first prompt, in a new tab whose
  shell that `pwsh` was typed into as it started, or after the Mac slept, and a `ninja`
  there is one row, while the builds of a pwsh `Start-Process` started (a `watch.ps1`,
  also each
  `pwsh -File build.ps1` it runs, also one that pwsh's profile started, also after a quick
  `pwsh -c` or `pwsh --version`, or with a `pwsh` you ran or pasted a moment after
  starting it, also the `git fetch` itself pasted right behind) no longer keep a hung
  `git fetch` running.
  A `fg` typed ahead of the end of a command, a `fg %1` right after a Ctrl-Z, and a Ctrl-Z
  in the middle of a bash command list (`make; fg %1`) no longer split the resumed job in
  two, drop the earlier command's row, give one command's exit status to the other, or
  leave the resumed job behind the stopped one. A pipeline stage that runs in a group of its
  own (`seq 1 40 | timeout 3600 xargs ./step.sh`) is judged by the lines the tab prints
  once the stage in front exits, when it is the tab's one background job that can run,
  instead of reading `quiet`, then `stuck`; a parked editor no longer takes those lines or
  keeps them from it. A command run with `sudo` (which runs it on a terminal of its own),
  under `script`, or as an agent's tool call on a terminal of its own (Codex, Gemini CLI)
  is one row beside its opener's, judged by what it does: printing, it reads running, and
  hung on a server that stopped answering it reads `stuck` while sudo waits at the terminal
  and the agent's screen keeps moving, also when the agent runs in `nvim`'s terminal or in
  a tab whose shell gave way to it (`exec codex`) or that runs it in place of a shell
  (`aterm -e codex`). A Ctrl-Z'd `sudo vim` reads `parked`; a command hung in front of
  `script`'s shell beside a job that shell stopped reads `stuck`, and a program there
  waiting for your keys (`vim`, a password prompt, the shell itself) reads by that
  terminal's own mode: fine. That mode is your wait only once your keys were seen reaching
  that terminal twice within a minute, and stays so while you type in another `nvim` window
  or Emacs holds your keys until Enter, so a hung call on a terminal Codex or Emacs opened
  (Emacs keeps each in a line mode with no echo) no longer reads fine, while a shell in
  Emacs's buffer at its prompt does, and so does a `node` REPL or a `bash` at `read -t 30`
  there; a REPL there hung on its socket (an asyncio one too), a shell there stuck on a dead
  network share, or one at its prompt beside a hung background job (a Go `./sync &` hung on
  its peer) reads `stuck`, as does `script -q rec.log npm
  install` once the registry stops answering and only its spinner moves, and a loop hung in
  `nvim`'s terminal while you type in another window, while `pytest` printing its results in
  `nvim`'s terminal reads running, and so does `mvn verify` there, whose JVM keeps waking.
  A `ping host &` of a `bash` run in the tab reads running while that bash waits at its
  prompt. A command a `zsh` or `bash` run in the tab runs reads running while it prints,
  also a zsh script or in a tab without the prompt's marks, and that shell's row reads
  waiting on it, not quiet; one you stop there with Ctrl-Z, also under a `bash` or
  `nix-shell` that writes none of the prompt's marks, reads `parked`, sent on with `bg`
  and hung it reads `stuck`, and one you bring forward with `fg` ends with its own
  status; `vim`'s `:sh` keeps vim's row, running a `make` you typed there (also
  right away) and waiting for you with one you stopped, which reads `parked` on its own,
  while a `ninja &` there reads running. A `tail -F app.log | xargs …`
  whose xargs reaps its finished children late reads waiting, fine, not zombie, while one
  whose ingest deadlocked with its children unreaped reads zombie, as does a deadlocked
  `python3 crawl.py | less` or a script deadlocked under its own pager, while one that
  waits for you to page on reads fine, also one feeding its pager from a poll loop
  (`subprocess.run(input=…)`), and a `python3` at its `>>>` holding a child it has
  not reaped reads fine, also beside a server it started (also one `socketserver` runs, on
  Linux), what is left of one it killed, multiprocessing's resource tracker, a queue's
  consumer it started or, on Linux, a worker it feeds through a pipe and that polls it,
  under `make shell` or in a pwsh tab, while a script
  deadlocked beside its server in `nvim`'s terminal reads zombie; an `irb` at its prompt in
  Emacs reads fine, also beside a server it spawned or run by a shell there, while one
  beside that server waiting on a hung child's output reads zombie; a script blocked
  writing to an `ssh` asking for a password (`python3 export.py | ssh nas …`, also `| sudo
  tee` on Linux) reads waiting on you, as does `ssh nas pg_dump app | python3 load.py`
  asking for one, also run by a `./dump.sh`, with load.py reading it through asyncio or a
  `select` loop, also beside its open database connection, or, on Linux, with load.py
  reading a `zstd -dc` it started, and a `git
  push` asking for one under `python3 deploy.py | tee /dev/tty |
  gzip`, and one deadlocked with a `gzip` it both feeds and reads under `less` reads
  zombie, also on Linux, as does a deadlocked `crawl.py | more` (util-linux `more` reads
  its keys from its standard error, polling since 2.35), also on a kernel whose wait
  channel names a compiler's clone (`poll_schedule_timeout.constprop.0`), and `fzf |
  python3 ingest.py`
  deadlocked reading a worker, while on Linux a build writing its warnings into `less` on
  page one reads fine, also before Linux 5.5; an `ssh` asking for a password under `python3
  sync.py | tee sync.log` reads waiting on you, also through a `grep`, a `| while read`
  loop (zsh's, or bash's in a subshell, also in a zsh script `make` runs), a zsh function
  (`| stamp | tee sync.log`), a `node` filter or an `ssh` that logged in (`| ssh logs 'cat
  >> sync.log'`), and a script whose `make` waits for you to page on in `less`,
  also through a `grep` or a shell function's `less`, reads fine. A
  command no longer reads running on lines
  another program printed (a hung `git push` beside a printing `tail -f &`, a hung
  background job beside a prompt that redraws its clock, a hung `sudo` command beside a
  printing background job, also a `sudo` one or one that ended, a hung `git fetch` as
  zsh prints that a background job is done, a waiting loop such as `until pg_isready; do
  sleep 1; done` beside a logging `rails server &`, a deadlocked `java` whose timer threads
  keep waking it beside a printing `tail -f &`, a hung client whose own timer wakes it beside
  a `tail -f &` when aterm reads it twice in quick succession, a hung `curl` beside a logging
  JVM in the background whose line aterm reads a moment after its last look), and a loop such as `while sleep 2; do date;
  done` reads running beside an idle `python3 -m http.server &` or a Ctrl-Z'd `ninja`
  whose finished steps wait unreaped, as does `./gradlew test` beside a `tail -f &` when
  aterm reads it twice in quick succession, while `ssh host make` over a shared
  connection and `tmux
  attach`, whose output a server outside the tab writes, still read running; a log stream
  printing thousands of lines a second, in a cooked or raw terminal, no longer reads
  `quiet` now and then. A `ninja`, `cmake --build`, `meson
  compile` or `cargo nextest` run, whose program starts each step in a group of its own, is
  one row judged by its steps' work, where it read `quiet` and then `stuck` while it
  compiled and showed each step as a row. An async prompt's worker (pure, spaceship)
  belongs to no command's row, also in a zsh run in the tab's or one started before the
  shell's first prompt, and a `curl … &` that a
  `bash` run in the tab put in the background is a row of its own. A row no
  longer outlives its command because a process substitution (`vim <(tail -f log)`) or a
  server its script left behind lives on.

- **Reading a restored session's log after a restart no longer skips its first records or
  mixes them with the earlier run's.** A session that came back under the same id reused the
  earlier run's numbering, so a reader that had followed it read on past the new run's first
  records, and the journal could show the two runs as one. Each run now takes a numbering of
  its own that a reader can tell apart, so a reader that followed the earlier run is told
  its records started over (`gap why=reset`), and the journal keeps the two runs apart.
  This was fixed in 0.108.0, whose notes left it out.

- **A session carried across an update whose saved state disagreed with its log starts
  over.** A saved summary that held a turn or run open that its log did not could show a
  turn that never ends. aterm now refuses such a summary and starts the session's log
  afresh, with a gap that says so, rather than guess. This was fixed in 0.108.0, whose notes
  left it out.

- **Mail that arrived just before an update is still answered by your next keystroke after
  it.** The new aterm forgot that mail had arrived since you last typed, so your first key
  after the update was not noted as your reply. That now crosses the update (fixed in
  0.108.0), and mail the bus offers again after an update is noted once, not twice (fixed in
  0.122.0); those releases' notes left both out. Whether a key reached the program
  (`reached=`) is kept on this machine, in its log and journal, and never shared with your
  fabric.

- (developer tool) **aterm's Windows and Linux Arm cross checks build clean again.** Helpers
  only macOS or Unix code calls are built only there (0.107.0), and the checks' test builds
  compile again (0.108.0); those releases' notes left it out.

## [0.137.0] - 2026-10-25

### Added

- **`aterm ctl aos` works in the shipped app.** Aos, the substrate that checkpoints,
  records and replays the typing-momentum glow, now answers in release builds:
  `status`, `attach`, `pause`, `repair` (with the shipped code it replays the recorded
  trace, checks that the live code reproduces the paused state and keeps the glow's
  contract, then resumes), `resume`, `detach` and `trace`. `publish`, `bundle` and the
  demonstration code still need a debug build and say so by name (`ERR aos publish
  needs a debug build`). A repair runs on the main thread for now. Results are graded
  Tested, not proved.

- **An agent's active goal is shown where you can read it.** When Claude Code has a
  `/goal`, or codex-alab or Muse Code has a goal for its thread or session, the line
  above where you type shows it as `◎ <goal>`, between the CLI's name and the harness
  switch, cut to fit. The tab's hover and its menu have the whole goal on a `goal:`
  line. `aterm ctl status` says `goal=`, and `aterm ctl survey` prints the goal under
  the session. A goal that is met, cleared or paused stops showing. agy keeps its goal
  where aterm cannot read it, and Gemini CLI has none, so neither shows one.

- (developer tool) **The real-agent lab captures Autopilot on every harness**
  (`lab autopilot-captures --harness all|claude|agy|muse|gemini|codex-alab`). One private
  headless aterm per harness and look, launched in Aterm Day or Aterm Night so each program
  starts on the ground it is shot on, drives the forever lab's scenes on Claude Code, agy, Muse
  Code and Gemini CLI (Cruise naming two needs, Land held by open work, Land held by its
  repository, Land landed, Off) and `codex-alab-proof`'s on codex-alab (Cruise, Land, landed, Off,
  a need). Each scene is kept as an image at 1x or 2x, with the chip's hovered title where a chip
  is drawn (400 columns, so the whole title fits; a title drawn short is a finding) and the
  `chrome` and `status` text beside it. `manifest.tsv` names every harness and scene, or why a
  scene is skipped, and the verb fails on a missing row, a finding, a drawn chip with no hovered
  title, or no chip where a harness draws one. With `--baseline` it also takes a paired Gemini
  CLI typing take.

### Changed

- **A codex tab waiting on an approval, a question or a sign-in now needs you.** Where no
  claim speaks for the tab (a proven codex-alab claim speaks for it, so aterm raises nothing
  there), codex's own report that it is blocked raises a need where a Claude Code box
  would: the menu bar's Needs you row and count, the window border, the pill and the tab's
  chip, a banner, and `needs=` in `status` and `survey`, which other aterms on this Mac and
  other Macs in your fleet read. The rows, the pill and the banner's text say it is codex's
  own report (`approval (codex's own report)`, `question …`, `sign-in …`). `needs=` carries
  the bare word, and the survey row adds `needs_by=program`, so other aterms and Macs on
  this version and `aterm ctl survey` say it is codex's own report too. `agent=` in
  `status`, `ls`, `task` and `await task` still says `unknown`; the survey's `agent=` names
  codex's word for its state, as before. One box gives one banner: where codex posted its
  own notification for the box, aterm posts none, and where aterm's came first, codex's for
  the same box is dropped while the box is shown. Codex's other notifications, a finished
  turn's included, still come through. From this version on, an in-place update keeps the
  need.

- **Session recordings replay exactly and check themselves against the screen.** With
  `temporal_recording = true` (Settings > Terminal > Record sessions for replay), each
  piece of output now replays at the clock reading it was first shown at, so a
  synchronized frame that timed out, bells close together and command timestamps come
  back as they were. While it records, the session also keeps snapshots of the real
  screen (after every 256 KiB of output or once a second, only when output arrives)
  and checks each replay against them: `aterm ctl temporal status` reports `witnessed=`
  and `diverged=`, and after a mismatch the recording starts again from the live
  screen. Replays also check shell-integration marks with the session's own key, as the
  live tab does.

### Removed

- **The hidden `[sys] stats_deck_style` setting.** It chose an unfinished stats deck
  design that is no longer being built; the deck under the titlebar is unchanged. A
  config file that still sets the key loads as before, and Settings says the key does
  nothing and is safe to delete.

### Fixed

- **Repository setup resumes after a network change.** It now notices local
  interface changes after vault setup finishes or when using existing
  credentials, and resumes the unfinished step.

- **System State resumes waiting work.** Restore keeps queued changes through
  an interrupted retry. A later disk-access grant resumes waiting restores,
  and a recovered vault subscriber lets setup continue to repositories.

- **Repeated partial redraws preserve the rainbow cursor trail.** Unchanged
  text that returns before its original typing run expires regains its ribbon
  even after more than four fragments were temporarily cleared. Original
  expiry and replacement checks still apply.

- **Text commands follow the visible input.** Copy works in Settings' theme
  filters and text fields, and leaves a blurred field's selection alone.
  Save and Find wait while the palette or Overview is open; commands chosen
  inside the palette still close it and act on the document.

- **Restore refuses incomplete preference backups.** A missing original value
  now reports a damaged backup instead of deleting the setting. A valid saved
  absence still restores normally.

- **Returning to a field cannot revive unfinished input-method text.** Leaving
  a field or tab retires its old composition, including when you return before
  its final text arrives. Fresh input continues normally.

- **A Restore never takes back aterm's own permissions, even cut short.** A Restore
  previous settings or an `aterm doctor --apply` that a quit or a crash cut short could
  leave Full Disk Access, Developer Tools, the debugger and Local Network held until you
  set something up again. The next launch now finishes what it began and sets them up
  by themselves, with nothing else: Keyboard & Trackpad and Desktop & Dock stay at Leave
  as is, and no Dock reset, sign-out or Spotlight step runs.

- **A Restore pressed before you answered the first setup offer keeps aterm's
  permissions.** It left no run to carry them, so they waited for a later choice. aterm
  now sets them up at once, with nothing else, and a Stop or a Cancel still holds them.

- **A widget list waiting for Full Disk Access is put back in the launch you grant it.**
  When the grant came while another setup step held aterm's records, the put-back waited
  for the next launch. It now waits for that step, up to ten minutes, and goes on.

- **A choice after an older aterm's setup runs only what it turned on.** On a Mac whose
  setup an older aterm finished, a System State choice ran the whole setup again,
  resetting the Dock and making the Messages and FaceTime sign-outs a second time, and
  the page left aterm's permissions out of the plan. The plan now shows them, and a
  choice sets up only the groups it turned on, with aterm's permissions.

- **Edit's Copy and Select All work in editor and Markdown tabs.** They
  follow the document and window receiving the action. A palette or Overview
  keeps those menu actions away from the content behind it, and an editor
  prompt keeps its document selection private. Copy's enabled state follows
  the actual selection; the editor's Undo and Redo wait until its prompt ends.

- **A keyboard macro keeps other editor views on the selected text.** Each
  committed step updates their selection positions in order, so Copy after
  a multi-step macro still copies the text you selected in the other view.

- **Returning to System State keeps a queued Check again.** A routine refresh
  no longer replaces a pending check of a typed vault address. Each reads its
  own source; a newer setup choice still retires the old check's broader scope.

- **Autopilot puts off Claude Code's "Teach auto mode about your environment?" offer.**
  Claude Code 2.1.310 raises it at the end of a turn in auto mode and again at every
  turn's end until it is answered, and Land and Cruise sessions stalled behind it
  with "typed, not submitted". The harness now answers `Not now` at every `approve`
  level, in the inline and fullscreen renderers and in narrow panes, never while you
  are typing, and records the answer in its ledger; `Not now` puts the offer off for a
  week and changes nothing else. It then decides the turn's end again, so its
  continuation is typed once the offer is gone.

- **System State refreshes when you return to its window.** Changes made in
  System Settings appear without another Check again. A typed vault address
  stays unread until Join or Check again.

- **A queued Stop still holds automatic setup after its worker finishes.**
  It cannot lose its target just before the ALab watcher looks again.

- **System State no longer says "Checking this Mac…" for good when it cannot read Local
  Network.** macOS never tells an app whether it may use the local network, so on a Mac
  where aterm had not reached the LAN the page waited on that row and never settled. Local
  Network now reads On once aterm has reached the LAN and Off once macOS refused it (your
  answer, which aterm leaves as it is), remembered across launches, and otherwise shows —
  with a short note while the rest of the page settles.

- **Leave as is on the plan aterm chose by itself is kept.** On a Mac where aterm chose the
  plan, pressing a group to what it already was sent nothing, so when aterm later found the
  ALab vault and widened its plan it could set that group anyway, signing you out of
  Messages and FaceTime, say. Any group you press now makes the plan yours, and aterm never
  widens it.

- **Stop while aterm widens its own plan puts that plan back.** A Stop pressed as aterm
  widened its plan on finding the ALab vault held the run, but the page then showed four
  more groups at Set up and offered to change them. The plan in force before the widen
  comes back as it was, and nothing it would have changed is touched.

- **Paste stays with the field that requested it.** Keyboard Paste uses its
  own window. On Linux, a late clipboard reply cannot follow a closed search,
  cancelled Settings draft or replaced tab into another field or document.
  Pasting into a command palette edits its filter, including over a terminal,
  without sending that text to the program behind it.

- **The editor advertises the right Save and Find keys on Windows.** Save's
  toolbar and Modified footer name Ctrl-S; incremental search names Alt-S.

- (developer tool) **The trail gallery no longer waits for its own stalled
  redraw to close.** Captures use the held control connection and omit guarded
  text/cursor reads during the deliberately open frame. A rainbow return with
  no live ribbon is retained as inconclusive and exits unsuccessfully.

- **A Restore's put-back that waits for Full Disk Access is kept.** After Restore
  previous settings, a Widgets value macOS keeps in another app's container waits for
  Full Disk Access to be put back. A later choice of another group, Set up now or a Join
  forgot it, so the grant never put it back. It now waits through them and is put back
  once aterm has the grant, unless one of them set that group up again.

- **Setup carries on after a choice cut short.** A System State choice whose aterm quit
  or crashed after it saved its plan, before its run started, left setup neither finished
  nor able to go on. The next launch now carries it on, and setting it up there resets no
  Dock and makes no Messages or FaceTime sign-out a run already made.

- **Restore previous settings keeps the plan as you left it on an ALab Mac.** On a Mac
  whose plan aterm chose by itself, Set up now after a Restore let the ALab signal widen
  the plan to the whole profile, turning the groups the Restore put back on again. A
  Restore now makes the plan yours, and nothing widens it while what it put back stands.

- **A System State choice made while aterm widens its own plan is applied.** On an ALab
  Mac, a choice made in the moment aterm saved its widened plan was refused. It now waits
  for that save, up to ten seconds, and is then applied.

- **A Stop pressed as Restore previous settings saves holds.** After a Restore, aterm's
  own permission steps go on by themselves unless you stopped setup. A Stop whose save
  landed just after the Restore saved its run was lost, so they went on. It now holds.

- **The vault's sync process is mended only while the vault is set up.** At launch and
  every 30 minutes aterm installed again a sync process it owed, or one whose copy of
  aterm was gone, even with the Secrets vault at Leave as is or setup stopped. It now
  does so only while the Secrets vault is at Set up and no Stop holds the run, still
  without a word. A Stop or Leave as is choice made during its vault read also holds
  the repair; unreadable setup records defer it.

- **aterm's permissions come back after an older aterm's Restore.** A Mac whose setup an
  older aterm restored, left unfinished or never verified did not get Full Disk Access,
  Developer Tools, the debugger or Local Network set up, because the plan it saved
  predates them. The next launch now adds them, approved by default, and sets them up with
  nothing else: Keyboard & Trackpad and Desktop & Dock stay as Restore left them, and no
  sign-out or Spotlight step runs. Only a Cancel you pressed still holds them. A widget
  list a Restore left waiting for Full Disk Access is put back once aterm has it, even
  after you change another group.

- **A fresh ALab Mac sets itself up in its first launch.** On a fresh Mac, aterm's first
  look for the ALab vault comes before you answer macOS's Local Network question, so it
  heard nothing and set up only aterm's own permissions until the next launch. aterm now
  looks again once you answer, when System State comes to the front, on Check again and
  every so often, and sets up the rest of the Mac in the same launch once the vault
  answers. While that run goes, System State says why its groups changed.

- **A vault that did not answer is asked again by itself.** When the ALab vault did not
  answer (Local Network not allowed yet, the network, the vault down), the Secrets vault
  row waited for good though its note promised another try. aterm now asks again after 1,
  2 and then 4 minutes. A join an admin Mac approved is seen at once, not after a long
  wait.

- **Secrets keep syncing on a Mac that is already set up.** If the vault's sync stopped,
  or what starts it was removed, on a Mac whose setup had finished, nothing started it
  again, so your credentials stopped following the vault with no sign outside System
  State. aterm now looks once setup is finished and every 30 minutes, and starts it again
  unless you turned sync off.

- **System State says what failed in its own words.** A step that failed as a whole is
  named by the rows it covers (Rust in Spotlight, Dock), not by setup's own step names,
  and its note says what comes next, never a path or a process: `aterm doctor` and the log
  keep those. Set up now sits beside a failure only when running setup again can fix it;
  otherwise Show takes you to the row, whose note says what to do. Typing a vault address
  no longer turns the headline to "Checking this Mac…" while nothing checks it, and a
  change aterm made but could not log is one calm line and an entry in the exceptions
  digest, not a failure. VoiceOver reads the headline's button as Set up now.

- **Debugger access's Turn On… works the first time.** Pressed soon after aterm started (as
  it is right after Full Disk Access's Quit & Reopen), System State's Turn On… for Debugger
  access did nothing: aterm had not yet read whether it is a hardened build, and took the
  press for one on a build that does not need it. The window now reads that, and whether
  debugger access is on, as soon as the page offers Turn On… (and reads debugger access again
  every few seconds while that read fails, as it can while a new Mac is busy), so the first
  press asks macOS for your password.

- **A command stopped with Ctrl-Z stays `parked` while the next one runs.** `sys jobs` read
  a stopped job as parked only while the shell held the terminal, so a `vim` stopped with
  Ctrl-Z read `stop=held`, then `quiet` and in time `stuck`, once the next command ran,
  and so did `gdb` waiting at its prompt while the program it debugs sat at a breakpoint.
  Now a stop is `parked` when job control took the terminal from it, and a job whose own
  command runs in front is judged by that command; a build whose step stopped at the

- **A Ctrl-C or a Ctrl-\ leaves none of `install.sh`'s temporary files, even in the
  instant one is made.** 0.135.0 still left one now and then: on a Mac a check's file
  (macOS's `mktemp -u` makes the file and removes it again), and anywhere the download
