  between. A second admin publishing in the same instant could silently replace the
  first one's version (a revocation, say), and both were told it worked. A publish now
  holds a `<vault file>.lock` beside the vault from its check to its write, and removes
  it when done. On a folder shared over SMB or NFS (v3 and later) that lock holds across
  Macs. A publish while another holds it is refused, naming the lock and the Mac and
  process ID holding it, and changes nothing. A lock left by a publish that was killed
  refuses every publish until you remove it, as the message says. A folder another app
  syncs between Macs still holds no lock across them.

- **`aterm init` no longer fails its Spotlight row on a build folder that already has a
  `.noindex` beside it.** The row "Rust build caches and Trust toolchain sysroots stay
  in .noindex folders" listed a Rust `target` or `build` folder that Spotlight indexes
  as one to move even when a `target.noindex` (or `build.noindex`) already sat next to
  it. Apply leaves such a folder alone, so after every Apply the row failed, still
  reading that folder as indexed by Spotlight. For a Trust toolchain build in aterm's
  package store whose `<build>.noindex` was already there, Apply tried to move the build
  onto that folder. In both cases init now leaves both folders as they are and no longer
  counts them as a change.

## [0.119.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added

- **`aterm init --develop` sets a Mac up to work on aterm, and changes no setting.** Run
  in a checkout, it records that checkout in `~/.config/aterm/init.toml` (a `[develop]`
  table; the file's other lines stay byte for byte as they were), fast-forwards it when
  it is clean and behind GitHub, checks out `vendor/astream` where that loses nothing and
  turns on `submodule.recurse`, then runs the checkout's own `targo --unverified --locked
  verify provision` for the tools its tests use. Run elsewhere, it records the aterm
  checkouts in your home that your `[github]` setup keeps; a linked worktree is never
  recorded. Each later `aterm init` keeps them aligned, and `aterm init --no-develop`
  removes the record. A checkout with uncommitted changes or untracked files, commits of
  its own, a detached HEAD, another branch checked out or another origin is left exactly
  as it is, the row says which, and none of its code is built or run; init never resets,
  stashes, rebases or pushes, and runs no repository hook. A `vendor/astream` on a branch
  of yours, at an astream commit whose bump is not committed yet, or with changes of its
  own stays where it is. Offline, the develop rows stand aside and init exits 69; a
  profile it cannot read is one row and never stops the base layer. It leaves the Dock,
  keyboard, trackpad and accounts alone, and refuses to run as root. `--only` now also
  takes `workstation` and the develop items (`develop`, `checkout`, `tooling`, or an id
  such as `develop.checkout@~/aterm`, which names that checkout alone).

### Changed

- **Publishing a release no longer needs the GitHub CLI.** `ship release` and
  `atpkg-publish` create releases, upload and download assets and read release lists
  through GitHub's REST API, using the Mac's own `/usr/bin/curl`. The token is handed to
  curl on its standard input, so it never shows in a process listing or the environment.
  An asset download follows GitHub's redirect only to its asset CDN and refuses any other
  redirect. A release list is read to its last page, and a list that ends early is
  refused. The release signs in with the release org's token file alone: `gh auth login`
  is no longer needed, and `ship provision` no longer checks it. The producer's Linux
  ceremony uploads with the new `atpkg-publish upload` verb instead of `gh release
  upload`. Replacing an asset uploads the new file first, so a failed upload leaves the
  old one served. git gets the producer's token from its own environment, never a file,
  and works under `credential.useHttpPath`. A Ctrl-C or `kill` of `ship release` while
  it reads GitHub ends that read and starts no other.

- **`aterm init` brings your GitHub checkouts up to date.** Besides cloning what is
  missing, it now fast-forwards each clean checkout in your home that is behind GitHub,
  and leaves any other as it is, saying why: one whose GitHub copy cannot be read never
  keeps a missing repository from being cloned. The fetch reaches GitHub alone and no
  repository hook runs. A checkout recorded for `--develop` is aligned by the develop
  items instead. The workstation settings are applied only by a
  bare `aterm init` or `--only workstation`.

### Removed

- `aterm harness accounts sync` no longer runs rclone: an `rclone:<remote>:<path>` source
  is refused by name, here and in `[fleet] accounts_source`. Name the sheet's CSV export
  URL, a `fleet-accounts.toml` another Mac on the LAN serves, or a CSV file you exported.

### Fixed

- **A test whose program macOS is still checking ends COULD NOT RUN instead of failing.**
  macOS's program check can hold a program before its first instruction for minutes or
  hours on a busy Mac. When one of aterm's tests waits its minute for a program it started
  and macOS still holds that program, the test now ends COULD NOT RUN, naming the program's
  pid and saying nothing was verified, where it failed as a hang. The warm-up run before a
  test's timed part says so in one line when it is ended while held, and a test skipped
  because macOS's trust service did not answer also counts how many of your programs wait
  at the check, without claiming either caused the other.
- **`brew` inside aterm no longer brings up macOS's "install the command line developer
  tools" dialog on a Mac without them.** Checking a poured bottle's linked libraries
  (and `brew linkage`) ran Apple's `otool`, moving a bottle's library names to your
  prefix ran `install_name_tool`, and a formula that needs a minimum Xcode ran
  `xcodebuild -version`; on a Mac without the developer tools all three are stand-ins
  that put up that dialog. aterm now reads the libraries from the files itself, runs the
  developer tools' own `install_name_tool` (and hands a bottle that needs it to Homebrew
  when there are none), and reads the Xcode version from the selected Xcode's own version
  file.

## [0.118.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added

- **aterm tells you when macOS's program check is stuck, and stops adding to it.** macOS's
  program check (`syspolicyd`) can hold a program before it starts. It and the privacy check
  (`tccd`) can end up each waiting on the other for good. Then most new programs cannot
  start on the Mac (macOS's own still do), a privacy check can freeze the screen and close
  every window, and only a restart of the Mac ends it; logging out does not. Every aterm, a
  headless one too, now reads the check's thread pool once a minute. After five minutes at
  macOS's thread limit it shows one alert, "macOS's program check is stuck", asking you to
  restart the Mac once your work is saved, and `aterm ctl @self status` says
  `syspolicyd=stuck`. Until it clears, the Autopilot types no continuation, takes no upgrade
  step, ends or restarts no agent and claims no Claude Code limit reset, so the account
  keeps that attempt for later. `aterm doctor` has a `syspolicyd:` row. While the pool is
  full, doctor no longer lists every program's command line or waits on a `targo` macOS
  holds, reads that would hang it; it says why instead. Builds and tests in a tab kept
  across an aterm update make macOS check aterm's earlier copy at every program they start,
  so start them from a new tab.

### Changed

- **Worker reports no longer put "needs you" alerts in the tab bar.** Reports remain
  available in the menu bar, tab hover and Overview, including reports carried over
  from older versions. Approvals, questions and other direct requests still show
  their pills, even when a report is waiting in the same tab.

### Fixed

- **aterm Caffeine says when Login Items keeps it from starting.** Turning aterm off
  under Background App Activity in System Settings ▸ General ▸ Login Items & Extensions
  stops the mug and keeps every login from starting it, yet Enable at Startup stayed
  checked and `aterm caffeine status` said `startup=on`. Its row now reads "Enable at
  Startup — Allow in Login Items…", unchecked, and opens Login Items, where the switch
  is; `status` and `startup` say `startup=blocked`, and `startup on` fails until the
  switch is on. A job launchd itself has disabled (`launchctl disable`) reads
  `startup=disabled` and unchecked, turning Enable at Startup on lifts that, and
  `aterm caffeine on` no longer fails for it with a bare "Input/output error": the error
  names the `launchctl enable` that lifts it.

- **`sudo aterm pkg self-uninstall` stops aterm Caffeine and removes its aterm.app.**
  Under sudo the uninstall asked `aterm caffeine` to stop the mug as root, which refuses
  someone else's home, so once Caffeine had run on the account the bundle was kept every
  time, the run its own SKIPPED line asked for included. It now asks as the home's owner,
  then removes Caffeine's files and the bundle.

- **The Dock pins aterm from `~/Applications`, and one Mac setting aterm cannot apply no
  longer stops the others.** `tools/install.sh` puts aterm in `~/Applications` when
  `/Applications` is not writable (a standard account). The Dock row looked for aterm only
  in `/Applications` and failed, and that error failed all of System State's Mac settings,
  so Caps Lock, scrolling, widgets and the other rows were never applied at first launch.
  Now the Dock pins the aterm in your `~/Applications` when `/Applications` has none, and
  the copy you run when both have one. A row that still cannot be applied (no aterm in
  either folder, or a value aterm cannot read to save before changing it) is left as it
  was, saying why, and the others apply.

- **System State is in the aterm menu, and setup's messages point there.** aterm ▸
  System State… (also in the command palette) opens the tab where Mac setup and the
  secrets vault are reviewed and applied; before, once its first-run offer closed, only
  `aterm ctl open app system-state` opened it again. *Mac setup needs attention* no
  longer sends you to `aterm doctor --check`, which never reads the secrets vault, and a
  vault join that failed or never finished, or a subscriber that could not be installed,
  now says to press Apply there with the vault row on and the Mac settings rows off
  (Apply runs every row switched on again, the Dock and account sign-outs too), with the
  terminal command in its details. Its System State button opens the tab set that way,
  the other rows and the vault field as they are (on a tab setup has not read yet, once
  it reads this Mac). A review you edited, a first-run offer or one a setup run holds is
  only brought to the front, with the offer's countdown stopped, and the button then
  says to check the rows before Apply; pressing it never takes the message down. Those
  messages end as soon as that Apply syncs the vault, instead of at the next launch, and
  the tab's vault field starts from the vault this Mac is in, so an Apply left as it is
  never moves the Mac to the vault first-run setup saved, even from a tab opened before
  you joined another; a vault typed there stays while setup still tries to join it.
  Setup's own retries no longer move it either, for a setup run started by this version
  or later: a vault you join from a terminal after setup began stays when the vault
  setup chose answers later (back at the office), and the vault row says how to move the
  Mac from System State.

## [0.117.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added

- **aterm tells you when macOS's program check is stuck, and stops adding to it.** macOS
  checks each new program before its first run (`syspolicyd`). It and the privacy check
  (`tccd`) can end up each waiting on the other for good. Then no new program starts on the
  Mac, a privacy check can freeze the screen and close every window, and only a restart of
  the Mac ends it; logging out does not. Every aterm, a headless one too, now reads the
  check's thread pool once a minute. After five minutes at macOS's thread limit it shows one
  alert, "macOS's program check is stuck", asking you to restart the Mac once your work is
  saved, and `aterm ctl @self status` says `syspolicyd=stuck`. Until it clears, the
  Autopilot types no continuation, takes no upgrade step, ends or restarts no agent and
  claims no Claude Code limit reset, so the account keeps that attempt for later. `aterm
  doctor` has a `syspolicyd:` row. While the pool is full, doctor no longer lists every
  program's command line or waits on a `targo` macOS holds, reads that would hang it; it
  says why instead. Builds and tests in a tab kept across an aterm update make macOS check
  aterm's earlier copy at every program they start, so start them from a new tab.

### Changed

- **With `[harness] usage_tap` on, a Claude Code usage limit is waited out to the second.**
  The usage tap reads Claude Code's own usage figures. At a usage limit the harness now
  continues the session (the same `usage-resume@v1`, the same 150 seconds of grace and the
  session's share of a minute) from the reset that session's own figures name, wherever its
  window reads 100% with the reset ahead. Before, it went by the notice's minute, or by the
  30-minute back-off where a narrow pane cut the notice before its reset. A five-hour limit
  goes by the five-hour window and a weekly one by the week; a limit that names no window
  goes by whichever window is full, the later reset if both are. A spend limit keeps its own
  rule. Only a reading Claude Code wrote after the harness first saw the limit counts, and
  a limit met again (after a turn, or in answer to the harness's own continuation) is read
  afresh. A limit that only the session's transcript shows is set against the reset its row
  names. Where the notice and the figures are more than six minutes apart, the later one is
  waited for, and the session's approval ledger gets a `tap-reset@v1` row. That row is a
  record, and nothing asks you anything. With no reset to go by, the figures showing a full
  window rolled over end the wait. A reading that comes while the harness waits decides the
  wait again at once, also after you press Esc on Claude Code's own countdown, and a harness
  that takes the session over (after an update or a restart) waits to the same reset. With
  the switch off no wait moves, save one book: a limit only the session's transcript shows
  was already waited to the reset its row names, and now the session's share of the minute
  and the limit's ledger row go by that reset too, not by where its words would fall. The
  switch ships off, and its help now says it times this wait.

### Fixed

- **System State is in the aterm menu, and setup's messages point there.** aterm ▸ System
  State… (also in the command palette) opens the tab where Mac setup and the secrets vault
  are reviewed and applied; before, once its first-run offer closed, only `aterm ctl open
  app system-state` opened it again. *Mac setup needs attention* no longer sends you to
  `aterm doctor --check`, which never reads the secrets vault, and a vault join that
  failed or never finished, or a subscriber that could not be installed, now says to
  press Apply there with the vault row on and the Mac settings rows off (Apply runs every
  row switched on again, the Dock and account sign-outs too), leaving the other rows as
  they are, with the terminal command still in the message's details. Those messages end
  as soon as that Apply syncs the vault, instead of at the next launch, and the tab's
  vault field starts from the vault this Mac is in, so an Apply left as it is never moves
  the Mac to the vault first-run setup saved, even from a tab opened before you joined
  another; a vault typed there stays while setup still tries to join it. Setup's own
  retries no longer move it either, for a setup run started by this version or later: a
  vault you join from a terminal after setup began stays when the vault setup chose
  answers later (back at the office), and the vault row says how to move the Mac from
  System State.

- **Mac setup no longer makes macOS warn that aterm tried to read another app's
  data.** Clearing Notification Center's widgets read its preferences, which
  macOS keeps in Notification Center's own app container. On a new Mac, setup
  did that before it asked for Full Disk Access, so macOS showed a notice (a
  dialog on macOS 26) that aterm was prevented from accessing data from other
  apps, and setup got back an empty widget list. Now, without Full Disk Access,
  the Widgets setting hides desktop and Stage Manager widgets, says Notification
  Center's widgets wait for Full Disk Access, and leaves Notification Center
  alone. Setup clears Notification Center's widgets by itself once aterm has
  Full Disk Access, without asking again: on setup's next try while setup is
  still running, or at aterm's next launch once it has finished. It relaunches
  only Notification Center for it, never the Dock, and leaves the desktop
  widgets as you set them since. A clear macOS does not keep is tried once more
  when ten minutes have passed (on setup's next try, or at aterm's next launch),
  then left alone until the next aterm update or until you press Apply in System
  State; if the grant never comes, nothing reruns. The grant is the app's that
  runs the pass: `aterm doctor --apply` or `aterm init` in an aterm tab needs
  aterm's, and run from another terminal it needs that terminal's. Restore
  preferences without Full Disk Access leaves Notification Center's widget list
  as it is and keeps its original in the backup; its row says to run Restore
  again from an app that has Full Disk Access (aterm's System State, or an aterm
  tab, once aterm has it; another terminal once that terminal has it; over SSH,
  once Remote Login's "Allow full disk access for remote users" is on), since
  nothing reruns a Restore by itself. A raw user or per-host `[[defaults]]` row
  that names Notification Center's domain, or any row that spells a path into an
  app's container or group container, waits for the grant the same way (a system
  row is judged by the file it names, so one naming Notification Center's domain
  is its file under /Library/Preferences and needs no grant; a row naming
  another sandboxed app's domain by its id alone is not recognised), and one
  whose domain has a `..` is refused. A widget list an earlier aterm saved as
  missing while macOS hid it has no known original: Restore leaves it as it is,
  with or without the grant, never deletes it, and says so. A Mac an older aterm
  left owing Notification Center its relaunch gets it once, from the first pass
  with the grant.

## [0.116.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added

- **One command puts the tools aterm's tests run on a Mac: `targo --unverified verify
  provision`.** From a checkout it fetches or builds each tool the tree pins, by version
  and sha256, into `~/Library/Caches/aterm/tooling.noindex`: fish 4.9.3, built on your Mac
  from upstream's source with nothing from Homebrew; Microsoft's PowerShell 7.6.7, every
  program in it checked against Microsoft's signature; and binaryen's `wasm-opt`. It
  places the browser lane's Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in the lane's own cache, and
  installs rustup from its pinned installer where none is. `--linux` adds lima for the
  Linux lane, `--record` builds wasm-bindgen for re-recording the wasm goldens, and
  `--check` only says what is missing. A download that does not match its pin is refused
  and leaves nothing behind, and a copy found in place without the pin's record is
  replaced. The tests use these copies ahead of anything on your PATH, and a test that
  cannot run names this command.

### Changed

- **`ship provision` audits the whole release host.** Besides the toolchain, signing and
  credentials it checks the base layer (`aterm init --check --only base`), the tools
  `verify provision` lays, macOS's LibreSSL, the publication engine, the site checkout and
  node with firebase-tools, and it exits non-zero naming what is missing. It no longer
  installs wasm-bindgen, which no release needs.

- `verify fetch-browser` is gone: `verify provision` fetches the browsers.

- The disk watch's build-cache sweep also removes a pinned tool nothing has run for a
  month; `verify provision` lays it again when a checkout next needs it.

### Fixed

- **A permission box Claude Code would deny on a timer is answered before the timer runs out, even
  if you typed in the session before it came up.** Some boxes carry a countdown (`⚠ Claude Code
  will automatically deny this request in 1:44, to avoid blocking progress on an unattended
  session`; the rm safety check in bypass mode shows one, two minutes from when the box appears).
  After you type in a session the harness keeps its hands off it for `human_grace_s` from your last
  keystroke, so a grace that ran past the countdown kept it waiting while Claude Code denied a box
  you never touched: the command failed and the work stalled, an outcome nobody chose. That is any
  keystroke within the grace before the box when `human_grace_s` is longer than the countdown (an
  hour at its least-power setting); at the default two minutes, only one in the last moments
  before the box. Now, when nobody has touched the session since the box came
  up, that wait ends 15 seconds before the countdown does, and the box gets the answer it would
  get with nobody at the keyboard, approved or declined as `[harness] approve` says (`HELD … (the
  box's answer; the vendor denies it at …)`, then `HOLD-ENDED …`); a key, click or scroll of yours
  after the harness's last look before the box skips every key of that answer still to go. A box
  you HAVE touched is yours, and the harness waits for you as before, however near the countdown.
  A touch is only what the aterm server records: a keystroke, click or scroll of yours in the
  session since the harness's last look before the box came up (`HELD … a person's gesture was
  counted on the session since it appeared: held as ever …`; while the agent works that look can
  be up to 20 seconds before the box, so at the default grace a keystroke in those last moments
  usually counts as a touch, and the box waits for you as before), or another driver's lease or named
  turn on the session while the box is up (`HELD … another driver's hand was on the session while
  it was up: held as ever …`; a key another driver sends with neither is not recorded, and does
  not count). The box is followed from the first look that shows it to the first look that shows
  none, and what Claude Code redraws in between changes nothing: the box re-wrapped by a resize,
  its footer cut to the pane, its `1 of 2` label when another request stacks behind it, the next
  request drawn in its place. If the wait outlasts the countdown, Claude Code denies the box, as
  before. So it is whenever whether you touched it cannot be told: a box the harness first saw
  already up, a host that does not count your keystrokes, aterm updating itself in place while the
  box is up. The countdown counts only where Claude Code draws it, under the box's content and led
  by its `⚠` (in a pane of any width, however many rows it wraps onto), and only once two reads a
  second apart show it ticking: the same words in a command, its description or a question the
  agent wrote never end your wait, and the journal says `HELD … a countdown on it is read again to
  see it tick` for the second it takes, and again each second while it stands still. A key near the
  deny that Claude Code does not take is seen not taken within seconds: under `approve = "all"` it
  is pressed again (a question's answer too, once the screen holds still half a second between its
  redraws), and under `safe` the box is handed to you with time left to answer it. A box `[harness]`
  hands to you is still yours, and Claude Code still denies it when its countdown runs out. A
  countdown drawn another way (`in about 2 minutes`, the screen-reader form, which does not tick)
  leaves the wait as it was. A question dialog's review tab that shows the countdown is now read,
  and answered the same way, instead of being handed over. A box taller than the pane, its head
  read from the history above the screen, is no longer handed to you because its countdown ticked
  while the history was read.

- **A new secrets vault lets Macs in from the start.** Only an admin Mac's subscriber
  lets a joining Mac in by the join password, or into an open vault, and nothing an
  admin ran to set a vault up installed it. For a vault served over the network,
  `aterm secrets create` now installs it as `join` does, and `aterm secrets password
  open`, `set` and `new` install it where it is not running (`--no-agent` skips it in
  both); `aterm secrets status` on an admin says whether it runs, naming `aterm secrets
  agent on` when it does not. A create whose server goes away right after it publishes
  still installs it, and the subscriber syncs the new vault. `password open`, `set` and
  `new` on a vault at a path no longer promise Macs are let in: such a vault has no join
  queue, and they say a Mac joins when an admin approves its key. A vault server
  whose store holds no vault yet says so when it starts: a Mac in the vault puts its
  copy there.

- **The AI footer's own words read on a light theme.** The composer's bottom rule drew
  its facts in the program's grey lifted toward the tab's ink, and on a light theme that
  grey sits near the paper: under Claude Code's `#999999` rule on Default Light the
  values read 4.3:1 and a clicked-off fact's `off` 2.7:1. The values now hold 4.5:1;
  a fact clicked off stays greyed out and says `off`, at 3:1 or more and always quieter
  than the values; and so do the top-effort key's `off` on the top rule, the Autopilot
  chip's `○ off` and other hands-off words, and agy's and Muse Code's small headings,
  quotes, unchecked boxes and nested bullets. Where these already read they are
  unchanged.

- **A secrets vault recovers by itself from a server that goes away.** A Mac whose join was
  cut off (the vault server went away after the vault was checked, or while you typed the
  join password) now asks again on its subscriber's next pass instead of an hour later, so
  an open vault lets it in within a minute; a join cut off in a terminal installs the
  subscriber that asks. So does a Mac still waiting whose request a server lost with its
  store. A Mac joined again under another name and stopped before it asked now asks under
  that name without the old name's join-password proof, which an admin Mac refused. A file
  deleted from `~/.secrets` while the server could not be reached is written again as soon
  as it answers, instead of at the vault's next version. A server that lost the ALab
  vault, or a vault it pins with `--pin` (moved to another Mac, or its store gone), gets it
  back within a minute of answering again from the subscriber of any Mac in the vault,
  instead of waiting for an admin command: a subscriber that cannot reach the server asks
  again at least once a minute, where it waited up to five minutes. A server that took
  back an older copy of a vault (from a Mac that slept through the versions since) gets
  the newer copy back from the first Mac in the vault that holds it and hears from the
  server while it still serves the older one. Both hold whatever the vault's join
  settings. That replaces what an admin published on the older copy meanwhile; once such
  versions reach the one those Macs hold, they are taken as the newest instead.

- **System State is in the aterm menu, and setup's messages point there.** aterm ▸ System
  State… (also in the command palette) opens the tab where Mac setup and the secrets vault
  are reviewed and applied; before, once its first-run offer closed, only `aterm ctl open
  app system-state` opened it again. *Mac setup needs attention* no longer sends you to
  `aterm doctor --check`, which never reads the secrets vault, and a vault join that
  failed or never finished, or a subscriber that could not be installed, now says to
  press Apply there with the vault row on and the Mac settings rows off (Apply runs every
  row switched on again, the Dock and account sign-outs too), leaving the other rows as
  they are, with the terminal command still in the message's details. Those messages end
  as soon as that Apply syncs the vault, instead of at the next launch, and the tab's
  vault field starts from the vault this Mac is in, so an Apply left as it is never moves
  the Mac to the vault first-run setup saved; a vault typed there stays while setup still
  tries to join it.

- **Mac setup no longer asks an unreachable secrets vault every minute, and its
  vault step is now journaled.** Away from the vault's network, the background
  setup asked the vault every minute for as long as aterm stayed open, logging
  "No route to host" each time, in turn with "waiting for the vault to approve
  this Mac". Now a try that does not finish waits a minute before the next, then
  two minutes, then four at most, and System State shows the last try's message
  meanwhile, so the log keeps one line. Setup tries again at once when your Mac
  changes network, when an aterm version that has not tried yet runs, when your
  Mac's vault state changes (an admin approving it, which your secrets
  subscriber picks up), or when you Apply in System State: an approval reaches
  System State about a minute after the subscriber gets it. The subscriber
  itself now asks the vault again as soon as your Mac changes network, instead
  of up to five minutes later. Two aterm versions running side by side, as after
  an update, share one pause instead of each restarting it. A vault that does
  not answer, or that is not there (a vault file on a disk that is not plugged
  in, an address with no vault behind it, a Wi-Fi login page), is now left alone
  entirely: no key, no join request, no subscriber. A join that fails for a
  reason only you can fix, such as a vault whose signing key nothing pins, is
  tried twice and then waits for one of those changes, and System State says
  so, instead of trying and logging again every four minutes. The vault step
  now runs the same way `aterm init` joins a vault. Joining, installing and
  starting the secrets subscriber, and writing the vault's files are each
  written to aterm's change journal (`converge/journal.ndjson` in aterm's state
  folder) before they happen, with how to undo them, and nothing changes when
  the journal cannot be written. A join that replaces the vault your Mac was in
  first copies that vault's settings to
  `~/.config/aterm/secrets/before-join-<time>`, and the journal says how to put
  your Mac back in it. A join password you give System State is used up by the
  join that sends it, and kept for the next try when that join fails. Setup
  opened from aterm's disk image still waits for you to open aterm from
  Applications instead of failing, and now tries again as soon as you do. `aterm
  init` off the vault's network now stops before it makes anything and says it
  is offline (exit 69), where it used to fail after making this Mac's key.

## [0.115.0] - 2026-10-22

### Fixed

- **A new secrets vault lets Macs in from the start.** Only an admin Mac's subscriber
  lets a joining Mac in by the join password, or into an open vault, and nothing an
  admin ran to set a vault up installed it. For a vault served over the network,
  `aterm secrets create` now installs it as `join` does, and `aterm secrets password
  open`, `set` and `new` install it where it is not running (`--no-agent` skips it in
  both); `aterm secrets status` on an admin says whether it runs, naming `aterm secrets
  agent on` when it does not. A vault server
  whose store holds no vault yet says so when it starts: an admin Mac puts its copy
  there.

- **A tab in a theme of its own keeps its AI footer readable.** On a tab given its own
  theme (`theme session set`, Choose Tab Theme, `spawn theme=`) the composer's bottom
  rule laid its fact marks (`◆ ⌂ ⎇ ◐ Σ` and the rest) and the harness's `∞` chip in
  the window theme's accent, chosen for another background: an aterm in Dracula drew
  `∞` at 1:1 on a Default Light tab. The marks now hold 3:1 and the chip 4.5:1 on the
  tab's own background in its own hue, and so do agy's and Muse Code's accented
  headings, links, inline code, bullets and numbers. Where the accent already read, it is
  unchanged.

- **A secrets vault recovers by itself from a server that goes away.** A Mac whose join was
  cut off (the vault server went away after the vault was checked, or while you typed the
  join password) now asks again on its subscriber's next pass instead of an hour later, so
  an open vault lets it in within a minute; a join cut off in a terminal installs the
  subscriber that asks. So does a Mac still waiting whose request a server lost with its
  store. A file deleted from `~/.secrets` while the
  server could not be reached is written again as soon as it answers, instead of at the
  vault's next version. A server that lost the ALab vault (moved to another Mac, or its
  store gone) gets it back within a minute from an admin Mac's subscriber, instead of
  waiting for an admin command; so does any vault the server pins with `--pin`, when it is
  open or has a join password.

- **System State is in the aterm menu, and setup's messages point there.** aterm ▸ System
  State… (also in the command palette) opens the tab where Mac setup and the secrets vault
  are reviewed and applied; before, once its first-run offer closed, only `aterm ctl open
  app system-state` opened it again. *Mac setup needs attention* no longer sends you to
  `aterm doctor --check`, which never reads the secrets vault, and a vault join that
  failed or never finished, or a subscriber that could not be installed, now says to
  sync the secrets vault there, with the terminal command still in the message's details.

- **The fabric's mint secret is read by the same strict rule as aterm's other private
  files.** Every command that reads it (`aterm fabric on` and `mint-for`, `aterm link
  broker` and `aterm link mint`) now refuses a secret that is not a plain file of yours
  with one name, one a Mac access list lets other users read (naming the `chmod -N` that
  clears it), a symlink, or one in a folder other users can open (naming the `chmod 700`
  that closes it); before, only its mode was checked. A pipe (FIFO) put where a secret
  or a private file belongs is refused at once instead of leaving the command waiting
  for something to write to it. A secret `aterm fabric on` made already passes. The
  check is astream's own owner-only rule, so aterm no longer keeps a second copy of it.

- **aterm's first-launch debugger-access question no longer touches your home folder
  while its windows wait.** Before it asks, aterm records the Mac beside `aterm.toml`;
  that record, and the one it writes when the question is already answered, are now
  written on a thread of their own, so a home folder on a network volume that stopped
  answering can no longer freeze aterm's windows at that moment. The record's folder is
  now flushed with it, so a power cut just after it was written cannot bring the question
  back. And when another aterm on the same config folder is changing debugger access,
  aterm now reads that change at once and settles the question, instead of looking again
  every few seconds until it gave up.

- **The debugger-access question and help now say what "once per Mac" means.** The
  record of the Macs aterm asked on lives in your account's config folder, so a second
  account on the same Mac is asked once too. The alert now opens "aterm asks you this
  once on this Mac.", and `aterm help permissions` and `aterm ctl help privacy` say once
  per Mac and account, and that in a launch that runs first-launch setup the question
  waits until that setup is applied with its macOS permissions choice checked. A Mac
  where debugger access was turned off in a way aterm did not see (`DevToolsSecurity
  -disable` in a terminal, or from aterm in another account) is asked once: macOS's
  `DevToolsSecurity -status` cannot tell that from never turned on. `aterm help
  permissions` also says that lldb attaches over ssh, with no dialog, to a program you
  signed with the `get-task-allow` entitlement (measured on macOS 26.6 and 27.0).

- **The debugger-access question is no longer lost once aterm has recorded the Mac.** In
  the moment between recording the Mac and raising the alert: an answer you gave the same
  alert in Settings now ends the question instead of asking it a second time; a No you
  had just given another of aterm's Security alerts now makes the question wait until
  aterm may ask again, instead of skipping it for good, and if you turned debugger access
  on yourself while it waited, it is not asked at all; first-launch setup holding the
  permission pages back no longer keeps it from ever coming; and when macOS's check of
  whether debugger access is on fails or times out just then, aterm checks again, for five
  minutes and at least three tries, instead of skipping the question for good.

- **Two coding agents that share one context file no longer take turns rewriting it.**
  A dotfiles setup can link one agent's global context file to another's, for example
  `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. aterm then wrote each agent's primer
  block into that one file, one after the other, every time it primed the agents. The
  file was rewritten twice each time, `aterm agents` always showed one of the two as
  `stale`, and the file was left holding Codex's block. That block adds a paragraph
  saying Codex's sandbox refuses aterm's control socket, so Claude Code, reading the
  same file, could conclude that every `aterm ctl` command fails for it too. Now a file
  two agents share gets one block, without that paragraph, and aterm writes it at most
  once each time. This holds from the first time aterm primes the agents, even when the
  link was made before the file it points to. `aterm agents`, `aterm agents install` and
  `aterm agents remove` give both agents the same state and mark their rows
  `(shared with …)`.

- **Mac setup's Dock pins now stick on the first try.** Setup changed the
  desktop and relaunched the Dock and Finder, then changed the Dock's pins a
  second later and relaunched the Dock again. The Dock it killed then was
  still starting: it wrote back the pins it had read at its start, so the Dock
  setting read "applied, but it still reads com.apple.dock persistent-apps,
  com.apple.dock persistent-others, com.apple.dock recent-apps". On one Mac
  that happened on every unattended pass for over three hours, until one pass
  won the race. Now one pass makes every widget, desktop and Dock change
  first, relaunches the Dock, Finder and Notification Center once each, and
  checks each setting only after the processes that read it are back up (the
  Dock once it has loaded the pins it was given) and have stopped rewriting
  what they read; a Dock that changes it again by then is reported, not
  hidden. A process that does not come back fails only the settings it reads:
  the others keep their change instead of being put back. That relaunch is
  written to aterm's change journal before it happens, after the settings'
  own lines, and a pass that ends between its changes and the relaunch
  relaunches each of them once on the next run. `aterm init` works the same
  way.

- **aterm Caffeine keeps the Mac awake through an update.** When aterm updated while the
  mug was on, the mug let go as it restarted onto the new build, which can take minutes
  while macOS checks the new copy, so an idle Mac's display, and on battery the Mac
  itself, could go to sleep in between. The mug now hands the hold to a small bridge
  (`aterm caffeine bridge`) until the new mug has taken it. A copy kept while macOS checks
  it is now also removed by the next start of a build-tree aterm, as the manual said.

- **Quitting aterm Caffeine from Activity Monitor turns it off.** Activity Monitor's Quit
  (and `kill`) ended the mug only for launchd to start it again at once, still keeping the
  Mac awake. It now quits as Quit Caffeine does. A logout still ends it with what was on
  kept for its next start.
- **aterm Caffeine's timed spans end on time with its menu open.** An update that landed
  while the mug's menu was open stopped its minute ticks until someone closed the menu, so
  a 1, 8 or 24 hour span, or an `aterm caffeine off`, kept the Mac awake past its end in
  the meantime. The mug now looks for an update only while its menu is closed.
- **`sudo aterm pkg self-uninstall` removes an aterm.app Caffeine ran from.** Once Caffeine
  had run, every uninstall asked the going bundle's `aterm caffeine` to stop it again, which
  fails under sudo, so a root-owned aterm.app was kept every time, the run its own SKIPPED
  line asked for included. A finished sweep's lock alone no longer asks.

## [0.114.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added

- **A secrets vault server answers the default vault URL with no flags.** On a Mac,
  `aterm secrets server on` (and `serve`) now registers `alab-secrets.local` over mDNS
  whenever it listens on every address at port 7484, the address every new Mac's setup
  joins, so `server on` alone makes that default work. `--advertise <name>` registers
  another name and `--no-advertise` none; a server on loopback or another port registers
  nothing. A Mac that already serves a different vault with no `--advertise` would now
  claim the default name: reinstall it with `--advertise <name>` or `--no-advertise`.

### Fixed

- **No other machine on the network can replace or hide a Mac's request to join a
  secrets vault.** The vault server refuses a request whose code is not its key's, and
  a request for the same key from another address now waits beside the Mac's own request
  instead of replacing it; a Mac still waiting stays queued when its address changes.
  `aterm secrets approve` refuses a key queued under two names
  (anyone can queue a key under a name of their choosing) and says to approve it with
  `aterm secrets approve <age1…> --name <host>`. A queue that filled up no longer
  locks new Macs out for 7 days: requests an admin already answered give way. A clock
  stepped back no longer blocks or drops requests. While a key is queued twice, an
  admin Mac on 0.113.0 or older stops approving joins, so update admin Macs with the
  server.

- **Saving `aterm secrets edit` over another admin's newer version keeps what that
  version did.** A Mac it let go stays out, an admin it added or removed stays that way,
  and its renewed join password is kept. A draft reopened unchanged publishes only if
  you say yes. An editor that fails or is missing leaves no plaintext copy of the vault
  behind. A vault too large to publish is refused before it is signed, saying how much
  fits, and a 63rd host section is refused when written instead of breaking every
  later publish.

- **A Mac let into a vault under another name can be found by its code.** `revoke`,
  `set --for`, `unset --for` and `admins` accept a Mac's join code, never read as another
  Mac's name (an older approver could let a Mac in under one), and `status` on that Mac
  shows its code beside the name it asked for. `revoke` and `admins remove` list
  every secret the Mac could read (an admin, every entry), so you know what to rotate.
  `approve <age1…> --name` with an invalid name is refused instead of naming the Mac
  `machine`. `set` keeps the final newline of a binary value read from stdin. `revoke`
  no longer refuses a Mac whose host section `unset` emptied. Joining another vault no
  longer sends the old vault's join-password proof to the new one.

- **Vault files are never left half-removed.** A removal that crashed or was refused no
  longer leaves a zeroed file that the next sync disowns. Temporary copies a cut-short
  sync left beside your files are cleaned up. A `state.toml` over 4 MiB is read again
  instead of failing every sync. A vault file changed during a sync is applied on the
  next one. aterm's own key folder is checked by what it is, not by how its path is
  spelled, and a symlinked parent no longer leads its folders elsewhere.

- **The secrets server stops advertising when it stops.** A server ended by a signal now
  takes its `dns-sd` registration and `caffeinate` with it. A relative `--store` names a
  folder under your home directory, however the server is run. Background jobs refuse
  to run an aterm from a disk image, App Translocation or a temporary folder, naming
  `--program`; first-run setup instead waits for aterm to be moved to Applications. Vault
  key fingerprints are 20 hex digits; the old 16 are their prefix, and stored pins still
  work.

- **`aterm fabric on` no longer accepts a fabric folder other users can read through an
  access list.** On a Mac a folder can carry an access list (ACL) that lets every user in,
  such as an `everyone allow read` entry passed down from a parent folder, and its mode
  still reads 0700. The fabric folder holds the secret that mints every capability, so
  `on` now refuses such a folder, naming the `chmod -N` that clears it, and changes
  nothing; a symlink or another user's folder there is refused too. A new mint secret is
  written only into a folder that passes the same check.

- **aterm Caffeine: Quit and uninstall do what they say.** Picking Quit in the menu at
  the moment aterm updated used to bring the mug back after the update, still keeping the
  Mac awake; Quit now wins. `aterm caffeine quit` no longer misses a mug that is
  restarting for an update, or reports one quit that launchd then started again.
  Uninstalling one of two aterm installs now quits that install's own mug (new: `aterm
  caffeine quit own`) and leaves the other's running; uninstalling a source-built aterm
  stops its mug first. Enable at Startup now does what its checkmark showed even if it
  was changed from a terminal while the menu was open. A mug started just before an
  update now restarts onto the new build.

- **aterm Caffeine with VoiceOver.** VoiceOver now says whether the mug is on or off, and
  pressing the mug with VoiceOver always toggles it, even after a menu item was picked
  with the right button. Asking for the menu while it is already open no longer reopens
  it after you close it.

- **aterm Caffeine keeps a copy macOS may still be checking.** On macOS 27.0.1, removing
  a program macOS has not finished checking can stall every launch on the Mac. The mug's
  own copy of aterm, and the keeper's, now count that check's time only while the Mac is
  awake, so a sleep or a clock change can no longer cut it short, and `aterm pkg
  self-uninstall` leaves such a copy in place and names it, with the minutes left, instead
  of removing it.

## [0.113.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added

- **`aterm ctl await sys` can now wait for a free build slot, spare memory and idle
  cores.** Four new terms join the wait: `load` (the 1-minute load average per core, a
  plain number: `'load<0.5'`), `cores_idle` (the cores less the 5-minute load average,
  never below zero: `'cores_idle>=4'`), `avail` (the memory the machine can hand out
  without paging, with its size unit: `'avail>=8GiB'`) and `slots` (the slots Trust's
  `build-slot` hands heavy builds, in `~/.cache/build-slot`). So `aterm ctl @self await
  sys 'slots>=1' and 'avail>=8GiB' timeout=600000` waits, with no polling, until a slot
  is free and 8 GiB of memory is available. Add `for=<duration>` to wait until both have
  held that long. A slot counts as free only when two reads at least a second apart both
  find nobody holding it, and a slot whose build kept running after its wrapper was
  killed can still count as taken. The reply says how many slots are usable out of how
  many (`slots=<usable>/<total>`). aterm reads the slots without taking any lock, so
  unlike `build-slot status` it never makes a build that is waiting for a slot skip one.
  Until a slot is proven either way, the term reads `slots=warming` and the wait keeps
  waiting. A slot aterm cannot prove never counts as free, so `'slots<1'` holds only
  once no slot could be free. Build slots are read on macOS only. Elsewhere, and where
  no slot record can be read, `slots` answers `ERR unavailable slots why=<reason>`.
  `aterm ctl help await` and `aterm help sys` describe each term.

- **On Linux under X11, the terminal bell makes a sound.** A bell from your shell,
  readline or a program such as Claude Code was silent on Linux, even with `bell_sound`
  on (the default). On X11 aterm now rings the bell for the window showing that tab (or
  the frontmost window), and your desktop plays it as it plays other programs' bells: on
  GNOME the sound theme's bell, or a flash under the visual bell, and nothing when the
  desktop's audible bell is off. It rings at most once a second, and serious mode keeps
  it quiet. `bell_sound = false`, or the Terminal bell sound row in Settings (now shown
  on Linux), turns the sound off and keeps the visual bell flash and the attention
  request; aterm no longer warns that `bell_sound` does nothing on Linux. On Wayland the
  bell is still silent.

### Fixed

- **Autopilot no longer approves a long Claude Code command whose box could be showing a
  different one.** When a Bash command has more than 64 `$(…)` substitutions, Claude
  Code asks before running it, even in a bypass session, and draws the command over
  several rows. On those rows, a long line that wraps looks exactly like a line break
  that starts a new command. In 0.112.0, under `approve = "safe"`, Autopilot settled
  this by taking the command from Claude Code's own session log when it drew the same
  rows, and pressed Yes if that command only read. But an older command still waiting in
  the log can draw the same rows as the new one. A harmless one-line `echo … touch path`
  looks just like `echo …` with `touch path` on its own line, and that second command
  creates a file. Now, under `approve = "safe"`, Autopilot judges every way the box can
  be read, and the log's command can only add a reading, never replace them. It presses
  Yes only when every reading only reads, so a box that could hide a write waits for
  you. A box whose every reading only reads is still approved.

- **The Overview's "On the fabric" group no longer stops refreshing when a read of it
  fails inside aterm.** While the Overview is open, this group reads once a minute which
  sessions on your fabric's other machines need you. If that background read hit an
  internal error, aterm kept running but the group never read again until aterm was
  restarted, and it kept showing its last list with no sign that it had stopped. Now a
  read that fails this way, or that aterm cannot start, counts as a failed read: the
  group keeps its last list, its header says `the last read failed`, and it reads again
  a minute later.

- **On Linux under X11, a window keeps drawing after X refuses its GPU surface for a
  moment.** X can refuse the surface of a window that has already drawn, for example
  once while the window is being torn down. aterm dropped that frame and then stopped
  drawing the window until you typed, clicked, resized or focused it, so the window
  could stay on its last frame even while its program kept printing. A window that X
  kept refusing switched to drawing on the CPU only after you had nudged it a few times.
  Now aterm tries again by itself a moment later, backing off, and gives up after five
  tries (about half a second). If the surface is refused three times in a row, aterm
  treats the GPU as lost and draws the window on the CPU instead.

- **On Linux, a window left tiled or full screen comes back at the size and place it had
  before.** When aterm quit or crashed with a window tiled to one side of the screen
  (GNOME's Super+Left or Super+Right, or a drag to a side edge) or full screen, the
  window reopened floating where the tile was and at its size, or at the whole screen's
  size in its top-left corner. It now reopens floating at the size and place it had
  before the tile or the full screen, as a maximized window already came back with its
  earlier frame to restore down to. Full screen counts whether aterm or your window
  manager's own key put it there, and on X11 a window maximized in one direction only
  counts as tiled. aterm does not tile the window again or put it back in full screen.
  On Wayland, which does not tell aterm where a window sits, the window gets back its
  earlier size. A seamless update still keeps such a window at the size and place it
  shows.

## [0.112.0] - 2026-10-22

### Changed

- **A package can no longer put a known shell on your PATH.** aterm's package manager
  already refused to lay a command named `sh`, `bash`, `zsh` or `fish` (or `sudo`, `ssh`,
  `git` and the other core commands), so even a stolen publishing key could not slip one
  in. It now refuses PowerShell's `pwsh` and `powershell`, `nu`, `dash`, `ksh`, `tcsh`,
  `csh`, `elvish`, `xonsh` and a dozen more shells, with their preview and versioned names
  (`pwsh-preview`, `bash5`). It also refuses a command whose name is not plain ASCII,
  because a Mac's disk treats some lookalike letters as the same name (a `pwſh` would run
  for `pwsh`). A package that names one gets no command under that name, and `aterm pkg
  doctor` (also `aterm pkg status`) now says so, naming the package and the name, where
  before the name was dropped without a word. A command of that name an older aterm
  already laid is removed by `aterm pkg repair` and by the next update. ALab's publishing
  tool refuses to build such a package at all.
- **`aterm init` and `aterm machines` no longer need gh.** `aterm init`'s GitHub setup
  checks your token with GitHub, keeps it in your login keychain through Apple's Command
  Line Tools git, points git's GitHub HTTPS sign-in at it, and reads both back. The
  read-back matches git's settings to GitHub the way git does (any spelling of the
  address, a user, a path, a file an `includeIf` brings in), so a setting elsewhere that
  would hand GitHub sign-ins to another helper as well, or ask as another account, is
  caught and named.
  The token is handed over privately and never shows in a command line or a program's
  environment. The machines controller keeps its machine user's token the same way: run
  `aterm machines github login` once (a controller that used gh's sign-in needs it too),
  type the token, which is not echoed, and aterm checks with GitHub that it is that
  account's and may manage SSH keys before storing it; hosts' keys are then registered and
  revoked straight over GitHub's API. The starter baseline no longer installs gh, and a
  starter you never edited follows.

### Fixed

- **Mac setup no longer restarts your Dock, Finder and Notification Center every
  minute.** When macOS did not keep one Dock setting, the background setup undid
  every setting it had just made, then tried them all again a minute later:
  each try changed your Dock, desktop and widgets, relaunched the Dock, Finder
  and Notification Center, put everything back and relaunched them again, about
  once a minute for as long as aterm stayed open. Now each setting settles on
  its own: one that took stays as set when another does not, and one that does
  not take is put back and left alone. Setup tries such a setting at most
  twice per aterm version and setup run, ten minutes apart; System State then
  shows it waiting for you, and its Apply (or `aterm doctor --apply`) tries it
  again. A setting setup already made stays as you set it if you change it
  while setup is still waiting on another one. Messages and FaceTime sign-out
  no longer wait on an unrelated Dock setting. Every preference setup puts
  back and every relaunch it makes is now written to aterm's change journal
  (`converge/journal.ndjson` in aterm's state folder) before it happens, like
  the changes it already recorded, with the values it replaces and writes.

## [0.111.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added

- **Open secrets vaults.** `aterm secrets password open` on an admin Mac lets
  every Mac that reaches the vault's server join with no password and no
  code: `aterm init` (press Enter at the password prompt) or the System State
  tab's Apply (leave the password empty) joins, and the admin Mac approves it
  within seconds, so the Mac's `~/.secrets` fills in that same Apply. Any Mac
  that reaches the server can then read the vault's shared entries; host
  sections still reach only their own hosts. A Mac you let go from an open
  vault stays out: its key is recorded in the vault, and only approving it by
  code lets it back in. Macs already waiting when you open the vault are
  listed, and `password open` asks before letting them in (any you do not let
  in join only by code, since one may be a Mac you let go earlier).
  `aterm secrets password set` closes the vault again with a password, and
  `password off` closes it to approval by code. A vault is open only when an
  admin makes it so; update every admin Mac first, since an older aterm cannot
  open a vault that has been opened.

- **Claude Code's agents panel wears the rainbow, and its dots tell you what each agent is
  doing.** Wherever aterm draws the border round Claude Code's input box, the agents panel
  under it (`⏺ main`, `◯ general-purpose …`, a workflow's `▰▰▱` bar) takes the border's
  palette (Cruise's rainbow, Land's sunset, Off's white): each agent's name in its own
  colour, top to bottom, and a workflow's bar along the whole palette, a crest of Claude's
  own ripple running over its filled cells while an agent works, in step with the harness
  card's ripple where the card is on screen. Each dot says: its colour
  is which agent, its brightness and glow how much work it is doing (a halo on a dark theme,
  a soft wash on a light one), its saturation how fresh its last work is; an agent waiting
  on a long command of its own (a `Bash` call still inside its timeout) keeps its full colour
  with a dimmer, steady light inside its ring (no glow past it), and with Claude's `❯` on its
  row the composer rule says what it
  waits on (`in Bash 4m12s`); a grey dot that breathes has done no work for two and a half
  minutes with nothing of its own in flight, or its command has outlived its own timeout
  (stuck); an amber ring waits on approval, and a finished or failed agent keeps Claude's
  green or red. Activity, times and
  token counts keep Claude's grey; a coloured cell, the cursor's row, a selection or a
  scrolled-back view keeps Claude's look. It changes only what is drawn: copies, `text`,
  `screen` and recordings keep Claude's panel. Serious mode keeps the colours and drops the
  glow and the breathing; `[claude_footer] agents = false` turns it off.

- **Click the token count in Claude Code's composer rule for a graph over time.** A click on
  `Σ` (or Return, Space or ↓ on it selected, or `aterm ctl open fact-menu usage`) opens
  the Traffic card hung above it: the tokens in and the tokens out as two bars over the
  session from its first token to now, each scaled to its own peak, the minutes Claude was
  working shaded, the start time and span beneath, and the working time, totals and peaks
  under that. A second click on `Σ`, Esc or a click elsewhere closes it. The card reads
  nothing while it is closed, and nothing it does reaches Claude Code.

- **Right-click a fact in Claude Code's composer rule for its menu.** A right-click (a
  ctrl-click on macOS) on the model, the effort, the working directory or the branch opens
  a small menu hung above it, drawn like the Autopilot menu. The folder's menu opens a new
  tab in the working directory or copies its full path; the branch's copies the branch name
  and, inside a repository, opens a new tab at its root; every menu hides its fact, and
  shows again any fact hidden in that session. Only the effort's menu types: its rows that
  turn the top-effort key on or off for the session type `/effort <key> on` or `off` as the
  key's own click does (below); no other row types anything into Claude Code. A copy or a
  new tab says `✓ copied` or `✓ new tab` beside the chips for two seconds. With a fact
  selected by ctrl+shift+tab, `↓`, shift+F10 or the Menu key opens its menu; `aterm ctl
  open fact-menu <model|effort|path|branch>` opens it from the wire and `aterm ctl controls
  fact-menu` reads its rows. A fact's title now says what its right-click offers.

- **Click the facts in Claude Code's composer rule to hide them, and click again to bring
  them back.** The model, the effort, the working directory and the branch that aterm writes
  under the input box are now clickable, like the Autopilot chip beside them. A click hides
  the fact: it reads greyed in the rule's own gray with `off` after it (`◆ Opus 5.5 off
  xhigh`, `◆ Opus 5.5 xhigh off`, `⌂ ~/aterm off`, `⎇ main off`), and a click on it shows it
  again. Nothing is typed into Claude Code, and a hidden fact stays hidden only for that
  session while aterm runs. Over a fact the pointer is a hand and the fact is underlined;
  where the chips are drawn, its title (the full working directory, `⎇ main · click: hide`)
  stands beside them. On macOS, ctrl+shift+tab walks the chips and then the facts, and
  Return or Space clicks the one selected. Screen readers hear each fact as a button
  (`Model: Opus 5.5`, `Working directory: …`).

- **Screen readers hear everything aterm draws on Claude Code's input box.** Under aterm's
  marks a screen reader reads Claude Code's own rows, so each mark is published on its own.
  The permission-mode light (`Permission mode: plan.`, with what a click does) is a button a
  screen reader can press, and the harness switch on the input box's top rule is read as a
  switch, on or off, with its `on` button when it is off. They sit beside the Autopilot and
  Team chips, the facts
  and the top-effort key. The words beside the chips (a chip's title, a refusal, the act just
  taken) can be read as text and never interrupt.

- **Click the top-effort key on Claude Code's input box to turn it on or off.** On a Claude
  Code build that has the top-effort key, the right end of the input box's top rule shows
  Claude's own tag while the key is on, and aterm draws the key's name greyed with `off`
  after it while it is off. A click on either types `/effort <key> on` or `off` into the
  empty composer as if you had typed it, waits for Claude to echo it, then presses Return,
  and says the answer beside the chips (`✓ <key> on (this session)`). A draft in the
  composer, a running turn, an open dialog, a halted or parked session or another driver
  refuses it and says why; a key you press or a click Claude Code is sent stops it before
  Return, and a stop after the `/` went says what it left in the composer.

- **Claude Code's mode pill reads `YOLO on` or `YOLO off`.** Wherever aterm draws the border
  round Claude Code's input box, the pill under it that reads `⏵⏵ bypass permissions on` shows
  `YOLO on`, and `⏸ manual mode on` shows `YOLO off`, in the pill's own colour, the row's
  other items moved up behind it (Claude's highlight of the one under the pointer moving with
  it) and a notice at the row's right end left where Claude drew it. It changes only what is
  drawn: copies, `text`, `screen`, recordings and the harness read Claude's own words, and a
  click on the row reaches Claude Code at the item under the pointer. The other modes keep
  Claude's pill.

- **Each coding agent's input box carries its own icon and name, and the context left is a
  fact you can hide.** The top line of every coding agent's input box now starts with the
  agent's own icon, drawn at emoji size in its brand colours (Claude Code's whole orange alien,
  agy's banner, Muse Code's diamond in Meta blue, Gemini CLI's sparkle, Codex's blue knot), and
  its name in its brand colour, two `─` in from the left, whatever the harness is doing: on,
  off, or not running at all. On Muse Code's line they take the place of its resting
  `Voice input (⌥ + v to start)` label, which comes back when they do not fit; a voice state
  with news (`Recording`, `Transcribing`) keeps its words, the icon after them. That line is the input box's top rule for Claude Code, agy and Muse Code, the
  rule above Gemini CLI's mode row (never its input band), and the shaded row above Codex's
  `›` prompt, which aterm writes on only when its cells show the shading. At the line's right
  the harness switch reads `alab harness ● on`, its letters in the border's rainbow (Land's
  sunset; under Off, white: `alab harness ○ off ▐ on ▌`), and the border's colours run from
  the icon into the switch; Codex's shading keeps its own colour. Codex gets the switch only as
  codex-alab, which carries itself; a vendor `codex` shows its icon and name alone. A narrow
  box gives up the switch's words first, then the name, then the icon, and the switch stays
  where it stood. Resting the pointer on the icon or the name shows the product and its build
  in the name's place (`Claude Code 2.1.304`, or `Gemini CLI` where no build is known), without
  moving the switch; a click there is the agent's, as on any rule cell. The icon is drawn over
  two blank cells: a screen reader still hears the agent's own line there, copies, `text` and
  `screen` keep it, and the switch is read as `alab harness on: Claude Code`. On the bottom
  rule, `◐ ctx 84% left`
  (drawn while Claude Code shows its indicator) is clicked like the path or the branch: a
  click greys it to `◐ ctx 84% left off`, a click on that shows it again, and
  `aterm ctl open fact-menu context` opens its menu.

- **`aterm init --only base.clt` installs Apple's Command Line Tools from a terminal.** It
  asks for your password once (`sudo`) and installs them as the machines agent does; without a
  terminal it says so and changes nothing. `aterm init --only` runs just the base items named
  (an id, a family such as `shell`, or `base`). When a first launch finishes and the Mac has
  no C compiler, aterm files one entry in its exceptions digest naming that command, instead
  of saying nothing; so does the next launch after a toolset installed with no window
  watching (over SSH), and the entry ends at the first launch after the tools arrive. On
  Linux a compiler that cannot build gets its own entry, and the entry ends at the next
  update after a compiler is installed. `aterm pkg doctor`'s C toolchain remedy names the
  same command.

### Changed

- **The fabric's session-log mirror is on by default, wherever the broker keeps it.**
  `aterm link broker` now keeps its log by aterm's own rules (each node's session records
  for 7 days or 256 MiB in all, unread mail for up to 7 days within 64 MiB, presence as
  its newest row, everything else 7 days within 32 MiB) and tells every bridge
  that connects. A bridge that finds those rules copies each session's turns, runs and needs
  onto the fabric for `aterm fabric brief`, as `[fabric] log = "turns"` did: ids, counts and
  closed words only, mail as counts, and never which session started another. Over a broker
  that keeps nothing it copies nothing, and `aterm ctl fabric status` says
  `mirror=unretained`. A node keeps at most 64 MiB of its records in the broker's window and
  waits there (`mirror=budget`) until the broker lets the oldest go. `[fabric] log = "off"`
  turns the mirror off; `"turns"` copies over any broker, as before.

- **The chip titles in Claude Code's composer rule are easier to read.** The words that appear
  beside the Autopilot chip and the permission-mode light when you hover or select one (and a
  light's "stopped in …" or "switched" note) are drawn in a stronger ink: four fifths of the way
  from the background to the text colour instead of halfway, and never under WCAG AA's 4.5:1. On
  dark themes they are lighter, on light themes darker. On aterm's own themes they still read
  softer than the conversation and stronger than the model, path and branch beside them.

- **Autopilot Off has its own white look, on the launch card and on the input box's border.**
  With a Claude Code session's Autopilot set to Off, the harness card on Claude Code's launch
  card is no longer taken away: the border, the trail, the kitty and its stars are drawn in white,
  pearl, silver and steel (on a light theme, pearl down to graphite, so it shows on the page), and
  the line under the card reads `✦ enhanced by aterm harness <version> · autopilot ○ off`. The
  input box's top border, with its `alab harness ● on` switch, now takes the session's colours
  too: Cruise's rainbow, Land's sunset, and under Off white, its switch reading `alab harness ○
  off ▐ on ▌`; clicking `on` turns the harness back on (Cruise). The switch's letters are dark
  enough to read on a light theme. The harness still keeps its hands
  off an Off session; with the harness switched off in Settings, for all sessions or for Claude
  Code, the card and the border stay plain but for that switch.

- **The harness card's rainbow keeps flowing, in time with Claude's mascot.** After its six
  seconds of show, the rainbow round Claude Code's launch card no longer stops: its colours keep
  travelling round the border, one trip every 12 seconds, and a shimmer runs out from Claude's
  mascot across the border, the trail, the kitty's rim, the stars and the line under the card —
  the same ripple Claude's mascot shimmers with, at its pace, and where the mascot shimmers
  (Claude Code's fullscreen view, its wand `✦` raised), on its beat: the card's rings are timed to
  the wand's flare, eased onto it a little at a time so they never jump. It moves once every
  128 ms, the grid Claude's ripple is drawn on, a moment before each of Claude's own redraws, so
  the card changes with the mascot on screen and those redraws draw its steps instead of costing
  frames of their own; between those steps a frame costs the card a copy. It stops at
  once, settled, where the window loses focus, with Reduce Motion or `motion = "reduced"`, while
  aterm sheds motion under load and in serious mode, and picks up again from the settled
  colours, without a jump, the moment it may move (focus coming back plays the six seconds of
  show first, as before). The kitty blinks once every six seconds while it flows.

- **The card's line makes aterm stand out.** In `✦ enhanced by aterm harness <version> · …`
  under the card, `aterm` is now bold and wears its own whole run of the card's colours — the
  rainbow under Cruise, the sunset under Land, the moonbow under Off; on a dark theme it is a
  step brighter than the rest of the line and flares harder as the shimmer passes. Where the
  pane is too narrow for the version, the line keeps `aterm` and the Autopilot's word instead of
  going: `✦ aterm harness · ∞ cruise`, then `✦ aterm · ∞ cruise`, then `✦ aterm ∞`.

- **Claude Code's update notice under the launch card now shows `✦ alab.systems`.** On the first
  launch of each new Claude Code build, Claude prints `Updated to latest. Got … features, …
  bugfixes, and … other changes.` and a `code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog for details` row under
  its launch card; wherever the harness card is drawn (Cruise or Land, and Off's white card), the
  summary row now shows `✦ alab.systems` in the card line's colours (its shimmer and flow too) and
  the changelog row is left blank. Cmd-click (Ctrl-click off macOS) on `alab.systems` opens
  https://alab.systems; a click on the blank row opens nothing, and while Claude tracks the mouse
  a plain click there is not passed to Claude, so its hidden changelog link never opens. It is
  drawn on the screen only: copying, `aterm ctl text`/`screen` and recordings still have Claude's
  own words. On a narrow pane the rows Claude wraps the notice onto are hidden with it (at 44
  columns both rows of the wrapped changelog line), and the narrow four-row launch card Claude
  draws there with its effort raised (its banner alone on the top row) gets the harness card and
  the banner too, down to 33 columns with the wand raised and 31 without. When the conversation
  scrolls the top of the launch card off the screen, the notice under the card's remaining rows
  keeps `✦ alab.systems`; once no row of the card is left, Claude's notice shows as it drew it, so
  a reply quoting it is never hidden. The notice also shows as Claude drew it while a find bar is
  up, when the harness card is not drawn, where Claude wraps its card's banner (32 columns and
  fewer), where Claude's rows do not read as its notice (a reworded notice), and in aterm's
  own scrollback, once the inline renderer's rows have scrolled up into it. Checked on
  Claude Code 2.1.304's own screens, fullscreen and inline, at 120, 50, 44, 34, 33 and 31 columns,
  and with the card scrolled off a 29-, 28- and 27-row pane.

- **Your login shell's rc file is created when it is missing.** The first launch, `aterm pkg
  seed`, `install` and `update` lay the ALab toolset's block (which puts the toolset on
  PATH) into the rc files you have, as before, and now also create the one rc file your
  login shell reads when it does not exist (`~/.zshrc` for zsh; for bash, `~/.bash_profile`
  on macOS and `~/.bashrc` on Linux; `~/.config/fish/config.fish` for fish). The login shell
  is your account's, never `$SHELL`, and no other shell gets a file; `install.sh`'s own PATH
  block (`aterm pkg shell-setup --path`) goes into that same file. A block you delete stays
  deleted until you run `aterm pkg repair`, and `aterm pkg doctor` says which it is.

- **An install over SSH installs the ALab toolset.** `install.sh` leaves the toolset to the
  first aterm window only when you are the person at the Mac's console. Over SSH, or on a Mac
  nobody is logged in to, it installs the toolset itself, as `--no-app` does, and says why.
  Under `sudo` it judges the user who typed `sudo`, and it never installs the toolset as
  root: it names `aterm pkg install --default-set` to run as that user instead.

- **`agents_auto_prime = false` also leaves Claude Code's settings alone.** aterm no longer
  adds its six Claude Code defaults to `~/.claude/settings.json` (the top effort mode,
  `xhigh` effort, the surveys and the drafted-feedback card quiet, autocompaction at 400k
  tokens) when `agents_auto_prime` is off; `aterm pkg doctor` then reports an unset key as
  staying unset. The README and `aterm help agents` name the six.

### Fixed

- **A run over another `$HOME` records its changes in that home.** `aterm doctor`, `aterm
  pkg repair`, `aterm init`, `aterm machines here` and the first-launch setup note each
  change in the converge journal (`converge/journal.ndjson` in aterm's state folder) before
  making it. A run with a scratch `$HOME`, such as an isolated launch or a test's, wrote that
  note into the journal of the home the account database names, the person's own. It now
  goes in the state folder of the `$HOME` the run changes. Root keeps its journal under its
  own home, because `sudo` keeps the invoking person's `$HOME`. On Linux the journal follows
  `$XDG_STATE_HOME`; on Windows it is under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\aterm`, where none could be kept
  before.
- **Save reflects the editor's active prompt.** File Save, the palette, toolbar
  and native command are unavailable while a prompt owns input. Completing or
  cancelling the prompt restores Save for a changed file, matching the editor's
  existing save behavior without discarding entered prompt text.

- **A delayed Linux Find paste stays with its original search.** A foreign X11
  clipboard reply cannot enter a different tab's search or a closed and reopened
  Find field in the same window.

- **A vault server on a Mac with a VPN stays reachable by name.** With a full-tunnel VPN or
  a Tailscale exit node on the server Mac, `aterm secrets serve --advertise` told the network
  `alab-secrets.local` was at the tunnel's address, which no other Mac on the LAN can reach,
  so every Mac's sync and join failed while the VPN was up. It now advertises the Mac's LAN
  address.

- **Vault requests carrying browser metadata are refused.** `aterm secrets serve` rejects
  requests with `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-*` headers before dispatch. aterm's own requests are
  unaffected. This header filter does not authenticate clients: plain HTTP reads without
  either header remain admissible.

- **`aterm init --check` no longer calls a Mac's vault files synced when they are not.**
  The secrets row said "kept in sync by the subscriber" whenever the Mac was in the vault
  and its service ran, even with a vault file missing or one that failed to write. It now
  reports such a Mac as a change, and `aterm init` writes the files again.

- **Setup no longer waits on the vault after git edits its config.** When a program
  rewrote a file the vault had filled in (git adding a credential helper to
  `~/.config/git/config`, say), or a vault file was deleted, System State kept saying the
  vault's files were incomplete until the next vault version or another Apply. The secrets
  service now applies the version it holds again within a minute: a deleted file comes
  back, a file a program rewrote stays as the program left it, and setup turns green.

- **The secrets service no longer spins on an entry it cannot write.** When a vault entry
  could not be written on a Mac (its folder is a symlink, or two names differ only in case),
  the background service fetched, decrypted and rewrote the vault in a tight loop and logged
  a line each time. It now retries after 5 seconds, doubling to 5 minutes, and logs a retry
  that fails the same way once.

- **`aterm secrets` no longer deletes a file of yours it found already in place.**
  When a vault entry's value matched a file a Mac already had (a token copied by
  hand, or a file set with `aterm secrets set <path> --file <the same path>`), the
  vault took it as its own, and removing or moving the entry later wiped and
  deleted that file. Such a file now stays yours: removing the entry leaves it,
  and a new value moves it to `~/.secrets/.replaced/` before writing.

- **Find reflects the editor's active prompt.** While Go to Line, command
  lookup or another prompt owns input, Find is disabled in the menu, palette,
  toolbar and native commands. Completing or cancelling the prompt restores it.

- **Clearing editor search clears its old footer message.** An empty query no
  longer leaves a previous query or “Failing I-search” message on screen.

- **Find shortcuts stay with the window they were typed in.** A shortcut held
  while a tab starts opens or navigates search in that window even if another
  window takes focus before the tab is ready. Each window's palette also keeps
  its own enabled commands when a shared setting or update refreshes the rows.

- **Accepting an editor search checks the current document.** If another view
  changed the selected match, Enter searches again from the search origin or
  reports no match. A selected match that is still valid stays selected.

- **A window with no control socket keeps the harness switches.** With no control socket
  nothing supervises a session, but the window still drew the harness's border round Claude
  Code's input box (and now its agents panel's colours) with the harness switched off in
  Settings, or with `Supervise Claude Code sessions` off. The agents panel's colours are now
