  Claude Code's auto amber (the same 1.88:1) or bypass red (3.47:1); each now takes the 4.5:1
  floor chrome's warning text takes on every built-in theme, and keeps its own colour on the
  dark ones.
- **An open menu is drawn over the caret and the cat, not under them.** With the Autopilot menu
  or a tab's context menu open over the composer, the caret's block and the resident cat (and the
  cursor's trail and glow) were drawn on top of the menu's rows, and so was a selection's
  highlight. The menu now hides the caret under it and cuts whatever lies across its edge, so the
  part beside it still shows; a selection the menu covers part of keeps its highlight on the side
  of the menu that holds the most of it while the menu is open. The Autopilot menu could also
  come up drawn in strips, only on the rows the program had just
  redrawn, until something else changed; it is now drawn whole at once.
- **The Autopilot menu's rows no longer move under a still pointer.** When a timer fired, or was
  armed or cancelled elsewhere, while the menu was open, the menu was laid out again one row
  shorter or taller and its rows slid under the pointer, so a click chose the row next to the one
  you were pointing at (`Cruise` instead of `Land now`). A row that leaves now leaves its place
  blank, so the rest stay where they were. When a row arrives and the others have to move, or the
  menu grows wider under a pointer resting beside it, a click on a row that moved since you last
  moved the pointer chooses nothing: it highlights the row now under the pointer, and the next
  click chooses it. On a Mac too, where every click arrives with a pointer-motion event at the
  spot you clicked.
- **`aterm ctl help open` names what it opens.** Its entry said only that "compatibility aux
  targets remain available", so `open autopilot-menu` and the rest could be found only by
  guessing. It now lists them (`prefs | about | menu | tab-menu | autopilot-menu | connections |
  update`, each also with `close`) and the aliases they answer to, and `help window`, `help
  controls` and the refusals of `open`, `window` and `controls` quote the same list: one table
  says which targets there are and which verb takes each.
- **After an update, the new window keeps the files access you gave aterm.** macOS judges the
  window an update starts by the copy of aterm it started from, at the place it first saw it, and
  the update deleted that copy seconds later. Switched on after the update, Full Disk Access then
  did not reach that window or the tabs it opened: on macOS 26 not for as long as it ran. The
  update now leaves the old copy at `/Applications/aterm.app.rollback` while that window runs,
  and the first launch after it deletes it.
- **On Linux, a screen reader reading by paragraph no longer freezes aterm.** In Settings and
  the Manual a blank line is a line with no text, and when Orca or another screen reader asked
  for the paragraph at or after one, aterm's accessibility code looked for its start forever
  and the window stopped responding at its next change. It now answers the paragraph that
  holds the position; every other answer is the same as before.
- **The harness reads an agent's "done" more exactly, and asks once less where it already
  knew.** A report that says done only as a condition or a time to come ("once it is
  finished and verified", "as soon as all tasks are complete", "after it is finished and
  verified") is no longer taken as done, nor is one about only part of the work ("the first
  task was completed", "almost everything is done"), and "Everything was already completed."
  now is. At the done check, `ATERM-TASK-DONE` followed by words that still name open work
  ("but one test still fails") gets the open-items challenge once instead of ending the task.
  A done reply to the done check (or, under Land, to the land instruction) that a usage limit cut is now read as
  the check's answer when Claude Code itself continues at the limit's reset, so the check is
  no longer asked a second time and Land types no extra nudge. Under Land, a done reply to the
  harness's answer to a question ends the task for a relaunch as it does for the loop. After
  an update from 0.106.0, a job already given the open-items challenge is not challenged
  again. A release line typed while background work runs is treated like one typed at an idle
  point: a done answer to it gets the check instead of `keep going`.
- **A relaunch or an upgrade no longer reopens or loses a task by misreading the
  conversation.** A conversation that only another agent session directed is kept as a task
  across an upgrade instead of being restarted afresh. A `/loop` wake on Claude Code builds
  that do not number turns no longer reopens a finished task, nor does Claude Code's notice
  of a scheduled task it missed while it was not running. A plain `keep going` after a
  usage limit is no longer read as the limit's retry of the done check, so its done reply no
  longer ends the task early. With `upgrade_ask` on, a finished conversation whose background
  tasks kept waking it is moved quietly instead of being asked the upgrade's notice, and a
  relaunch no longer types a carry-on into a finished task however many megabytes of those
  wakes came after its `ATERM-TASK-DONE`. `aterm harness upgrade` run by hand now respects a
  tab under Autopilot Land and types no Cruise carry-on there.
- **A harness that takes over while a turn runs reads that turn's end as the one before it
  would have.** When the harness was replaced in the middle of a turn (a seamless update, a new
  window, a settings change, a restart after a fault) and the turn ended before the new harness
  first looked, the new one read it as a turn it knew nothing of: it ended a task whose
  `ATERM-TASK-DONE` report still named open work instead of asking about it, typed `keep going`
  at the end of your own exchange, kept waiting on a spend limit a `/compact` of yours had
  already moved past (78 minutes too long), and after a try at a spend limit whose own turn met
  the limit again it tried again up to 5 minutes too soon, or 70 minutes too late after a try
  whose turn had worked on. The harness now notes a running turn even when it is the
  first thing it sees, and its successor reads that turn's end as a turn that ran, its work the
  time Claude Code's own `Worked for` row reports.
- **A harness that takes over at an API error keeps its retries spaced.** At an overloaded API
  (`529 Overloaded`) or another API error, the harness retries after 1, 5, 15, 30 and then 60
  minutes. A harness that took over (a seamless update, a new window, a settings change, a
  restart after a fault) started that ladder again and retried a minute later, up to an hour
  sooner than the one before it would have. Each record the harness writes at such an error
  now carries how far up the ladder it is and when the error last appeared, and the next
  harness carries on from there.
- **A harness that takes over at a spend limit tries when the one before it would have.** At a
  spend limit, or a model's limit that names no reset, the harness tries again 30 minutes after
  the limit appeared. One that took over before that first try counted the 30 minutes from its
  own start instead, up to 30 minutes late; it now counts them from when the limit appeared.
- **A harness that takes over before its try at a limit was read waits on that try.** When the
  harness types `keep going` at a spend limit and its next look comes late (the Mac asleep, a
  pause for an outage), a harness that took over more than a minute after the try, before
  anything had looked, took the limit's notice still on screen as the try's answer. When the
  try's own turn then ran and met the limit again, it tried 30 minutes too soon. It now treats
  its own first look as the try's first, however late it comes, as the harness that typed it
  does, and so too for a done check typed in the try's place at a limit's end.
- **The first harness after an update from 0.106.0 or earlier carries on where the one before
  it stood.** Those builds wrote no record of where their harness stood, so the first harness
  of this build to take over a session started over: after a run of short turns it typed
  `keep going` on the back-off's first rung, up to an hour sooner; it retried an overloaded
  API on its first rung, up to an hour sooner; it read a spend limit's try as a usage window's
  first, 2 hours sooner; it took your own prompt that met a model's limit as the fallback
  model's relaunch and typed into the standing limit; and it typed the open-items challenge
  again, or the Land instruction again after a done report. It now reads where the one before
  it stood from what that harness journaled: the waits it held and the streak they name, its
  retries' rungs, its tries' answers, a task's end, the relaunch's first ask, the challenge.
  Two things that journal does not say are still not read: your own exchange the older
  harness left to you, and Off standing over Land or over a done check.
- **After aterm reopens its tabs, each tab's harness carries on where the one before aterm
  ended stood.** When aterm starts again after it quit or crashed, it reopens every tab under a
  new identity, and the harness in each tab started from an empty record: after a run of short
  turns it typed `keep going` on the back-off's first rung (up to an hour sooner), it started a
  usage limit's or an API error's retries over and so tried again sooner than the one before
  would have, it typed the open-items challenge again, and under Autopilot Land it typed the Land instruction again where the
  harness before had already nudged or finished the landing. The harness in a reopened tab now
  reads the record and journal of the tab it was reopened from as the start of its own, and
  notes that it did; its record keeps that note while a state from before the restart (a switch
  to a fallback model, a Land in progress) still stands, so a harness that takes over later in
  the same tab reads it too. When aterm reopens its tabs a second time, a tab's harness reads
  back only as far as the tab it was reopened from still carried that record, so it no longer
  relaunches Claude Code onto its own model at a model limit's reset after the harness before it
  had already switched back.
- **A long-running session's harness record keeps what a takeover needs.** When a session's
  record passes 1 MB the harness trims it to its newest entries. After about 500 of its own
  actions since a switch to a fallback model, or since Autopilot Land's instruction, the trim
  dropped that entry: a harness that took over then did not switch the model back at the
  limit's reset, or typed the Land instruction again. The trim now keeps such an entry while
  it stands, with the few later entries that change it, so the record stays within 1 MB
  however long Land or the fallback model stays set; and the bookkeeping it writes beside
  each action no longer counts against what is kept, so Settings ▸ Harness shows "Partial" no
  sooner than before.
- **A tab's "cannot bring it back" mark survives an aterm update.** When aterm could not
  bring a tab's agent back, the tab's mark told you the command to start it by hand and stood
  until that conversation ran again. After a seamless update the new aterm forgot why the mark
  was there: the first program that started in the tab, a Claude Code at its first-run screen
  included, took the mark down, and resuming the conversation in another tab no longer did.
  The update now carries that word with the tab, and the mark ends as it would have.
- **After an aterm update, a tab you last typed in before it no longer reads as never typed
  in.** When you last typed was kept by the running aterm alone, so the updated one read every
  tab as untouched. A relaunch aterm carried through a hold (its tab held, then released)
  asks whether anyone typed in the shell since the hold began, and with no answer it waited
  out its limit and then asked you, even when nobody had. The outgoing aterm now hands over
  how long ago you last typed in each tab, as it stands at the moment it hands over.
- **A restore line is no longer lost where no window's harness looks at the tab.** When the
  resumed Claude Code reported that something the session ran did not come back, the one line
  aterm types to say so was typed only by the window's own harness at the tab's next idle
  point; a hand-run `aterm harness upgrade` never typed it and recorded it lost after five
  minutes. A sweep now types it too where the tab's own Autopilot is Cruise or Land, under the
  same checks, and still never into a tab set to Off.
- **An "agent down" row whose shell is gone is answered by the new tab it asks for.** When
  aterm started a tab's agent afresh and the shell it ran in was gone, the row asked you to
  open a new tab and start Claude Code there, and then stood for a day after you did: only
  an agent in its own tab answered it. The first Claude Code started after it in another
  tab, in the same directory and under the same Claude home, now answers it, one row each.
- **A tab reopened by an older aterm's restore knows its old tab's loop turns again.** No
  aterm before this one recorded which tab a restored tab stood in for, so after such a
  restore the old tab's own `keep going` after a finished task read as your prompt, and
  aterm could type a carry-on into the finished task. Every tab the upgrade ledger records
  moving the conversation in now counts as one of its earlier tabs, until the ledger
  records the conversation elsewhere or that tab with another one.
- **The harness's per-tab files no longer pile up forever.** aterm kept every tab's harness
  ledger, loop journal, goal hold and earlier-tab note under `drive/` for good, one more set
  per tab. Past 2048 files or 64 MiB (the session journal's budget) a window's sweep now
  removes the oldest tabs' files, and never those of a tab that is open, that a saved layout
  or an upgrade record still names, that a kept tab's note points back to, or that was
  written in the last week.
- **A relaunch through a hold no longer waits on a shell nobody ever typed in.** In a tab no
  person had typed in (one a script or `aterm ctl` made and drives), aterm could not say since
  when nobody had, so a relaunch carried through a driver's hold waited out its limit after
  the hold lifted and then asked you whether the shell had been used. aterm now knows how
  long it has served each such tab (an update hands that over too), and relaunches at once
  where nobody typed since before the hold.
- **An "agent down" row you answered stays answered after aterm restarts.** Once you started
  Claude Code again in a tab an upgrade had left with no agent, the row went away; but aterm
  kept that only in memory, so after a restart within the day the row came back the moment
  that agent ended. aterm now keeps it beside the upgrade records.
- **A Claude Code build that does not start is caught before the upgrade ends an agent for
  it.** The upgrade's first move onto a build never run on this machine ended the agent
  before anything had run the build, so a build broken at its start took one working agent
  down before aterm held every other agent off it. aterm now runs `<build> --help` once
  before that first move (a tenth of a second); a build that exits with a failure there is
  moved onto by no agent. A probe that cannot run the build, or does not finish, still lets
  the move go.
- **An upgrade that restarted a fresh conversation takes your word on its row.** When the
  upgrade's restart of a conversation nobody had asked anything left its agent down, `aterm
  harness upgrade <tab> --skip` (and the row's own words) answered "no upgrade is recorded",
  and `--now` told you to run `claude --resume <id>`, which Claude Code refuses for a
  conversation with no message. The row now takes the word, and every place names the same
  command as the tab's mark: `claude`, under the Claude home the agent ran in.
- **An account move to a login named by a Claude home's own directory is seen.** Claude Code
  names its login by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when no login variable is set, so an agent started
  in that home with no login variable runs the login aterm moved it to. aterm read it as on no
  login, kept the old account's usage limit standing for it, and held the tab until that
  account reset (up to a week).
- **A crash no longer tells a worker that finished in a worktree to carry on.** Under a
  relative `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, a Claude Code that enters a worktree goes on writing its
  conversation under the worktree's own home. Where aterm crashed (or the agent did) before
  the window had read that, the relaunch read the conversation where it was filed, ending on
  your prompt and the move, and typed its carry-on into the task the worker had finished in
  the worktree. The relaunch now looks in the worktrees of the repository the agent started
  in, and types nothing where the worker's finish is there.
- **A crash right after you set Land, Off or a hold no longer forgets it.** The crash journal
  wrote a tab's layout at most every 2 seconds, so when aterm crashed or was killed within
  about 2 seconds of a change to a tab's Autopilot (Cruise, Land, Off or a Land timer) or of
  a hold, the restored tab came back with what it had before the change: a tab set from
  Cruise to Land came back under Cruise, and its relaunch typed Cruise's carry-on and
  `keep going` into work you had chosen to land. Such a word is now written on the next
  turn of aterm's loop, 10 to 34 ms after it was set where measured.
- **`aterm ctl hold` and `meta set autopilot` answer `OK` only once the word is on disk.**
  Their `OK` used to come as the word was stored, before the crash journal's copy reached the
  disk, so a script that killed aterm on the reply could lose the hold it had just been told
  was set. Where aterm keeps the layout for a crash (`restore_session`), the reply now waits
  for that copy; if it is not on disk within 5 seconds the reply says `journaled=0`, and the
  word stands all the same. A fleet halt's holds are still answered at once, so a fleet halt
  reaches every tab without waiting on the disk.
- **A crash journal write that fails is tried again.** When the disk refused a write of the
  crash journal (a full disk), aterm did not try again until the layout changed, so a hold or
  Autopilot word written then could be missing after a crash. It is now retried every 2
  seconds until it succeeds.
- **A held tab whose hold you lifted while aterm was still reopening tabs stays without its
  agent after a second crash.** Its agent is yours to start, as it is once the reopening is
  over; a restart or crash in those first moments used to relaunch it and type its carry-on.
  The record that names the agent and the line that resumes it is written as you lift the
  hold, so a restart in those moments no longer leaves it unsaid.
- **After `/clear` or `/resume` in Claude Code, a crash of aterm reopens the conversation the
  agent moved to.** aterm saved the new conversation for a crash up to 2 seconds after it saw
  the move, and Claude Code records the move just after it draws, so with nothing drawn since,
  the saved layout could keep naming the old conversation; a crash then reopened that one and
  typed its carry-on into it. aterm now saves the move at once and looks once more 2 seconds
  after the screen goes quiet. An agent that crashed keeps the conversation its own last record
  named, even once another Claude Code start removes that record.
- **After `/clear` or `/resume`, Autopilot reads the conversation the agent is in.** Its checks
  of whether a conversation has a task or is finished, a usage limit's reset and the resume
  command it shows read the conversation the agent had left until aterm next looked.
- **A `~/.claude` on a network share that stops answering no longer freezes aterm.** aterm
  reads each agent's record as it saves the layout; it now waits at most 50 ms for that read
  and keeps its last copy otherwise.
- **Windows: a Land, Off or hold set just before you sign out or shut down is kept.** The layout
  Windows' end-of-session save writes was refreshed every 2 seconds and carried no holds; it
  now carries them, and is refreshed as soon as such a word changes.
- **After `/clear`, a restore no longer tells Claude Code to carry on.** Claude Code 2.1.302
  records `/clear`'s output in a form aterm did not read, so a cleared conversation read as
  having a task: after aterm quit or crashed, its relaunch typed "Continue where you left off
  … keep going" into a conversation nobody had asked anything. That output is now read as the
  command's own, and the relaunch types nothing there.
- **Your own exchange with an agent stays yours when Claude Code writes its record late.** When
  you talk with a supervised Claude Code yourself, the harness marks that turn as yours to answer
  and types nothing after it. It marked the turn by the last row of the conversation's record,
  which Claude Code writes on a timer: a reply that ended on a tool's call, or a record more than
  about a second behind the screen, was marked by a row that later readings no longer named, so
  a seamless update, a new window, a restored tab or a relaunch typed the done check, `Nobody is
  here to answer…` or the relaunch's carry-on into your exchange. The turn is now marked by your
  prompt, which is on the record when the turn ends; marks an earlier aterm wrote are still read.
  A command you run in Claude Code afterwards that the agent does not answer (`/config`,
  `/login`, `/usage`, a `!` shell command) no longer counts as a turn of its own, so it no longer
  hands your exchange back to the harness either.
- **Under `upgrade_ask = true` the live upgrade no longer types its notice into your own
  exchange.** When the conversation's last turn was your own exchange with the agent, which the
  harness leaves to you and types nothing after, the upgrade still typed its notice there (or
  its repeat, in a round that asked before your exchange), and the agent answered it inside your
  exchange. Such a session now moves to the newer build the default way: at a genuinely idle
  moment, resumed with nothing typed.
- **Your own exchange stays yours after the harness retries it past an API error.** When your
  message to a supervised Claude Code met an overloaded or failing API (or a usage limit), the
  harness typed the retry and left the retry's short answer to you. If that harness stopped
  between typing the retry and reading its answer (a seamless update, a new window, a crash or
  aterm's own end), the record of your exchange was closed by the retry, so the next harness or
  the relaunch typed the done check, `Nobody is here to answer…` or the relaunch's carry-on into
  your exchange. The record now stays open through the retry, and the retry's answer is left to
  you while the work before and after the error stays within the exchange's 10 minutes.
- **A harness that takes over a supervised session leaves your own exchange to you, as the one
  before it did.** A harness that took over (a seamless update, a new window, a restart) could
  type `keep going` at the end of your own short exchange with the agent, where the harness
  before it would have typed nothing: when you wrote after the task had ended, after an earlier
  exchange of yours or after Autopilot Off, the new harness still read the session as carrying
  its old task; when the harness before it stopped while your exchange ran, the new one read
  the exchange's end as a turn nobody was known to have started; and when you pressed Esc on the
  agent's answer to the harness's `keep going` and then wrote to it yourself, the new harness
  still read the session as carrying its task. All now read the session as the harness before
  them left it.
- **A command that clears the scrollback keeps its exit status.** Erasing the scrollback
  (ESC[3J, which macOS's `clear` writes, and Gemini CLI when it resumes a chat) used to take
  the running command's block and every block before it, so the shell's exit status had
  nowhere to land: `aterm ctl blocks` lost the command, `status` kept the exit code of the
  command before it, and the harness could not read how an agent that redraws on resume had
  exited, so it relaunched it at most once. The erase now takes only the blocks, marks and
  annotations that lay wholly in the erased lines: the running command keeps its block, and
  its exit status lands as usual. `status` reports the latest finished command's exit even
  when an erase right after its prompt took its block. An erase on the alternate screen no
  longer takes any block. The blocks of earlier commands on a screen that `clear` or Ctrl-L
  blanked stay too, with their exit codes, and `aterm ctl blocktext` answers that their
  output is gone (`ERR block output evicted from scrollback`) instead of reading the next
  command's lines from the same rows, as Ctrl-L's did before (`clear` used to drop them).
- **A command that clears the screen reads as what it printed, never as other lines.** A
  command that cleared the screen while it ran (`clear; make`, a script that starts with
  `clear`, a program that redraws on the main screen) kept the rows its block had before the
  clear: `aterm ctl blocks` showed it ending above where its output started (`out=5 end=0`),
  `aterm ctl blocktext` read nothing or lines that were not its output, and the cat kept
  watching a blank row. The rows the clear blanked now move to the top of the cleared screen,
  with the same id and exit status: `blocktext` reads what the command printed that is still
  in the scrollback, then what it printed after the clear; its rows never run backwards; its
  prompt keeps its place in the scrollback, so jumping to the previous prompt still reaches
  it; and the cat watches the new output. A command line the clear wiped reads as gone unless
  the shell named it (aterm's shell integration does), so with another integration `status`
  no longer names the program after whatever the command drew over its command line
  (`detail=python3` for a `vim` that drew `$ python3 …` there). When the scrollback is erased
  while a command runs (Cmd-K, `ESC[3J`, which macOS's `clear` also writes), `blocktext`
  reads what is left of its output (the erase used to take the block itself), so a program
  that redraws with `clear` reads as its latest screen. What it reads of a command a clear or
  an erase caught running is only what is left, and `blocktext` does not say that part is
  missing; once the command has finished, a clear or an erase that takes part of its output
  makes `blocktext` answer that the output is gone, as for any earlier command. After Ctrl-L
  at a prompt the block lines up with the prompt the shell redraws at the top, its command on
  the prompt's last line when the prompt has two, and a screen cleared after a command
  finished but before the next prompt marks that command's output as gone if the clear
  blanked any of it, instead of lending it the shell's lines. A seamless update or a restored
  session keeps every command whose lines it still holds, with its id and exit status, not
  only those whose prompt line it holds: such a command (`seq 300`, whose prompt scrolled
  off) used to be left out once its prompt was older than the scrollback carried over.
- **The resident cat no longer sits on aterm's chips.** It took a chip row for empty ground and
  sat on it, hiding the Land timer's digits. Every cell aterm draws into the grid over the
  focused pane (Claude Code's footer facts, the harness card's line, the Autopilot menu) is now
  ground the cat never rests on; it sits beside them, and a chip that grows or moves is clear of
  it by the next frame.
- **A quiet desktop costs nothing again.** Three timers woke aterm while nothing happened. Each
  tab's context menu was recomposed every 30 s to re-derive its timeline's `… ago` ages though
  nobody had it open: the menu now keeps when each event happened and reads its age as it opens,
  so no timer runs for it, window on screen or not (only an agent upgrade's words in a tab's menu
  still refresh every 30 s while one is pending). Each supervised tab woke about every 80 s to
  find its harness claim renewed: the deadline now follows the claim's live lapse wherever the
  loop turns, so a claim renewed by a harness that reads the tab's status between renewals, as
  aterm's own does every step, never fires it (with no turn between renewals it still fires once
  a lease, finds the claim renewed and re-arms). And the disk watch's minute look told the
  window twice a minute that nothing was wrong: now once a change, and at most every 6 hours
  otherwise.
- **Settings ▸ Harness names an agent's session without its spinner.** A Codex session's row
  read `⠦ Add tested calculator functions | proj-codex`, a frame of the spinner Codex animates in
  its title, frozen there and drawn as a blank indent. The row, the Autopilot menu's name, the
  menu bar's window list, the connection card, the session picker's rows, the tab menu's
  connection lines and the connection map now drop a leading spinner frame (any braille frame,
  Claude Code's moons and the other circle spinners) from an agent's own title; a name you gave
  the tab is kept whole, and Claude Code's `✳` stays.
- **The harness card wears Claude Code's top-effort launch card.** At its top effort level
  (Claude Code 2.1.302) the vendor's mascot raises an arm and holds a wand (`╱✦`),
  which moves the card's text two columns right; aterm did not take that card for a launch card,
  so a session at that level showed only the vendor's banner, with no rainbow border, kitty or
  `✦ enhanced by aterm harness` line, for the whole run. The card is now found with the wand in
  hand at every width that draws it on three rows, and the line goes under it at its own text
  column. A row that only names the build (`Claude Code v2.1.302 …`), with or without symbols
  before it, is still not a card.
- **The harness card no longer blinks while Claude Code's mascot plays its entrance.** On the
  fullscreen renderer (`CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1`) Claude Code 2.1.302 plays a one-second
  entrance once per build: the mascot sits a row low in a puff of dust and raises both arms
  beside the card's words. aterm found the card only on the frames where the mascot stood as it
  rests, so the rainbow border, the kitty and the `✦ enhanced by aterm harness` line went off
  and on several times in that second. Once the decoration is on, it now stays on through the
  rest of the entrance: while the card's words (the banner and version, the model, the working
  directory) stand where they were, the frames where only the mascot moves keep it. It still
  goes on the frame the card really leaves: scrolled, cleared, covered, the program gone, a
  resize, the narrow layout, or a newer card under it. When the decoration first comes on is
  unchanged: once aterm has read the running build, which on many launches is only after the
  entrance has played.
- **A turn after a landing is no longer called landed when the harness restarts.** After a
  landing, you or a script could type a new turn whose reply also ended `ATERM-TASK-DONE`. When
  the harness restarted after that (Autopilot Off and back to Cruise or Land, a settings change,
  a seamless update), it read that reply as the landing. The tab said `✓ landed` and
  `task=landed` instead of `✓ done`, and the journal claimed the agent finished "after the land
  instruction" when no land instruction came before that reply. Now a landing carries across a
  restart only while the screen's last reply is still the landing's own words. The harness
  records a mark of the agent's last words with each point it journals, and compares the
  restarted harness's first point with the landing's: another reply, whether the journal
  recorded its turn or it was typed while Autopilot Off had stopped the harness, is read as it
  is. Its token reads `✓ done` and nothing is typed. A Cruise timer over that done task still
  fires: the tab turns to Land and reads `✓ done`. A plain landing still reads `✓ landed` after
  a restart, also when the harness rode out a seamless update or a resize redrew the landing's
  reply after it (a landing said in words alone no longer gets the land instruction typed again
  there).
- **A new tab on a busy Mac gets its warm shell.** Before aterm starts a shell ahead of your next
  tab, it checks that your startup files leave no process behind. Any process of yours that exited
  during that check (a build, a test run) left the check unfinished, so on a busy Mac aterm never
  learned that your shell starts cleanly, and a shell it had already started was thrown away and
  not tried again for an hour (`metrics` read `spare_discard=scan-unknown`). The check now looks
  again and counts a process that has gone as gone; a process still running is checked as before.
  A process macOS starts on its own during the check (Spotlight indexing your files), one that
  exits before the check reads it whole, and a background job another of your terminals or tools
  started during the check no longer count as left behind either (`metrics` read
  `spare_discard=escaped`).
- **Claude Code's rating card in a pane under about 30 columns is still the card**: where the
  pane is too narrow for even its first `1: Bad` box, the harness read no card, took its rows for
  the worker's last words and could type its continuation into the standing card. It now reads
  the card at every width from 16 columns and dismisses it as in a wide pane.
- **Three Claude Code dialogs in a narrow pane get the answer they get in a wide one.** A held
  message from another session under about 34 columns (its `Deliver this message to Claude` wrapped
  before `Claude`) is delivered instead of coming to you; the usage-limit dialog under about 22
  columns (its `automatically` broken in two) waits for the reset instead of coming to you; and
  Computer Use's request at 18 to 24 columns is read with its whole refusal.
- **A question whose `Submit` Claude Code drew over the harness's own text says so when it comes
  to you.** Where the button was drawn over the text's last row and the rest of that row was glued
  to it (`Submitked.)`), the harness read the dialog whole with its text a row short and told you
  it had not written that text; it now says the question could not be read whole. Nothing is
  pressed either way.
- **A permission box taller than the pane is answered whole.** In a pane too short for a long
  command (a 30-line script in an 18-row split), Claude Code's box lost its title and command off
  the top of the screen, and every level held it for you until the pane grew. Claude Code writes
  the whole box on the main screen, its head right above the screen in the history, so the
  harness now reads the head back and decides the box as if the pane showed it whole: only
  where the head reads as that box's own (its top rule nearest above the screen, every row up
  to the screen read, nothing redrawn meanwhile, the joined rows one box with the options the
  screen shows), and its key is fenced on that screen. Anywhere else (the fullscreen renderer,
  a head evicted, a question) it is held as before.
- **A draft over an older Claude Code's `/` menu is sent only onto its own command.** Claude Code
  2.1.289 and before mark the menu's selected entry in colour only, and the harness took the top
  entry for it: after you arrowed to another entry (or the menu kept a selection from earlier),
  a draft such as `/config` left standing was sent with an Enter that ran the entry you had
  moved to (`/update-config`). The harness now reads the entries' colours: it sends the draft
  only when the selected entry is its command, tells you once when it is another, and leaves it
  alone where the colours do not say which entry is selected (a menu of two).
- **The same question asked again right after the harness answered it is answered again.** Under
  `long-term` or `short-term`, when Claude Code asked a question again so soon after the
  harness's Enter that no read saw it working between, the new dialog's empty field read as the
  harness's text gone from the old one, and the question came to you. A question the harness's
  own Enter answered, its field empty again and nobody's key since, is now a new dialog and gets
  the text afresh; after a key of yours it still comes to you.
- **A box you refuse with Esc is held for your full grace, whatever program you run.** The harness
  counted `human_grace_s` from the last turn end it had seen, not from your Esc, so a box you
  refused at once could be continued within a second; it now counts from the first read of the
  Esc.
- **`aterm drive phase` says what Esc does on a box**: `exit esc` under a trust dialog whose Esc
  quits the program (Claude Code's, Muse Code's, Gemini CLI's, agy's), and no Esc line where
  nothing says.
- **The journal's line for a turn's end shows the worker's whole last line in a narrow pane**
  (the wrapped rows joined), for every agent.
- **A question's notes field you opened is yours.** Under the recommended word, which never
  opens one, a Muse Code question with its note open (or holding your text) is left to you:
  its Enter would have sent it.
- **Muse Code**: its network box gets its one-shot `Yes, proceed` at full power (never its session
  or always grant); its background-work panel no longer hides the composer or a box; its several-
  question and multi-select forms and their review go to you; under long-term or short-term its
  question gets the policy text as a note; its Meta-account walls are sign-in walls with its own
  fix.
- **Muse Code's MCP tool box is read, and goes to you naming the tool.** The `Would you like to
  allow this tool action?` box an MCP server's tool raises was a box aterm could not name; it is
  now read as a call of that tool (`tool action: mcp__<server>__<tool>`) with its one-shot allow,
  its session and always grants and its refusal, and the harness hands it to you at every level,
  as it does Gemini CLI's MCP box. Its network box of a command (a sandboxed command reaching a
  host, or a Unix socket with `Allow once` · `Reject`) still goes to you, now naming the command
  instead of saying the box offered no refusal. The tool box and the Unix-socket box were drawn
  by the real Muse Code 1.4.10 outside the lab, its own sandbox on, its proxy variables pointed
  at a local stand-in for Meta's API that refused every other host.
- **Every agent's answered question is announced once** with `CHOSE … policy=<word>`, as Claude
  Code's dialogs were.
- **Gemini CLI**: turns are continued under YOLO, with its UI details hidden and with
  `ui.showShortcutsHint` off; in shell mode (`!`) nothing is typed. **agy**: an API refusal (403,
  404 model, a refused 400) goes to the menu bar instead of being re-sent; a daily quota is waited
  out until the time Google's RetryInfo names.
- (developer tool) **`targo --unverified verify fmt` checks new, unstaged source files** cargo
  builds. The lab gains `muse-selftest`; `lab harness TAG key=value` quotes a bare word; the lab's
  `turn` reads Gemini CLI's composer through its reader.
- **Windows: Ctrl+H deletes one character, not a word.** At a PowerShell, cmd or Git Bash
  prompt, Ctrl+H (and Ctrl+Shift+H) deleted the whole word before the cursor: behind ConPTY
  the console host read its backspace byte as Ctrl+Backspace. aterm now sends Ctrl+H as the H
  key pressed with Ctrl. Unlike Windows Terminal it leaves Shift out, because PowerShell has
  no Ctrl+Shift+H binding and would type a literal `^H`. Ctrl+Backspace still deletes a word,
  and Ctrl+C is unchanged. Claude Code still deletes a word on Ctrl+H; it reads the key that
  way itself.
- **The command palette's filter takes the readline keys.** Ctrl+W, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+H and
  Alt+Backspace delete in the palette's filter as they do in the find bar, the rename field
  and Settings, where they used to type `w`, `u` or `h`, and other Ctrl chords no longer type
  their letter. `aterm ctl key` drives the filter the same way.

- **The harness no longer answers Claude Code's "New MCP server found in this project" dialog.**
  Every choice in it, Esc included, is saved for good in the project's
  `.claude/settings.local.json`, and the harness was choosing "Continue without using this MCP
  server", which turned the server off for good; the dialog (and the one for several new
  servers) now waits for you at every `approve` level, and `claude mcp reset-project-choices`
  undoes a choice already saved.
- **The harness no longer turns on Claude in Chrome for later sessions.** When Chrome
  setup finished connecting, the harness chose "Continue with browser tools", which keeps
  the browser tools on in every later session. It now chooses "Continue without browser
  tools" at every step of the setup, and that choice saves nothing.
- **With no `theme` set, the terminal is the dark Default again, whatever the OS appearance.**
  0.105 drew Default Light on a light OS when no theme was set, so updating turned unconfigured
  terminals white. Following the system is now a choice you make: turn on Follow system in
  Settings (it writes `dark:Default,light:Default Light`, or your theme's own pair), or write a
  `dark:…,light:…` pair in aterm.toml. Settings shows an unset theme as Default with Follow
  system off, Reset returns to it, and choosing a theme over it writes that theme's name. If you
  turned on Follow system in 0.105 with aterm's own themes, 0.105 did not record it; turn it on
  again.

- **On a new Mac, aterm now asks for file access when it starts, on macOS 26 Tahoe and macOS
  27.** No app can switch on its own file access: only you can, in System Settings. So when
  aterm finds Full Disk Access off on a Mac where it has never seen it on, System Settings opens
  at Privacy & Security ▸ Full Disk Access a few seconds after you open aterm, at a pause in
  your typing, with aterm's panel beside it: what the switch lets programs in aterm read, what
  it trades, and aterm's icon to drag into the list (or press + below it and choose aterm).
  Answer **I've switched it on** or **Not now**; when aterm reads the grant, the panel says so.
  If you answer **Not now** or leave the panel alone, aterm then asks macOS for your Documents,
  Desktop and Downloads folders one at a time, so those dialogs come now rather than in the
  middle of an agent's work, and once every folder has an answer it does not ask again. The
  page comes up by itself once per aterm version, not for 30 days after **Not now** (90 after a
  second time), and never on an ad hoc build; aterm presses nothing in System Settings.
  `[privacy] warmup = "on-request"` leaves the folders to Settings ▸ Security's button,
  `"never"` turns them off, and `[privacy] notice = false` keeps the page from coming up by
  itself. Settings ▸ Security's **Open Privacy & Security…** and the "To look at" entry's
  **Open Settings** now bring the same panel. On macOS 27 aterm could not tell whether it had
  Full Disk Access, because macOS 27 keeps no per-user privacy database where aterm looked; it
  now reads the system one, so Settings ▸ Security and `aterm ctl privacy` say granted or
  denied. For a few minutes after aterm updates itself, macOS judges the window's own file
  reads by the old copy it just removed, and turning Full Disk Access on then could leave the
  window and its tabs refused for minutes; aterm now makes that check from a short-lived
  helper, which macOS judges as aterm, so the switch reaches them at once. Tabs kept across an
  update follow the switch as new ones do.
- **A long text the harness types arrives whole.** A text of about 1.1 KB was cut at 1,022
  bytes, the most a macOS terminal's input queue takes at once, and the harness journaled `ERR
  write failed partial accepted=1022` instead of the text. A guarded `aterm ctl send if=…` now
  delivers its whole text, in order, as the program reads it; a guarded press sent while the
  rest of the text is still on its way is refused with zero bytes (`ERR busy sink`) and should
  be sent again once the text has gone. `reset flush` and the restart signals drop such a text
  whole, never its first kilobyte alone with the rest still delivered.
- **A tab whose task was done under Land is no longer told to carry on after a restart.** When
  aterm quit or crashed, or Claude Code exited on its own or was restarted in place (for its
  memory, a model's limit or `aterm ctl restart`), the harness typed its "Relaunched: …" or
  "Restarted: …" line, which ends "Continue where you left off". An update's restart types
  nothing by default; under `[harness] upgrade_ask = true` it typed its "Upgraded: … Continue
  where you left off" line. Under Land these were typed even when the last reply said the work
  was done, which restarted work you had asked to wrap up. Now nothing is typed there. The tab
  reads `✓ done`, or `✓ landed` when the landing carried over, and the upgrade ledger's row says
  `done:said-done`, "nothing typed: under Land, its last reply said done". If the reply said
  done only in words, Land asks for the wrap-up once, as it does anywhere else. A Land session
  that was still working, including a landing that Claude Code's memory banner cut short, is not
  read as done, and gets none of Cruise's carry-on either (`done:landing`): Land's own
  instruction, a nudge or nothing follows, as at any point under Land. Any Cruise session is
  carried on as before.
- **agy's API errors, survey and first run are read.** The inline `⚠ agent executor error …`
  block is a wall by its status (a refused key a lost login, the rest API errors) instead of an
  ended turn the harness kept typing into; its random `[1] Good [2] Fine [3] Bad [0] Skip`
  survey is dismissed with `0` and never taken for the composer; its first-run colour-scheme and
  terms screens are boxes no level presses. A lost agy login says to quit and run it again, or
  give it a valid Gemini API key.
- **Codex's usage reading trusts no forked copy and no login you signed out of.** Limits are read
  per login, a window past its reset counts as empty, the largest share of the current window
  is used (an old copied 60% no longer hides a real 95%), and `aterm harness usage` counts a
  subagent's first turn, which 0.163.0 starts within milliseconds of its copied history.
- **Correction to 0.105.0's kitty-command flash note:** closing a split pane above or below
  leaves the flash in the other pane running, but closing a pane beside it still ends the
  flash: your pane gets wider, and the flash ends whenever the width changes, because the text
  may move when lines rewrap. This release changes nothing there.
- **Muse Code installed by Meta's installer is supervised.** That installer's `muse` runs the
  build as `muse-bin-<version>`, which aterm did not recognise: the session was unsupervised and
  its boxes went unanswered.
- **The harness no longer types over Muse Code's prompt hint, or into a draft when it brings
  you mail.** The grey hint Muse Code shows in its empty input box (`/export saves the
  conversation to a text file`) was taken for a draft of yours, which the harness would have
  sent once it had waited long enough. A message the harness brings a session is typed only
  into an empty input box, judged as the turn-end check judges it, so text you were typing,
  Muse Code's `/` menu filter among it, is left alone.
- **More Muse Code screens are read.** The first of several questions, and the review of
  their answers before they are sent, now reach you; they had stood unanswered. A box still being
  drawn is no longer handed to you as a box with no title. The harness no longer types into a
  drawer or picker you opened (`/model`, `/settings`, …) or into the side chat, and it finds
  `ATERM-TASK-DONE` above Muse Code's notices of background work and at the end of a reply
  taller than the window. A login Muse Code lost, a quota it used up (`You've used your weekly
  quota`) and a fault only you can fix stop the harness from continuing the session. A Muse
  Code run again in the same tab reads as a new session.
- **agy boxes the harness could not read, or read too eagerly.** A box for a multi-line
  command (its options quote the command over several rows) stood unanswered and unescalated
  for minutes; it is now answered. An answer agy saves to its settings (`(Persist to
  settings.json)`) is never pressed as the one-time Yes. agy's `(Recommended) …` answer is
  found where agy puts the mark, at the front; a multi-select question drawn with `[ ]` boxes,
  a write-in already committed, and a subagent asking for approval are left to you; a turn that ends on agy's
  quota, credits or high-traffic error is waited out or handed to you, not continued; and the
  hints agy shows in its input box (a permission mode's, its queued-messages hint) are not
  taken for a draft. Each was found by agy itself, working a real task in aterm and reviewing
  aterm's reader of its screens.
- **On macOS, starting Claude Code in a new folder from an aterm shell gets its trust
  question answered at once again.** The harness keeps its hands off a session for
  `human_grace_s` (120 s) after your last key, and that key was the Enter that started the
  agent, so the folder-trust dialog stood two minutes on `No, exit`. aterm now records how many
  keys you had pressed at the instant your shell signed that the command started, before
  anything the agent drew could be on screen (`status launch=`, `text --json`'s `"launch"`),
  wherever its shell integration runs: zsh, bash, fish and PowerShell, on any host. When your
  last key then was that Enter (Caps Lock or Num Lock on included) and you have pressed none
  since, the dialog is answered as soon as it settles, each key skipped if you key first. It
  still waits out the grace when you pressed anything after the Enter, when a
  dialog was already on screen, when the line started something other than `claude`
  (`exec`, a wrapper, or in zsh and fish an alias by another name; bash reports the command an
  alias expands to), when the shell has no aterm integration (ssh, tmux), when keys of yours are
  unread, on Linux and Windows (aterm cannot yet see there whether the agent has read your keys:
  `status input=-`), or when another driver holds the session.
- (developer tool) **The real-agent lab keeps Muse Code off your own Muse files and out of the
  shared `/tmp`.** Muse Code 1.4.10 read your `~/Library/Application Support/Muse` (its
  session-name database) even with its home pointed at the lab's scratch; the lab's jail now
  denies it, `~/.local/share/muse`, and the Antigravity app's
  `~/Library/Application Support/Antigravity*` and `~/.antigravity*`. Muse Code's per-user
  registry in `/private/tmp/tbh-<uid>-rt/muse` stays there whichever of `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, `TEMP`,
  `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or `HOME` is pointed at the scratch, so `lab down` now removes the lease,
  socket and session record that run's Muse Code left there, and nothing else; `muse-selftest`
  fails when that directory holds anything new after `down` besides its shared directories and
  lock and what a live Muse Code outside the lab names. Muse Code's other temporary files go to
  the scratch. `muse-selftest`, `agy-selftest` and `gemini-selftest` now also fail when the agent
  holds any file in your home outside the lab.
- **An upgrade that gives up tells the agent so before the harness continues it.** When an agent
  upgrade stopped asking at the end of a turn, the line that tells the agent the upgrade is off
  waited for the screen to go quiet, and the harness typed `keep going` there first; the line
  was then dropped, so the agent never heard that the upgrade's notice no longer applied. The
  line now waits out that settle (up to two looks, about 80 seconds) before the harness types
  anything, and only then is the agent continued as before.
- **One unreadable upgrade record no longer freezes the upgrades view.** When one tab's agent
  upgrade record could not be read (its file unreadable, or written in a form this build
  cannot read), every tab's upgrade rows and tab marks stayed as they were until that record
  could be read again. The other tabs' rows and marks are now kept up to date. The tab whose
  record cannot be read keeps what it shows, its row and its tab mark, including a row an
  update carried over for it, and nothing new is raised for that tab until its record reads
  again, so an old row no longer turns into a `claude --resume` prompt over a running agent.
- **aterm says when it cannot list the agent upgrades' records.** When the folder agent
  upgrades keep their records in could not be listed (its permissions, or a file in its place),
  the upgrade rows and tab marks stayed as they last were and nothing said they were out of
  date. A line, `Agent upgrade records unreadable`, now names that folder under Details while
  it stands. It goes at the first look that lists the folder again, and when upgrades are
  switched off. Likewise, an upgrade record aterm cannot read (one `sudo aterm` wrote, for
  example) now raises `Agent upgrade record unreadable` with the file under Details, and it
  holds only its own tab's row and mark as they are (the tab its agent runs in), not every
  tab's.
- **A restart an update could not carry on is named by its own agent.** When aterm updated itself
  while an agent's restart was under way and the new aterm could not finish it, the row said
  `Couldn't resume Claude` and told you to type `claude --resume`, whatever the agent was. It now
  names the agent the restart's record names, so a Codex is told `codex resume`.
- **An agent aterm could not bring back after a restart is always named.** If clearing a tab's
  "still trying" word failed while aterm was finishing a relaunch it could not make, the tab was
  left out of the "Couldn't resume" row. The tab is now named even when that word cannot be
  cleared.
- **The "Couldn't resume" row after a restore stays accurate.** If you dismissed the row, or it
  stood on screen for its full time, the next one no longer names those tabs again; a row that
  never reached the screen, or was pushed off a full one, is still named in the next. Each tab is named where it is now, so a tab
  renumbered after another closed is not named by its old number, and a tab closed since is
  left out. After a seamless update, the row the earlier aterm left up stays beside the new
  one instead of being replaced by it. If two rows were said at once, the newer one now wins.
- **A relaunch after a restore that hit an internal error no longer says the agent did not come
  back while it is coming back.** aterm now checks whether the relaunch had started typing, and
  if so it looks for the agent instead. It also no longer tells you to type `claude --resume` into
  a tab where an agent is running. If the error comes back at every try and no agent ever comes
  up in the tab, the "Couldn't resume" row still names that tab.
- **A relaunch line is never typed twice after an internal error.** If aterm hit an internal
  error just after typing an agent's relaunch line, before noting that it had typed it, the next
  try could type the same line again at the shell's prompt. aterm now notes the typed line
  before it does anything else.
- **An internal error in the harness for one tab no longer stalls every other tab.** If one tab's
  part of the harness's pass hit an internal error, the whole pass stopped and restarted, and hit
  the same error again each time, so no other tab got supervision. The error now affects only
  that tab's part of the work, and that part is tried again after a pause that grows from a
  second to an hour while the error repeats, so a passing error no longer stops that tab's
  supervision for good.

## [0.105.0] - 2026-10-16

### Added

- **The harness supervises Muse Code (Meta).** At full power its shell and file boxes get Enter
  on `Yes, proceed`, a pipeline's stage box `Allow this stage once` and its trust box `Trust and
  continue`, never a standing grant; its question gets its `(Recommended)` answer, else its
  first, by the cursor and Enter; `approve = "safe"` and `"none"` hand every Muse Code box to you.
  A turn's end is continued with the text first and Enter once its echo holds still (an Enter in
  the same burst is a newline there), and a box is answered within about two seconds though its
  status row stays up. Its walls say its own remedy: a rejected `META_API_KEY` is to be updated
  or unset, a signed-out Muse Code signs in with `muse login` in a shell, and a limit past its
  reset points at its `/upgrade`. Settings ▸ Harness has **Supervise Muse Code sessions**
  (`[harness.muse] enabled`), and `aterm agents` primes it through `~/.config/muse/AGENTS.md`.
  Its boxes were measured on the real Muse Code 1.4.10 against a local stub of Meta's API, with
  no account. Muse Code is not relaunched when it exits.
- (developer tool) **The real-agent lab drives Muse Code** (`lab muse`, `lab muse-captures`)
  against a local stub of Meta's model API, beside Gemini CLI and agy.
- **`aterm ai`: one working login per AI CLI on every machine, a doctor, and reviews across
  AIs.** `aterm ai` shows claude, codex, agy and muse with one word each (`ok`, `idle`,
  `limited`, `due`, `unproven`, `signed-out`, `not-installed`, `off`), read from files alone:
  aterm reads no keychain item and runs nothing under a login to check it. `aterm ai doctor`
  then signs in, on a terminal you are at, each CLI that needs it through its vendor's own
  flow (Claude Code's through the accounts renewal; Codex's only when it is signed out, since
  its login revokes the current one), and `--on <host>,…` or `--fleet` does the same on your
  other machines over ssh. `aterm ai review` hands this directory's change to every other AI
  CLI used on this machine, on by default: each reviewer works in the repository with all its
  tools, settings and MCP servers, at the asking agent's own permission level, read from the
  asker's launch flags (a Claude Code run with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` gets yolo
  reviewers; a person in a shell gets yolo too). `[ai] review_permissions` pins `yolo`,
  `edits`, `ask` or `plan` instead, and `[ai] reviews = false` turns reviews off.
  Secret-looking files are held back from the change, answers are sanitized and
  credential-shaped tokens redacted, and a review is kept a day (`--show <id>`). The choices
  live in `[ai]` in `aterm.toml` and in an optional fleet document that carries them for many
  machines: `ai-fleet.toml` beside it, any file `[ai] fleet` names, or an `https://` URL,
  signed with `aterm ai fleet keygen` and `aterm ai fleet sign`, verified against the key
  `[ai] fleet_key` pins, fetched every six hours and held for offline use; an edited, replayed
  or expired document is refused and the held one stands. Settings ▸ Harness ▸ AI CLIs has
  every choice, with Fetch now. `aterm help ai` has the rest.

- **`aterm harness usage` works in a Codex session.** Run from Codex's own tools, it adds up every
  turn of that conversation per model (the TUI's thread and the subagents it spawned) from
  Codex's session files under `CODEX_HOME`, with list-price dollars where OpenAI publishes a
  price. A fork's or subagent's copy of its parent's history is not counted again (counting
  every file counted about 20 times the tokens served on the machine it was measured on).
- **`aterm ctl status` carries `reset_at=` and `reset_words=`** (`-` for none): where the window's
  harness placed a Codex wall's reset, and the words it placed. `aterm harness limits` prints
  that time only while the wall it reads shows those words; otherwise it places the reset in its
  own zone and says why on stderr.
- **The harness now supervises agy, Google's Antigravity CLI, and aterm reads Muse Code.**
  In an aterm window an agy session is handled as Claude Code and Codex sessions are: its
  permission boxes (a command, a new file, an edit) get their one-time Yes, pressed with the
  number agy draws beside it, and never its "always allow" options nor any answer agy saves to
  its settings; a question it asks gets its recommended answer (agy marks it `(Recommended)`
  at the front), else its first — a multi-select question, or one whose write-in answer you
  began, is left to you; and a job whose turn ends gets `keep going` typed into agy's input
  box. A draft you left in agy's input box is never typed over, and the hint agy shows there in
  a permission mode is not taken for one. A turn that ends on agy's quota, credits or
  high-traffic error is waited out or handed to you instead of continued.
  Settings ▸ Harness lists agy sessions and has a Supervise Antigravity CLI sessions switch
  (`[harness.agy] enabled = false` in aterm.toml). For Muse Code, `status agent=` and `await agent` now say
  whether it is busy, idle or waiting, but the harness does not act on it: its permission
  boxes have not been measured yet. Neither agent is relaunched when it exits or moved to a
  newer build while it runs. aterm never presses either one's sign-in options, which open a
  browser on your desktop; when agy loses its login, the harness tells you to quit agy and
  run it again. Shells aterm starts no longer inherit the `ANTIGRAVITY_*` variables agy gives
  the shells its tools run, its CSRF token among them.
- **`aterm harness limits` shows a Codex tab's usage windows.** Where Codex's `/status` card is on
  the screen, each of its limit rows (`5h limit`, `Weekly limit`) is printed as a window under
  aterm's own window ids (`five_hour`, `seven_day`), as the used figure (100 minus the card's
  `% left`), with the reset placed in the time zone Codex runs in. Credits are still shown for
  Claude Code only.
- **`status`, `ls` and `meta` have room for Autopilot's next two answers: when a session
  lands, and how its landing ended.** `aterm ctl @<sid> status` and every `ls`/`sessions` row
  now end their harness fields with `land_at=` and `task=`, and a bare `meta` ends with
  `land_at=`. `land_at=` will name, in unix seconds, the time a "Cruise until a time, then
  Land" session switches to Land; `task=` will say how a landing stands: `open`, `landed` (the
  agent finished after the land instruction), `done` (it said it was finished before a landing
  was asked), `spent` (no done reply after the nudges) or `theirs` (a person's own exchange).
  `task=` is printed only for an agent session this aterm's own harness is supervising, so a
  session another supervisor holds never shows a stale answer. Scripts that read these lines by
  key are unaffected.
- **`aterm ctl log` and `aterm ctl brief` say what a session has been doing, as a tree a
  program or an AI can read.** `log` lists the session's record oldest first: each shell
  command it ran, with its exit code and how long it took; each program that held the front
  (`less`, `vim`); for an agent such as Claude Code or Codex, each turn — who started it (you
  at the keyboard, or an `aterm ctl turn` with its ledger id), when it settled and how — and
  the approval boxes, questions and limits inside it. Every record says where aterm saw it and
  how sure it is. `log` narrows to one node, a level, some kinds or the turns alone, and reads
  on from where you left off (`since=` with `ep=`, so a self-update's restart is always said);
  `--json` gives the same records as objects. `brief` folds the same record into a short
  summary under a token budget (600 by default): the program in front, what it needs from you
  and since when, the newest turns and what was left out; `brief all` covers every session
  (Owner only). A command's arguments are never recorded: a command keeps only its program
  word (and a known subcommand), as `status detail=` shows it. Neither are the keys you type,
  nor screen text other than a usage limit's reset time. The record stays in this instance's
  memory: nothing is written to disk or sent anywhere.
- **List-price dollars for Claude Code accounts, the groundwork of the account stats.**
  aterm now carries a dated price table read on 2026-10-15 from Anthropic's and OpenAI's
  public pricing pages, each row naming its page, with one-hour cache writes and long-prompt
  prices kept apart. A model missing from it is unpriced, never guessed. A new fold prices
  every transcript of a Claude Code home from the last 8 days, subagents and workflows
  included, into 5-minute buckets, each message once in the home even where another
  transcript repeats it. Fast mode, US-only inference, web search and an advisor's work are
  counted as approximate. It is built to keep them in a private spend file beside the
  accounts state, so a second fold reads only the bytes appended since. From a window's usage
  reading it derives what a full window holds (`C ≥ $ ÷ used`), with its error bar, and what
  is left (`≈ C × (1 − used)`), with the newest reading's age, or the word that says why
  there is none, such as `on-credits` when usage credits served a message in the window, or
  `low` when the reading is too small or no whole five minutes of spend lie before it. None
  of it is set against Claude Code's own cost figure, which also counts calls its
  transcripts leave out. Nothing in aterm runs the fold, writes the spend file or shows these
  figures yet: the account stats will. `aterm harness usage --json` still prints `usd: null`.

- **Autopilot: one click sets how hard the Claude Code harness drives a session.** Two small
  chips now sit at the left of aterm's part of the rule under Claude Code's input box whenever
  aterm's harness is running. The first is the session's Autopilot. `∞` (Cruise) is the harness
  as it was: it answers what comes up and keeps the work moving until the agent says plainly that
  it is done. `⤓ land` (Land) asks the agent to finish the step in hand, start nothing new, leave
  the work committed and say so, and then types nothing more; an exchange of your own (a message
  of yours the agent answers within ten minutes) is left to you there too, with no land
  instruction typed after it. `○ off` (Off) takes the harness's hands off the session, so it runs
  as plain Claude Code, the baseline to compare against. Switching Off back to Cruise or Land (or
  the harness itself off and on) carries no task over from before, so a turn of yours it then
  sees run and answered within ten minutes is left to you; the point it comes back to is waited
  on and then acted on, as on any agent it attaches to, even over an exchange you had while it
  was off, so that it never stalls work it cannot tell from yours. Once a landing has spent its
  nudges such a turn of yours is left to you as well. A click moves Cruise → Land → Off → Cruise
  and types nothing into Claude Code. The second chip, `⚙`, opens Settings ▸ Harness. The mode
  belongs to the session and survives a restore and a seamless update; `aterm ctl @<sid> meta set
  autopilot cruise|land|off` sets it from a script, `status` and `ls` print `autopilot=`, and
  `[harness] autopilot` sets the default for sessions with no word of their own (`cruise` when
  absent). `[harness] enabled = false` still turns the harness off everywhere. Codex sessions
  have no chips; Settings and `meta set` cover them.
- **Claude Code's launch card shows when aterm is wrapping the session.** While the harness
  supervises a session in Cruise or Land, the card Claude Code draws at launch gets an animated
  rainbow border, a pixel-art aterm kitty riding a rainbow with stars, and a line naming the
  harness's version and the mode, for example
  `✦ enhanced by aterm harness v0.105.0 · autopilot ∞ cruise`. Land draws it in sunset colours,
  and Off leaves the card as Claude Code drew it. The animation plays for six seconds when the
  card appears, when the mode changes and when the window comes back to the front, and then holds
  still at no cost; reduced motion and serious mode show the still frame. Only the window's light
  changes: the session's text, and what `aterm ctl text` reads, is untouched.
  `[claude_footer] card = false` turns the card off.
- **Settings ▸ Harness shows what the harness is set to and what it did.** The page has the
  harness's status and version, its switches, each open session's Cruise | Land | Off, counts read
  from the harness's own ledgers for today and the last seven days (boxes approved, questions
  answered, continuations, landings, resumes after a limit or an API error, relaunches, upgrades,
  escalations, and how long it waited on you), how much of the time agents spent waiting for input
  in wrapped and in bare sessions during this run of aterm, and the effective `[harness]` table
  with which values are yours. Open it with `⚙`, View ▸ Coding Agent Harness…, or
  `aterm ctl open app settings /harness`; `aterm help harness` describes Autopilot.
- **When aterm brings up System Settings' Developer Tools list, its own panel sits beside it,
  saying why, with aterm ready to drag in.** No app can put itself on that list: only you can,
  and macOS asks for your password. So aterm does the rest. While System Settings is in front, a
  small aterm panel beside its window says what the list changes (macOS checks each new program
  aterm starts before letting it run, one at a time, so builds and tests wait; programs started
  by an app on the list should skip that check) and what you trade (everything run in aterm,
  agents and downloaded tools included, should then start without macOS's first-run malware
  scan), and holds aterm's icon: drag it into the Developer Tools list, or press + below the list
  and choose aterm. When aterm reads its switch on, the panel says so and closes. It hides when
  another app comes forward and closes when System Settings does. **Not now** (or closing the
  panel) keeps aterm from bringing the list up by itself for 30 days, 90 after a second time;
  your own presses still open it. The panel never presses anything in System Settings: the drag
  is yours. Whether this list takes a drop is not measured yet, so the + route is always
  offered beside it.
- **Settings ▸ Security leads with a DEVELOPER TOOLS card that says where the list stands for
  aterm.** It says whether aterm is on the list and switched on (and since when), switched off,
  not on it, or that aterm cannot tell and why; how many new programs macOS checked in the last
  ten minutes; how to add aterm, that only aterm's switch needs to be on, and what that trades;
  when aterm last opened the list for you; and, while your **Not now** holds, until when aterm
  leaves the list alone. Its *Open Developer Tools…* button brings up the list, with the panel
  beside it unless aterm already reads itself on. On a short window the card keeps its state
  line and button and leaves out the rest. The Developer Tools lines moved here from the MACOS
  ACCESS card, and the panel and the line in "To look at" (which gains a **Security** button)
  both lead to it.
- **`aterm ctl devtools hand-over [now]` asks the window to bring you to the Developer Tools
  list.** Every program in an aterm session can send it, so the window holds it to its own
  rules: the bare form waits for a quiet moment, and `now` only shows the panel; neither does
  anything while aterm reads itself on the list, while it has read neither the list nor macOS's
  answers about it, while your **Not now** holds, or within ten minutes (one, for `now`) of the
  last time; the bare form also does nothing on an ad hoc or dev build, or while aterm's row
  reads on and macOS still checks (the page then holds nothing to add). The answer says which. `aterm doctor` uses it: at a
  terminal it asks for the panel, prints two lines naming it, then opens the list itself; run by
  an agent it asks the window to do it at a quiet moment. Otherwise doctor opens the list itself
  only when no aterm window takes the request (for an agent, at most once in ten minutes and not
  while your **Not now** holds), or at a terminal when the window shows no panel, does not
  answer, or answers from an earlier reading that aterm is on the list, or that it cannot tell,
  while doctor has just read it is not; at a terminal it first prints the whole explanation, as
  the panel would have said it. `aterm doctor --help` now names `--read-only`.
- **agy (Google's Antigravity CLI) and muse (Meta's Muse Code) are managed agent programs,
  like Claude Code and Codex.** aterm installs each from its vendor and keeps it at the
  vendor's latest, and `agy` or `muse` typed in an aterm tab runs the managed copy; neither
  is mirrored or shipped inside aterm. An agy download is accepted when Google's update
  service and the per-version manifest beside it agree on its version, URL and sha512, and
  on macOS when it carries Google's Developer ID signature. The managed agy runs with its
  background updater off, aterm answers `agy update` and `agy install`, and its directory is
  read-only, so agy's updater cannot rewrite it even under an older aterm that hands those
  commands to agy. muse installs on macOS only, vouched for by Meta's Developer ID
  signature, and has no updater of its own. The update pass also contacts
  antigravity-cli-auto-updater-974169037036.us-central1.run.app,
  storage.googleapis.com/antigravity-public, api.meta.ai and lookaside.facebook.com;
  `[packages] exclude = ["agy", "muse"]` keeps either off a machine. The packages record
  names each program by its product name, so Codex reads Codex CLI there.
- **The harness keeps track of usage credits and Claude Code's usage warnings, and never treats
  them as a limit.** When Claude Code says usage credits carry a session past its limit (`Now
  using usage credits`), the turn simply goes on: the harness waits for nothing and types
  nothing for it. With `[harness] usage_notes = true` (off by default) on a machine that lists
  no Claude accounts, and on one that does unless `accounts = "off"`, aterm also records it for
  the account, with Claude Code's own warning that a window is filling (`You've used 80% of your
  weekly limit`), and "To look at" gets two lines: usage credits in use (once a day per
  account) and the week nearly used while credits are off. `aterm harness limits` now shows
  `credits=in-use` (`"credits":"in-use"` in `--json`), and `aterm harness accounts` shows the
  credits and the warned window. A session on a login renewed with `aterm harness accounts
  renew`, or still on the login it replaced, is recorded for its account, as its limits are.
- **`aterm harness accounts stats [--json]` says what Claude Code's profile knows of its
  account:** the plan and its tier (`Max 5x`), whether usage credits are on, out or off
  (with Claude Code's reason), and, as a hint, how the plan bills Fable (`Fable included`,
  `credits only`, `limits end <date>`, or `unknown` when Claude Code keeps that flag under
  another name or shape). It reads, on demand, the file Claude Code 2.1.301 reads for the
  home the command's environment names, and writes nothing. That is the home's
  `.claude.json`: `~/.claude.json`, the one inside the directory a set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`
  names (`~/.claude` itself included), or `~/.claude.json` again for an empty one. Under
  `CLAUDE_CODE_CUSTOM_OAUTH_URL` that file is `.claude-custom-oauth.json`. Claude Code reads
  a `.config.json` in the Claude directory in its place when that is not empty, or is empty
  and writable while the other is absent, and so does this, except under an empty
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` with no `CLAUDE_PID`, whose Claude directory it cannot know: there it
  looks for none. Each of these files can also hold an API key, MCP servers' tokens and the
  login's email and names, so it is read by an allowlist: only the plan, credits and usage
  fields and the two Fable flags are ever decoded, the rest is skipped unread, and the
  file's bytes are zeroed before they are freed. The account is labelled by its home,
  whichever of its files was read: by its roster row where the home is enrolled (the row
  with no `dir` for `~/.claude.json`, the row whose `dir` the set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` names
  for any other), else `main` for `~/.claude.json`, else `home-<key6>`; `--json` adds its
  key, a hash of the account's own id that is the same on every machine — the id itself is
  never kept or printed. A home it cannot resolve (a relative `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` with no
  `CLAUDE_PID`, or no absolute `$HOME`) reads `no-home`, not `no-profile`. This machine and
  Claude Code only for now; usage windows are not shown yet.
- **Name the cat and give the command in one run, in a script written without spaces.**
  `猫咪坐下` and `ねこおすわり` now command the cursor cat, in either order, and the whole run
  flashes. That reading is a guess (`猫咪洗澡` also begins a question about bathing a cat), so
  the run waits: Enter on a line of nothing but pet talk sends it, and so does the pet's name
  typed after it; anything else on the line drops it unseen. Words that would mean something
  else glued stay out of it: a name that is also an everyday word (`宝宝`, Thai `ลูก`), a
  command word that is a thing (`猫咪玩具` is a cat toy) and one that spells another word
  (`喂猫咪` is feed the kitty, `ネコ好き` a cat lover). With a space or `、` each is a word
  again. The name must be two characters or more, and Korean keeps its space.

- **Claude Code autocompacts at 400k tokens.** A window now adds `"autoCompactWindow":
  400000` to `~/.claude/settings.json` where the key is unset. On every model it takes the
  place of the window Claude Code would pick itself (a server-tuned one or a model's own
  default included), clamped to the model's context, so on a 1M-context model such as Opus
  5.5 a conversation is summarized at 400k tokens instead of near 1M. Each turn re-sends far
  less of the conversation, so it uses less of your plan's usage limits and answers sooner,
  and Claude Code's own "Want to autocompact at 400k tokens instead?" offer no longer
  interrupts a session. If you answered that offer "Keep", aterm adds nothing.
  `/autocompact` still sets the window for a model, a value of your own stays, and
  `aterm pkg doctor` reports which applies.

### Changed

- **aterm strips `GEMINI_*` from the shells it spawns**: Gemini CLI's shell tool passes
  `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_CLI` and `GEMINI_CLI_NO_RELAUNCH` to its shells. The agent primer is
  v23.
- **Under `question_priority = "long-term"` or `"short-term"`, a Codex question is answered by the
  worker too.** aterm writes the policy text as the note of `None of the above` (arrows onto
  it, Tab, the text, Enter only once the field shows it) instead of pressing the recommended
  answer; a question with no notes field is answered with its recommended answer, and says so.
- **A Codex that aterm relaunches keeps the permissions you chose in the session.** It resumes
  in the approval and sandbox mode its last turn ran in, so a `/permissions` change is no
  longer undone by its launch flags; the sandbox is never resumed narrower than the one Codex
  was first started with, across every relaunch (a later choice of Read Only is kept).
- Scrollback back-removal prepares its partial boundary once before committing,
  removing duplicate validation walks and decompression while retaining failure safety.
  Relay clients reuse request and count parsing, and development checks share their
  source inventory and manifest walk; an unreadable dependency graph stops further
