  unrecoverable error, and a limit still blocking three continuations an hour past its reset
  each write `EXCEPTION seq=<n> kind=<word> when=<later|now> <why> => <action>`, then `CLEARED
  seq=<n> exception=<word> after=<s>s …` when it ends. Waits that end by themselves (a reset, a
  fallback model, an API outage, Claude Code's countdown, a sleep) are one `WAITING` line; for
  a spend or credit limit the action is the admin's for a seat or an organization that cannot
  buy credits; in the window, an exception that can wait is one line of "To look at" naming its
  tabs (a lost login stays the tab's own alert), never the band or a notification.

- **A screen the supervisor cannot read is noted, then recorded, then one line of "To look
  at".** A tab that has read busy on background work alone for half an hour while Claude
  Code's title shows its idle `✳` gets one `STUCK …` journal line and nothing typed; at 90
  minutes it becomes a Warn record in Messages and an `aterm.log` error, and at 3 hours a "To
  look at" entry asking you to open the tab and type `keep going` (`Show tab`). It ends when
  the screen or the title moves, or the loop ends.

- **A Claude Code tab stopped at a dialog aterm cannot read is now told in "To look at"
  after an hour.** Claude Code's auto-mode billing notice (`Enter to continue · Esc to
  cancel`) is one: it has no options aterm reads, so the tab sat silent for as long as it
  stood. Now a tab whose screen has no input box and has not changed in words, while Claude
  Code's own title shows its idle `✳`, gets one `STUCK …` journal line at 10 minutes (with
  the rows on screen), a Warn record in Messages and an `aterm.log` error at 30, and at an
  hour one "To look at" line asking you to open the tab and answer the dialog (`Show tab`).
  Nothing is typed for you, since a key aterm cannot place answers the wrong dialog. It ends
  when the screen moves. A Claude Code panel you opened yourself and left open (`/usage`) is
  told the same way, once.

- **A conversation that `/compact` cannot shrink is one line of "To look at", for its tab.**
  Before, the supervisor kept compacting with nobody told; now, once the third `/compact` ends
  on Claude Code's `Compaction failed · conversation could not be reduced below the context
  limit` (about six minutes in), the line asks you to press Esc twice in the tab and go back a
  few messages (`Show tab`), and it ends when the wall leaves the screen. Claude Code only: a
  Codex tab's full context is not reported yet.

- **Claude Code's rating surveys are switched off.** A window now adds `"env":
  {"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY": "1"}` to `~/.claude/settings.json` at start, unless
  that entry exists or you set a nonzero `feedbackSurveyRate`. The switch stops every `1/2/3/0`
  survey ("How is Claude doing this session?" and its siblings), running sessions included,
  where `"feedbackSurveyRate": 0` stopped only the session survey; your own value, or an `env`
  that is not an object, is left alone. `aterm pkg doctor` reads the switch as Claude Code does
  (`1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`, no longer `off` or `no`) and says when your value leaves surveys
  on (a session aterm supervises still dismisses each with a `0`); from the next Claude Code
  build aterm stages, the managed `claude` launcher exports it too (for `--setting-sources`
  without `user`; the settings file still wins, and the store binary run directly does not get
  it).

- **Claude Code's "Bug report drafted" card is hidden.** A window now adds `"feedbackDrafts":
  "quiet"` to `~/.claude/settings.json` where the key is unset, so the card (`1 to review · 2
  to send · 0 to dismiss`) no longer covers your session; a typed `/exit` with drafts queued
  still asks, and `"off"` stops the drafting too. Your own value stays, and `aterm pkg doctor`
  reports it.

- **`aterm ctl privacy` says where the Full Disk Access question stands.** A new `access_card`
  row (an object in `--json`) gives `state=<quiet|asked|opened|granted|declined>`,
  `asked_at=`, `opened_at=`, `verified_at=` and `renew_at=` (unix seconds, `-` when unset),
  and `needs=`, how often macOS showed the "access data from other apps" dialog or refused
  aterm a read since the window started; `state=opened` lapses after 14 days.

- **An upgrade records why it waits.** `aterm harness upgrade --status --json` now lists each
  tab's last 24 changes of wait (`waits`: when, the word and the facts that decided it) and
  the first time each distinct wait was seen (`firsts`), so a multi-day stall's first cause
  stays visible. It gates nothing; older builds ignore both keys.

- **What needs a look, but not now, is one entry in "To look at", dismissed once.** Such
  things no longer go on the band one at a time: the menu-bar item shows `❯•` and lists them,
  Settings ▸ Messages shows them first, and `aterm ctl messages need=later` reads them, each
  with why you are needed and the one thing to do. Dismiss all files each entry in
  `messages.log` and keeps that fact quiet for a week (a month for a choice of yours, longer
  each time, across restarts and updates); an entry also ends when its cause ends (within ten
  minutes for a check that keeps reporting it) or after 14 days.

- **`aterm ctl messages live` lists only what is on the band or queued for it;** `need=later
  live` lists the entries of "To look at", and `aterm ctl chrome` gains a `statusitem` line
  for what the menu-bar item shows (`❯•` and how many).

- **Settings ▸ Messages can dismiss one entry of "To look at", or all of them.** Each entry
  has Dismiss after its action and the first of two or more has Dismiss all; the entry goes
  into `messages.log` at once and the page says "Filed in the log".

- **`aterm exceptions` reads that list with aterm not running.** It prints what was waiting
  when aterm last ran and the newest ten filed entries, from
  `~/Library/Logs/aterm/messages.log`; `--all` prints every filed entry in the log's newest
  MiB, and `aterm doctor` says how many are open.

- **`aterm ctl screen since=<etag>` answers "unchanged" without reading the grid.** Every
  `screen` frame now ends with an `"etag"`; sending it back as `since=<etag>` returns
  `{"unchanged":true,"seq":…,"gen":…,"etag":…}` until anything moves, so a polling agent stops
  paying for the whole grid. `screen` now refuses unknown arguments (`ERR usage: screen
  [--json] [since=<etag>]`) instead of ignoring them.

- **A live agent upgrade that waits on you says so under Claude Code's input box.** When the
  one thing holding a ready upgrade is you at the tab (input in the last 20 seconds, or in its
  first hour within `[harness] human_grace_s`, two minutes by default), the rule leads with `⇣
  Claude Code 2.1.286 waits while you use this tab` (`… is ready · waits …` once the agent
  answered READY under `[harness] upgrade_ask = true`), or `… waits until your draft is sent
  or cleared` with an unsent prompt. It goes once the move starts, a turn runs, something else
  holds it or you have been away a minute; before, nothing said why the move waited.

- **A supervised agent's memory has a ceiling aterm measures, and past it aterm warns**
  (`[harness] memory_ceiling`, `auto` by default). Past the ceiling is one Messages row per
  episode with the footprint, the Mac's state and the tab's `claude --resume <id>`, restated
  as that changes; aterm restarts the agent on its conversation at its next idle point only
  when the Mac is in trouble (critical memory pressure, or warn while swapping at least 4
  MB/s), the agent is the dominant consumer (the largest supervised agent and at least a fifth
  of memory in use), `relaunch` is on and the restart's own checks pass. `auto` is an eighth
  of the Mac plus half the memory available now, between 4 GiB (or a quarter of a small Mac)
  and half the Mac; a number sets GiB, `off` disables warning and restart, and the footprint
  measured is the physical one, not `ps`'s resident set.

- **An agent can tell the harness it is really done.** A supervised agent whose report ends
  with `ATERM-TASK-DONE` on a line by itself gets nothing more typed (no `keep going`, no done
  check) until a person types; the aterm primer teaches the token and the done check asks for
  it.

- **A tab at the API's own rate limit shows the next try too.** `API Error: 429` now reads
  `limited → 09:00 · 5m00s` (a screen reader hears "limited, next try 09:00"); the time is
  dropped when it passes with no try, or after the supervisor restarts.

- **A question can be decided by the worker itself, by a long-term or a short-term policy.**
  Set `question_priority = "long-term"` or `"short-term"` under `[harness]` (Settings:
  **Question priority**), or per session with `aterm ctl @<sid> meta set questions
  long-term|short-term|recommended|ask`: the supervisor types a fixed policy text into the
  question's `Type something.` row (or in place of `answer_text` for a question asked in
  prose) and presses Enter, never over text you typed. Where it cannot type it picks the
  recommended option; the default, `recommended`, is unchanged.

- **Kitty animations play, and Kitty images stack.** An animation started with `a=a,s=3` plays
  by itself at each frame's `z=` gap (40 ms for a frame sent without one; the first frame has
  none until set with `a=a,r=1,z=`), looping `v=` times; `s=2` waits at the last frame and
  `s=1` stops it, and an animation in a tab you are not looking at waits. Overlapping images
  now layer and blend in kitty's order (by `z`, then send order, then placement order), a put's
  `X=`/`Y=` offsets work, frames may be PNG, and a placement relative to a virtual
  (Unicode-placeholder) placement moves with it, all refused or ignored before; a cell holds at
  most 16 images, and unlike kitty, redrawing the same image in the same place replaces it.

- **`aterm ctl status` says when a resize left a screen one row off.** `render=desync-risk`
  appears a second after the size is back if the screen is still off, for Claude Code and
  programs that clear on resize (others read `unjudged`); `aterm ctl resizes` prints an
  `epoch` row, `subscribe … events` pushes `render desync-risk epoch=…` and `healed epoch=…`,
  and `aterm.log` gets a line for each. Windows ConPTY sessions are not judged.

- **aterm repairs a Claude Code screen a resize left one row off, by default.** It reports a
  terminal one row shorter, then the true size, so Claude Code repaints; no key is sent, so
  drafts and pastes are untouched, and it yields to a halt, a driver, your keys or a
  selection, at most three times an hour. `[render] repaint_nudge = "off"` (read at launch)
  turns it off and `"log"` only writes `would-nudge` lines to `aterm.log`; when it cannot
  repair, "To look at" says *Tab 3 may be one row off* and asks you to drag the window edge
  one row and back.

### Changed

- **On Windows, the default font is Cascadia Mono PL.** With no `font_family` set, Windows 10
  and 11 draw in Cascadia Mono PL 2407.24, built into aterm, with real italic and bold; its
  cell is 9x21 at the default 16 px (JetBrains Mono's was 10x21), so the same width holds more
  columns, and `ș ț ķ ļ ņ ŗ` keep their commas. It draws no programming ligatures: `font_family
  = "JetBrains Mono"` brings back the old font exactly, `"Cascadia Mono"` (without PL) still
  means Windows 11's installed copy, and Linux and macOS are unchanged. Its Powerline branch,
  lock and line/column glyphs and Nerd Font icons in prompts (oh-my-posh, Starship) come from
  the built-in Symbols Nerd Font instead of unrelated Segoe UI Symbol or Arial glyphs; aterm
  still draws the arrow, round and slant separators full height, and the extra separators small
  and centred. The Windows app folder carries `NOTICE.txt` and a `licenses` folder.

- **The Claude Code footer's `Σ` is one total, with Claude's working time, and the `○ fast`
  chip is gone.** `Σ` reads `Σ 7h52m ↑395M ↓2.0M`: Claude's working time, then all models'
  tokens in and out, merged (`aterm harness usage` still breaks them down by model);
  `[claude_footer] usage = false` hides it, the limit wall now reads `⧗ 5h ♻ 3pm`, and a
  narrow pane keeps only `Σ 7h52m`. Claude Code marks fast mode itself with `↯`, so aterm no
  longer types `/fast`; the `⏸ plan` chip and `ctrl+shift+tab` are unchanged, but with only
  one chip ← and → now reach Claude.

- **An agent the upgrade stopped has a `Show tab` on its row.** The upgrade row that stays on
  the band (an agent stopped, not exiting or not ready after its restart, or a paused Codex
  goal) now offers `Show tab N`, names the window when there are several (`… in window 2, tab
  1`), and follows the tab when you move it or open or close a window.

- **The earned flying kitty flies its meteor.** When Rainbow Kitty's caret jumps eight cells
  or more along its row, the flying head flies there banked and squinting, and squashes as it
  lands; before, it only jumped.

- **Under `[harness] approve = "safe"`, a Bash read the agent runs under zsh is pressed only
  when it expands nothing.** Where the Bash tool's shell may be zsh, as on macOS, a line with
  a `$`, a backtick, a backslash, a brace, parentheses, an assignment or a loop (`ls
  "$TMPDIR"`, `wc -l {a,b}.rs`) now asks you; plain reads are pressed as before, and the
  default `approve = "all"` is unchanged.

- **A script's `notice` posts under `script` or a tag of its own, never under one of
  aterm's.** `notice post` and `notice progress` now refuse every tag Settings ▸ Messages uses
  for aterm's own reports (crash, config, update, toolchain, packages, privacy, session,
  window, render, a11y, fabric, harness, system) with `ERR notice: that tag is aterm's own;
  post under script or a tag of your own`, where only toolchain, update and harness were
  refused. `notice post script …` or any other word (`deploy`, `ci`) works as before.

- **The harness's automatic stops are warnings now; each old stop is one switch away.** aterm
  no longer halts, kills or waits on a working agent on its own judgment:
  - **Live upgrade:** a Claude Code or embedded Codex conversation moves to a newer build only
    at a genuinely idle point (its turn over, nothing of its own still running, no box, no
    draft, nobody at the tab), with nothing typed before or after, except one carry-on line for
    a session an older aterm already asked to wind down, and no Codex goal paused; until then
    its Messages record says the newer build is installed and moves over when idle. `[harness]
    upgrade_ask = true` brings back the notice, `ATERM-UPGRADE-READY` and carry-on flow.
  - **A frozen agent** (`status input=stalled` for `stall_term_after_s`, ten minutes) gets one
    warning naming `aterm ctl @<sid> signal term` and keeps running; `[harness] stall_term =
    true` ends it for its relaunch, as before.
  - **Under `approve = "safe"`,** the rm circuit breaker on a possibly-empty variable is
    approved with a `WARN` ledger line (`rm-breaker-warn@v1`) instead of waiting; `[harness]
    rm_breaker_ask = true` sends it to a person, as `approve = "none"`, your own ask rules and
    hooks, and every other breaker still do.
  - **A lost fabric bridge** no longer halts its sessions: `status` says
    `hold_advisory=fabric-lost` and one Messages record names `[fabric] hold_on_bridge_lost =
    true`, which restores the halt. A hold a person set still halts.

- **What aterm tells coding agents is facts, not orders (primer v13).** The block in
  `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` and OpenCode's
  `AGENTS.md`, the bundled skills and the matching `aterm help` pages (the agent brief,
  `permissions`, `fabric`, `drive`) now say what happens when, instead of telling an agent to
  stop, check first or refuse; no fact was dropped, and a person's hold and keyboard still
  win. Stricter rules go in the same file outside the `<!-- aterm primer -->` markers, which
  aterm leaves alone; `aterm agents install` writes v13, and the block settles on v13 once
  your window runs this release.

- **A rerouted tool name warns in one line and runs, instead of stopping your command.**
  Inside an aterm session, `clippy`, `rustfmt`, `rustdoc` and `lean` with no Trust tool
  installed now run the upstream copy after a line naming `aterm pkg install <program>` or
  `aterm pkg repair` (they exited 127), `z3` runs upstream after a line naming `ay` (it exited
  2), and so does a stub that cannot reach aterm's package manager. Only a name with nothing
  to run still exits 127; `[reroute] announce = false` silences the lines and `[reroute]
  strict = true` brings back the refusals (`aterm help reroute`).

- **Keys sent to a program that is slow to read its input are written, with a warning.** A
  driver's keys, text and turns were refused with `ERR busy input-unread` after a second of
  unread input, which on a heavily loaded machine blocked healthy agents and aterm's own
  supervisor; the reply now says `OK seq=<n> warn=input-unread input_bytes=<n>
  input_wait_ms=<ms>` (on a `turn`, at the end of its verdict line on stderr). Writing is still
  refused to a program published as `stalled`, a stopped job with input queued, or a stalled
  program whose queue `signal term` or `reset flush` dropped, and the stall ages stretch with
  the load average per CPU (up to tenfold), so a CPU-starved program is called slow, not
  frozen, and "spinning" is judged against what one thread can get on the loaded machine, so a
  program frozen in a busy loop is still recognized under heavy load; `turn` still presses
  Enter only once while it sits unread.

- **The menu-bar `❯` item no longer rebuilds its menu each time a frozen program's row
  changes.** It shows the same up-to-date rows when you open it.

- **The web terminal's sparkle words scan the way the app's do.** On `/terminal`, a peeking
  cat's colours come from the cells it will cover, and a word still being typed waits for the
  next delimiter; the page changes when the site next takes a new engine.

- **An "agent the upgrade ended" row you dismissed stays quiet for a day, whatever the
  failure.** Such rows now come back once a day per tab, so a dismissal hides a new failure of
  that tab until the next day; the tab's mark and the log still carry it.

- **Every row that stays on the band says why you are needed and the one thing to do.** The
  GPU-lost row (open a new window), the screen-reader-lost row (quit aterm and open it again)
  and the Codex goal left paused (type `/goal resume`) now do too, and like every standing row
  they appear only after two seconds. The "Move aterm to Applications" row keeps its ten
  minutes; a message with no class holds at most two minutes.

- **A tab whose agent will not come back no longer marks itself for things you cannot fix.**
  "Relaunch keeps failing (still trying)" and "not relaunched: [harness] relaunch = false" are
  now log lines, and a relaunch held for an hour by something only you can end (a hold, a job
  in front of the prompt, the conversation open in another tab) becomes a "To look at" entry.
  The one remaining mark, an agent aterm could not bring back at all, names `claude --resume
  <id>` to run in that tab (or, with no command to name, is a "To look at" entry).

- **A limit the in-window supervisor will resume is a note on the tab's row, not a stop.** The
  tab shows `limited → 4pm · 3h41m` calmly, without the red rim, the filled diamond or "Agent
  can't continue", and a model or spend limit no reset ends says what to do (`→ /model to
  switch`, `→ add credits`); a limit nobody will answer (the supervisor or `resume_limits`
  off, another supervisor's claim, a lost login, Claude Code's critical-memory banner) keeps
  the stop. `aterm ctl status` reads `level=note` (or `story`) where it read `limited`.

- **`[privacy] observer` now defaults to a sentinel.** Where your account can read the system
  log, aterm watches only for the line macOS writes when it shows a consent dialog, with one
  `log stream` child restarted every fifteen minutes, about 0.4% of one core at rest.
  `observer = false` turns it off and `observer = true` keeps the full stream with the
  per-dialog banner, the "denied aterm access" banner and the tab mark, which now appear only
  then; no environment variable or control verb can turn it on from a tab.

- **The folder warm-up no longer asks for "other apps' data" by default.** macOS forgets that
  answer when the process is replaced, so the dialog had no lasting effect; Documents, Desktop
  and Downloads are unchanged, and `app-data` can still be listed in `warmup_folders`.

- **`aterm help permissions` says a disk walk from a session on macOS (`find /`, `find ~`, `du
  ~`, `rg` from `$HOME`) raises that dialog, whose answer does not last, and names `aterm pkg
  which <tool>` instead.**

- **A script's `aterm ctl notice post ... hold=` is at most two minutes.** A longer `hold=` is
  refused with the usage line, where up to an hour was silently accepted.

- **A Claude Code tab left a row off before an update is repaired after it too,** as is a
  Claude Code tab carried blank that does not redraw within 1.5 s. **Limit:** a tab already
  displaced when 0.100.0 or earlier hands off is not covered.

- **Upgrade answers with its reason and no snooze, for two minutes.** The answer to your press
  says why it cannot move past the agent's own work and folds into the log after two minutes
  (it stood half an hour), without "Not today" and "Skip version". The toolchain record says a
  running session is "still on the old build".

- **A Kitty image that declares a width or height over 10,000 pixels is refused, as kitty
  refuses it.** An image or animation frame whose `s=` or `v=` is above 10,000 now gets
  `EINVAL` and does not draw, whether it is sent whole or in pieces, PNG included. Before, a
  raw image up to 65,535 pixels a side drew, and a PNG drew at its own size whatever it
  declared. A PNG that declares no size is read at its own size, as before.

### Fixed

- **Tool output can no longer make the Claude Code harness act.** Text in an MCP tool's result,
  a `!` command's output or a file Claude read could look like a Claude Code error notice, and the
  harness typed it back as your turn, ran `/login` or `/compact`, or parked the session. The
  harness now acts on a wall only when Claude Code's own record of the session confirms it, and
  it never types screen text into a turn.

- **Scrollback no longer loses lines from the middle of history.** Output dense with long
  links could make a block of history that aterm could not read back; it was dropped, and the
  rows above it shifted. Such output is now stored in pieces aterm can read, and a block that is
  damaged anyway keeps its place as blank rows, counted as lost.

- **Reopening a file that changed on disk no longer reports an unsaved draft.** A file opened
  in the Editor or the Markdown viewer and later changed (a `git pull`, then a relaunch)
  showed "An unsaved draft conflicts with newer disk content" and kept another copy of the old
  text each time, until the file could not be opened.

- **Resetting a setting keeps your comments.** Use default and Reset deleted the comment lines
  you had written above the key in aterm.toml, and Undo did not bring them back.

- **`aterm fabric on` and `off` no longer break aterm.toml.** A `[ fabric ]` or `["fabric"]`
  spelling got a second table, the file stopped parsing, and every setting (automatic updates
  included) fell to its default. Both now refuse an edit they cannot make cleanly, keep a
  dotfiles symlink a symlink, and no longer overwrite a change Settings made at the same time.

- **A crash journal that cannot be read is kept, and the message names it.** aterm deleted it
  and then pointed you at the deleted file. Leftover temporary files from an interrupted quit,
  and old supervisor fault logs, are now cleaned up.

- **A link's caption names the site a click opens.** The caption under an OSC 8 link found the
  host differently from the browser, so `https://evil.example\…google.com/` showed google.com in
  bold, and a long `user@` part or extra slashes pushed the real host out of view. It now reads the
  address as the browser does. A plain-text URL no longer runs on through hidden (`ESC[8m`) text,
  and one with faint text in it shows the caption while the link modifier is held.

- **Program output can no longer switch off the multi-line paste warning.** A file shown with
  `cat` could plant a two-line clipboard and turn on bracketed paste, which outlived it, so the
  next paste skipped the warning and a shell without bracketed paste ran each line. Bracketed
  paste a finished program turned on is now handed back with its other modes.

- **A terminal answer is never typed into the shell.** A settings or capability query a program
  left unfinished was answered when the shell took the terminal back, and zsh read the answer as
  keystrokes. A query cut short is no longer answered, and an answer a program asked for is no
  longer lost when it resets the terminal in the same write.

- **In fish, New Tab opens where the shell is.** A folder a program reported (or a remote shell
  left behind after `ssh`) stayed the new-tab folder until the next `cd`; fish now reports its own
  folder at every prompt, as zsh and bash do.

- **A peer node cannot use up this node's fabric subjects or end a wait early.** Mail to sessions
  this node does not host, and notices to senders a peer made up, each opened a subject the broker
  never gives back; a third node's `expired` ended a `post --wait-ack` with a false `ERR expired`.

- **A folder-trust dialog and an `rm` are judged against the folder Claude Code was started in.**
  aterm took the folder the tab's shell last showed a prompt in, which stays where it was after
  `cd x && claude`, in a git worktree and when aterm restarts Claude in place (`aterm ctl meta`
  said `cwd=…/proj agent_cwd=…/proj/sub`), so a relative `rm` was judged against the wrong folder.
  It now reads the program's own folder first and the shell's second.

- **The harness no longer relaunches an agent into a tab another supervisor has claimed.** When
  an update attempt failed and was rolled back, an agent that had crashed during it, in a tab an
  outside supervisor had claimed back, was started again in that tab by the window's harness.
  Every such exit is now left to the supervisor that holds the tab. An agent that the harness's
  own upgrade or restart ended is still brought back.

- **The crash row counts a program shown in two windows once, and `aterm exceptions` says
  when `messages.log` cannot be read.** An unnamed job in a session open in a second window
  (`Open Session in New Window`) was counted as two lost programs. A `messages.log` that
  could not be read (no read permission, or a folder or link in its place) beside a readable
  `messages.log.1` made `aterm exceptions` and `aterm doctor` count that older copy's entries
  as open, though the current file may hold what closes them. Both now name the file that
  cannot be read.

- **`approve = "safe"` presses a plain Read again (Claude Code 2.1.284 and later).** aterm
  misread the path in those versions' Read box (`Read(/etc/hosts)`), so the safe level held
  every Read. A Read under a folder the harness may read is pressed again. These are still held
  for you: a secret or a path anywhere else; an offset, limit or page range
  (`Read(/etc/hosts · lines 1-5)`) on such a file, or on a link merely named like that; a path
  with a character outside printable ASCII (a newline, a tab, a letter such as `é`); and a
  path any of whose folders also holds a name that differs from the drawn one only by
  characters the box may not draw (a zero-width space, a soft hyphen).

- **A Read in your project that an ask rule or hook (yours or a plugin's) sends to you now waits
  for you.** The default `approve = "all"` pressed it. Claude Code offers `Yes, allow reading
  from <folder> …` on every Read box outside its working directory and `--add-dir` folders, and
  asks about nothing inside them, so a Read box on this machine without that choice is held at
  every level. A few boxes Claude Code raises itself lack it too and are held as well (a name it
  distrusts, such as `x~1.txt` or `paper.aux`; a folder with a very long path). A Read outside the
  project carries that choice even when your rule sent it, and so does a project file whose path
  Claude Code sees spelled another way (a link, a different capital letter,
  `/System/Volumes/Data/…` in front), so `all` still presses those: to have such a rule respected
  (`ask: ["Read(~/.ssh/**)"]`), set `approve = "safe"` (it presses only folders the harness may
  read) or `"none"`.

- **A Bash or WebFetch box your own ask rule or hook sends to you is no longer pressed for you
  (Claude Code 2.1.286 and later; on 2.1.284 and earlier, a Bash command Claude Code cannot
  check).** At the default `approve = "all"` the harness pressed such a box and the tool ran, and
  a WebFetch box stood unanswered. They now wait for you at every `approve` level, including in a
  narrow pane and when boxes stack (`2 of 5`). A Write or Edit box that your rule or hook
  forces shows no reason, so the default level still presses it; `approve = "safe"` holds it.
  On an older aterm, `approve = "safe"` or `"none"` holds the Bash box.

- **On Claude Code 2.1.291 and later the harness sends the `/compact` it types at a full
  context.** While Claude Code's slash menu was open, aterm lost track of the tab's composer: the
  `/compact` stayed typed, the tab came to you at once, and the retries and the `aterm exceptions`
  entry never followed. They now run as they do on 2.1.287. Until you have this build, a full
  context in such a tab is yours to `/compact`.

- **A permission box a subagent raised is answered again on Claude Code 2.1.291 and later, and so
  is the goal Claude proposes.** Both read as `idle`: the subagent's box was pressed at no
  `approve` level and the agent waited, and the `Claude proposes a goal` dialog stood unanswered.
  aterm now answers the box at your `approve` level, and at the default level it answers the goal
  `Not now`.

- **Long sessions use less CPU and memory.** Once scrollback is full, search drops the oldest row
  without re-encoding every posting list it touched. aterm's Codex context and sandbox check reads
  past a 16 MiB tool output allocating 34 MB instead of 318 MB. A Settings, About or document tab
  you leave frees its rendered page (six visited tabs: 4.5 MB to 0.75 MB). An inline image's source
  bytes are freed once no screen or history row holds it.

- **The merge gate no longer thrashes a Mac whose kernel holds memory wired.** It sizes its
  builds from the memory the machine can give them; when that is too little for the land
  tier's builds at once, they run one at a time and one start line names the usable figure
  and the remedy (a reboot).

- **The merge gate no longer claims the merge contract when a wedged `trustd` made tests skip
  their code-signing and TLS checks.** The verdict names one skip with the binaries and the
  remedy (a reboot) instead of reading `0 skipped — merge contract satisfied`.

- **A commit no longer recompiles all of aterm-gui.** The per-commit build stamp (commit,
  dirty flag, build number, build time) is now set in the `aterm` binary and installed at
  start, so an empty or docs-only commit rebuilds in about 8 s instead of about 3 minutes;
  `aterm --version` reports the same stamp.

- **`tools/release.sh` stops within minutes on a machine too small to verify every library**
  and names the RAM that can; it used to run for hours and then report "could not run". Its
  disk check asks only for what the remaining steps need, and a failed cut says whether a
  re-run resumes the build or starts again.

- **When the merge gate's trust lane fails, it names each failing library and its numbers**
  (for example `aterm-net RATCHET-REGRESSION(<49) 44/197`) instead of listing every possible
  cause, and it says a library ran out of memory only when the run shows it did.

- **`aterm pkg` names a case or Unicode clash instead of printing `Occupied`.** An archive
  holding `bin/tool` and `BIN/TOOL` is refused with the path and why: this filesystem treats
  them as one name.

- **On a small machine the merge gate states its RAM once**, then only what that RAM changes:
  how many test binaries run at once and whether the trust lane waits for the tests.

- **A forwarded control verb (`aterm ctl @<session> …`) no longer stalls after its connection
  is torn down.** On a loaded machine it could hold the lane for minutes; it now stops within
  200 ms.

- **On an 8 GiB Mac the gate's trust lane no longer fails the merge contract by chance.** It
  verified beside the test builds, whose load swung its proved counts; on a host that small it
  now verifies after the builds and tests, and says so in one line at the start.

- **On an 8 GiB Mac about 60 headless tests no longer fail the merge contract** ("no answer
  from … aterm.sock within 10s"). The test pool now runs only as many test binaries as memory
  holds beside the builds (2 here), and says so in one line at the start.

- **A double-click selects a whole Persian, Bengali, Sinhala or Mongolian word.** Words
  spelled with an invisible joiner or separator (`می‌خواهم`, `র‍্যাব`, `ශ්‍රී`, `ᠬᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ`) were
  selected in part; ⌥←, ⌥→ and ⌥⌫ in the find and tab-rename fields and M-f and M-b in the
  editor now step over the same words, and ⌥⌫ no longer deletes half a Hindi word.

- **A style sequence that ends in `;` resets what it should.** `ESC[1;m` left the following
  text bold and `ESC[38;5;m` turned on blinking; both now read the empty last value as the
  default, as xterm does.

- **A control string that a program cuts short with CAN or SUB is dropped, as other terminals
  drop it.** A half-written clipboard write, title, link or Kitty image no longer takes
  effect, and the next program's Kitty image still draws.

- **A program killed halfway through sending a Kitty image no longer swallows the next
  program's image.** A Kitty image sent in pieces and cut off between two of them took the
  next Kitty image any program sent as its missing piece, and neither drew. Where the shell
  reports its prompts (shell integration), the next prompt or command now drops the unfinished
  image. As in kitty, a delete sent between the pieces now runs and drops the unfinished image,
  a placement sent between them now shows while the image goes on loading, and a placement, a
  delete or a file image marked as a first piece now runs at once instead of taking the next
  Kitty image as its next piece. So does a first piece kitty refuses (a frame for an image
  aterm does not hold, raw pixels with no size, or a command naming both `i=` and `I=`), with
  its usual error. A query naming no `i=`, or a command naming both, sent between the pieces is
  answered and the image being loaded still draws.

- **`aterm pkg` holds a package archive to its signed size, and refuses one whose file names
  your disk treats as the same.** A damaged or tampered archive could decompress far past its
  signed size, and on macOS `bin/tool` and `BIN/TOOL` installed as one file, which `aterm pkg
  verify` then reported as changed.

- **With Kitty file transfer turned on, a program can no longer make aterm delete one of your
  files.** aterm now deletes only the temporary files the Kitty protocol lets it delete.

- **A few kilobytes of inline images can no longer make aterm use gigabytes of memory.** Each
  screen keeps at most 128 MiB of sixel, Kitty and iTerm2 images, dropping the oldest first.

- **Text that is not valid UTF-8 shows one replacement mark per bad sequence, as other
  terminals show it.** `cat` of a Latin-1 or Windows-1252 file, or of a binary, no longer
  pulls the rest of the line to the left.

- **Chinese, Japanese and other non-ASCII text inside a tmux passthrough, tmux control mode or
  another control string no longer spills onto the screen.**

- **⬅️ ⬆️ ⬇️ take two cells, as programs count them, and ✓ or ★ followed by the emoji selector
  stay one cell wide.** Window titles and the tab bar measure them the same way.

- **On Linux, HTTPS works when `SSL_CERT_DIR` lists several directories.** It failed with "no
  CA certificates could be loaded".

- **Tab-title summaries honor `NO_PROXY` IPv6 entries, and an entry such as `0.0.7` no longer
  exempts 10.0.0.7.**

- **Tab-title summaries use a proxy named only in `ALL_PROXY` or written with a login
  (`http://user:password@proxy:3128`), and a proxy setting they cannot use fails the summary
  instead of going around the proxy.** Both forms were dropped without a word and the request
  went straight to the provider. An `https://`, SOCKS or scheme-less proxy URL now fails the
  summary with an error naming the variable; give an `http://` proxy URL instead.

- **An `aterm.toml` or `[disk]` cleanup setting aterm cannot read now turns disk cleanup off
  instead of leaving it on.** `auto_free_gib = 0` written in an inline table (`disk = {
  auto_free_gib = 0 }`) was ignored, so cleanup stayed on at 10 GiB. When `aterm.toml` cannot
  be read or parsed, `disk` is not a table, or a `[disk]` key other than `warn_free_gib` has
  the wrong type or sits below another table's header, every removal is off, automatic cleanup
  and `aterm harness disk --apply` alike, until it is fixed. `aterm harness disk` says why, and
  "To look at" shows a "Disk cleanup is off" line naming the setting until it reads again. The
  config editor and `aterm --validate-config` show each such setting with the reason it is not
  read, and Settings ▸ Modified marks its row (a row that holds several shows the first). If the
  volume stays below its `auto_free_gib` floor (10 GiB unless set) meanwhile, a "Disk space is
  low" line says no cleanup ran and opens `aterm.toml`; it ends when space is back or the
  settings read again. While `auto_free_gib` itself cannot be read, an open low-disk line stays
  open.

- **Tab-title summaries work with servers and proxies that answer `100 Continue` or `103 Early
  Hints` first.**

- **A slow or stalled server can no longer hold a tab-title summary or a `dial` past its time
  limit, and a `dial` no longer drops the connection after a large reply.**

- **Tab-title summaries from the managed Ollama keep working on a busy Mac.** Before it sends
  anything, aterm checks which program owns the model server's socket. One `lsof` that took
  over 2 seconds ended that check, and the summary was skipped with 4 of its 6 seconds unused.
  A slow `lsof` is now retried until the 6 seconds run out.

- **Find, copy and double-click land on the right cells after emoji, Indic and Sinhala text.**
  After ©️, ▶️, a skin-toned emoji, a Devanagari conjunct or ශ්‍රී, find highlighted the cells
  beside the match, a copy gained or lost letters and a double-click picked the wrong word. A
  double-click on a line's empty part now selects nothing, and 🥷🏽 draws as one emoji.

- **A regex in find matches what it says.** With find's default ignore-case, `[[:^lower:]]` and
  `[[:^alpha:]]` matched letters they exclude; a stray repeat after a flag (`a(?i)*`) is now
  refused, and a pattern too costly for a long line is refused instead of stalling every
  keystroke, also in the web terminal's find, which could show a partial list as complete.

- **Large inline images and wallpapers show.** A 4096×4096 inline image, a large 16-bit PNG,
  or a wallpaper the size of a 6K display or a 24-megapixel photo showed nothing.

- **A TOML file can no longer crash or stall aterm.** A deeply nested aterm.toml or a cloned
  project's `.cargo/config.toml` could crash it, and a very long table name took seconds to
  read; a setting with extra values (`[1, 2, 3]` where two belong, `cursor_style = { bar = 99
  }`) is now reported instead of read in part.

- **A very long word in your `[sparkle_words] lexicon` file no longer slows drawing.** A word
  over 32 characters in a script written without spaces (Chinese, Japanese, Thai) is skipped,
  and the log says so.

- **Help, the man page, the control-verb catalog, the agent skills and Settings agree with
  each other and with the code.** The man page and `aterm ctl --help` give the right Linux
  socket directory, the meaning of ctl's exit codes 1 and 2 and which shells get session
  variables; `aterm ctl help` and docs/INTROSPECTION.md describe what `family`, `grant`,
  `dial`, `dims`, `connect`, `title`, `timeline` and `subscribe` reply; the skills and primer
  say what `no-bridge=1` means; and Settings, the Manual, `--help`, the Help page and the
  starter config show the same defaults, with Robi off until you turn it on.

- **Lift Hold, the Install press past a cap and `verify --full`'s memory line say what is
  true.** A refused Lift Hold says "Couldn't lift the hold" and to press it again, Install
  with too much open names what is over the limit and where, and `verify --full` waiting on
  RAM says how much would let both tiers build together.

- **Update capture refusals, Linux pre-install checks, disk notes and the candidate gate say
  what is true.** An update that cannot move your tabs keeps one Messages record saying what
  the retry waits for (past a cap, naming the window, tab or split and the limit), and one
  held only by unsaved Settings text asks you to save Settings. On Linux a release failing its
  check before install says `aterm <version> failed when checked here` with its exit status
  and first output line; `aterm harness disk` no longer claims it unlinked an executable it
  could not read; and the candidate gate on too small a host names each library's need and the
  RAM that verifies it.

- **On Linux, a slow-starting shell no longer gets a good update undone.** When several aterms
  started together (a terminal reopening tabs) and their shells took over 20 s to print a
  prompt (a network home folder, heavy startup files), the next tab undid and refused a
  healthy update; a silent session still running now gives them one more wait, while a build
  whose shell never starts is still undone.

- **An update that must leave something out of its hand-over leaves out what can be made
  again.** The connections granted between sessions, which `connect` makes again, are now
  dropped first, so a `--hold` pane's last screen and undelivered messages cross.

- **An update no longer forgets a still-failing "Couldn't check for updates" because another
  aterm window's same warning got better.** The new version took any window's same-day "works
  again" record as its own, dropping the warning and the day's "Update checks keep failing"
  line; only a record from the hand-over's own seconds counts now (another window's in those
  very seconds still can), and a warning that did clear no longer comes back after the update.

- **Keys typed into the old window in the last moment of an update are no longer lost.** With
  a `video` recording or export running, or a slow message log, keys typed in the update's
  last second were dropped; they now reach their tabs before the hand-over, and Hold This
  Session or Lift Hold in that moment says aterm is busy updating and changes nothing.

- **On Linux, a slow window no longer says updates work again while a stopped `aterm update`
  command still holds the update lock.** A check that failed before reaching the lock said so
  and restarted the two-hour wait; the notice now stays until a check finds the lock free.

- **A `subscribe … cells` stream re-sends the screen when a config reload re-colours it.**
  Changing `bold_is_bright` or `faint_opacity` now re-sends the frame on the next tick, as a
  palette change already did.

- **On Linux, a clock correction while aterm starts no longer undoes a good update.** When
  several aterms started together and the clock was corrected in that second (a board with no
  battery-backed clock), or they took turns in a different order than they read the clock, the
  new build was rolled back and refused before any prompt; the wait now uses a clock
  corrections do not move.

- **On Linux, an update that does not start is undone even after a release machine was
  replaced.** If the running build's signing machine had been retired, a new build that died
  at every start was kept and `aterm update rollback` refused, until a reinstall by hand; the
  earlier build now comes back unless the release channel withdrew it.

- **A withdrawn update installed on disk no longer raises "Couldn't install updates".** A
  newer installed build the channel withdrew was reported, hourly and at every launch, as
  waiting; it no longer counts as waiting.

- **On Linux, an update waiting for `aterm update apply` no longer costs every aterm a re-read
  each minute.** With an update held (`[update] auto_apply = false`, or an install held back),
  every window and session re-read the ~100 MB download each minute and each new session
  before its shell, and every window launch read the whole installed aterm; each is now read
  only when it has changed.

- **On Linux, an automatic update held back at the last moment keeps the earlier update's
  safety net.** The record of the update before it was dropped, so a window crashing at start
  was not rolled back and `aterm update rollback` had nothing to roll back; it is now kept.

- **On Linux, an `aterm update` command stopped with Ctrl-Z no longer stops updates without a
  word.** It holds the update lock while stopped; after two hours the window says what holds
  it, and `aterm update apply` names a stopped command as a holder.

- **On Linux, interrupted downloads and failed rollback copies no longer pile up beside
  aterm.** Each left a file up to aterm's size in `.aterm-update`; they are removed at the
  next check, install or rollback.

- **On Linux, a release your system cannot run says so, and is not downloaded again.** A
  release built for a newer glibc failed with "identity probe exited exit status: 1" and was
  downloaded again at every check; it now says "aterm N can't run on this system" with the
  loader's own words, and installs the copy it has if your system can run it later.

- **On Linux, Settings ▸ Packages keeps working in a window that was open when aterm
  updated.** Such a window said "Package tool missing" and every Packages button failed until
  it was closed.

- **On Linux, installing a held update by hand no longer says failing update checks have
  recovered.** After `aterm update apply` or a reinstall the window announced that updates
  work again with no check having succeeded; it now waits for one.

- **On Linux, launching aterm windowed where no display answers no longer rolls back a good
  update.** With a stale `DISPLAY` or `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` (kept in tmux, `ssh -X` from a machine
  with no X server), each launch counted as a failed start and the fourth rolled the build back
  and refused it and every later release; a launch now counts only once its display answers, so
  a window that crashes over `ssh -X` is still rolled back.

- **A notice closed in an update's last seconds stays closed.** It came back in the new
  version for its full time, and a warning that cleared then was recorded as cleared twice; it
  is now recorded once (except when updating from an older version, which does not say when it
  handed over).

- **Settings text an update could not put back is saved whole.** The notice showed each field
  cut to one line of about 240 characters and dropped fields past the 16th; the full text now
  goes to a file next to aterm's message history, named in the notice, written only once the
  new version has taken over.

- **An update held up by unsaved work keeps saying so.** "Update waits for you" showed for 45
  seconds and then never again; the row now stays until the work is saved, the update lands or
  stops trying, or you open it, and comes back the next time unsaved work holds an update.

- **The glowing border that explains a paused terminal during an update shows while the
  terminal is paused.** It started up to two minutes early, around a terminal that still
  worked, and could run out before the pause; it now spans the pause, and each pause gets its
  full time.

- **An update that tries again by itself is no longer listed as a problem.** Settings ▸
  Messages recorded it as "Couldn't install" under Problems; it is now recorded as waiting. A
  try that will not be repeated, or one you started yourself, is still recorded as not
  installed.

- **Quitting aterm after an update closes the shells it held, also when its link to the
  session keeper had reconnected.** A reconnected window counted its shells twice, so the next
  update's window was turned away and quitting left those shells running with no window,
  brought back under a false "aterm stopped unexpectedly".

- **Two aterm windows switching to the same update no longer pull it out from under each
  other.** A window giving up the update for a newer release could leave the other switching
  onto a deleted copy or starting the older version; a window now waits for other switches,
  and switches only while its update is still the one installed.

- **A healthy update is no longer rolled back because another aterm window was busy with the
  update at the same moment.** A start the old window stopped stayed counted against the new
  version if another window held the update lock over ten seconds, and two such moments rolled
  it back and refused it; the take-back now waits on disk for the next aterm to take the lock.

- **Quitting a Codex you started yourself no longer brings back the one that crashed.** Where
  aterm's relaunch of a crashed Codex was waiting, your own Codex's exit was taken for aterm's
  restart, ignoring your typing, a hold and `[harness] relaunch = false`, and the crashed
  Codex's `codex resume` line was typed back; aterm now counts only the exits its own upgrade
  or restart caused, as for Claude Code.

- **A desk with more than 64 windows, or a window with more than 256 tabs, updates in place
  again.** Each try froze every tab and gave up; now the extra windows come back as tabs of the
  last window and extra tabs move to the next window with room (or a new one), with every shell
  and title, and the new version says once what it merged; the merged desk updates again and
  reopens whole after a quit or crash. A desk too big even for that (64 full windows, or a tab
  split more than 32 times) waits for the desk to change and names the window or tab past the
  limit.

- **The windows of an aterm that was force-quit or killed come back, even when other aterm
  windows updated before the next start.** Each window start kept only the newest eight notes,
  often dropping the killed aterm's, so its desk was treated as closed on purpose; a note is
  now kept until its desk is reopened.

- **An aterm showing only document and Settings tabs installs its update even when it cannot
  save which tabs were open.** With aterm's data folder unwritable, the update retried every
  minute forever; it now installs without those tabs (nothing unsaved is lost) and Messages
  says why, once. A passing failure such as a full disk is still retried, and a failed save no
  longer leaves a file that opens your tabs twice.

- **Updating a window that shows only document and Settings tabs no longer freezes it while
  another aterm is busy starting or quitting.** If that aterm was stopped (Ctrl-Z), the window
  hung until it resumed; it now waits half a second at most and tries the update again later,
  without opening the saved tabs twice.

- **A `--hold` pane whose command failed is no longer flagged as a new failure after every
  update.** Its tab was marked failed again and `events` followers were told it had just
  failed; the update now carries whether you had seen it.

- **`aterm ctl update status` says why an update waits on a headless aterm, and what fixes it,
  even when a tab's foreground program could not be read.** On an aterm started with
  `--headless` (or with a control socket another process owns), it said the sessions "could
  not be proven safe" instead.

- **A window started from a terminal, whose new version would not start, comes back as a
  window.** After three failed starts, an `aterm --window` launched from a terminal came back
  as a terminal session in that terminal.

- **The newest notices, help and gate rows say what is true.** The lost-shell-integration note
  puts the count of unnamed tabs after the names, the scrollback note says why a kept-open
  pane's lines stayed behind, and a file changed on disk shows one recovery line. The harness
  help and the supervise skill no longer say a usage-limit reset is never taken; the gate's
  could-not-run rows name the suite and the binary it lacks, and `ship yank` without a build
  number shows the full command.

- **A pane kept open after its command ended keeps its turn history across an update.** A
  `--hold` pane driven with `aterm ctl turn` came back with an empty `history`, so `aterm
  drive ledger` called it typed by hand and `aterm drive report` found nothing; its turns and
  the tail of its full-screen archive now cross, and one whose turns could not cross says
  which may be missing (`unheld_below=`).

- **A topic followed, an escalation raised or a supervisor's claim taken while an update
  finishes is no longer lost.** A `topic add` or `topic drop`, a keyed `meta set attention
  owner=…` or a `meta set supervisor` answered `OK` after the update's snapshot was missing in
  the new version; the update now tries again with it, and a `topic` change during the
  hand-over waits for it, as `hold` does.

- **Right after a seamless update, a command sent to aterm is answered, and keys go to the
  pane you typed them into.** A `send`, `key`, `tab` or `update apply` in the first
  milliseconds got `ERR input dispatch failed: main-thread reply dropped` (or a false `OK`),
  and keys typed into a pane whose program ended during the update ran in another pane.

- **A turn-id count at the top of its range no longer blocks every later update.** Each update
  stood down with only aterm.log saying why; it now goes ahead, and aterm.log notes that turn
  ids may repeat.

- **A turn whose caller hung up keeps its place in `history` across an update to an older
  version.** Versions before 0.100 do not know `status=hangup` and dropped such turns from
  `history` and `aterm drive report`; aterm now writes them as `status=timeout` for those
  versions. A turn aterm cannot read makes `history` say which may be missing
  (`unheld_below=`) and gives a resumed subscriber a `GAP`, and a tab's history or archive
  left behind is named in aterm.log.

- **`aterm ctl metrics`, Robi's tips and the GPU fallback say what is true.** `metrics`
  refuses an unknown argument (such as a mistyped `reset`) with a usage line instead of
  resetting nothing; on Linux and Windows, Robi's tips show that platform's shortcuts and no
  macOS-only commands; resizing no longer writes swapchain debug lines to aterm.log, and a
  failed GPU start, or a lost GPU on Linux and Windows, prints one line with the cause and the
  switch to the CPU renderer.

- **Installing an update yourself no longer freezes every tab only to fail, when the new
  version asks for a lighter hand-over.** With `[update] auto_apply = false` (or Install
  pressed during the check), aterm read that request only after freezing; it now reads it at
  download. Software Update's Install, when it cannot start yet, says "Not installed yet" and
  why.

- **After an update from aterm v0.98 or older, a background tab no longer shows a command that
  has finished.** Those versions refreshed a tab's title only while it was in front; the new
  version takes each tab's title as it was at the update, or shows a background tab's folder
  when that reading was missed.

- **A session can opt into at most 32 broadcast topics, so a script that kept adding them can
  no longer block every update.** A 33rd `aterm ctl topic add` answers `ERR topics full (max
  32): drop one first`; a tab carried from an older aterm with more keeps them all.

- **A window whose tabs were granted the same connection over and over can update again.**
  Repeated `aterm ctl grant` rows could make every update fail; the hand-over now carries each
  connection once and, if still too large, leaves out the connections of the tab holding the
  most (make them again with `aterm ctl connect`). `RUST_LOG=session_edge=info` logs them as
  dropped once, when the update happens.

- **An update on a desk of more than 62 tabs no longer takes the slow path because the new
  build's Info.plist could not be read for a moment.** Near the open-file limit, one failed
  read made every update for ten minutes or more freeze all tabs for seconds instead of about
  20 ms; the next attempt now reads it again.

- **A downloaded update whose signing machine has since been revoked is no longer installed
  when aterm starts.** aterm installs a downloaded update at start only if it confirmed within
  the last day that its signer is still trusted; otherwise it starts on your build, and the
  check right after either confirms the signer (installing within seconds) or throws the update
  away, and the wait never counts as a failed install; pressing Install while it waits says so
  instead of closing and reopening the window, and a running aterm reconfirms hourly. If no
  check can confirm it (the channel's newest release is not an app release, or a signing-key
  change means this build can no longer read the trusted list), `aterm ctl update status` says
  why; after a key change, reinstall from the current release. A revocation published less than
  a day before can still be missed.

- **`aterm exceptions`, the diagnostic commands, `aterm pkg`'s plumbing, agent relaunch lines
  and the paste question say what is true.** `aterm exceptions` lists warnings first, says how
  each filed entry ended ("fixed", "answered Allow") and when the log cannot be read, as does
  `aterm doctor`; `aterm explain-config` starts with where aterm.toml is, and `aterm
  show-face` with no font points to `aterm list-fonts`. `aterm pkg lease`, `lane`, `verify`,
  `link`, `unlink` and `refresh` say what they refused, a timed-out agent relaunch line says
  what held it (Codex too), and on Linux the multi-line paste question says each line may run
  as a command.

- **A Claude Code that crashes in the first minute after a seamless update is brought back.**
  During the 45 seconds aterm waits before supervising a tab another supervisor may take back,
  a crash left a bare shell prompt; aterm now watches from the start, relaunches a crash on
  its conversation, leaves a `/exit` you typed alone, and leaves a tab taken back to its
  supervisor.

- **An automatic update that a tab's contents keep refusing no longer freezes every tab every
  30 seconds.** A refusal that comes back now waits 10 minutes after the second, then 30,
  never longer than the hourly retry, and "Update waiting" says so ("tries again when you
  close some, in 10 minutes at the soonest").

- **An update from 0.98 or older installs in place on a desk of busy shell tabs.** Those
  versions could write a handoff file over 4 MiB, which was refused every time; the new
  version reads up to 32 MiB (and still writes at most 4 MiB, so a rollback keeps working).

- **On Linux, an update whose terminal sessions hang at start is rolled back on a copy used
  only from the terminal.** A session counted as a healthy start after ten seconds even if its
  shell had printed nothing; it now counts only once the shell's first output arrives.

- **In-window notices, the contributor build path, macOS privacy prompts and the release docs
  say what is true.** Configure Connection… and Disconnect Session… on a tab with no
  connection say so; the lost-shell-integration row no longer blames an update after a crash
  recovery, and the scrollback cap under memory pressure is sized to the Mac's RAM. A
  non-Trust compiler on an Intel Mac or Linux is refused with a line saying Trust ships only
  for Apple-silicon macOS; privacy prompts say everything you run inside aterm shares one
  folder grant; and `brew uninstall --zap` removes aterm's config, logs and cache directories.

- **On macOS, a seamless update no longer hands your sessions to another program that read its
  one-time secret.** The secret travels in the new version's environment, which any program
  running as you can read (`ps eww`); the old version now also requires the asker to be an
  aterm release signed by aterm's Developer ID and refuses anything else while it waits for
  the real one. A program running as you can still slip past by sharing its connection and
  replacing itself with aterm, so this narrows the risk without closing it; an update signed
  under a different name now moves your sessions as a child of the old version instead of
  being turned away on every try.

- **A pane kept open after its command ended keeps its scrollback across an update.** A
  `--hold` pane, or a failed start kept on screen, came back with only its last screen; now
  its whole scrollback crosses, never at an open tab's expense, and when it cannot (an update
  to an older version, a request to carry no scrollback, a deep pane not read within five
  seconds, or a failure) the note says how many lines stayed behind and why.

- **With the PTY keeper on, a crash right after a second update in a row puts each kept shell
  back in its pane.** Every shell came back as a separate tab, and an agent's pane started its
  conversation a second time beside the one still running.

- **Wide panes and half-sent titles no longer refuse a seamless update.** Tab stops past a
  pane's width and an unfinished escape sequence are dropped first, and the largest panes are
  redrawn by their programs if that is still not enough.

- **A seamless update lands while a tab streams sixel pictures or sits behind tmux
  passthrough.** The update waited for a pause that never came; tmux passthrough and
  control-mode streams now cross exactly, and a half-sent sixel picture is dropped after the
  free retries, replaced by the stream's next frame.

- **An update from 0.97 that the new version asked to leave scrollback behind no longer says
  the carry failed.** The note now says the new version asked for it.

- **The in-app Help, `aterm pkg`'s update and machine commands, more help pages and the config
  editor say what is true.** Help says the clipboard-read and window-ops opt-ins take effect,
  lists the split-pane shortcuts (⌘D, ⌘⇧D, ⌘⌥ arrows, ⌘⇧↵) and shows `aterm ctl turn`; `aterm
  pkg update`, `rollback`, `uninstall --all` and `seed` give the state once, and rolling back a
  program that is not installed says so; `aterm pkg machine` says Universal Control and
  Spotlight settings apply once a day, at the first window or session. `aterm help ty` and
  `clean` list commands that run, `aterm help doctor` and the other diagnostic commands open
  their page, and the config editor's save and recovery lines say what happened and what to do,
  and a refused save of a recovered aterm.toml shows why.

- **Package maintenance, attach-mode windows, the release and verifier help, and Find say what
  is true.** `aterm pkg install --default-set` and `update` stop before installing when the
  disk cannot hold the toolset and say how much is needed; `gc`, `verify`, `pin`/`unpin`,
  `repair` and `run` state what happened with one command to run. With `windowing_behavior =
  "attach"`, a new tab unanswered for 10 s no longer opens a second window; `aterm help ship`
  gives the one release command and what a bare machine runs first, and `aterm help trust`
  starts with the command to run; Find says why a count is a floor (the match limit or the
  history depth).

- **Connection failures, package notices, the harness help, the toolchain rows and the
  operator brief say what is true.** When `aterm ctl ls`, `instances` or `windows` cannot
  reach an instance it names the cause, and a dead `--sock`/`--pid` target points to `aterm
  ctl instances`; package notices give real numbers and one next step (a disk refusal shows
  what is needed, free and to clear; a broken aterm.toml is reported once). `aterm help
  harness` gives the live upgrade's default correctly and the keys that widen the supervisor's
  power; the ALab tools rows in Settings ▸ Messages give the full undo for Universal Control
  and name a shell aterm cannot hook into; and the operator brief says the window already
  supervises every Claude Code and Codex session and that you take a lease before you drive
  one.

- **Replacement notes, the multiplexer check and agent rows say what is true.** When aterm is
  replaced under a running `aterm ctl` call, the note says in one line what happened and what
  to re-issue, without calling every replacement an update, and a `--pid`/`--sock` call that
  finds nothing points to `aterm ctl instances`. `ATERM_MUX=0` turns the screen/tmux check off
  in every pane and `ATERM_MUX_NOTICE=0` silences its note; agent rows name the tab by its
  place, and the warning that agent upgrades cannot run names the folder to fix.

- **Banners, `aterm conn` and the agent PATH warning say what is true.** The macOS
  permission-waiting banner names the tab whose program asked, and the file-access-denied
  banner just says to turn on aterm in Full Disk Access. `aterm conn` prints every session
  as the `@<sid>` you can paste back, says which drives which after a spawn, and names the
  session a refusal is about. When aterm cannot put the managed claude and codex first on
  PATH, the warning opens with that fact.

- **The agent primer and skills, the Claude Code footer and the supervisor's messages say
  what is true.** The primer no longer says a lost fabric bridge halts a session, says the
  harness continues only Claude Code and Codex sessions, and names the aterm.toml the
  window reads when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set. The agent skills match what aterm does:
  desktop notifications are off by default, a timed-out task is already queued, and a
  starting bridge answers `queued=1`. The footer's path and branch follow the directory
  Claude's Bash tool works in, and the permission light greys out for a mode it cannot
  read. The supervisor says "Codex reported" on a Codex worker and names the setting that
  stopped it.

- **Update, accounts, keeper and Windows-source messages say what is true.** The desktop
  banner for an update aterm cannot install says what to do (install the signed release,
  or move aterm or ask an admin). `aterm harness accounts` drops columns that were always
  empty, and a session waiting for another account says so. When aterm cannot read its
  update records it says no update installs until it can, and `aterm keeper stop` prints
  the pid of a keeper it cannot end. On a Windows build from the public source, `aterm
  update` says the rebuild it names needs the Trust toolchain for Windows, which is not
  published yet.

- **`aterm --help`, the window's tab text, update logs, the docs and the Linux and
  Windows notes say what is true.** `aterm --help`, `aterm help` and `man aterm` say that
  `aterm ctl` drives an aterm window's sessions and that the agent brief prints in a
  window's tab, and explain each containment mode once. Tab and pane hover text says each
  fact once, without "(heuristic)" or FOCUSED. Update trouble messages point to the log
  aterm actually writes, also with `$XDG_STATE_HOME` set and on Windows. The introspection
  and agent docs spell the commands an install puts on PATH (`aterm ctl`, `aterm
  --headless`). The Linux installer says when `--version` names a release newer than the
  latest, and the Windows notes no longer point to a build that cannot work.

- **What a program prints can no longer slip text into your prompt, and a pasted command
  asks first.** A kitty colour query naming an unknown key echoed that key back into the
  shell's input; now only a plain name is echoed. When the shell has not turned on
  bracketed paste, pasting a single line that ends in a newline (which runs it at once)
  now asks first, as a multi-line paste already did. A tab title beginning with ⚠ is
  shown in the menu-bar item folded to one short line, and the clipboard writes programs
  make are held to a bounded amount of memory per tab.

- **A Containment shell can no longer start programs outside its sandbox.** Under
  `--containment containment`, a contained program could ask macOS (`open`, or Apple
  Events) to start or drive a program that is not sandboxed; now both are refused. git,
  Python, compilers, `codesign` and the shell itself work as before.

- **A scoped control token stays within the session it was given.** Its typing could land
  in another tab or the command palette when the front tab changed mid-request, and it
  could capture the whole window with `image` and list every session with `privacy`. Its
  input now goes only to its own session, it is refused the window image (its session's
  own inline images still read), and `privacy` lists only the sessions it can read.

- **Mail and delegated tasks believe only the sender they can verify.** A task's answer
  and a worker's report are taken only from the worker itself, so another node cannot
  answer for it. `aterm drive task` text can never be read as the message's address or
  kind, and `--wait` shows a reply's control characters escaped in a terminal.

- **The shell prompt no longer hands its integration key to child programs.** In bash, a
  prompt your startup files exported carried the tab's shell-integration key into every
  program's environment, letting it fake command boundaries.

- **atpkg writes and runs only what it means to.** The automatic Spotlight pass no longer
  writes through a project's config symlink to a file outside the project, and a stub
  whose atpkg moved no longer finds `atpkg` in the current directory.

- **A window hands its terminals only to a keeper that checks code.** A keeper started
  with `--identity uid` would offer a crashed window's terminals to any program of the
  same user; a window that checks code now registers nothing with it. If you turned the
  keeper on, restart it once after this update (`aterm keeper stop`, then `aterm keeper
  start`): a keeper from an earlier build is refused until it is replaced.

- **A seamless update lands while a tab streams pictures.** A tab showing kitty or iTerm2
  images froze the desk about 34 times and then gave up, every 30 seconds, for as long as
  it ran. The update now lands and drops only the half-sent picture, which the stream's
  next frame replaces. Oversized colour and title stacks no longer refuse the update, and
  keys typed while the old window writes its last messages reach the shell. A control
  socket that rebinds during the wait now gets a retry instead of counting against the
  new version.

- **After a seamless update, a pane scrolled up stays where it was.** It is no longer moved
  into output written after the update. Turn ids from before the update are not reused
  after it, and a rolled-back update no longer prints an exited pane's last line a second
  time.

- **`install.sh` no longer refuses a Linux reinstall as "below apply floor" after a signing
  machine was revoked.**

- **The quit dialog, configuration, `aterm ctl` refusals, help topics and `aterm update`
  say what is true.** The quit dialog says your shells and their scrollback end and your
  windows and tabs come back when aterm starts; on Linux the title-bar warning says
  whether a repeat closes the window or quits, within 2 seconds. `aterm help config`
  names the commands that check an edit, and `--validate-config` and `--show-config`
  match what aterm.toml does. `aterm ctl` refusals say why: which of the `@<sid>` or the
  token failed, the grid size or limit an out-of-range request crossed, and why the
  operator is unavailable. The `agents`, `ay`, `ny`, `nn` and `trust-backends` help pages
  describe what ships. `aterm update` points a wrong word at the right command, and Linux
  rollback refusals name the build and the reason.

- **The keeper, help, palette, fabric and the dev build say what is true.** `aterm keeper
  stop` reports `keeper=stopped` only when the keeper has ended, and names one still
  running with an error exit. `aterm help reroute` says the stubs return after `aterm pkg
  uninstall --all` only with the next explicit install. `aterm help rust` suggests `aterm
  pkg repair` only when there is a toolchain to link, and `aterm help permissions` gives
  the Full Disk Access remedy once. The tab menu's controlled and controller session rows
  connect to the tab you right-clicked, and the palette no longer offers terminal commands
  with no terminal in front. `aterm fabric` and `aterm help fabric` say a lost bridge
  leaves its sessions running and is relaunched. The installer and the dev build stop
  after a minute with one line when macOS's code-signing service does not answer, instead
  of hanging.

- **A code-signing check macOS never answers no longer hangs aterm.** When macOS's
  code-signing service (`trustd`) stops answering, the keeper's identity checks, `aterm
  doctor` and `atpkg relocate` refuse within seconds and say `trustd` did not answer — an
  installed build with the keeper on no longer hangs before its first window. Later
  checks are refused at once until it answers again.

- **A certificate check macOS never answers is refused after 30 seconds instead of
  hanging.** When macOS's certificate service (`trustd`) stopped answering, aterm's TLS
  connections waited forever. Now the first is refused after 30 s with a line saying the
  service did not answer, later ones at once, and connections work again as soon as it
  answers.

- **`aterm doctor`, drive, fleet, the harness CLI, the menu bar and Software Update say
  what is true.** `aterm doctor` no longer fails when `$SHELL` is unset — it checks the
  `/bin/sh` aterm starts then — and a shell that cannot start is named missing or not
  executable, with the fix. `aterm drive --help` and `aterm fleet --help` give commands you
  can type, and say which waits stop at the 10-minute host cap. `aterm harness upgrade
  --status` says under each row what holds the upgrade, and a deferral shows the time left.
  Clicking a "To look at" line in the menu bar opens that entry. Software Update, the menu
  bar and `aterm update status` name why a copy cannot update (run from the disk image or a
  temporary copy, a plain binary, an unreadable update folder) instead of "Offline".

- **Help, `aterm ctl`, `aterm pkg`, Settings and the installer read as a whole.** Inside a
  session, `aterm help topics` opens the list of every verb and topic, and the agent brief
  points coding-agent drivers to `await agent` and fits a 100-column terminal. `aterm ctl
  help` lists the `stale` fabric state with how to end a stale bridge, and `ready`, `wait`
  and `await` state their replies and the 30 s default and 600 s maximum timeouts. `aterm
  pkg doctor` says each rustup `trust` problem once, with a fix that works. Settings ▸
  Security shows a missing or moved aterm bundle as its own line. The installer's closing
  lines are shorter, and the README says Intel Macs get the toolchain without the Trust
  compiler.

- **A fish tab opened by aterm 0.94 through 0.100 under its own prompt takes a newer
  integration again.** A prompt `config.fish` defines (`starship init fish | source`,
  oh-my-posh) kept those tabs from ever taking a newer integration: `status
  integration_rev=` read `-`. The live agent upgrade now upgrades every shell that does
  not report this build's integration; the shell's own prompt is untouched, and from then
  on it takes each update's integration at its next prompt.

- **bash's default prompt no longer grows at every prompt.** `PS1` gained one 84-byte
  shell-integration mark per prompt (95 to 1,691 bytes over 20 prompts, bash 3.2 and 5.3
  alike), and every prompt re-sent them all. A tab that already grew them sheds them at
  its first prompt on this build's integration, also with a `PS1` holding a byte its
  UTF-8 locale cannot decode (a Latin-1 `é` from an older rc file).

- **An update step that could not finish is no longer held against the new version.** A
  download hash check on a disk or network volume that stopped answering now ends within
  two minutes, where it held every aterm's update check until a relaunch. A `codesign` or
  `spctl` run killed on a loaded Mac is tried again instead of telling you to reinstall a
  healthy aterm or throwing away a good download. A window whose sibling installed the
  same update first, or that waited on another aterm or a momentary hiccup, no longer
  spends one of the new version's two install attempts or delays its download by up to a
  day. A bundle modified after it was signed is still refused.

- **A staging step that times out every time no longer downloads the whole update again
  at every check.** On a network that stalls Gatekeeper's check, every aterm fetched the
  release again about every 40 minutes. It now waits longer each time (at once, then 15
  minutes, an hour, at most four hours), the notice says so, and Check for Updates still
  tries again at once (for example after you free disk space). A download found to be bad
  keeps its own schedule.

- **An update downloading in a terminal session no longer looks stuck to the window.**
  About 65 minutes into a download on a slow link, the window warned that another aterm
  "may be stopped or hung" and could go on to say another aterm was stuck staging.

- **A release withdrawn while it downloads ends the check as held, not failed.** When the
  release's signer was revoked, or the release was withdrawn or quarantined on this Mac
  mid-download, the check said it failed and would retry, which it never would. It now
  says the release is not being installed.

- **aterm's update floor file is never erased by a read that failed, and a file that stays
  unreadable is said.** A moment's failure to read it (too many open files at launch, a
  disk error) replaced it with defaults, losing what keeps a withdrawn or replayed release
  out. Such a read is now refused and retried. A file that stays unreadable (owned by root
  after a `sudo` run, say) raises the persistent update notice naming the file and the
  fix, where updates used to stop with no notice.

- **A filtering proxy's page in place of a release signature is a download problem, not a
  reason to reinstall.** It was read as a stale trust anchor ("reinstall aterm"), which a
  reinstall behind the same proxy never cleared; it is now retried like any download
  failure.

- **On Linux, `aterm update check` names the release it just installed.** It named the
  version that was running, as if nothing had changed.

- **An update held after it failed to start is tried again the next day, even where
  Gatekeeper checks keep timing out.** Three inconclusive checks (a captive-portal
  network) dropped the daily retry for good. They no longer count; the retry moves to the
  next day instead, and `aterm update status` says so.

- **`aterm drive await-turn --reconnect-s`, and `supervise`/`watch` on the
  one-call-per-request client, ride out an aterm self-update again.** `await-turn` exited 1
  at the first update instead of printing `RECONNECT` and reading the new instance, and
  `--mail` switched itself off. An update cut (exit 75) now counts as a request the server
  never answered, and the outage is still bounded by `--reconnect-s`.
